title: Mike Macdonald: Kenneth Walker is playing at the highest level in the league right now
summary: Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald knows how good a running back he'll be facing when he coaches against the Chiefs on Sunday night.
full_text: Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald knows how good a running back he'll be facing when he coaches against the Chiefs on Sunday night. Madonald coached Kenneth Walker in Seattle, Walker won the Super Bowl MVP at the end of last season, and then Walker left for Kansas City, where he's gaining yardage a record-breaking pace . "Ken's playing really great football," Macdonald said on SiriusXM NFL Radio . "I think it's a combination of, you see the stats and you're like, man, that's a lot of stats. And then you turn the tape on and see how they're playing and how he's playing and you're like, 'That makes sense. No one has tackled this guy yet.' It's the things we knew about Ken, that he does really well. He's so strong, he's decisive, he's got great vision. He's also come alive in the pass game. They're doing a great job with him. He's playing probably at the highest level in the league right now." Macdonald said his defense had a big challenge on Sunday night. "It's got to be a team effort on defense," Macdonald said. "It's gonna take waves of Seattle defense to eliminate those explosive plays he's been able to create."
author: Michael David Smith

title: Ben Johnson originally called a punt, but Cairo Santos asked to try a 58-yard field goal
summary: After Bears head coach Ben Johnson initially called for a punt late in Thursday night's win over the Patriots, Bears kicker Cairo Santos convinced his coaches to let him try the 58-yard field goal that sealed the win.
full_text: After Bears head coach Ben Johnson initially called for a punt late in Thursday night's win over the Patriots, Bears kicker Cairo Santos convinced his coaches to let him try the 58-yard field goal that sealed the win. Earlier in the fourth quarter, Santos had missed a 53-yard field goal attempt, and Santos had never made a field goal as long as 58 yards in his NFL career. So it's easy to understand why Johnson was planning to punt. But Santos told special teams coordinator Richard Hightower, whom the players call HT, that he would make the 58-yarder if given the chance. "I was right next to HT and Ben originally called a punt, and then the injury allowed us to talk about it. I was talking to HT that I felt good about it," Santos said. "Ben asked, 'Does he want it?' And I heard it and I told HT I want it and he said, 'Ben, Cairo says he wants it.' Thankful that Ben trusted me on that, and I delivered a great kick right down the middle." Why was Santos confident he could make a 58-yarder only minutes after missing a 53-yarder? "It's just who I am, really," Santos said. "The misses annoy me, but I can clear it so quick. The next opportunity, I can just lock into my routine and trust that I can execute." Johnson was wise to trust his kicker, and that 58-yarder proved to be the play that clinched the win for the Bears.
author: Michael David Smith

title: NFL tells teams that uncalled hip-drop tackle on Aaron Rodgers was clear example of penalty
summary: In Week 4, Browns defensive lineman Adin Huntington committed a textbook example of a hip-drop tackle on Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers.
full_text: In Week 4, Browns defensive lineman Adin Huntington committed a textbook example of a hip-drop tackle on Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers. It was such a perfect example of what the hip-drop tackle rule is designed to prevent that in the NFL’s officiating video that is sent to every team, it was shown to demonstrate what not to do. Unfortunately, the officials on the field missed it. NFL officiating and rules analyst Walt Anderson narrated Hutington's tackle on Rodgers and pointed out that it constitutes exactly what is not permitted under the hip-drop tackle rule. "This is an illegal hip-drop tackle," Anderson said. "We want players to realize, and we're working at messaging the officials, that if they see all of the elements of this — the wrap, the swivel, the unweighting and then the dropping or trapping of legs — all four elements are clearly visible on the play. Hip-drop tackle would be the correct call. Whether this is called on the field or not, this is subject to additional discipline, including a fine." The uncalled penalty was a big one: It happened on third down, leading the Steelers to punt. If the 15-yard penalty had been called, the Steelers would have had first-and-10 in long field goal range. The Steelers ended up losing the game by three points. Huntington was fined, but the officials should have flagged it at the time, too. If they had, the rest of the game might have been different.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Mike Vrabel's clock management included an intentional offside penalty
summary: Vrabel has a long history of having his players commit penalties intentionally to manage the clock to his team's advantage.
full_text: With 1:56 remaining in the fourth quarter on Thursday night, the Bears faced third-and-inches, and Patriots defensive lineman Cory Durden jumped offside. The fans in Chicago cheered, thinking New England had just made a big mistake. Actually, Patriots coach Mike Vrabel had just called a smart play. Vrabel told Durden to jump offside intentionally because he figured the Patriots were unlikely to stop the Bears from picking up a first down when they only had inches to go anyway, and he'd rather concede the first down without running any time off the clock and then use his timeouts on the next set of downs. It proved to be smart: The Patriots' defense stopped the Bears on the next three plays, the Patriots used their three timeouts, and the Bears kicked with 1:39 remaining. Unfortunately for the Patriots, Bears kicker Cairo Santos kicked a career-long 58-yard field goal that put the game effectively out of reach. But if Santos had missed, the Patriots would have had a real chance at a game-winning touchdown, and they would have had an additional 40 seconds to do it because of Vrabel's smart clock management. Vrabel confirmed after the game what he had done, not wanting Durden to get blamed for the penalty. "For the record, we told Cory to jump offsides on third-and-six inches," Vrabel said. "We felt like that was going to be the best way to get them stopped, and that's on me, so our guys executed. And Cairo made a huge kick." Kirk Herbstreit, the commentator on the Prime Video broadcast of the game, correctly noted that, for the Patriots, it was better to give the Bears first-and-10 than third-and-inches in that situation. "The fact that it's third-and-inches instead of first-and-10, actually with the clock, hurts New England," Herbstreit said after Bears quarterback Caleb Williams had been spotted just short of the first down on the previous play. When Durden jumped offside, some thought it was a bonehead penalty, but Herbstreit knew what was happening. "This guy did this on purpose," Herbstreit said. "Going back to the clock, we just said, if they get the first down you have to waste a timeout on the third-down conversion. Now they get the first down. Vrabel, the way he operates, that's something they would do." Vrabel has made similar calls before. In fact, during the 2020 offseason, the NFL changed its rules to stop the clock after offensive penalties late in the fourth quarter because of the way Vrabel, then the coach of the Titans, had run the clock by intentionally committing penalties in a playoff win over the Patriots. On Thursday night, Bears coach Ben Johnson should have declined the Patriots' offside penalty to keep it third-and-inches. But Johnson apparently hadn't thought through the consequences of accepting the penalty and the first down that came with it. In the end, the Bears won despite Vrabel's tactic. But it was another example of how Vrabel is among the best coaches in the league at managing the clock late in the game.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Ben Johnson: Cole Kmet's knee injury doesn't look good
summary: Caleb Williams said after the game, "I don't have the words to describe what Cole is to me, to this team, to this organization."
full_text: Bears tight end Cole Kmet appears to have suffered a very serious injury during Thursday night's win over the Patriots. Coach Ben Johnson said after the game that nothing will be definitively diagnosed until Friday, but the early indications were that it's a bad injury. “We’ll know more about it tomorrow, but I don’t think it looked very good," Johnson said. Bears quarterback Caleb Williams said it hurt to see a player who means so much to him carted off the field. "It was tough. I don't know exactly what it is, but getting carted off is never good. You're at least going to miss some time. I don't have the words to describe what Cole is to me, to this team, to this organization. He's the longest-tenured Bear, I believe," Williams said. "He's been through it and it's challenging. It's tough. I'll be right there with him through every step of whatever the injury is. Cole's been there for me every step of the way, through the first year, through the second year, and now through this year. I could only do the same for him."
author: Michael David Smith

title: Faulk discloses Parkinson's disease diagnosis
summary: Hall of Fame running back and Southern University coach Marshall Faulk has disclosed that he has Parkinson's disease.
full_text: ' Hall of Fame running back and Southern University coach Marshall Faulk has disclosed that he has Parkinson's disease. Via Jack Baer of Yahoo Sports, Faulk revealed the diagnosis in an appearance on the Caring Neurologist podcast. "I get a physical twice a year," Faulk said. "I'm a little anal about my health. I literally asked my doctor because I noticed it as I was playing golf. I noticed the rigidity in my hand after I play a lot or practice a lot, I thought it was just normal nerves when putting and stuff like that. But it started to be times where I wasn't playing — I mean, where I was playing, but I wasn't in a match, and it would still do that. "I was like, 'Wow, is that something? Is that normal?' And the doctor was like, ' You need to go get checked . You need to go have X, Y and Z done.'" Faulk, a former NFL MVP, two-time NFL Offensive Player of the Year, three-time first-team All-Pro, and seven-time Pro Bowler, has been receiving treatment and taking medication. "Since I've started on the medication, I don't really have a lot of issues," Faulk said. "I might sleep a little more. . . . Other than that, the rigidity in my hands, I still have that. Can't say that it's gotten worse. The little tremors that I get, they are what they are. I just pay attention to my gait, how I walk, when I'm working out, my ability to balance. It's still where it is. "I don't look at it as something that's terminal. It's like, 'Hey, you get to live with this.' There's far worse things out there." There's a known link between Parkinson's disease and football. It's one of the specific conditions that make a player who retired prior to the final settlement of the concussion class action automatically eligible for payment.
author: Mike Florio

title: Bears TE Kmet carted off with a knee injury
summary: The Bears quickly ruled him out.
full_text: Bears tight end Cole Kmet injured his right knee on fourth quarter reception. Kmet caught an 8-yard pass from Caleb Williams before linebacker Robert Spillane and cornerback Christian Gonzalez both tackled Kmet low. Kmet immediately grabbed his right knee. Kmet couldn't put weight on his right leg and required a cart to leave the field with 5:34 remaining in the fourth quarter. He gave a thumb's up to the Soldier Field crowd as he departed for the training room. The Bears have ruled him out. Kmet caught three passes for 28 yards.
author: Charean Williams

title: Brian Schottenheimer: George Pickens "needs to understand he impacts us in the run game"
summary: Cowboys receiver George Pickens was rewarded for a stellar contract year by being kept from getting a fair market deal.
full_text: Cowboys receiver George Pickens was rewarded for a stellar contract year by being kept from getting a fair market deal. This year, he's playing under the franchise tag — with a second tag looming if he has another great season. Although his per-game targets and catches through six 2026 games are roughly comparable to his 17-game average in 2025 (8.66 targets and 5.5 catches in 2026 versus 8.05 and 5.47 in 2025), his yards per game are down (71.3 yards per game in 2026 and 84.0 in 2025). He has only one 100-yard game and only one touchdown this year. (In 2025, he had five 100-yard games and nine touchdowns.) Meanwhile, questions have emerged about Pickens's effort, especially when the ball isn't coming his way. Coach Brian Schottenheimer addressed that issue in a Thursday session with the media. “I think GP is one of those guys where I don't ever see him really affected in terms of the emotion of, ‘Does he get the ball? Does he not get the ball?’” Schottenheimer said regarding Pickens, via Todd Archer of ESPN. “These guys play a lot of snaps. I think part of it is us rotating those guys through, but he needs to understand that he impacts us in the running game as well. And he's got to do the same thing in the run game, picking up safeties and blocking corners just like Javonte [Williams] does, picking up blitzes so he can catch balls. And that's part of the team-first mindset and GP does understand that. And when he's going, they're going to place off to his side. When he's not going, then the safeties get pretty good runs at our backs and that’s got to improve .” Schottenheimer has been instrumental in getting the most out of Pickens during his time in Dallas. And it's a calculated risk to call him out publicly. That said, messages like this are often sent through the media when efforts to address the situation privately haven't worked. Regardless, Pickens (like other great receivers) wants the ball. In July, Tom Brady explained the unique mindset of the receiver position, where the players are on an island and isolated from the action unless they're getting the ball. If the Cowboys are going to have both Pickens and CeeDee Lamb, they need to find a way to involve both of them, early and often. Like other great receivers of the past, failing to find a way to get the ball in their hands eventually will have an impact on their overall attitude.
author: Mike Florio

title: Report: Multiple teams have trade interest in Jonathan Taylor
summary: It is unclear whether the Colts will be sellers at the trade deadline.
full_text: Multiple teams have trade interest in Colts running back Jonathan Taylor, Stephen Holder of ESPN reports. It is unclear whether the Colts will be sellers at the trade deadline. The Colts fired General Manager Chris Ballard on Monday, with Ed Dodds serving as the interim G.M. Head coach Shane Steichen could be on his way out, too, if the 2-4 Colts can't turn it around. Taylor, 27, led the league in carries (323), touchdowns (18) and first downs (84) last season. "I haven't given any thought," Taylor said when asked about his future Thursday. "That'd be crazy right now, especially because we've got a great Minnesota Vikings team that we have to go against. I think it would be a discredit and a disservice to my teammates and this whole organization to think about what could, what should, what may be." A second-round pick of the Colts in 2020, Taylor has signed two contract extensions. The most recent, a three-year deal, was signed in August and his annual average of $22 million ranks third at his position. Taylor has 122 carries for 492 yards and seven touchdowns in six games this season. He has 1,673 carries for 8,090 yards and 76 touchdowns.
author: Charean Williams

title: Thursday Night Football: Bears fend off Patriots 30-24
summary: Caleb Williams was 22-of-33 for 308 yards and two touchdowns.
full_text: The Bears honored Mike Ditka pregame. They honored him with a win, too. Chicago led from start to finish — though it made things interesting all night — and held off the Patriots 30-24. The Bears are 5-2 and the Patriots 4-3. Bears kicker Cairo Santos made a career-long 58-yard field goal with 1:34 remaining to give Chicago a two-score lead. It came one snap after Caleb Williams inexplicably took a 10-yard sack on third-and-5 at the New England 30. It appeared to push the Bears out of field-goal range, but Ben Johnson trusted his kicker, who missed earlier from 53 off the right upright. The Patriots quickly got in field-goal range, and Andy Borregales kicked a 47-yard field goal with 37 seconds remaining. Trailing by six, the Patriots tried an onside kick, but Rome Odunze recovered for the Bears. The Bears led 10-0 early and 20-7 with 14 seconds left in the first half but allowed a last-play touchdown to the Patriots as Rhamondre Stevenson scored on a 48-yard catch-and-run. It was back and forth until time ran out on the Patriots. Chicago outgained New England 405 to 380 as Williams went 22-of-33 for 308 yards and two touchdowns. Luther Burden caught four passes for 130 yards and a touchdown, all in the first half, and four other receivers had at least three catches. D'Andre Swift had 22 carries for 78 yards and a touchdown. Drake Maye was 24-of-31 for 321 yards with two touchdowns and an interception. He also ran for 26 yards and a touchdown on four carries. Stevenson had five catches for 93 yards and a touchdown and ran for 22 yards on six carries. A.J. Brown, after his three-drop game on Sunday, had three receptions for 48 yards.
author: Charean Williams

title: Marlon Humphrey complains about "slander" of Lamar Jackson
summary: Ravens cornerback Marlon Humphrey isn't happy with the manner in which Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson is treated.
full_text: Ravens cornerback Marlon Humphrey isn't happy with the manner in which Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson is treated. And Humphrey said so on Thursday. "It seems like Lamar's the only quarterback [who] kind of gets the slander that he gets for anytime anything is going on," Humphrey told reporters, via Jamison Hensley of ESPN. "I feel like you just don't see these same articles. I'm in the hot tub and it's this, that, and the third. Unfair treatment." Humphrey didn't specify any recent examples during Jackson's absence due to an ankle injury. "I just feel like sometimes it seems like it gets away from . . . I don't know if it's because of lack of agent or what, that no one can kind of defend him," Humphrey said. "But I do know this, if Lamar Jackson can play, if he's healthy enough to play, he will play, and that's kind of all I can say for that." It is one of the practical consequences of not having an agent who can contact reporters, broadcasters, or anyone else in the media who is saying anything negative about Jackson. During the weeks preceding the 2018 draft, for example, there was no one to push back on the likes of former G.M. Bill Polian, who was arguing that Jackson should switch to a different position. With no established agent to defend him and advocate for him, it's possibly one of the reasons the two-time MVP was available at the bottom of round one, where he was selected 22 spots after Josh Rosen. Ultimately, Lamar Jackson is the only one who speaks on his behalf. And Lamar doesn't seem to ever be bothered by any noise that may emerge. Humphrey may have realized after saying what he said that Jackson may not be thrilled that Humphrey said anything. "I think anything relating to Lamar is the thing that I don't talk about," Humphrey said. "I think the only one that really does talk about [Lamar] is Lamar. I think if Lamar can play, it'd be great. If he doesn't, we got Snoop [Huntley]." While there have been questions in past years regarding whether Jackson chose not to play while less than 100 percent at a time when he lacked the financial security of a new contract (which is smart), there hasn't been much if any criticism of Jackson during his latest absence. He obviously has an ankle injury and, although some reports described him as day-to-day, we reported on the day it happened that he's week-to-week . Based on his participation in practice over the past two days, this could be the week Jackson returns. And Baltimore could use him; the 4-2 Ravens host the 3-2 Bengals on Sunday.
author: Mike Florio

title: Bears DB Malik Muhammad doubtful to return with toe injury
summary: Bears rookie defensive back Malik Muhammad is doubtful to return tonight.
full_text: Bears rookie defensive back Malik Muhammad is doubtful to return tonight. He has a toe injury that has sent him into the training room. Muhammad may have gotten injured on a pass breakup against A.J. Brown with 9:07 remaining in the third quarter. He was in the game, but wasn't involved on the next play when he went to the ground. The fourth-round pick has three tackles, a tackle for loss and a pass breakup tonight. Tyrique Stevenson has replaced Muhammad.
author: Charean Williams

title: Drake Maye's second TD makes it a one-score game again
summary: Drake Maye's 30-yard touchdown pass to rookie tight end Eli Raridon has the Patriots back within one score of the Bears.
full_text: Drake Maye's 30-yard touchdown pass to rookie tight end Eli Raridon has the Patriots back within one score of the Bears. New England, which has not led tonight, trails the Bears 27-21 with 3:46 left in the third quarter. The teams have traded touchdowns to open the second half, with Chicago opening the half with a nine-play, 72-yard touchdown drive. The Patriots' touchdown drive was nine plays and 80 yards. The Patriots overcame two penalties for 15 yards on the drive. A.J. Brown had a 16-yard reception, giving him two catches for 34 yards. Maye is 18-of-22 for 253 yards with two touchdowns and an interception. The pick in the end zone, with the Patriots at the Chicago 15, is the only reason New England isn't leading.
author: Charean Williams

title: Bears respond to disastrous end of first half with TD drive
summary: Bears coach Ben Johnson didn't want to talk about how the first half ended.
full_text: Bears coach Ben Johnson didn't want to talk about how the first half ended. The Patriots scored a touchdown in the final 14 seconds on two plays, including a catch-and-run, 48-yard touchdown by Rhamondre Stevenson at the buzzer. The Bears put it in their rearview mirror and opened the second half with a nine-play, 72-yard touchdown drive. Caleb Williams threw a 12-yard touchdown pass to tight end Colston Loveland after the Bears received the second-half kickoff. Loveland also had a 22-yard reception on the drive. Williams is 14-of-21 for 225 yards and two touchdowns, and Loveland has five catches for 58 yards and a touchdown.
author: Charean Williams

title: Thursday Night Football: Luther Burden, Bears lead Patriots 20-14 at halftime
summary: The Bears wide receiver has four catches for 130 yards and a touchdown.
full_text: Luther Burden has 130 receiving yards, setting up three of the Bears' scoring drives with big catches. His 26-yard reception to the New England 28 set up Cairo Santos’ 43-yard field goal. He nearly scored a 62-yard touchdown two drives later, but Kevin Byard tackled him at the New England 4 to set up D'Andre Swift’s touchdown run. His 22-yard reception set up his own 24-yard touchdown catch on a wide receiver screen with 14 seconds left in the half. And the Bears lead the Patriots 20-14 at intermission. It should be worse. The Patriots got the ball back with 9 seconds left in the half and Drake Maye hit A.J. Brown for 18 yards for the wide receiver's first catch tonight. They called timeout with 3 seconds left, and with the Bears blitzing, Maye dumped the ball off to running back Rhamondre Stevenson, who ran 48 yards to the end zone. The Bears had outgained the Patriots 211 to 161 before Stevenson's 48-yard catch-and-run. Caleb Williams has completed 9 of 16 passes for 167 yards and a touchdown. Swift has nine carries for 37 yards and a touchdown. The Patriots couldn't get out of their own way most of the game. New England had a first down at the Chicago 15 with 3:32 left in the half when Maye tried to hit tight end Eli Raridon in the end zone. Instead, Bears linebacker D'Marco Jackson stepped in front of Raridon for the interception. The Bears then got another gift from the Patriots when rookie linebacker Gabe Jacas had an inexplicable roughing-the- passer penalty. He pushed Williams long after the 22-yard pass to Burden. Maye ended the half 12-of-15 for 169 yards with a touchdown and an interception. He also ran for 22 yards and a touchdown on three carries. Stevenson has four catches for 80 yards and a touchdown.
author: Charean Williams

title: Drake Maye's touchdown run has Patriots on the scoreboard
summary: The Patriots had two punts and turned it over on downs on their three first-quarter possessions.
full_text: The Patriots had two punts and turned it over on downs on their three first-quarter possessions. The second quarter has started better for them. The Patriots went 74 yards in nine plays, with Drake Maye running it in from the 7 on a scramble. New England trails 10-7. Patriots coach Mike Vrabel threw the red challenge flag after officials ruled Maye down inside the 1. Replay reversed it to a touchdown, with Maye stretching the ball across the goal line. Hunter Henry had a 16-yard catch and Eli Raridon a 15-yard reception on the drive as the tight ends powered the Patriots. Maye is 8-of-10 for 76 yards.
author: Charean Williams

title: Bears lead Patriots 10-0
summary: D'Andre Swift took a hit on his knee on a third-down play for no gain on the Bears' second possession.
full_text: D'Andre Swift took a hit on his knee on a third-down play for no gain on the Bears' second possession. He scored a touchdown on their third possession. Swift's 4-yard touchdown run has the Bears leading the Patriots 10-0. Luther Burden had big catches on both of the Bears' scoring drives. His 26-yard reception to the New England 28 set up Cairo Santos' 43-yard field goal. He nearly scored a 62-yard touchdown two drives later, but Kevin Byard tackled him at the New England 4 to set up Swift's touchdown. Burden has two catches for 84 yards. Caleb Williams is 4-of-7 for 95 yards. The Bears outgained the Patriots 106 to 63 in the first quarter.
author: Charean Williams

title: Tonight is Mike Vrabel's first career game at Soldier Field
summary: Mike Vrabel is in his 27th season as a player or coach in the NFL.
full_text: Mike Vrabel is in his 27th season as a player or coach in the NFL. Yet, tonight marks his first career regular-season game at Soldier Field. Larry Mayer of the Bears' team website reported this stat that seems impossible. Vrabel played for the Steelers (1997-2000), Patriots (2001-08) and Chiefs (2009-10); he was an assistant for the Texans (2014-17); and he was the head coach of the Titans (2018-23) and Patriots (2025-present). He never played and has never coached in the NFC, which limits the number of times his teams have gone against the Bears on the road. The only previous away game Vrabel had against the Bears was in 2002 as a player for the Patriots. The Bears, though, played their home games in Champaign, Illinois, that season while Soldier Field was being renovated. The Patriots won 33-30. As Ben Volin of the Boston Globe points out, Vrabel's Titans played preseason games at Soldier Field in 2019 and 2023.
author: Charean Williams

title: 49ers WR Mike Evans remains out of practice

title: Saquon Barkley limited in return to Eagles practice
summary: Barkley has missed the last two games with an ankle injury.
full_text: Word on Thursday morning was that Eagles running back Saquon Barkley would return to practice and the team's first injury report ahead of their Monday night game against the Cowboys confirms that he was back on the field. Barkley was listed as a limited participant after missing the last couple of weeks with an ankle injury. Barkley is reportedly on track to play against Dallas, but he stopped short of making any guarantees. "I would love to play Monday night. I would be doing myself a disservice to sit here and say Monday night I'm guaranteeing myself to play. I do know I have all trust in the trainers," Barkley said, via Tim McManus of ESPN.com. "To be honest, I was trying to go last week. It sounded great in my head and then you sit and you're like, maybe they were right. But I'm happy to have the opportunity to go out there and test it and God willing continue to trend in the right direction throughout the week and to be able to go and play Monday night." Defensive back Michael Carter (abdomen), tight end Dallas Goedert (knee), guard Willie Lampkin (illness), wide receiver DeVonta Smith (hamstring), linebacker Nolan Smith (concussion), and wide receiver Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) were out of practice for the Eagles. title: Nick Sirianni again says little about Jalen Hurts
summary: The Eagles continue to make coach Nick Sirianni available for regular press conferences.
full_text: The Eagles continue to make coach Nick Sirianni available for regular press conferences. He continues to say as little as possible about the Jalen Hurts situation. On Thursday, Sirianni was asked whether he agrees with the NFL Players Association seeking a full investigation of the handling of the situation. "Guys, I'm not going to go into any of that," Sirianni said. "I respect your question. Obviously, I understand that everybody has questions about this, and I care deeply about Jalen and I want -- his wellbeing is first and foremost, but really, I'm here to talk about the Cowboys and our team in this week of practice." Hey, at least the reporters tried. That said, they had an opportunity o Wednesday to get some answers from offensive coordinator Sean Mannion on collateral questions relating to the Hurts situation, but didn't. Mannion was asked a couple of Hurts questions regarding his role in assisting Tanner McKee. "He's been around, and I know -- Just speaking on the Jalen thing, obviously, just want him to get healthy and just care for the guy and the work that he puts into our team each and every week," Mannion said. "Certainly, want him to continue to be around and be a positive impact for us while he's getting himself healthy. That's the ultimate priority. He was around last week, and I know he's tackling the health stuff he's got going on, but he'll still be a big positive impact anytime he's around the team." Although the Eagles are committed to citing patient privacy when asked about Hurts's condition (despite the fact that his entire diagnosis has been disclosed via multiple statements), there were areas on which Mannion may have helped shed useful light. When did you find out Jalen had been taken to the hospital? Did players ask you about Jalen's trip to the hospital? After Jalen went to the hospital, did you believe there was a chance Jalen wouldn't play the game in London? Did you at any point begin getting Tanner McKee ready to play? When did you know Jalen would definitely play? For how long did you not know whether Jalen would be available? While unrelated to the diagnosis, treatment, or prognosis, specific questions about Mannion's knowledge, impressions, and actions relating to the preparation of McKee would shed light on the failure of the team to downgrade Hurts to "questionable" for the game. Because, certainly, there was a point at which his availability to play was in question. Mannion also could have been asked when Hurts first complained about issues with his calf, and whether he noticed any limitations to his mobility during practice. Mannion also could have been asked whether the decision to not use the tush push play on fourth and 1 from the Jacksonville 37 was influenced by Hurts's condition. The broader question for the organization, as noted by Chris Simms on Thursday's PFT Live , is the failure of the team to make G.M. Howie Roseman available at any point over the past week to address the situation. He runs the show. He surely is the one person in the best position to answer any and all questions about how it was handled. Apart from whether the situation was handled properly from a medical and football standpoint, the Eagles have done a poor job of providing meaningful answers to obvious questions. While those questions will be unavoidable in the coming investigation under the CBA, the Eagles apparently have successfully run out the clock as it relates to media inquiries.
author: Mike Florio

title: Marlon Humphrey on Ja'Marr Chase: It would be cool if I didn't match up with him so much
summary: Humphrey and Chase have faced off nine times. In those games, Chase has torched the Ravens for 77 catches for 1,245 yards and eight touchdowns.
full_text: ' Ravens cornerback Marlon Humphrey has covered Bengals wide receiver Ja'Marr Chase many times. Maybe more times than he'd like. Humphrey and Chase have faced off eight times in the regular season and once in the playoffs. In those nine games, Chase has torched the Ravens for 77 catches for 1,245 yards and eight touchdowns. The Ravens and Bengals will meet again on Sunday, and Humphrey said today that covering Chase and fellow Bengals wide receiver Tee Higgins is a big challenge, and one of the toughest assignments an NFL cornerback can draw. "It would be cool if I didn't match up with him so much," Humphrey said. "He's obviously one of the best in the game. Tee is right up there with him, in the Top 10, I think, in this league. There will be plays made, I think the biggest thing going into this matchup is to try to win more than they win and try to limit the explosives. That's the biggest thing when you're guarding those Top 10, Top 5 guys. It's an all-hands-on-deck game. We look forward to the challenge. I think it'll be a great opportunity." Despite the success Chase has had against him, Humphrey said he's eager for a big game on Sunday between the 4-2 Ravens and 3-2 Bengals. "I'm very confident. I think we've had some tests this year, but this will be by far the biggest test yet," Humphrey said. If Chase's past is any indication, it's going to be a very big test for Humphrey and the Ravens' secondary.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Rare NFL penalty: Bears become first team in 16 years to get flagged for illegal forward handoff
summary: The failed trick play against the Patriots sent viewers scrambling to learn about one of the most obscure rules in the NFL rulebook
full_text:
There have been thousands of penalties called in the NFL over the past 15 years, but until Thursday night, there was one penalty that had NEVER been called in that span: Illegal forward handing.
During the first half of the Bears ' game against the Patriots , Chicago got flagged for that exact penalty. If you don't know what "illegal forward handing: is, don't worry, most people don't, and that's because it almost never gets called.
Never heard "illegal forward handing" in my life. Tonight is truly historic.
On the play, Caleb Williams took the snap and immediately handed the ball off to guard Joe Thuney . This was a trick play by the Bears and not only did it NOT work, but they lost five yards after the officiating crew threw a flag.
the rare illegal forward handoff 😭 pic.twitter.com/NEz82wd19L
The reason you don't see offensive linemen get more handoffs is because in most instances, it's against the rules. As the NFL rule book clearly states, "except where permitted by rule, handing the ball forward to a teammate is illegal."
So what exactly does that mean?
Although you can't have a forward handoff in those last two situations, you can have a backward handoff or pitch it backwards to a teammate once your past the line of scrimmage or after a turnover.
The penalty on Thursday night marked the first time in 16 years that an illegal forward handoff has been called in a game. According to NFLpenalties.com , the last time this flag was thrown came in a Packers-Lions game on Oct. 3, 2010. In that game, Lions cornerback Chris Houston picked off Aaron Rodgers and then got flagged after he attempted to hand the ball to a teammate who was in front of him .
This is one of the rarest penalties in the NFL and we all got to witness it on Thursday night.
author: John Breech

title: Brian Schottenheimer issues challenge to George Pickens as Cowboys search for answers on offense
summary: With Dallas sitting at 2-4, Schottenheimer acknowledged that he must coach better
full_text:
Brian Schottenheimer and his offense are feeling the heat after a 2-4 start.
The Cowboys have scored fewer than 20 points in consecutive Dak Prescott starts for the first time in seven seasons, and Dallas has work to do to compete for the NFC East crown.
One of the players now carrying the blame for Dallas' 31st-ranked rushing offense is George Pickens . Pickens' 1,429 receiving yards in 2025 ranked third in the NFL, and his 428 this season sit outside of the top 10. However, Schottenheimer has issued a different type of challenge to his Pro Bowl receiver.
"I think GP is one of those guys where I don't ever see him really affected in terms of the emotion of does he get the ball? Does he not get the ball? These guys play a lot of snaps. ... He needs to understand that he impacts us in the running game as well," Schottenheimer said. "He needs to understand that he impacts us in the running game as well. He's got to do the same thing in the run game, picking up safeties and blocking corners, just like Javonte [Williams] does, picking up blitzes so he can catch balls. That's part of the team-first mindset, and GP does understand that. When he's going, they're going to play soft inside. When he's not going, the safeties get pretty good runs at our backs. And that's got to improve."
Dallas' offense has become too simplistic in Year 2 under Schottenheimer in 2026. This season, the Cowboys rank as second-to-last in the NFL in motion rate (42.7%), 28th out of 32 teams in under-center rate (30.4%) and 20th in play action rate.
"I think some of it is deserved," Schottenheimer said of the criticism coming his way. "We got to play better. I got to coach better. And so when you grow up in a family that your dad's a head coach for over 20-something years [21 years], you understand that this is part of the job description. No one likes it. I block out most of it. Some of it gets to me doing this job and having to speak to you guys is part of that. But at the same time, I've got strong shoulders. I know what a great coach I am. I know what this team is capable of, and that's what I focus on."
Tempo (average time between snaps in seconds)
So how does Schottenheimer plan to fix the run game? By calling more runs to allow Williams to get in more of a rhythm. However, the caveat he threw out is that Dallas should not fall behind early in games. The Cowboys have spent the fifth-most time trailing (3:23:30) in the NFL this season.
"I think it starts with calling more runs, which requires being in more, I keep using the word normal, close games where you're not having a play from behind," Schottenheimer said. "I do think that the more you run it, the better you feel. You figure out combination blocks and things like that. I will say early on in most of our games, we've not run it as well as we are capable of. And there's been times where again, as the head coach and the play caller, I have to make the decision of, 'okay, clock says X, we're down X, what is it? All right, it's time to go.' So those are decisions that we discuss and we make those decisions, but it starts with just letting these guys get into a groove, let these guys get bats at the plate, if you will. And that's a big part."
author: Garrett Podell

title: Bears vs. Patriots prediction: Chicago aims to stop Drake Maye's hot streak on 'TNF'
summary: Here's how to watch, what to know, and an expert prediction before the Pats and Bears face off in Chicago
full_text:
In the Week 7 edition of "Thursday Night Football," the Chicago Bears play host to the New England Patriots .
Chicago is coming off a win in Caleb Williams ' return to the lineup, having held on for a 31-23 victory in a game that moved the Bears to 4-2 on the season. The Bears bounced back from their dispiriting loss to the division rival Green Bay Packers the week before, when the offense looked like a disaster with backup Tyson Bagent under center. Chicago will look to keep the good times rolling here.
New England also won what -- on the surface -- looked like a close game against the New York Jets , but finished with a seven-point margin of victory thanks only to a late field goal. The Patriots have won three consecutive games after starting the season 1-2, and their quarterback has found a groove after looking nearly broken to start the year. The Pats, too, are looking to keep the train on the tracks on Thursday night.
Will the Bears capture another win, or will the Patriots continue their hot streak? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game.
Drake Maye has found himself over the last three weeks, completing 66 of 103 passes for 878 yards, 10 touchdowns, and one interception after going just 51-of-80 for 585 yards, one touchdown, and six picks through the first three games of the season. Maye has rediscovered the deep ball, in particular, going 12 of 20 for 350 yards and four scores on throws beyond 15 yards in the last three games, per Tru Media. Before that, he was just 9 of 20 for 281 yards and four interceptions on those throws.
Maye finished with a strong game against the Jets despite A.J. Brown looking horrifyingly bad in his return from an ankle injury. Brown dropped (at least) three passes and turned his 10 targets into only 27 yards. Maye also lost Romeo Doubs to a shoulder injury on an early-game touchdown pass, so he was working with a limited receiving corps behind Brown. Still, he threw for 235 yards and three touchdowns without turning the ball over.
Brown will presumably be better here, and Chicago hasn't been great against outside receivers, but last week's return of Kyler Gordon could lead to slot man Demario Douglas having a tougher go of things than he has over the last few weeks. Kyle Williams could get in on the action with Doubs sidelined, though Efton Chism has been getting more snaps because the Patriots trust him as a blocker.
Chicago checks in a surprising eighth in opponents' EPA per dropback so far this season, per Tru Media, thanks to a high sack rate and a few timely interceptions. Opponents have averaged 8.4 yards per attempt against the Bears, though, indicating that you can indeed move the ball through the air if you can get a pass off and avoid a turnover.
Defensive coordinator Dennis Allen has generated pressure at an above-average rate (39.7% of dropbacks) despite working with a somewhat limited group up front, and the Patriots will be without two starting guards here. So, the running backs (particularly Rhamondre Stevenson ) will have to be on their game in pass protection on Thursday night.
The Patriots have struggled to run the ball thus far this season, with Stevenson, TreVeyon Henderson and Corey Kiner combining for an average of just 3.9 yards per carry on 151 rushing attempts. Stevenson leads the way in the backfield largely because the Patriots trust him the most in short yardage and pass protection, but he hasn't been efficient or explosive. Henderson had an explosive rushing touchdown on his first run of the season but has failed to record one since.
Kiner was a little-used third-stringer until he salted away the game against the Jets last Sunday. He could perhaps work his way into more touches after a nice showing in that game, given the rushing struggles of the two leads and the fact that Henderson also fumbled against New York.
The Bears have allowed opponents 4.4 yards per carry on running-back rushes so far this season, with much of the success coming by way of yards before contact. It may be difficult for the Patriots to generate those types of yards with their injury issues along the offensive line, and their backs haven't exactly done the best job of breaking tackles this year, so the challenge of moving the offense down the field will likely fall squarely on Maye's right shoulder.
Caleb Williams returned last week from a three-game absence due to a hamstring injury and looked no worse for wear. Williams completed 30 of 36 passes for 305 yards and a touchdown. The Bears kept things simple for him with a 3.9-yard average depth of throw (eighth-lowest for any quarterback in a single game this season), per Tru Media, and he was extremely efficient as a result.
Williams has only played in three games so far this year, but he's leading the league with a 72.5% completion rate and is up to a career-best 7.8 yards per attempt. And that's despite a truly awful game against the Vikings in Week 2, where he went 15-of-26 for just 138 yards and an interception. In his first couple of appearances, it seemed like journeyman wideout Kalif Raymond (14 targets in Weeks 1 and 2) was his primary option, but on Sunday, it was Luther Burden III and Colston Loveland -- the most expected options -- leading the way with eight and seven targets, respectively. Rome Odunze saw five looks.
Given the way they're each deployed, it seems likely that Odunze will see a bunch of Christian Gonzalez 's coverage on Thursday night -- especially with Carlton Davis III ruled out. Odunze is the biggest of the trio and plays most often on the perimeter, and he also tends to run the most routes. If that's the way things go, we should expect the passing game to flow through Burden and Loveland yet again.
The Patriots have allowed opponents to complete 31 of 46 passes for 301 yards on throws to the slot this season, per Tru Media. Burden could have a nice night working inside if he's on the field more often than he was last week (eight targets on only 18 routes), though Marcus Jones does have an interception this season and is allowing only 1.46 yards per coverage snap in the slot, per Pro Football Focus.
By contrast, New England has allowed only 29 catches for 279 yards to tight ends to date, so Loveland may not find the coverage as friendly. The Bears would do well to line him up all over the formation rather than solely in line, and perhaps use multi-tight end sets where he plays more of a receiver role, and Cole Kmet or Sam Roush handles the blocking aspects of the position.
The Bears also tried against Atlanta to do what they do best: run the ball with volume. D'Andre Swift and Roschon Johnson (the latter filling in for the injured Kyle Monangai ) combined for 29 carries. They ran for only 96 yards on those totes, but they did find the end zone three times.
Chicago's offensive line actually created some nice push, generating 1.45 yards before contact per carry, according to Tru Media, but the backs slumped to only 1.83 yards after contact, as they combined for only four broken tackles. (For context, consider that the Seahawks ' running backs combined for 10 in their awful game against the Broncos on Thursday night.)
The Pats have allowed only 3.9 yards per rush this season, thanks in part to yielding an average of only 0.75 yards before contact. Swift and Johnson (Monangai is out again) will have to do a better job of breaking tackles this time around if they want to generate yardage and create favorable down-and-distance scenarios for Williams and the passing game.
I see this being a high-scoring game, what with two offenses that can pile up points quickly. Chicago's offense in two non-rain/non-Brian Flores games with Caleb Williams under center has been electric, particularly on the ground, and Caleb Williams opens things up for the passing game. New England is struggling to run the ball, but Drake Maye has been on fire as of late. I'll lean toward the Bears here…

title: Paris protests force Steelers to cancel fan event ahead of historic NFL game
summary: Sunday's historic game at Stade de France will proceed as planned, with the NFL working alongside local authorities and increasing security
full_text:
When the Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints meet on Sunday in the NFL's first regular-season game hosted in Paris, they will do so with an intense civil unrest as the backdrop. Protests in the French capital will not impact the NFL Week 7 game, but they did lead to the cancellation of a fan event. The Steelers announced on Thursday that they will not hold the scheduled Steelers House gathering due to the protests.
The event was scheduled to unfold over the weekend near the Bastille. There is an authorized march scheduled to begin at Place de la Bastille on Saturday.
Sunday's game, meanwhile, will unfold at Stade de France in Saint-Denis, which is located just under six miles from the center of Paris and away from the scheduled demonstrations.
"Following recent events in the Bastille neighborhood, and after careful consideration, we felt it appropriate not to move forward with the planned Steelers House fan event in Paris," the Steelers said in a statement. "Preparations for Sunday's NFL Paris game at State de France continue as planned, with the NFL working closely with local authorities and partners on all operational and security matters."
There have thus far been no disruptions at NFL sites in the lead-up to Sunday's contest. While concerns over fan and player safety heightened over the last two weeks, the league insisted repeatedly that the game would go on as planned. The NFL first addressed the concerns on Oct. 14 when it stated it looks forward to welcoming fans to Paris later this month.
One measure the NFL will enact, though, is an increase in security. NFL executive vice president of club business, international and league events, Peter O'Reilly, said this week that the security presence "will be heightened" as the league works in tandem with local authorities and the U.S. State Department. He said the NFL has had people in Paris since early October and that they are "being very vigilant in everything we do, in all of our planning on an hour-by-hour basis."
Former NFL Security Committee member and current CBS Sports analyst Amy Trask said that while teams handle international travel differently from one another, they share similar rules with regard to curfews and activities outside of game day. Trask also detailed the role security plays in these overseas competitions.
"You've got security on site the moment people are approaching the venue," Trask said. "In other words, the security is not simply at the gate when people are entering the venue. There is security well outside of the venue. There is security before you even enter the parking lot, so there will be security throughout the area. Some of the security will be noticeable, recognizable. Some of the security will be undercover, meaning simply not in uniform, not dressed in a manner where you will immediately notice it is security. It was my experience that there is ample security at the NFL events.
"... As I noted, when the games are in the United States, that's local security, municipal security, state security, national security. Now you will add to this Parisian security, French security as well."
The protests have been ongoing for nearly a month and stem from discontent over the French school system and the nation's cost of living. Protesters, many of them students, called upon the government to address under-resourced schools, poor conditions and teacher shortages. They report, in some cases, that the schools are physically falling apart with crumbling ceilings, water in the walls and rats in the buildings.
Some protests have turned violent. Police arrested thousands of people in connection to the demonstrations and utilized tear gas, stun grenades and other crowd-control measures to address those protests that devolved from peaceful gatherings into riots, according to CBS News .

title: Saquon Barkley trade proposals: Six deals Eagles could consider, including stunning Giants reunion
summary: A return to New York headlines six potential landing spots for Barkley if Philadelphia decides to reset its roster
full_text:
The Philadelphia Eagles might be at an inflection point in their championship contention window. Injuries to myriad starters, the loss of Jalen Hurts for the season, Lane Johnson's retirement and an offense that cannot seem to get off the ground raise questions about whether general manager Howie Roseman tears his roster down at the Nov. 10 NFL trade deadline. If he does, star running back Saquon Barkley might be headed out of town.
Trading Barkley would be the ultimate admission that the Eagles, as currently constructed, cannot achieve their goals. The financial impact of moving him will lock this franchise into a rebuild, as he carries a salary cap hit of $26.4 million in dead money for 2027. At the same time, the large sum of unusable cap space gives the Eagles leverage over trade partners in that they can drive up the price. Suitors could also be inclined to pay up, considering Barkley is only guaranteed $2.5 million next season and has no guaranteed money in the final year of his contract in 2028.
On the other hand, Barkley is an aging running back who will turn 30 years old the week before the Super Bowl . He has not been able to replicate the magic of his career-best 2024 season, so the former NFL Offensive Player of the Year's best days may be behind him. That could make teams tepid about spending first-round draft capital in a potential trade.
There are a number of teams that need help at running back, and despite the questions about Barkley's longevity, he would likely elevate their offenses to a significant degree.
Here are six potential trades that would move Barkley out of Philadelphia.
Giants receive: Saquon Barkley
Eagles receive: Cam Skattebo , 2027 second-round pick, 2027 sixth-round pick
In such a weak NFC East, the division-leading Giants have a path to the playoffs, but they need a functional run game to get there. Even with their abundance of options, it seems John Harbaugh does not know who to deploy at running back ( especially if you ask Najee Harris ). Reuniting with Barkley eliminates all questions. Plus, Harbaugh himself said this week that it would be "great" to be in a "Saquon Barkley circumstance" where the Giants had a clear-cut No. 1 ballcarrier.
A return to New York makes plenty of sense for Barkley, but it would likely cost the Giants a premium to pull it off, given the intra-division nature of the trade. For multiple years of control of the Eagles' star running back, they may have to part with their own top running back asset in addition to meaningful draft capital.
Seahawks receive: Saquon Barkley
Eagles receive: Emanuel Wilson , 2027 third-round pick, 2027 fifth-round pick
Declining to bring Kenneth Walker III back in free agency has haunted the Seahawks, especially with Zach Charbonnet missing the first six games due to the torn ACL he sustained last season. The offense is far more ineffective than it was during last year's Super Bowl run because of the nonexistence of the run game, which ranks second-worst in EPA per rush. Charbonnet will return in Week 7, but he is not a bellcow back, and first-round rookie Jadarian Price is still on injured reserve. Seattle should make a run at a lead running back to revitalize an offense that, in its current form, is not good enough to make another deep postseason push.
Barkley's arrival would create a logjam at the position, so Seattle may try to send one back to Philadelphia. And with three third-rounders and three fifth-rounders in its coffers, those are the picks that make the most sense to move.
Vikings receive: Saquon Barkley, 2027 seventh-round pick
Eagles receive: 2027 third-round pick, 2027 fifth-round pick, 2027 sixth-round pick
The recent trade history between the Vikings and Eagles makes them sensible partners for another deal. Minnesota holds Philadelphia's upcoming third-round pick, while Philadelphia owns Minnesota's seventh-rounder in next year's draft thanks to the Jonathan Greenard trade they completed in April. Those picks could go back to their original homes if these teams do business with each other once again.
The Vikings' run game is serviceable and is in line for a boost with Jordan Mason set to come off injured reserve this week. But the pairing of Mason and Aaron Jones is only that: Serviceable. Barkley would be a clear upgrade for an offense that ranks in the bottom half of the league in scoring and yards per game. Bolstering that group should be a priority as Minnesota attempts to capitalize on its league-best defense and keep its perfect start to the season rolling.
Bengals receive: Saquon Barkley
Eagles receive: 2027 second-round pick, 2027 fifth-round pick
The name value alone of an offense that boasts Joe Burrow , Ja'Marr Chase and Saquon Barkley would be tremendous. Imagine what it would deliver in terms of production. The Bengals' typically unstoppable unit is limited in 2026 by a run game that ranks just 27th in yards per game, so a boost on the ground would open all kinds of opportunities for Burrow downfield and rekindle that elite attack. Chase Brown has been a disappointment to the point where Samaje Perine is becoming an increasingly large part of the ground game. That signals a cry for help at the running back position.
As the Bengals attempt to cash in during Burrow's prime, this is the time to mortgage the future and invest draft picks in splashy trades like one for Barkley.
Broncos receive: Saquon Barkley
Eagles receive: 2027 second-round pick, 2027 fifth-round pick
Sean Payton already reclaimed play-calling duties, but that might not be enough to save the Broncos' offense. Something else is clearly missing from this unit. Long-term assets like RJ Harvey and Jonah Coleman make the future of the running back group bright, but it is underperforming right now, and that is a problem for a team that has Super Bowl aspirations. An infusion of immediate help would lower J.K. Dobbins and Harvey a rung each on the depth chart, and perhaps that is precisely what the group needs while Coleman recovers on injured reserve.
The Broncos are flush with 2027 late-round picks, so moving a Day 3 selection in addition to a second-rounder would not hurt.
Texans receive: Saquon Barkley
Eagles receive: Woody Marks , 2027 seventh-round pick, 2028 second-round pick
The David Montgomery trade is aging like a bust of a move as he cedes work to Woody Marks in a disappointing run game. It would be an admission that the move did not pan out as expected if general manager Nick Caserio traded for another running back, but it might be a worthwhile one if it takes an otherwise surprisingly effective offense to another level. C.J. Stroud is playing the best football of his career and looks determined to pull the Texans out of the 0-4 hole they dug themselves into but might have trouble doing so if the ground game is a drag.
That the Texans hold the Eagles' 2027 seventh-round pick (which has already changed hands thrice) could aid in their pursuit of Barkley, even if it is just a throw-in as the final sweetener in the trade package.

title: NFL legend Marshall Faulk diagnosed with Parkinson's disease, says he is 'in a good place'
summary: The Hall of Fame running back said he was diagnosed after noticing an issue with his hand and has been managing the condition through treatment
full_text:
Marshall Faulk, an NFL legend and the coach at Southern University, revealed that he has been diagnosed with Parkinson's disease, a progressive disorder of the central nervous system affecting the body's movement. Faulk, 53, said that he has been dealing with the disease for about 18 months. He first realized that something was wrong when he was having issues with his hand while playing golf. He mentioned the issue to his doctor during a routine physical.
"I was like, 'Wow, is that something?'" Faulk said on an episode of "Caring Neurologist" with Dr. Sandeep Thakkar. "'Is that normal?' And the doctor was— he literally was like, 'You need to go get checked.'"
Faulk is in good spirits and considers himself lucky because he got the diagnosis early. He said that it can be managed through treatment while comparing it to recovering from injuries during his NFL career.
Since getting treatment, Faulk said that he has become more active, is sleeping more and that his life is relatively the same. He said that while he still experiences rigidity in his hands, the condition has not gotten worse.
"The little tremors that I get, you know, they are what they are," he said. "I just pay attention to my gait, you know, while I walk, when I'm working out, my ability to balance. It's still where it is."
Faulk wants to advocate for people to seek help if they experience symptoms. Surprisingly, he said that he had not had a conversation about his diagnosis with his family or friends.
"If it comes a time to where my lifestyle changes, then I will," he said. "Then that conversation could be had. I'm functioning. I'm good. You know, I just I think I caught it early. I'm in a good place."
Faulk was named Southern's coach on Dec. 1, 2025. He previously served as Deion Sanders' running backs coach at Colorado.
A 2011 Pro Football Hall of Fame inductee, Faulk is widely considered one of the greatest running backs of all time. At San Diego State, he led the FBS in rushing three straight years. He finished second in the Heisman Trophy voting in 1992 and was fourth in the voting in 1993.
Faulk was the No. 2 overall pick in the 1994 NFL Draft . He earned two Pro Bowls with the Colts before entering another stratosphere after he was traded to the Rams in 1999. That season, Faulk helped the Rams win the Super Bowl while becoming the second player to post 1,000 yards rushing and receiving in the same season.
Faulk won league MVP in 2000 after he led the NFL in touchdown runs (18) and yards-per-carry average (5.4). He helped the Rams get back to the Super Bowl in 2001.
A seven-time Pro Bowler and three-time All-Pro, Faulk retired after the 2005 season with 12,279 rushing yards, 6,875 receiving yards, 100 rushing touchdowns and 136 total touchdowns. He, Marcus Allen and Tiki Barber are the only players in NFL history with 10,000 rushing and 5,000 career receiving yards.

Indianapolis Colts owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon just let the rest of the NFL know a rebuild is coming in Indianapolis after the firing of general manager Chris Ballard on Monday.
Irsay-Gordon ended Ballard's regime six games into his 10th season in charge. Indianapolis made the playoffs twice (2018 and 2020), going 1-2 in those two trips. The Colts ' 72-82-1 regular-season record under his management ranked 17th in the league during Ballard's reign. Indianapolis's five straight missed playoffs represent the Colts' longest drought in over 40 years. An AFC South title never happened with Ballard.
Now, the Colts are set to start over in 2027 with a new front office. Now is the time to rebuild since the 2027 NFL Draft is widely regarded as one of the most loaded classes in years. One issue is that the Colts don't have a first-round pick, thanks to trading their 2026 and 2027 first-round draft choices, along with wide receiver Adonai Mitchell , to the New York Jets last season in exchange for All-Pro cornerback Sauce Gardner .
So, who could Indianapolis trade away to recoup some draft pick value? Well, three-time Pro Bowl defensive tackle DeForest Buckner basically put out a trade request after losing 26-20 at home against the previously 0-5 Tennessee Titans in Week 6.
"I'm sick and tired of the same song and dance every year," Buckner told reporters postgame on Sunday .
Buckner is 32 years old and a pending free agent next spring, but he could provide an immediate impact for a team looking to contend this season. His 4.0 sacks through six weeks are tied for the 10th most in the NFL , while his 19 quarterback pressures rank as the seventh most among defensive tackles in 2026.  For a real deal contender, Buckner could be worth a third-or fourth-round pick.
Who could inquire to be Buckner's new NFL landing spot? Let's take a look at four potential landing spots.
The 49ers make too much sense. That's where Buckner played his first four seasons, culminating in San Francisco losing Super Bowl LIV to the Kansas City Chiefs to conclude the 2019 season. He was traded to the Colts for a first-round pick in the 2020 offseason.
San Francisco is going through its regularly scheduled injury catastrophe, so it could always use more bodies. The 49ers have the oldest roster in the entire NFL, with an average age of 28.5, and they once again lead the NFL in games missed because of injury, with 118 individual games. Adding another productive defensive line piece could pay dividends now and later.
The last time the 49ers started 6-0 was Buckner's last season in San Francisco, which culminated in a Super Bowl trip.
The Kansas City Chiefs are in win-now mode every year with Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce leading their franchise. That's even more true in 2026 with free agent acquisition running back Kenneth Walker III , the reigning Super Bowl MVP, off to a historic start this season.
One of their major weaknesses through five games is their pass rush. The Chiefs have the fourth-lowest sack rate in the entire NFL at 4.2%, and they're the only team in the whole league to not have a player with multiple sacks this season. Kansas City, as a team, has gone sackless in three of its first five games.
Pairing Buckner with seven-time Pro Bowl defensive tackle Chris Jones could provide a major boost to both veterans as well as the Chiefs' sagging pass rush.
The Minnesota Vikings are 5-0 on the strength of defensive coordinator Brian Flores' aggressive unit. Flores' defense leads the NFL in:
The Vikings' blitz rate of just under 70% is the highest by any team in any five-game span in the last 10 seasons, per CBS Sports Research. Some might call what Flores is doing early on this season "smoke and mirrors" with an outlier blitz rate, but adding a player like Buckner could solidify Minnesota's pass rush blitz or not. He could also be a nice mentor for rookie first-round pick defensive tackle Caleb Banks and another high-level contributor for Flores to incorporate into his scheme.
The Green Bay Packers , a team that has been playing mix-and-match with an injury-plagued offensive line, have stabilized the unit with the same starting five combination for the last three weeks. That has also coincided with their defense leveling up during their current three-game winning streak, while not having to be on the field as often, thanks to the offense sustaining drives. Green Bay leads the NFL in scoring defense (11.3 points per game allowed) during the streak, but it needs more help along its defensive line as the season develops.
Green Bay lost defensive tackle Javon Hargrave for the season with a torn Achilles, so it would make sense for them to place a call for Buckner. Adding Buckner to a defensive line that will get All-Pro edge rusher Micah Parsons back later in the year could give the Packers ' defense the boost it needs to help power a deep playoff run in January and February.
