title: Cowboys' Jerry Jones says Dallas could be 'active' at trade deadline: Here's who it should target
summary: Jones still believes his 2-4 squad could turn things around in a wide-open NFC East in 2026
full_text:
FRISCO, Texas -- The 2026 NFC East division is wide open, and Dallas Cowboys owner/general manager Jerry Jones knows it.
The NFC East went a combined 0-6-2 the last two weeks, making it the first division in NFL history to go winless in consecutive weeks when playing four-plus games. That's why Jones feels his 2-4 Cowboys could still make a run at a division crown. The first-place New York Giants (3-2-1) are trying out Minnesota Vikings bust J.J. McCarthy as their starting quarterback, and the Philadelphia Eagles will likely be without Super Bowl MVP quarterback Jalen Hurts for the rest of the 2026 season as he recovers from blood clots.
Ahead of the Nov. 10 NFL trade deadline, Jones still sees Dallas as a potential buyer, not a seller.
"I'll be real clear, I could see being active at the trade deadline if it was something that could help the team this year," Jones told reporters at the league's owners meetings on Wednesday.
Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer shares Jones' faith that a turnaround could be just around the corner for Dallas.
"Number one, Jerry is never afraid to make moves, and number two, we have a lot of football left," Schottenheimer said on Thursday. "We're excited about winning a big game in Philadelphia on Monday."
Let's take a look at what Dallas has left in its draft pick war chest and then three players the Cowboys could acquire to help Jones' 2026 squad.
This is the big fish right here. The Cowboys currently rank 11th-worst in the NFL in quarterback pressure rate (34.5%) and fifth-worst in sack rate (4.2%), per TruMedia. Their pass rush is one of their most urgent remaining needs on defense. Two of the veteran Pro Bowl edge rushers they acquired this offseason, Rashan Gary and Von Miller , look to be past their expiration date when it comes to finishing rushes for sacks. Plus, the Cowboys are still struggling to replace All-Pro Micah Parsons ' production after shipping him to the Green Bay Packers just before the kickoff of the 2025 season.
Should Jones be comfortable parting with high-round draft capital, Los Angeles Chargers 24-year-old Pro Bowl edge rusher Tuli Tuipulotu makes a lot of sense. The age is at a point where the Cowboys would be trading for prime years of a player's career, and, like Joey Porter Jr., he is a former second-round pick in the final year of his rookie deal, looking to cash in on a large new deal. Tulipulotu's contract situation could make him available in a trade should the 0-6 Chargers decide to hold a fire sale ahead of the highly anticipated 2027 NFL Draft .
He exploded for 13 sacks, the sixth most in the NFL, and 70 quarterback pressures, the 11th most in the league, in 2025 en route to earning his first Pro Bowl selection. He's on pace for another decent season through the first third of 2026. He's up to two sacks and 19 quarterback pressures already, while Los Angeles has spent the fourth-most time in the NFL trailing their opponents at 3:46:47.
This is the headline-grabbing move if Jerry truly wants to be "all in" again.
The Dallas Cowboys reportedly attempted to trade for Miami Dolphins 2025 first-team All-Pro linebacker Jordyn Brooks in the offseason, when he had just one year left on his contract, before Miami extended Brooks on a three-year, $48 million contract with $35 million guaranteed in the summer.
However, the Dolphins are in the middle of a tear-it-down-to-the-studs rebuild in their first year with new head coach Jeff Hafley and new general manager Jon-Eric Sullivan, both of whom come from the Green Bay Packers' draft-and-develop franchise model.
Miami is 0-5 and has the NFL's worst scoring offense (14 points per game), and the Dolphins are the only team that has not led at any point in 2026. That makes them only the second team in the Super Bowl era (since 1966) to not have a lead in the first five games of a season, along with the 2005 Houston Texans , per CBS Sports Research.  The Dolphins are also paying more for players not on their roster (an NFL-record $179 million in dead cap hits) than for the players on their roster ($156 million).
Brooks is 29 years old and under contract through the 2029 season, his age-32 season. That's basically the rest of his prime. Jones not having to worry about Brooks' contract situation is likely a relief, and on a hopeless 2026 Dolphins team, he is still a bright spot. Pro Football Focus grades Brooks as the NFL's No. 9 linebacker against the run with a run defense grade of 78.6. He would be an immediate help to the Cowboys' league-worst run defense, which is allowing an average of 149.8 yards per game. Brooks could also help Dallas' pass rush as a blitzer from the second level as PFF's No. 7 pass rushing linebacker with a 79.1 pass rush grade.
One might look at this trade option and think, "Wait, a second. Dallas is loaded at wide receiver with CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens !" Yes, but this trade is more about special teams with a little bit of WR3 or WR4 upside.
Denver Broncos wide receiver Marvin Mims Jr. is still a developing wide receiver at 24 years old, but he is already one of the NFL's best return men. Mims Jr. is a two-time Pro Bowl returner and earned first-team All-Pro returner accolades in 2024 when he led the NFL with a 15.7 yards per punt return average. He has both a kick and a punt return touchdown in his career, and he led the NFL with 452 punt return yards in 2025.
Dallas does have a three-time Pro Bowl and 2024 first-team All-Pro return man in KaVontae Turpin , but the shine may be wearing off the TCU product. He had a brutal fumble on a kickoff return in the loss to the Buccaneers in Week 5, and the 5-foot-7, 170-pound return man is now 30 years old.
The Bucs force the fumble on the kickoff and get the ball right back! @TBvsDAL on Prime Video Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/PFpX0gXqBy
Turpin still remains one of the shiftiest and speediest returners in the league, but at his age and size, Dallas might want someone younger and slightly bigger in Mims, who is 5-11 and weighs 182 pounds. The Cowboys might be able to get a draft pick for shipping Turpin out, and they could perhaps use that and another later-round pick to bring in a younger, bigger replacement. Plus, Mims went to high school down the street from the Cowboys' team facility, The Star, at Lone Star High School. Jones loves his Texas ties.
author: Garrett Podell

title: Chiefs to place Josh Simmons on injured reserve; LT not eligible to return until Week 11
summary: Simmons has been dealing with a bulging disc in his back
full_text:
The Kansas City Chiefs will be without their starting left tackle for a while longer. Josh Simmons will be placed on injured reserve, according to Chiefs head trainer Rick Burkholder.
"Josh worked his tail off and [was] diligent every day," Burkholder said, according to ESPN . "However, we feel he's plateaued in the rehab process. He's just not there yet."
Simmons has been dealing with a bulging disc in his lower back. He practiced last week as a "ramp up" but was listed on Wednesday's injury report as being out with a back injury and for personal reasons, which Burkholder said was because Simmons took the rest of the day off after the decision was made to place him on injured reserve, per ESPN .
Burkholder did say that Simmons does not need surgery on the bulging disc, but that he simply needs more time to recover from the injury.
Simmons was the Chiefs' first-round pick (No. 32 overall) in the 2025 NFL Draft . He played in just eight games during his rookie season, missing time for personal reasons in Weeks 6 through 9 and then suffering a dislocated and fractured wrist in Week 13 that knocked him out for the remainder of the season.
Undrafted rookie Kahlil Benson has been filling in for Simmons to start the season, and will presumably stick in the role at least until Simmons is eligible to return to the field in Week 11. Benson has been credited by Pro Football Focus with allowing 12 pressures through the first five games of the season, ranking 30th among 75 qualified tackles who have played at least 100 snaps.
author: Jared Dubin

title: Re-drafting top 10 of the 2024 NFL Draft: Caleb Williams holds onto top spot, Drake Maye moves up
summary: Drake Maye jumps over Jayden Daniels to No. 2 after a Super Bowl run, while Caleb Williams holds onto the top spot and Malik Nabers crashes the top five
full_text:
The 2024 NFL Draft was a fun one. Six quarterbacks were selected in the top 12 for the first time ever, while the first 14 picks all came on offense. For NFL executives, if you hit on your first-round quarterback, you set up your city and organization for future success. If you whiff, you'll be out of a job soon enough.
In an exciting quarterback class, there was a clear-cut top three. Caleb Williams out of USC was a Heisman Trophy winner with ridiculous arm talent that was viewed as the favorite to go No. 1 overall. Behind him was Jayden Daniels , another Heisman Trophy winner who established himself as an electric playmaker during his final season at LSU. The other quarterback in the running to go No. 1 overall was Drake Maye out of North Carolina. However, the former ACC Player of the Year wasn't able to build on his 2022 success, as his Tar Heels finished 8-5 in 2023.
This Thursday, two stars from the 2024 NFL Draft in Williams and Maye will face off in what is one of the most highly anticipated "Thursday Night Football" games in recent memory. Let's go back in our time machine to that draft two years ago, and re-draft the top 10. Is Williams still the No. 1 overall pick? Was Maye at No. 3 overall a steal? Let's take a look.
The Chicago Bears shouldn't regret their pick at No. 1 overall. Maybe fans doubted it for a few moments. Jayden Daniels led the Washington Commanders to the NFC Championship game as a rookie, while Drake Maye made it to the Super Bowl in Year 2. Williams has not reached those heights just yet, but I think he can.
In 2025, Williams led the Bears to an 11-6 record, a division title and a playoff victory over the rival Green Bay Packers . He threw for a franchise-record 3,942 yards and made enough highlight-reel plays that landed him on the cover of "Madden." Williams was one of the biggest stories in the NFL last season, even though his 58.1% completion percentage ranked No. 32. He's improved on his accuracy this season. His 6% off-target rate ranks best in the NFL right now, and during the Week 6 win over the Atlanta Falcons , Williams completed a career-high 83.3% of his passes.
Maye had a second-year jump for the ages, as he completed 72% of his passes for 4,394 yards, 31 touchdowns and eight interceptions. He was the NFL MVP runner-up behind Matthew Stafford , and became the second-youngest quarterback to ever start in a Super Bowl. Maye was the first quarterback since Tom Brady in 2007 to lead the league in completion percentage and yards per attempt, and really improved when it came to going downfield. His 58% completion percentage on throws of 15+ air yards ranked No. 1 in the NFL. As a rookie, he ranked last in that category (29%).
Currently, Maye's New England Patriots are on a three-game winning streak, during which the quarterback has thrown 10 touchdowns and 1 interception. Maye is still leading the league in completion percentage (56%) and passing touchdowns (16) on throws of 15+ air yards over the last two seasons. This is a good leader, a dual-threat athlete who can make you pay with his legs and can make all the throws you want your quarterback to make. The Commanders choose Maye over Daniels this time around.
Daniels was one of the best rookies in NFL history, taking a lowly franchise from 4-13 to 12-5 and an NFC Championship appearance. He joined Lamar Jackson in becoming the second quarterback to ever record 4,000 passing yards and 1,000 rushing yards in a season, including playoffs, and scored the most total touchdowns (37) and total yards (5,416) by a rookie, ever. Daniels elevated everyone on the Commanders in 2024, as Washington's offense had three games that season where they recorded zero punts and zero turnovers.
The past year and a half hasn't been as exciting, unfortunately. Daniels missed 10 games due to multiple injuries in 2025, including a dislocated elbow, and is 0-3-1 in his four starts this season. His elbow also popped out again in the second game of the season. Daniels is still an electric playmaker when healthy, but it's hard to fathom that he hasn't won an NFL game in over a year.
The Arizona Cardinals go wide receiver again at No. 4, but take a different player this time around. Marvin Harrison Jr. was a flop and has already been traded away to the Houston Texans .
Malik Nabers caught 109 passes for 1,204 yards and seven touchdowns as a rookie, and recorded the second-most receptions (127) in his first 19 games behind Odell Beckham Jr.'s 133. Despite the quarterback issues in New York, Nabers has recorded at least 112 yards receiving in each of the last three games this season, including 165 yards against the New Orleans Saints last Sunday.
Maybe if we give Justin Herbert one of the best tight ends in the NFL, the Los Angeles Chargers aren't 0-6 this season. Bowers set a tight end rookie record with 112 receptions to go along with 1,194 yards and five touchdowns. He missed five games due to injury in 2025, but still caught a career-high seven touchdowns.
Bowers is on a heater to begin the 2026 season, having caught 28 passes for 382 yards and three scores in his first four games played. He's just the fifth tight end all-time to put up those kinds of numbers in the first four games of a season. The last time it happened was with Rob Gronkowski in 2015.
The New York Giants could use a lockdown cornerback, and find just that in Quinyon Mitchell at No. 6 overall. "Quinyonamo Bay" was a First Team All-Pro in 2025, as he led all defensive backs with a 39.6% completion percentage allowed (min. 100 coverage snaps) with zero touchdowns allowed in coverage. He actually just recorded his first regular-season interception a couple of weeks ago in London, but has four interceptions in the playoffs!
JC Latham is finally morphing into a star tackle for the Tennessee Titans , but it took a couple of years. If the Chargers didn't take Joe Alt at No. 5 overall in 2024, I think the Titans would have selected him at No. 7.
Alt was a stud as a rookie in 2024, but injuries have started to take their toll. He missed 11 games in 2025 due to an ankle injury, and has been sidelined with a neck injury recently. With Alt in the lineup last year, the Chargers were 5-1 while averaging 25.3 points per game. They went 6-6 without him while averaging just 18.3 points per game.
We mentioned above that Latham is finally living up to that top 10 draft billing. His 95.0% pass-block win rate ranks fifth among all offensive tackles this season over at PFF, and his 95.9% pass-block win rate on an island ranks third. Latham is a massive human being at 6-foot-6, 342 pounds, and would be an upgrade over Jawaan Taylor . We could take a pass rusher or defensive lineman here for the Falcons, but Gervon Dexter Sr . has been a great addition on the interior, and the Falcons just used two first-round picks on pass rushers with James Pearce Jr . and Jalon Walker . Pearce is eligible to return from suspension in two weeks.
In his two seasons with the Los Angeles Rams , Jared Verse recorded 12.0 sacks, 45 QB hits, 22 tackles for loss and made two Pro Bowls. The former Defensive Rookie of the Year is a well-rounded EDGE, having ranked sixth-highest in pressure rate through his first two seasons and second-best in run-stop win rate among pass rushers. Verse falls a bit in this re-draft because he hasn't been an adequate Myles Garrett replacement with the Cleveland Browns up to this point, and is still searching for that first sack.
Let's give the Minnesota Vikings another Byron Murphy . Byron Murphy II and Leonard Williams were a dynamic duo on the interior for the Seattle Seahawks during their Super Bowl run, as they combined for the most pressures (108) QB hits (35) and sacks (14.0) among 300-pound duos in 2025. The Texas product recorded seven sacks in 2025, and has three sacks through six games this season. The Seahawks have struggled out of the gate overall, but not Murphy.
author: Jordan Dajani

title: NFL trade rumors: 5 receivers the Rams should target in a deal, including Cowboys' George Pickens
summary: With Davante Adams out, the Rams suddenly need some help at wide receiver
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams have been one of the biggest disappointments in the NFL this year, and one reason why they've struggled so far is injuries. Myles Garrett , Aaron Donald and Puka Nacua have all missed multiple games due to injury, and now, you can add Davante Adams to that list.
The veteran receiver is expected to miss six to 10 weeks after rupturing his hamstring in the Rams' Week 6 loss to the Cardinals . Under the best-case scenario, Adams isn't expected to be back until December, which means the Rams now have a gaping hole at receiver.
According to ESPN , the Rams are planning to "at least explore the possibility of trading" for a receiver. If we know one thing about Rams general manager Les Snead, it's that he loves to wheel and deal. He's proven throughout his career that he's not shy when it comes to pulling the trigger on a big trade, so it's very possible we'll see the Rams make some sort of deal before the NFL's Nov. 10 trade deadline gets here.
With that in mind, let's check out five possible trade options for the Rams at receiver.
There is no team that loves to make a big trade more than the Rams, and this would be huge. Going after Pickens would make sense, and that's because the Cowboys actually might be willing to deal him. Pickens is playing on the franchise tag this year, and there's a good chance that he ends up leaving Dallas after the season. If that happens, the Cowboys would get nothing, but if they traded him now, they'd at least get something in return.
At 2-4, it's hard to say if the Cowboys should be buyers or sellers at the deadline, but at this point, it could go either way. They play in a bad division, so it might not make any sense for them to start trading away their best players, but they still have two games before the trade deadline. If they lose both, that could make them more open to making a deal. Cowboys owner Jerry Jones has already said he might be a seller at the deadline if the right deal comes along.
At same time Jerry Jones does not rule out being a seller at the deadline if a blockbuster offer like they got for Micah Parsons last year came along.
Pickens' production in Dallas has been underwhelming this year. He's caught just 33 passes for 428 yards for the Cowboys, but he might be able to put up bigger numbers if he joins a Rams' offense that ranks second in the NFL in passing yards per game. A move to Los Angeles would also give Pickens a chance to play with the reigning NFL MVP.
Although adding Pickens would make some sense, it wouldn't be easy. The Rams don't have a lot of draft capital to send to Dallas, so they'd have to get that figured out. The Rams also don't have very much salary cap space, so they'd have to figure out a way to fit the rest of Pickens' fully guaranteed franchise tag salary under their cap. Pickens' deal is worth $27.3 million, and the Rams would owe him the pro-rated amount of that, which would be about $18.2 million.
The Jaguars receiver appears to be in the doghouse in Jacksonville. Thomas has gone two straight weeks without making a single catch, and Jaguars coach Liam Coen appeared to bench him during Jacksonville's loss to Houston on Sunday. Thomas played in the first half against the Texans , but Coen kept him on the bench in the second. Thomas got targeted just three times in the loss, and his day ended with zero catches and one drop.
"Just week to week. Week to week. Guys have to step up and make plays," Coen said of why Thomas spent the second half on the bench, via the Florida Times-Union .
The Jags would still have a strong receiving room without Thomas. Not only do they have Parker Washington and Jakobi Meyers , but Travis Hunter has seen an uptick in offensive snaps recently, which has left Thomas as the odd man out.
Thomas has talent, and we saw that during his rookie year in 2024 when he caught 87 passes for 1,282 yards and 10 touchdowns. Though that was before Coen became the coach. This year, he has just nine catches for 105 yards, which puts him on pace for 26 catches and just 297 yards.
At this point, it feels like Thomas just needs a change of scenery, so being shipped out to Los Angeles would make a lot of sense.
For the Rams, the best part about Thomas is that they'd have him on his rookie deal through the end of the 2027 season, so he'd come cheap.
When Jennings signed with the Vikings back in May, he probably figured he was going to have a big year. With opposing defenses worried about Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison , that should have opened things up for Jennings, but that hasn't happened.
Through five games, Jennings has caught just two passes for nine yards, which is an extremely low total even when you take into account the Vikings' offense has been historically bad this year. Jennings has understandably been frustrated, and those frustrations are starting to show on the field.
Jauan Jennings was pissed off he didn’t get the ball when he was wide open in the end zone on Sunday A total of 5 targets in 4 games will do this to you pic.twitter.com/25tacVpI0f
Jefferson was asked about Jennings this week, and he urged his new teammate to be patient.
"Obviously, he's gonna be frustrated because he wants that ball and he feels like he's worked that route or that moment to get the ball and create that separation," Jefferson told reporters . "That's every player, every guy that wants to have a big moment and a big role in a game.  The ball is just not finding him at this moment, but it will."
Jennings might show some patience, but if he doesn't start getting the ball soon, it wouldn't be shocking to see him quietly ask for a trade. The veteran receiver caught 55 passes for 643 yards and nine touchdowns while playing for the 49ers last season, and he would probably enjoy a return to the NFC West, whether that's with the 49ers or Rams.
This move feels like it would make a lot of sense for both sides. On the Titans ' end, they have several solid receivers, but everyone is essentially going to waste while playing in a Tennessee offense that ranks dead last in the NFL in passing yards per game. Rookie Carnell Tate leads the team in both receptions (29) and receiving yards (344), and free agent addition Wan'Dale Robinson is right behind him.
Ridley has basically been the odd man out this year: He's caught just five passes for 81 yards through six games. If the 1-5 Titans decide to hold a fire sale, then it wouldn't be surprising at all to see them dump Ridley.
The 31-year-old actually took a pay cut this year to stay with the Titans. The upside for the Rams is that Ridley doesn't have any guaranteed money left on his contract after this season, so they wouldn't be on the hook for anything in 2027.
One thing that could scare the Rams away is that Ridley (Hip) is on the injury report this week. He also missed a total of 10 games last season due to injury. Considering the Rams' luck with injuries right now, those two things might be enough of a red flag to keep them away, but the 2018 first-round pick would certainly be an intriguing option.
With Alec Pierce still out, the Colts might not be interested in trading Downs, but that certainly could change at some point over the next two weeks. If the 2-4 Colts lose their next two games (at Minnesota, at Jacksonville), then it wouldn't be a shock to see this team go into fire sale mode ahead of the trade deadline.  Also, the Colts just fired general manager Chris Ballard — the guy who drafted Downs — so that might make the team more open to a trade.
Downs is in the final year of his rookie deal, which is one reason why a trade could be win-win for both sides. The Colts would get something in return for a player they're possibly going to lose anyway, while the cash-strapped Rams would only have to worry about Downs' $3.9 million base salary. Since he's already played six games, the Rams would only owe him about $2.6 million.
Any deal would almost certainly involve draft picks, and the Colts will likely be doing…

title: Should Vikings trade for Justin Herbert? Making the case for and against potential blockbuster deal
summary: Minnesota has a championship-level defense, but the offense could use a spark
full_text:
The Minnesota Vikings are making history, but not the type of history you want to publicize.
Minnesota has won its last 10 games dating back to the end of last season. That's the good stuff. The bad stuff is that the Vikings' 21 touchdowns over that span are the fewest during any 10-game winning streak in the NFL since the 1928-29 Packers . Also bad -- thought not quite as bad -- is that the Vikings' nine touchdowns this season are the fewest for a 5-0 team since the 2003 Panthers .
The '03 Panthers ended up playing in that year's Super Bowl . The Vikings could do the same thing this year, but the odds of that happening are slim. The Vikings not only play in arguably the NFL's toughest division, but they share a conference with arguably the NFL's best team, the 6-0 49ers .
Minnesota's current situation has stirred up rumblings about a possible blockbuster trade that would bring Justin Herbert to town. The Chargers reportedly did not consider trading Herbert earlier this month, but it's fair to wonder if they're having second thoughts with the trade deadline just around the corner.
The Chargers are 0-6 and appear to be on the precipice of a total reboot. Herbert is struggling to the point where a change of scenery might be necessary for him if he is going to regain the swagger that made him a two-time Pro Bowler.
Similar trades have happened with mixed results. Matthew Stafford and Jared Goff have both enjoyed successful second chapters after swapping teams. Russell Wilson , however, did not enjoy a similar story in Denver after being traded from Seattle.
How would history remember a possible trade involving Herbert and the Vikings? To find out, let's dive into the cases for and against the Vikings trading for Herbert, along with a final verdict.
It's clear that the Vikings have a championship-caliber defense (they're currently No. 1 in the NFL in fewest points allowed) but need help on offense. Herbert, in theory, could help the Vikings bridge that gap while becoming a surefire Super Bowl contender.
While this season has been a mess so far, Herbert was without a doubt one of the league's best quarterbacks during his first six seasons. He threw for the second-most passing yards in league history during a player's first six seasons -- only Peyton Manning threw for more yards. Herbert's 163 touchdowns was the sixth-most in league history for a player in that span.
Herbert is prolific, and he has gotten better (prior to this season) in terms of taking care of the ball. He threw just three interceptions in 2024, and while that number jumped to 13 in 2025, that total isn't horrible when you consider that he threw 512 passes that year.
Looking at the Vikings this season, Herbert would be given the keys to an offense that certainly has potential. He'd get a chance to work with All-Pro wideout Justin Jefferson , two-time Pro Bowler tight end T.J. Hockenson , and ageless wonder Aaron Jones , whose skill set is similar to former Chargers teammate Austin Ekeler .
Herbert's age is also something that should be considered. Only 28, Herbert should have a ton of great football left in him. He would conceivably be the team's long-term answer at quarterback.
Let's start with the amount of assets the Vikings would have to send to Los Angeles. At a minimum, the Vikings would likely have to part ways with at least one first-round pick and most likely two. Any trade involving Herbert would require multiple high draft picks. It could also mean trading Kyler Murray to Los Angeles.
There's also the prospect of having Herbert learn a new offense while jumping on a moving train. Unlike Stafford and Goff, Herbert wouldn't have the luxury of having an offseason to learn a playbook and to develop a rapport with his new teammates. He'd be asked to do that immediately, which is not an easy task.
If the Vikings kept Murray, that would create an awkward situation for not only Murray and Herbert, but for everyone involved. Sides would undoubtedly be taken, which would create a divided locker room.
Now, add in the fact that Vikings don't have a great offensive line, which would expose Herbert's lack of elite mobility. That's one of the issues now in Los Angeles, and it would continue to rear its ugly head in Minnesota.
Another con for Herbert: Murray's mobility is one of the things that has allowed him to have success with the Vikings. He can extend plays while getting outside the pocket. Murray has his flaws, but mobility isn't one of them.
Murray's play has also improved in recent weeks. Over his past two games (wins over the Dolphins and Saints ) he's completed a combined 76.1% of his passes while averaging 238 passing yards per game. He has also continued to take care of the ball, which has been a key component of the Vikings' success.
No, the Vikings should not try to acquire Herbert by the trade deadline. It's too messy and not worth Minnesota jeopardizing their current championship prospects. Besides, plenty of teams have been able to win a Super Bowl following the Vikings' current blueprint: leaning on their defense and having your offense simply not lose the game.
Yes, the Vikings' offense will have to have their moments this season if Minnesota is going to win the NFC North and make a serious run at a Super Bowl. While they haven't found their top gear yet, it's safe to assume that Murray and Co.'s best days are still ahead of them, especially if Jefferson can stay healthy.
With all of that said, that doesn't mean that the Vikings shouldn't try to grab Herbert this offseason if this season ends up being a disappointment. They also shouldn't avoid trying to strengthen other parts of their offense at this year's trade deadline in an effort to improve their Super Bowl chances.

title: CBS Sports names future Hall of Famer JJ Watt lead analyst for the 'NFL ON CBS'
summary: Watt began calling games with Jim Nantz and Tracy Wolfson at the start of the 2026 season
full_text:
Future Hall of Famer J.J. Watt has been named the permanent lead analyst for the NFL ON CBS, having signed a multi-year agreement to continue working alongside Jim Nantz and Tracy Wolfson, the network announced on Thursday .
Watt joined CBS Sports in 2023 as a studio analyst on THE NFL TODAY before moving to calling games with Evan Washburn in 2025. He started calling games with the network's lead team in 2026 and will continue to do so for the foreseeable future.
"I've had a front-row seat to JJ's growth as a top-tier broadcaster, watching him tackle this role just like he did his hall-of-fame playing career," said David Berson, Chairman, Global Sports Group, Skydance. "He's insightful, entertaining, passionate, meticulous in his preparation, and the ultimate teammate. He has a unique ability to see things and communicate to fans of all levels. We are thrilled to have him leading our NFL coverage."
"I am incredibly honored and grateful to have the opportunity to represent CBS Sports and all of the fantastic people who make this place so special," Watt said. "From the brotherhood of THE NFL TODAY to my crews calling games, I couldn't ask for better teammates alongside me on this television journey. I am thankful to David Berson for his leadership, vision and trust. I love this job and can't wait to see ya Sunday with Jim and Tracy and many more Sundays to come!"
A first-round pick in 2011, Watt played in the NFL for 12 years, 10 of them with the Houston Texans and two with the Arizona Cardinals . Widely considered one of the best defensive players in history, Watt is a three-time Defensive Player of the Year and five-time First Team All-Pro who also finished second in MVP voting in 2014.
He finished his career with 114.5 sacks, 195 tackles for loss, 317 quarterback hits, 70 passes deflected, 27 forced fumbles, 17 fumbles recovered and two interceptions. He also caught three passes, all for touchdowns, during the 2014 season. He is eligible for Hall-of-Fame induction in 2028.

title: Are Chiefs, 49ers on collision course for third Super Bowl meeting? Here are teams that could stop them
summary: Kansas City beat San Francisco in 2020 and 2024
full_text:
Stop us if you've heard this before: The Chiefs and the 49ers are among the best teams in the NFL .
Kansas City and San Francisco are a combined 11-0 and are two of the three remaining undefeated teams, joined by the 5-0 Vikings . Since 2019 — the season they first met in the Super Bowl — the Chiefs have the most wins (including playoffs) in the NFL, and the 49ers are third, behind the Chiefs and the Bills .
Are we looking at a Chiefs-49ers Super Bowl for the third time in eight seasons? SportsLine projections currently have it as the most likely matchup for the Lombardi Trophy. These are the five most likely through six weeks:
As you can see, none are particularly likely. That's because one, it's only Week 7, and two, any specific matchup is extremely unlikely until deep into the playoffs. SportsLine still gives eight AFC teams and seven NFC teams at least a 5% chance to make the Super Bowl. While the Chiefs and the 49ers are the favorites to emerge from their conferences, it's an extremely tight race.
Teams with 5% or better chance to make Super Bowl, via SportsLine
So what's making these teams so good, and who — or what — could stop them? Let's dig in.
The 49ers and Chiefs share one major strength: their offenses. They rank third and sixth, respectively, in points per drive.
It starts with the rushing game. The 49ers lead the NFL in rushing success rate (a down-to-down measure), and the Chiefs lead the NFL in rushing expected points added (which takes into account situation and rewards big plays more).
Kenneth Walker III has been a revelation for the Chiefs. They had the least explosive running back rush rate from 2024-25. This year, they are second in explosive rushing rate, and Walker leads the NFL with 665 rushing yards (despite having already had his bye week) and 6.3 yards per rush. His seven rushes of 20+ yards are tied for the most in the NFL.
Both teams are also among the best passing teams in the NFL. San Francisco is second in net yards per attempt, and Kansas City is third. The 49ers have allowed the fewest sacks in the NFL (five); the Chiefs are second with six. While the 49ers aren't as explosive on the ground as the Chiefs are, they are more explosive through the air. San Francisco's explosive passing rate is third in the NFL. (The Chiefs are eighth, not far behind.)
So, long story short, Brock Purdy and Patrick Mahomes are both playing excellent football, and both have great ecosystems — from play callers to offensive lines to running games — around them.
Defensively, both teams do an excellent job of limiting explosive plays, and a big reason for that is sure tackling. The Chiefs have the lowest missed tackle rate in the NFL, and the 49ers are second. The Chiefs are also the best rush defense in the NFL by success rate.
Both teams have been stout against the pass thanks to excellent cornerback play. For the Chiefs, second-year cornerback Nohl Williams has been terrific this year, as has first-round rookie Mansoor Delane . For San Francisco, it's Upton Stout , Deommodore Lenoir and Renardo Greene.
So far this season, 79 players across the NFL have been the primary defender on at least 25 passes.
The Chiefs also have the league's best run defense on a success rate basis.
Add in significant star power, too — Chris Jones in Kansas City, Fred Warner in San Francisco, for example — and both teams have been among the NFL's best this year.
The 49ers are dealing with so many injuries that they're running out of IR-designated return spots. Teams only get eight per year, so San Francisco has kept Nick Bosa (calf/knee), who hasn't played since Week 2 and would have normally gone on IR, on the active roster.
The most injured spot, by far, is wide receiver. Mike Evans is one of two wideouts to appear in all six games this season, but he left Monday's win over the Commanders after aggravating the Achilles soreness he has dealt with all year, and he will miss time. The only other wide receiver to appear in all six games is Jacob Cowing , who has one catch.
49ers wide receiver injuries
Fractured ribs/Achilles soreness
Ankle ligament sprain and rupture
Currently, the 49ers have three healthy wide receivers — Cowing, Brandin Cooks and Jordan Watkins — on their active roster. Kirk could be close to returning, too. Still, it's a really fragile group, and Evans's late departure in the first half on Monday showed his absence could be the straw that finally breaks the camel's back.
49ers offense vs. Commanders
Injuries have been a consistent issue for this team the past couple of years. Somehow, the 49ers just keep winning, but it is an issue that considerably lowers their ceiling, especially against some of the league's best.
San Francisco's defense is leaps and bounds better than last year overall, but one issue remains: run defense. The 49ers are 24th in defensive rushing success rate, even without having played many of the NFL's best rushing attacks. Overall, this hasn't caused too much of an issue because the 49ers, one, score so much that other teams are often passing to keep up, and, two, don't give up explosives. But that doesn't mean it won't be an issue in the future. The 49ers face Bijan Robinson this weekend in what will be their sternest test yet.
Only the Dolphins have fewer sacks than the Chiefs' eight, and the Chiefs' 4.2% sack rate ranks 29th in the NFL.
The good news for Kansas City is that it is getting a ton of pressure. It ranks a solid 12th in pressure rate, and its 47 quick pressures (within 2.5 seconds of the snap) are tied for eighth-most. Plus, that's with the Chiefs having only played five games. They just need to turn more of those pressures into sacks. Steve Spagnuolo has a deep Rolodex of blitz packages, and he often knows exactly when to use them.
We'll also note one other issue. The Chiefs have been pretty bad defending under-center play action: 30th in passing success rate and 28th in yards per attempt. The Colts and the Raiders specifically exploited this issue:
Under-center play action vs. Chiefs
Even Malik Willis had two big completions on these types of throws.
Kirk Cousins finds a wide open Thomas for the TD! @KCvsLV on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/6tDZKxqR2D
Brock Bowers apareceu! 👋 📺: #KCvsLV - ao vivo e em português no NFL Game Pass pic.twitter.com/EshBP6WfhM
The Kansas City linebackers play really close to the line of scrimmage, which has helped a lot against the run but can make it hard for them to get back if they trigger down on play action. Teams could look to take advantage there.
Don't forget about special teams! The Chiefs and the 49ers both have major issues here, ranking 30th and 31st, respectively, in special teams expected points added.
Just something to keep an eye on.
We can't list out everyone, but here are three options from each conference:
Josh Allen is 5-1 against Patrick Mahomes in the regular season but 0-4 against him in the playoffs. Three of those four postseason losses have been by six or fewer points. At some point, that has to even out ... right? The Bills' offense has been outstanding this year, and much of that has been without D.J. Moore. There are defensive concerns, but if you have Allen, you have a chance.
Lamar Jackson has looked like a bona fide MVP candidate — if not among the front runners — when he's been on the field. An ankle injury caused him to miss the last two games, but if he's back and fully healthy, he looks terrific. Derrick Henry is a load to bring down, and Zay Flowers is looking like a breakout star in Declan Doyle's offense. Plus, the defense is starting to come around under new coach Jesse Minter.
How about the only team to beat the Bills, who are thought to be the top competition, so far this season? Drake Maye had a brutal start but has been much better in recent weeks, including in the win over Buffalo when he threw three touchdown passes and ran for 54 yards. The defense has been solid as ever, too.

title: NFL punishes Patriots, Eagles and Jets head coaches with near-record fines, per report
summary: Mike Vrabel, Nick Sirianni and Aaron Glenn will be taking a massive hit to their bank account
full_text:
The NFL sent a stern message this week by handing out three of the largest head coaching fines in league history. Mike Vrabel, Nick Sirianni and Aaron Glenn have all been hit with a $250,000 fine, according to Sports Illustrated .
Each coach was punished for their conduct toward game officials in recent weeks. Coaches are allowed to yell at game officials if they don't like a call, but the NFL doesn't want to create a hostile environment where coaches feel comfortable berating officials.
Things have gotten testy this year between players, coaches and officials, and the NFL clearly wants to cut down on that. Following Week 4, two different game officials were suspended for unprofessional conduct toward players .
Speaking of Week 4, Vrabel was actually hit with an unsportsmanlike conduct penalty that week for using profanity against an official after he didn't agree with a flag that was thrown on the play.
Patriots coach Mike Vrabel was hit with an Unsportsmanlike Conduct penalty. The Bills tied the game a few plays later. pic.twitter.com/6JsrQWfAeA
"I told them that it was a terrible — I'm not going to say — effing call," Vrabel said after New England's 29-26 win over Buffalo, via The Athletic . "I've said that 87 times since I've been a head coach. There was nothing derogatory. You know, you'd have to ask (the referee). I think he was a little sensitive."
As for Glenn, he hasn't been hit with a penalty flag yet this year, but he did blow up on the officiating crew during the Jets' Week 5 win over the Browns.
Incredible video sent in by a listener of Aaron Glenn absolutely LOSING HIS MIND on the refs over the atrocious officiating in the first half. And he had EVERY RIGHT to be furious. The officiating was a complete joke. #Jets pic.twitter.com/SGjVDNJOnN
On Sirianni's end, if you turn on any Eagles game, you'll likely see him chewing out a ref. One of his biggest tirades came in Week 3 against the Bears after Jalen Hurts was called for intentional grounding. Sirianni did NOT agree with the call.
Nick Sirianni was letting the official have it after the intentional grounding call 😳 pic.twitter.com/jcOXDINW5S
The good news for each of these three coaches is that they might get their money back. According to the SI report, the money will be placed in abeyance, and each coach could have the fine rescinded if they show good behavior going forward.
If the fines do stick, they would be among the largest coaching fines in NFL history. The league rarely hands out massive fines like this to head coaches.
Here are the largest fines that any coach has ever been given: 1. Bill Belichick (Patriots): $500,000 (Spygate in 2007 ) 2. Brian Daboll (Giants): $100,000 (Violating concussion protocol in 2025 ) 3. Mike Tomlin (Steelers): $100,000 (Interfering with a kickoff return )
If you need a refresher on the Tomlin incident, he interfered with Baltimore's Jacoby Jones on a kickoff return that might have gone for a touchdown.
That time Mike Tomlin tried to trip Jacoby Jones on Thanksgiving night (video: Chughes612) pic.twitter.com/SX9OJpmd3U
At the time Tomlin was fined, it was the second-largest head coaching fine ever, behind only Belichick's.
Since then, several other coaches have been hit with a $100,000 fine, in addition to Daboll. Back in 2020, Jon Gruden (Raiders), Sean Payton (Saints), Vic Fangio (Broncos), Pete Carroll (Seahawks) and Kyle Shanahan (49ers) were all fined $100,000 for violating COVID protocols by not wearing a mask during a game . These five, along with Tomlin, Daboll and Belichick, are the only eight coaches to be hit with at least $100,000 in fines.
Payton also lost out on millions when he was suspended without pay in 2012 for the part he played in Bountygate. That wasn't technically a fine, though, so it didn't make the list.
If Vrabel, Sirianni and Glenn ended up paying out the $250,000 fines, that means they'll each have paid out the second-largest coaching fine in NFL history.

title: Titans release DT Jordan Elliott after incident with firearm at team facility
summary: The veteran defensive tackle appeared in five games this season after following Robert Saleh to Tennessee from San Francisco
full_text:
The Tennessee Titans released defensive tackle Jordan Elliott on Tuesday following an "incident" at the team facility last week. The Titans offered no further details in a statement , saying only there was an incident on Thursday, Oct. 15, and that Elliott was no longer part of their team.
Elliott became frustrated with a teammate on the practice field. He was later seen storming out of the locker room and went to his vehicle to grab a firearm, according to A to Z Sports . However, the situation was de-escalated before anything tragic happened. ESPN confirmed this report , saying that Elliott was upset with right tackle JC Latham , and that the firearm never left Elliott's parking spot. The Metro Nashville Police Department told A to Z Sports that no reports had been filed. Reports indicated fellow defensive lineman John Franklin-Myers helped de-escalate the situation, something that was confirmed by Titans head coach Robert Saleh during his Wednesday press conference.
On Thursday, an NFL spokesman said that the league is investigating the incident, according to ESPN , which noted that if a violation is found while he's not on a team, Elliott could serve a suspension as a free agent.
Saleh told reporters that Elliott is a good man who has never committed a crime in his life. He gave credit to the Titans organization and the league for "pausing" and asking why a "great man" and "great father" would do something like this? Saleh also said he viewed this as more of a "call for help" than a "criminal act."
"I will stand on the table for Jordan's character," Saleh said. "Unfortunately, rules are rules with regard to guns on property. And sometimes it's far greater than the knee-jerk reaction of kicking somebody when they're down. My message to 31 other teams would be if you need a hell of a run-stopping D-tackle that can help you on a playoff run, give me a call, I'll tell you everything you need to know about him. He's a good man. Had a terrible lapse in judgment that I recognize as a call for help more than a criminal act. It's unfortunate the way it went down. But as far as Jordan's concerned and the locker room and all that, I think people see it differently here than the knee-jerk reaction of the world."
Clip of #Titans coach Robert Saleh standing up for Jordan Elliott despite a “terrible lapse in judgment.” Saleh notes players recently have taken their own lives. While not saying Elliott is in that mindset, Saleh is mindful this could’ve been a “cry for help.” 🎥 @Titans pic.twitter.com/FlrcEz4V67
Elliott has played in five games this season with one start, and has recorded 11 tackles. He was inactive this past Sunday against the Indianapolis Colts , with Saleh telling reporters Elliott was "dealing with personal stuff." Elliott had followed Saleh over from the San Francisco 49ers , as he spent the past two seasons out in Santa Clara, making 29 starts in 31 games played.
Elliott's release is not the only strange occurrence the Titans are dealing with, as the team also made starting cornerback and $58 million free-agent addition Alontae Taylor inactive in Week 6. They didn't just bench him; they took his uniform away. It was described as a coach's decision, and Saleh has refused to elaborate on the situation.
"We'll discuss it as a staff and make a decision that is best for the team moving forward," Saleh told reporters on Monday.
The Titans return home this week to host the 4-2 Cleveland Browns , who currently lead the AFC North.
