This is not nearly as appetizing a matchup as it seemed in the preseason, but someone has to win the dreadful NFC East, and these are two of the four teams that can do so. The Cowboys are once again in prime time after a "Thursday Night Football" loss to the Buccaneers and a "Sunday Night Football" loss to the Packers, and they've lost five straight prime-time games overall. The Eagles, now led by backup quarterback Tanner McKee , are looking for something offensively, and perhaps it can happen against a struggling Cowboys defense. With the Commanders on bye and the Giants facing the Texans , this is a great opportunity for both teams.
Sunday, 1 p.m. ET on Fox (Stream: fubo, try for free )
Only one team -- the 1992 Chargers -- has started 0-4 and made the playoffs, but the Texans are making a push to join them. Houston has won two straight after that awful start, and a win Sunday would improve its postseason odds to essentially a coin flip. The Giants, meanwhile, lead the NFC East at 3-2-1, and in that struggling division, all wins are going to be important, regardless of who they come against.
Thursday, 8:15 p.m. ET on Prime Video
Here's another intra-conference matchup among the top five most important games this week. Both teams are 4-2 this season, yet neither leads its division. The Patriots are a game back of the 5-1 Bills , who are on bye this week, and the Bears are a game and a half behind the 5-0 Vikings . Simply keeping pace here will be the goal for both, though neither team's playoff chances would be knocked too far down with a loss.
author: Zachary Pereles

title: It wouldn't shock me IF ... NFL Week 7: Broncos bench Bo Nix, Kenneth Walker III has muted return to Seattle
summary: Could Aaron Glenn finally get a divisional win? How will JJ McCarthy fare?
full_text:
An NFL season is like strapping into a rollercoaster and blindfolding yourself. It's thrilling, slightly terrifying, and, most notably, it leaves you never knowing when the twists and turns are coming. Each week is a constant reminder that we truly don't know what's going to happen, even if we dig as deep as we can into each storyline and stat to see who has the edge.
That said, we've been fortunate here to keep you in on a few developments that were right around the corner this season. Last week, we noted that we wouldn't be surprised if Tennessee pulled out its first win of the season, and they proved us right. However, we whiffed on the other predictions, especially MarShawn Lloyd exploding for 100 yards rushing. Despite the tasty matchup against a poor Dallas run defense, the Packers back mustered just 10 yards on the ground. Hey, while we'd love to get every pick right, the nature of this story is to pull out some obscure and/or bold-ish predictions, which means we're inherently going to miss on a few.
Nevertheless, we're rolling our sleeves back up, pointing the bat toward the outfield, and calling our shot on some storylines and/or individual performances that we wouldn't be shocked to see happen over the course of Week 7.
To put it nicely, Bo Nix has been bad through the first six weeks of the season. The Broncos quarterback seems skittish attempting any pass that goes much further than the line of scrimmage, and the Denver offense is suffering because of it. Nix's 4.9 air yards per attempt this season is the lowest of any quarterback through six games in the last 20 years. Meanwhile, his passer rating and EPA per dropback are 23rd among 29 quarterbacks to throw at least 100 passes this season. Despite the ball traveling the fewest through the air than any other quarterback in the league this season, Nix's turnover-worthy throw rate ranks 17th.
For instance, Nix nearly threw a pick-six on the opening drive of Denver's eventual win over Seattle on a throw that was about five yards down the field towards the right sideline.
Bo Nix NEARLY threw a PICK 6 pic.twitter.com/4mZ1xhJsVo
Denver has already shaken up the offensive playcalling duties with Sean Payton taking back the play sheet over David Webb. If the offense continues to struggle, the next step is to make a change at quarterback, even if it is only for a brief period.
The Cardinals defense just stifled Matthew Stafford and the Rams last week, holding them to 16 points in an upset win at SoFi Stadium. If Arizona puts together a similar performance and they take advantage of some of Nix's riskier throws, another upset could be brewing, and if things get out of hand, it wouldn't be stunning to see Nix finish this game on the bench.
Gambling angle to note : Bo Nix is +117 to throw an interception (via DraftKings Sportsbook).
Kenneth Walker III has arguably been the story of the first half of the regular season. He's unquestionably the top offseason acquisition, as the Chiefs running back has the most rushing yards (665) in the first five games with a team in NFL history. Those rushing yards are the third-most by any player through five games in the past 50 seasons. Walker also joined Jim Brown (1963), Eric Dickerson (1983), Emmitt Smith (1995), Marshall Faulk (2000), and Priest Holmes (2002) as just the sixth player all-time with at least 750 scrimmage yards and eight total touchdowns in the first five games of a season. He's simply been sensational.
Naturally, given how prolific Walker has been, he's eyed for another massive performance on Sunday night, especially because he'll be going up against his former team, the Seattle Seahawks , who he earned Super Bowl LX MVP honors with last year. This homecoming/revenge game has plenty of juice to it, but it might not deliver with Walker dominating up and down the sidelines.
Seattle is tied for the third-fewest rushing yards per attempt (3.5) allowed so far this season. They're also tied for the seventh-fewest missed tackles on rushing attempts and second in yards before contact per rush (0.57). Those stats suggest that the Seahawks should be able to get after Walker quickly and that they don't have an affinity for missing tackles.
Gambling angle to note : Kenneth Walker III's over/under rushing yards total is set at 87.5 and -110 to the Under. Walker's over/under for rushing + receiving yards is 111.5 and set at -113 to the Under (via DraftKings Sportsbook).
You know the 2026 regular season has gone absolutely haywire when we're buying a little bit of J.J. McCarthy -- new starting quarterback for the New York Giants -- stock. Outside of an interception, however, McCarthy looked sharp coming in during the fourth quarter of New York's loss to the Saints . The former first-round pick completed 11-of-21 passes for 243 yards, a touchdown and an interception. The Giants also scored 17 points while he was under center. That was enough for John Harbaugh to name him the starter, and now he'll make his first start this Sunday in Houston against the Texans .
While that sounds daunting given the reputation of the Texans' defense, they haven't been as lethal as they were a year ago. Through six games, Houston's defense ranks 20th in scoring (23.8 points per game allowed). They've also had three games this season with at least 30 points allowed.
300+ passing yards allowed
With the Texans coming back from a game in London last week, this might be an opportunity for McCarthy to shine in his starting debut and take advantage of what has been a sneaky shaky Houston defense.
Gambling angle to note : J.J. McCarthy is +266 to throw for at least 2 TDs (via DraftKings Sportsbook).
I think points could come in bunches during this NFC North matchup between the Green Bay Packers and Detroit Lions to the point where we're flirting with a total of 70 points scored. This would mark just the fourth time this season that two clubs have combined for at least 70 points, and one of those other games already involved the Lions (Week 2 vs. Bills , 72 points scored).
The Lions play at a tremendous pace, running 66.4 plays per game (seventh-highest in the NFL). Not only do they run a lot of plays, but they score a ton, as their 32.8 points per game average ranks second in the league. While Green Bay has a strong pass defense, there's simply too much firepower on the Lions offense to expect them to contain them wire-to-wire, especially as they'll come into this game well-rested after having the Week 6 bye. Moreover, the Lions defense has been Swiss cheese. Yes, they'll be getting star safety Brian Branch back, but this is a unit that has the worst total defense (404.4 yards) and third-worst third-down rate (29.6%) in the NFL entering Week 7. That might improve slightly with Branch, but it's still a weakness that Jordan Love will be able to exploit with Christian Watson and Matthew Golden .
On throws with at least 20 air yards this season, the Lions are allowing an opposing passer rating of 116.2 (fifth-worst in the NFL) and four passing touchdowns (tied for league-high). Over the past two games, Love is second in the NFL in passer rating (135.4) on such throws, so it could be bombs away throughout the afternoon at Ford Field.
Gambling angle to note : The total for Packers-Lions is set at 53.5 with the Over priced in at -110. An alternative total of 59.5 is +179 to the Over, and the alternate total of 69.5 is +576 to the Over (via DraftKings Sportsbook).
Now that the Jets finally snapped their interception-less streak earlier this season, it's time for Aaron Glenn to get off the schneid when it comes to the AFC East. Did you know that Glenn enters Week 7 without a single divisional win under his belt? The Jets head coach is 0-7 so far against division foes in his head coaching career, and the games largely haven't even been that competitive. Overall, Glenn's Jets have been outscored by 129 total points in those divisional games.
Fortunately for Glenn, he, in theory, has an easy road…
author: Tyler Sullivan

title: NFL Week 7 picks: Our experts face off on Patriots at Bears, Cowboys at Eagles and more
summary: CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games
full_text:
What did we learn in Week 6? The Houston Texans are officially back, as is Caleb Williams with the Chicago Bears , and we have some serious questions about the Los Angeles Rams , who were upset by the Arizona Cardinals at home last Sunday. The Cardinals now have more wins at SoFi Stadium this year than the Rams and Los Angeles Chargers combined.
This week, the Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints will play the first-ever NFL game in Paris, the San Francisco 49ers look to remain perfect against the Atlanta Falcons , and Kenneth Walker III aims to lead the Kansas City Chiefs to victory over his former team, the Seattle Seahawks . This could be a revenge game for the ages.
Which teams should you pick in Week 7, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Oct. 21 over at DraftKings Sportsbook.
Dajani (Bears -3): I can't remember the last time I've been this excited for a Thursday night game. Caleb Williams will suit up for the first time at home since his hamstring injury, and this is the first Bears home game since the passing of Mike Ditka. I have concerns about this Bears pass defense and how it will fare against a red-hot Drake Maye , but the fact is that Chicago has allowed 9.3 points per game at home this season. The Bears' offense has also averaged 35 points per game in their four wins, and I think Williams is out to make a statement. This will be a high-flying affair that comes down to the very end, and a push is very much in play. But give me Chicago at home, with the backing of an emotionally charged atmosphere. Remember, the Bears' lone Super Bowl win came against the New England Patriots under Ditka.  … Prediction: Bears 28, Patriots 24
Dubin (Bears -3): I also see this being a high-scoring game, with two offenses that can pile up points quickly. Chicago's offense in two non-rain/non-Brian Flores games with Caleb Williams under center has been electric, particularly on the ground, and Caleb Williams opens things up for the passing game. New England is struggling to run the ball, but Drake Maye has been on fire as of late. I'll lean toward the Bears here because of the Patriots' injury issues along the offensive line, which could hold the run game back further and put even more on Maye's shoulders.  … Prediction: Bears 31, Patriots 27
Dajani (Saints +3.5): The Steelers are impossible to figure out. From week-to-week — or even half-to-half, as evidenced by last week's overtime victory against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . If you're going to give me the hook at +3.5 in an international game, I'm probably going to take it. The Saints are a perfect 8-0 ATS in their last eight games away from home, and are 3-0 ATS all-time in international games. I think Gayle Benson's recent comments stirred up the locker room, and the Saints responded with a win in which they dropped 34 points — even if it came against the New York Giants . … Prediction: Steelers 23, Saints 20
Dubin (Steelers -3.5): The Saints finally played a game from ahead last week against the Giants, and they didn't necessarily look comfortable doing it. They have mostly been a second-half offensive team throughout this season, struggling early on before piling up yards and points in comeback mode. I don't trust this offense enough to build a lead against Pittsburgh's defense (ninth in yards, 12th in points, fifth in EPA per play) right now, so I'll lean toward this game playing out in a similar fashion to New Orleans' early-season contests, with the Steelers taking a lead and the Saints trying to stage a comeback, only to fail this time around. … Prediction: Steelers 21, Saints 17
Dajani (Falcons +3): I'm thinking about backing the Falcons in this spot. The 49ers had an emotional victory over the Seahawks in Week 5 and are now on a short week after Monday night's win against the Washington Commanders . It looked like we were in for a blowout after the 49ers went up 23-3, but Washington then outscored San Francisco, 14-0, while outgaining the 49ers 201 yards to 7 yards. That was ... interesting to see. The 49ers have found a way to keep winning games despite all of the injuries. Nick Bosa , Mike Evans , Deebo Samuel , Upton Stout and Mykel Williams were among the players who did not practice on Wednesday. This week, I'm going to take the points with Atlanta. … Prediction: 49ers 22, Falcons 20
Dubin (49ers -3): This line feels several points too low, even with Mike Evans potentially out in addition to all of the other wide receiver issues. So long as the Niners have Kyle Shanahan calling plays and Brock Purdy , Christian McCaffrey and George Kittle involved, I think their offense cooks. And Atlanta can't quite reach the same level offensively — even with Bijan Robinson and Drake London on hand. The Niners have been excellent against the run this year, and if this game winds up being one where Penix has to match Purdy throw for throw, I don't see that going well for Atlanta.  … Prediction: 49ers 26, Falcons 16
Dajani ( Bengals +3): The Bengals are fresh off their bye while the Baltimore Ravens are fresh off ... a loss to the Cleveland Browns . It was their 15th loss when leading by at least seven points in the fourth quarter since 2020, which ranks the most in the NFL. Lamar Jackson has a chance to return this week, but I'm curious to see how "spry" he looks. The two-time NFL MVP was playing some fantastic ball before the unfortunate ankle injury, and it's worth mentioning he's 7-2 in his career against Joe Burrow .
I was high on the Bengals entering this season, and I'm not ready to move off that take. I think this Baltimore secondary is in for a tough test in stopping Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins . The former averages 120.4 receiving yards per game vs. the Ravens, while the latter caught two touchdowns the last time he faced them. Higgins actually hasn't faced Baltimore since Oct. 6, 2024!  It's been a while. Give me the upset here. We aren't 100% sure if Jackson is even returning to the lineup, and he'll have to face one of the best interior pass rushes in the NFL. Dexter Lawrence , Jonathan Allen and Kris Jenkins Jr. are the only defensive tackle trio to record multiple sacks this season. … Prediction: Bengals 29, Ravens 27
Dubin (Ravens -3): I'm assuming that Lamar Jackson is back for this game. If he's not, then you can switch my pick to the Bengals. If Jackson is in alongside Derrick Henry and Zay Flowers , I just don't think this Baltimore offense can be stopped. When those three have shared the field this season, the Ravens are averaging 9.9 yards per play. NINE POINT NINE. Unfortunately, the sample size is only 63 plays due to injuries to Jackson and Flowers at different times. If there is any team that can compete with an explosive offense, it's probably the Bengals, but I don't see them quite keeping up here. … Prediction: Ravens 30, Bengals 26
Dajani ( Lions -3): Just take the Over in this matchup. The Lions really burned me coming off the bye last year, losing to J.J. McCarthy , but I'm going to back them in this spot. The concern is, of course, the defense, which ranks dead last in the NFL with 404.4 total yards surrendered per game. HOWEVER, I will mention that Kelvin Sheppard 's unit forced five straight three-and-outs from the Cardinals in that 45-21 win in Week 5. Plus, Brian Branch is set to return to the lineup as well. Give me the Lions at home.  … Prediction: Lions 35, Packers 30
Dubin (Lions -3): This one has all the makings of a shootout, with two explosive offenses going back and forth. Jared Goff and Co. are coming off the bye, and they have scored 31 or more points in four of their five games to date — and they scored 26 while piling up 452 yards in the other one. Nobody except maybe Kenneth Walker III is doing it at a higher level than Jahmyr Gibbs right now, either. Meanwhile, Green Bay can throw the ball all over…
author: Jordan Dajani

title: Super Bowl stock report for Week 7: Caleb Williams puts Bears back in contention, Rams devolve into disaster
summary: We assess the NFL title race after Week 6 and identify three upcoming games that could reshape the Super Bowl picture
full_text:
There might not be a better encapsulation of the topsy-turvy nature of the NFL than the fact that the Los Angeles Rams own two fewer wins than a Cleveland Browns squad most expected to be in contention for the top pick in the 2027 draft. The Rams are an utter disappointment through six games and will fall well short of delivering on their title of preseason Super Bowl favorites if they do not turn their season around in the next few weeks.
With the Rams out of the top tier of contenders for now, the door is open for someone else to take command of the championship race. Perhaps the Chicago Bears can be that team now that Caleb Williams is healthy and is back to leading a seemingly uncontainable offense.
The season is a month and a half old, so early-season noise is beginning to clear up. The real Super Bowl threats are emerging from the rest.
Here is how the championship race shapes up heading into Week 7.
Odds via DraftKings , +2000 or better
Going 2-1 without Caleb Williams manning the offense was crucial for the Bears. Avoiding a dreaded early-season slump kept all of their goals intact and left them primed to compete at the top of the crowded NFC North upon his return. The Week 5 drubbing against the rival Green Bay Packers amplified the need for Williams to get back into the lineup, though, and he delivered an emphatic response to that embarrassing loss upon his reinsertion into the offense with a monster individual performance in a 31-23 win on the road over the Atlanta Falcons .
It was the Bears' highest-scoring game since Week 1, which showed just how much Williams elevates this team. He completed his first 12 passes against a Falcons defense that has been surprisingly competitive this season en route to the sixth 300-yard effort of his career. His +12.4% completion percentage over expected was his second-best mark to date, and the 83.3% total completion rate was both a career high and the best by any Bears quarterback with at least 30 pass attempts in franchise history. The hamstring seems just fine.
This looks like a breakout season in the making for Williams. All he needs to do is stay on the field. So long as he is available, Chicago seems likely to boast a top-tier offense.
The season-opening loss in Australia was chalked up as a travel-related fluke. The defeat in Denver was a hard-fought battle between two playoff hopefuls. The shootout loss to the Buffalo Bills was a high-variance game against perhaps the best team in the NFL. At face value, each of those results was understandable. Frustrating, yes. But understandable. Then came the stunner in Week 6. Dropping a home game to the Arizona Cardinals completely recontextualized all of the previous losses. If the Rams are capable of losing to that kind of team, then maybe they just are not that good after all.
The most concerning part of this 2-4 start is that there are more reasons for worry than there is room for optimism. Sure, the schedule ahead is far more manageable than what the Rams faced in the season's first month and a half. But dropping a game to the Cardinals means that Sean McVay's crew is capable of losing to practically anyone else it sees during the softer part of its slate. The injury situation makes it all the more likely that the Rams suffer another devastating loss, too, because without Davante Adams , Poona Ford and Kobie Turner (who all landed on injured reserve this week), the floor just got a whole lot lower.
Special teams remains a complete disaster; the defense is solid, but clearly misses Myles Garrett, and Matthew Stafford's decline from his 2025 MVP form handicaps the offense. The Rams need to stack wins in the next four weeks against the Las Vegas Raiders , Los Angeles Chargers , Washington Commanders and Cardinals in order to dig themselves out of last place in the NFC West. If they do not, they might legitimately be in danger of missing the postseason entirely.
The Super Bowl is quite clearly a stretch for the Browns, but should they really hold the sixth-longest odds to win it? They are far more likely to reach the playoffs than some of the other teams in this range, considering they lead the AFC North through six weeks (for the first time since 2014, no less). That 2014 squad ended up at 7-9 and finished last in the division, so if history is any indication, then it makes sense as to why the market is still so low on this team. But at the same time, there are reasons to believe their 4-2 start is for real.
For one, they continue to play excellent defense in the post-Myles Garrett era. Cleveland ranks in a tie for seventh in points allowed per game with second-year star Carson Schwesinger leading the charge. And on the other side of the ball, Deshaun Watson remains above water while his rookie wide receiver tandem of Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion has the makings of a long-term dynamic duo. In his first year as coach, Todd Monken keeps getting the most out of all those pieces and more.
The "Who have they beaten?" argument is fair given the lack of elite opponents and Lamar Jackson's absence for the Baltimore Ravens last week, but three of the four victories came against teams with winning records. The Browns can only play the teams on their schedule, and there are not many daunting challenges on the road ahead, so the wins might just keep piling up. The playoffs are within reach if this train keeps rolling at its current pace.
Sunday, 8:20 p.m., NBC, stream on Fubo
When the Seattle Seahawks line up across from the Kansas City Chiefs on "Sunday Night Football," will they be wishing Kenneth Walker III was still on their side instead of the other? These teams are trending in opposite directions, and their trajectory changes coincide exactly with the Seahawks declining to re-sign Walker and instead watching him land in Kansas City. Zach Charbonnet could make his season debut for Seattle this week, which ought to be a boon to an offense that desperately needs an infusion of rushing ability.
Sunday, 1 p.m., CBS, stream on Paramount+
If Lamar Jackson cannot play with his ankle injury, the Ravens will be in danger of dropping their second consecutive divisional game. This is a prime opportunity for the Cincinnati Bengals to leap past their rivals, especially since they had an extra week to prepare. Every game is critical in a division where three teams stand at 4-2 and the Bengals are only a half game back of the logjam at 3-2.
Thursday, 8:15 p.m., Prime Video
Week 7 opens with a gem. Williams vs. Drake Maye is a spectacular showdown between two elite young quarterbacks who are presently playing their best football of the season. This intra-conference clash provides an excellent opportunity for a couple of Super Bowl hopefuls to see where they stack up against playoff-caliber competition. Chicago might hold an edge due to the injuries on New England's offensive line and at wide receiver, but Maye is back in the kind of form that could be good enough to will the Patriots to a few touchdowns regardless of his supporting cast. The Patriots scored at least 26 points in each of their last three games and likely need to keep that streak alive to keep up with Ben Johnson's high-octane unit.
author: Carter Bahns

title: NFL Week 7 upset alert: Can Giants upset Texans with JJ McCarthy at QB? Can Falcons beat 49ers?
summary: Baltimore and Denver are two other teams firmly at risk of being upset
full_text:
The NFL is funny sometimes. Just when you think you have everything pegged, the league will rip the carpet right out from under you before you even realize it. On a week-to-week basis, any team appears capable of winning, no matter how bleak things may seem from the outside looking in.
Take the Cardinals-Rams games for instance. Los Angeles was dubbed a superteam coming into 2026 and the prohibitive favorite to win the Super Bowl . All the while, Arizona was pinpointed as one of the worst teams in the league and possibly earmarked for the No. 1 overall pick. What happened on Sunday? The Cardinals rolled into SoFi Stadium and handed us arguably the biggest upset of the season. The only thing that stung about Arizona's stunning victory was that we didn't highlight it in last week's post. I had the Cardinals coverering in my weekly picks column , but that was thinking more along the lines of hitting the backdoor cover late.
While we weren't able to sniff out that upset, we did put you on to the Texans taking down the Jaguars in London and the Tennessee Titans taking down the Colts in Indy in last week's piece. We nearly had the Bucs as we win as well, but they couldn't outlast the Steelers in overtime.
That's enough looking back at Week 6. Now, it's time to set our sights on Week 7 and identify a handful of favorites that are officially on upset alert.
All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET
The Rams are reeling. Not only are they 2-4 to begin the season and in last place in the NFC West, but the injury bug is starting to take massive bites out of the roster. Following the loss to Arizona, head coach Sean McVay announced that star receiver Davante Adams ruptured his hamstring and is out for 6 to 10 weeks. On top of that, newly signed kicker Blake Grupe tore his ACL and is out for the year, as is defensive tackle Poona Ford (ruptured triceps). Fellow defensive tackle Kobie Turner is also going to miss at least a month with a groin injury. And that's not even mentioning Myles Garrett (knee), who is still sidelined. That is a lot of bodies piling up for the Rams, which -- as we started to see last week -- makes them vulnerable to just about any club.
That includes a Raiders team that is currently looking to stop a three-game losing skid after beginning the year 3-0. While they've come back down to earth a bit, two of those losses ( Chiefs and Bills ) were by a field goal. Both of those games were played at Allegiant Stadium. Special teams issues have plagued the Rams this season, and they have the worst special teams EPA in the NFL. It's mistakes on that side of the ball that create a perfect concoction for an upset. Moreover, Matthew Stafford hasn't looked like the MVP version of himself from a year ago, ranking 16th in EPA per dropback and 13th in pass success rate. He could be further thrown off his axis when squaring up against Maxx Crosby , who has the second-most pressures (35) in the NFL this season.
Welcome to the J.J. McCarthy era in New York. I'm genuinely curious to see how this goes for the former Vikings first-round pick, who made his debut last week in the fourth quarter. In that brief showing, McCarthy largely played well, throwing for 243 yards, a touchdown, and an interception. Does this give the Giants a boost? McCarthy will have weapons at his disposal in Malik Nabers and Isaiah Likely , and it's possible his rushing ability ignites what has been a lackluster ground attack thus far. Meanwhile, these aren't exactly last year's Texans when it comes to the defense. Coming into Week 7, Houston ranks 20th in scoring defense (23.8). They're also forcing teams to go three-and-out just 14.1% of the time, the third-lowest rate in the NFL. Conversely, the Giants are allowing the fifth-fewest passing yards per game (190.2) in the NFL this season, so maybe they cool off C.J. Stroud .
It's important to note that the Texans will also have a slight rest disadvantage here. While they may be home, Houston is fresh off a game in London last Sunday, which could be a factor in this contest. For what it's worth, the Giants are 4-0 (ATS and SU) in their last four games against Houston.
At some point, the injuries to San Francisco's wide receiver room have to matter, right? When Mike Evans (Achilles) didn't return for the second half of Monday's matchup against the Commanders , the Niners offense mustered a field goal on the opening possession of the third quarter and then punted three straight times (all three-and-outs) to end the game. With the Week 8 bye right in front of them and San Francisco playing on a short week and on the road, it may behoove them to keep Evans sidelined for this game, with hopes of a two-week break being the remedy for the stretch run. If that turns out to be the case, we got a quick sample of an Evans-less offense for the 49ers , and it wasn't the prettiest.
When Evans is on the field, the 49ers have 0.29 EPA per play compared to a -0.03 EPA per play without him. Translation: That's going from the best offense in the NFL to the 16th-ranked offense in the NFL. That brings San Francisco down much closer to Atlanta's level and makes them a live home dog.
It's borderline irresponsible to back the Broncos right now because their offense is totally lost. Bo Nix is averaging just 4.9 air yards per attempt this season, which is the fewest through six games by any player in the last 20 seasons. They won last week in spite of his performance and the defense taking advantage of some questionable throws by Sam Darnold . Now, they head out on the road to face a Cardinals team that has been pesky this season. Most recently, they held Matthew Stafford and the Rams offense to 16 points in a road win. If that's the kind of defensive effort Arizona is going to bring, why should we think the Nix-led Denver offense will fare any better than L.A. from what we've seen out of them through six weeks? I have confidence in Jacoby Brissett , Trey McBride , and the rest of the Arizona offense to get in the low-to-mid-20s on Sunday, which should be enough against Denver.
Seattle will have the home-field and rest advantage over Kansas City after playing last Thursday. However, do you want to know where the Chiefs have the advantage? Quarterback. Sam Darnold was actively putting Seattle behind the eight ball last week in their loss to the Broncos, throwing two interceptions on the final three drives of the game. Turnovers have been a problem for Darnold so far this season, and his 1.4 interceptions-per-game average is the most among players with at least four starts this season. If that persists in this matchup, you're giving Mahomes and old buddy Kenneth Walker III short fields that they'll almost certainly take advantage of to stay undefeated this season. Kansas City is 24-5 in interconference games since 2020 (best in the NFL) and is 8-2 in its past 10 Sunday night road games.

title: AFC North Week 5 recap: Browns knock Ravens off their perch
summary: The Ravens lost their spot at the top of the division after falling to the Browns in Week 5, while the Steelers pulled off a comeback win, and the Bengals enjoyed a bye week. Cleveland Browns (4-2) Cleveland now sits atop the AFC North after defeating Baltimore, 13-10. The Browns’ offense struggled to get anything […]
full_text: CLEVELAND, OHIO - OCTOBER 18: Andre Szmyt #25 of the Cleveland Browns celebrates with Ronnie Hickman Jr. #33 after kicking the game winning field goal to defeat the Baltimore Ravens in the game at Huntington Bank Field on October 18, 2026 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Gregory Shamus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Ravens lost their spot at the top of the division after falling to the Browns in Week 5, while the Steelers pulled off a comeback win, and the Bengals enjoyed a bye week. Cleveland Browns (4-2) Cleveland now sits atop the AFC North after defeating Baltimore, 13-10. The Browns’ offense struggled to get anything going for most of the game. Cleveland’s lone touchdown of the day came from Austin Estime after a fourth-quarter fumble recovery set the offense up at the 35-yard line. Deshaun Watson struggled heavily against the Ravens’ defense, going 16 of 26 for 164 yards while being sacked five times. Jerry Jeudy was the most productive of the Browns’ wide receivers, catching four passes for 69 yards, including a 33-yard reception to get the offense in range for the game-winning field goal. Jaleel McLaughlin led a banged-up backfield with nine carries and 41 of the team’s 93 rushing yards. Cleveland’s defense rebounded in a big way after allowing 10 points on Baltimore’s first two drives. The Ravens’ offense, led by backup quarterback Tyler Huntley, struggled to move the ball for the remainder of the game while Derrick Henry was effectively neutralized on the ground, even without Browns star defensive tackle Mason Graham in the lineup. Reigning Defensive Rookie of the Year Carson Schwesinger, who was questionable with an ankle injury, led his team with 13 total tackles and forced the critical fumble on Henry in the fourth quarter. Quincy Williams, Isaiah McGuire, and Maliek Collins accounted for the Browns’ three sacks on Huntley. Andre Szmyt missed his first field goal of the season while making two others, including the game-winner on the final drive of the game. Pittsburgh Steelers (4-2) Pittsburgh rallied from a 13-0 deficit to beat the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in overtime, 26-19. The Steelers scored just three points in the first half before ripping off 23 in the final two quarters and overtime. Aaron Rodgers’s two passing touchdowns brought him to 539 in his career, tying Peyton Manning for the third-most in NFL history. The 42-year-old completed 33 of his 49 passing attempts on the game for 253 yards and an interception to go along with his pair of scores. Jaylen Warren led the ground attack with 50 yards on 14 rushes, while a returning Rico Dowdle chipped in 40 yards on seven carries. D.K. Metcalf led all receivers with 93 yards on 11 catches, trailed closely by rookie Germie Bernard’s 87 yards and a touchdown on 11 receptions. Tight end Darnell Washington also had a touchdown catch to go with 25 yards on four catches. The Steelers’ defense feasted against backup quarterback Jalon Daniels. Jalen Ramsey and Nick Herbig each had two sacks and Yahya Black had one, while Jamel Dean and Daylen Everette each came away with an interception. Payton led the defense with 11 tackles, bringing him up to 55 on the season, the eighth-most in the league. Chris Boswell finished 4 for 5 on field goals, bringing his number of missed kicks up to four for the season and putting him on pace for a career-high. Baltimore Ravens (4-2) Baltimore lost the division lead with a 13-10 loss in Cleveland. Lamar Jackson’s second straight absence from the offense was glaring as Huntley struggled for much of the day, finishing 19 of 31 for 165 yards and a touchdown. Zay Flowers was the leading receiver with 66 yards on six catches, while rookie Josh Cuevas caught Baltimore’s only touchdown. Derrick Henry failed to get going on the ground after a strong start, rushing 17 times for just 58 yards with a costly fumble that led to Cleveland’s only touchdown. Rookie Ja’Kobi Lane impressed in his return to action after suffering a wrist injury in the season opener, converting first downs on all four of his catches for a total of 40 yards. Baltimore’s defense was suffocating for much of the game. The pass rush was effective against Deshaun Watson, sacking him five times. Trey Hendrickson logged his second sack as a Raven after a two-game absence due to finger surgery; Nnamdi Madubike, Roquan Smith, Tavius Robinson, and Calais Campbell all got to Watson as well. As usual, though, cracks began to form where they always do: on third down, in the fourth quarter. Jerry Jeudy’s 33-yard catch moved Cleveland into field goal range for Andre Szmyt’s game-winner. That also set up a contrast with Ravens kicker Tyler Loop, who renewing discussions about his job security by missing his third field goal of the season in a game decided by three points. Cincinnati Bengals (3-2) The Bengals rested up during their early bye week and will look to join the AFC North’s four-win club on Sunday in Baltimore.

full_text: Sep 27, 2026; Rio De Janeiro, BRA; Baltimore Ravens head coach Jesse Minter looks on during the game against the Dallas Cowboys at Maracana Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Ravens fans and fans across the country. The Baltimore Ravens are 4-2 through the first third of Jesse Minter’s first season as head coach. He and Anthony Weaver have delivered a top-15 defense to start the year, while Declan Doyle’s offense is firmly among the best in the league. This week, Baltimore Beatdown wants to know how you would grade Minter and his staff in their first six games. Answer the survey below and share your additional thoughts in the comments! Nikhil’s grade: B Injuries are an unfortunate but excellent way to test a new coaching staff early in their tenure. Minter and Co. have not been able to meet the sky-high preseason expectations with just one multi-possession win, but they deserve credit for winning close games through a slew of injuries. It is very possible that the Ravens are 2-4 right now if not for the staff’s ability to keep the team on the rails down the stretch. There is still plenty of room to go. Minter has publicly taken the defense’s third-down struggles on his shoulders, and the unit as a whole is still not playing up to their talent. Doyle is still searching for the right levers to pull in short-yardage situations, but injuries have also impacted him the most. His offense could finally take full flight with Lamar Jackson back on the field and taking snaps from a true center in Cam Jurgens. To be frank, Anthony Levine’s special teams units have hurt more than they have helped. Continued struggles from Tyler Loop could test the staff’s commitment to the second-year kicker, especially with Jake Moody back on the practice squad. The Ravens’ margins have gotten very tight with a competitive AFC North and a tough rest-of-season schedule, so they cannot afford to lose multiple games due to special teams. Now, it’s your turn. Cox/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Baltimore Ravens are dealing with a laundry list of injuries entering Week 7, but Wednesday’s injury report included positive updates on several key players. Chief among them was quarterback Lamar Jackson’s return to practice after a two-week absence due to an ankle injury. Head coach Jesse Minter twice used the word “preparation” when referring to Jackson’s participation, which was officially categorized as limited, and the two-time MVP was not in uniform when leaving the field. Taken together, those signs suggest that he is preparing to play but is not physically ready. Minter maintained his previous stance that the team was taking Jackson’s injury “day by day.” Jackson’s preparation could have included taking snaps from Cam Jurgens as the two work to develop their chemistry and communication at the line of scrimmage. Wednesday was their first shared practice since the former Eagles center arrived in Baltimore via trade two weeks ago, as well as his first day of full participation with his new team. Jurgens spoke to reporters after practice, an excellent sign towards his availability for his Ravens debut on Sunday against the Bengals. The Ravens listed 13 other players on their first injury report of Week 7. Here is the full list ( * denotes new injury): Full participation TE Mark Andrews (full) OLB Trey Hendrickson (finger) C Cam Jurgens (concussion) Limited participation WR Rashod Bateman (shoulder) S Jaylinn Hawkins (knee) * TE Matthew Hibner (hand) G/C Vega Ioane (ankle) * LG John Simpson (groin) LT Ronnie Stanley (non-injury related/rest, toe, ankle) CB T.J. Tampa Jr. (knee, designated to return from injured reserve) RG Andrew Vorhees (foot) DT Broderick Washington (ankle) Did not participate DL Calais Campbell (non-injury related/rest) OLB Tavius Robinson (pectoral) Robinson’s injury is by far the most alarming. He leads the defense with 3.5 sacks and has been a crucial run-stopper off the edge. An absence would elevate undrafted rookie Ethan Burke into a larger role; he had two pressures in three pass-rushing snaps on Sunday in Cleveland. The Bengals are coming into their trip to Baltimore much healthier after their bye week. Cincinnati reported just one injury on Wednesday: safety Kyle Dugger, who was limited with a quad injury. title: James Cook has improved efficiency from rushing title season, even against heavier boxes
summary: Believe it or not, James Cook has had a better start to 2026 than a season ago when he led the NFL in rushing yards. And he’s done it despite defenses placing a relatively high priority on stopping him. Through six games in 2025, the Buffalo Bills feature back had rushed for 537 yards at […]
full_text: Believe it or not, James Cook has had a better start to 2026 than a season ago when he led the NFL in rushing yards. And he’s done it despite defenses placing a relatively high priority on stopping him. Through six games in 2025, the Buffalo Bills feature back had rushed for 537 yards at a 5.0 yards-per-carry clip. Through six games this season, Cook has 627 yards on the ground at a 5.4 yards-per-carry clip. At this point of the season last year, Cook had seen 89.7% of his runs against seven or more defenders in the box. On those runs, he averaged 5.08 yards per tote and had a 10-plus yard run rate of 12.4%. This season, the percentage of Cook runs with seven-plus box defenders is up to 92.3%. He’s averaged 5.34 yards per carry on those runs with a 10-plus yard run rate of 21.9%. My word. Beyond his incredible efficiency improvement from the high bar set in 2025, Cook has also been excellent this season against seven or more defenders in the box relative to his running back contemporaries. Through Week 6, there’ve been 38 running backs who’ve carried the football 40 or more times against seven or more defenders in the box. Here’s where Cook ranks in many rushing categories in those scenarios: 108 carries (2nd) 577 rushing yards (2nd) 5.34 yards per carry (3rd) 21.9% explosive run rate (1st) 55.6% success rate – 6th He is 30th in yards after contact per rush in those scenarios at 1.82 yards. But that’s never been Cook’s speciality. His subtle cutting skills, flexibility, and breakaway speed are how he wins, although he has added more power and wherewithal through contact as he’s developed in Buffalo. And I cannot finish this article before a noticeable hat tip to the Bills offensive line. Against seven or more box defenders, Cook’s 3.52 yards before contact is far and away the highest average in the league. The running back’s own elusiveness is a factor there too. There’s plenty of football left this season. But right now, after winning the rushing title a year ago, Cook has actually gotten more efficient toting the rock. And he’s been among the league’s best even when the opposing defense is making a concerted effort to stop him by not providing him light boxes. Stats courtesy of Fantasy Points Data*

Therefore let’s highlight Falcons safety Jessie Bates, a highly-productive, wily veteran ballhawk who now sits on a 2-4 Falcons club with quarterback issues. This article is the third n the trade-candidate series I plan to sprinkle onto the site until the actual trade deadline until November 10, which is 19 days from now, and lands after Week 9. Past installments in this series: Derwin James , Brian Thomas Jr. , Age: 29 For quite a while now, Bates has been one of the NFL’s premier play-making safeties. He’s third among active players in career interceptions with 27, and 2021 is the only season to date he has not reached at least three picks. At 6’1” and 210 pounds, Bates has quality size but is know for his rangy coverage, instincts, and plus ball skills. He was a second-team All-Pro in 2025, his third such distinction. The cherry on top — Bates has been a very reliable tackler for a long time. The 2024 campaign is the only year in which his missed tackle rate reached double digits, and it’s currently a rather low 8.3% entering Week 7. 2026 snap splits Free safety: 51.4% Box: 37.2% Slot corner: 10.7% Defensive line: 0.4% Bates is the consummate patrolling free safety. He’s played a seismic 95.7% of the Falcons defensive snaps through Week 6, alongside fellow 90-plus snap percentage safety Xavier Watts. Atlanta doesn’t have a myriad of up-and-coming safeties on the roster if the GM were to trade Bates, although Billy Bowman has flashed at times as the team’s nickel corner, and Sydney Brown was acquired via trade in March. Thus far in 2026, Bates has 31 tackles, one fumble recovery returned for a touchdown but no interceptions. How he’d fit with Bills Exquisitely. And I’ll keep this short, because Bates would be that spectacular of a fit. Cole Bishop is mostly used in the box and the slot. He’s better suited closer to the line of scrimmage than further away from it. CJ Gardner-Johnson has been average at best as a true free safety. The latter role is where Bates thrives. His stellar tackling ability would be a welcomed addition to Jim Leonhard’s defense too. However, like I mentioned in the James article, the Bills do have a pair of young, athletic safeties in Jalon Kilgore and Jordan Hancock I presume the coaching staff will eventually like to see more of after the bye week. That does complicate a potential Bates fit in Buffalo. Financial obligation for Bills to trade for him 2026 salary: $13M If the Bills trade for Bates after Week 9, they’d be on the hook for $6.51M in prorated 2026 base salary. He’s an impending free agent after this season, which simultaneously creates plenty of flexibility for the Bills if he were to be in their future plans and lowers his asking price. Projected cost to acquire Using Syndicate32.com’s trade machine , the projected cost to trade for Bates is an early Round 3 pick in 2027. That feels just right for a player of Bates’ caliber, at his age, and with his contract situation. Should the Bills trade for Jessie Bates? If the Bills are indeed interested in adding to their safety room via the trade market before the deadline, Bates should be at the top of their list. Convincing the Falcons to trade Bates would probably be the biggest hurdle here, because he’s a captain and playing almost 100% of the defensive snaps this season. I do believe presence of Watts, who appears to have a bright future safety in Atlanta, could help. Ultimately, the Falcons deciding to field trade calls regarding Bates probably hinge on the next few games against the 49ers, Buccaneers, and Bengals before the deadline. Bates is precisely the type coverage specialist free safety this defense could certainly use, there’s presently no 2027 financial commitment to him, and he’s been a consummate professional on and off the field for his entire career. With a projected asking price of a third-round pick (or even a second-rounder), if I was Brandon Beane and our staff deemed we’d make a trade-deadline play at safety, the first call I’d make would be to Falcons GM Ian Cunningham about Bates.

title: There’s more to the Sam Franklin Jr. spitting story than the suspension
summary: With all the chatter surrounding the surprise suspension of Buffalo Bills special teams ace Sam Franklin Jr. for spitting at Las Vegas Raiders tackle DJ Glaze, I saw a lot of speculation on the video and the lack of well… anything that it showed at all. “How can they suspend him with no evidence?” Or […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - OCTOBER 18: Sam Franklin Jr. #28 of the Buffalo Bills walks off the field during halftime in the game against the Las Vegas Raiders at Allegiant Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. The Bills defeated the Raiders 33-30. (Photo by Candice Ward/Getty Images) | Getty Images With all the chatter surrounding the surprise suspension of Buffalo Bills special teams ace Sam Franklin Jr. for spitting at Las Vegas Raiders tackle DJ Glaze, I saw a lot of speculation on the video and the lack of well… anything that it showed at all. “How can they suspend him with no evidence?” Or “Is it a he said, he said situation?” Well, it sounded like a fun way to merge my full-time job with my football work. I’m not in a glamorous field mind you, but as part of my career I am a trained investigator and have been involved with plenty of investigations over the years. This set off to be an explainer on civil investigatory process, but along the way I found out that there was actually quite a bit more to the issues between Sam Franklin and DJ Glaze than have been reported. Investigative process I have a massive disclaimer to start with. What follows is how things would play out if I were in charge of looking into LoogieGate. If the NFL has a competent system, they likely did something similar. That said, the NFL hasn’t always displayed the highest level of competence in these matters, so there’s no guarantee they’ve done any of this. Let’s begin! In the world of Skarekrow, due process is a real thing. With C.J. Gardner-Johnson, you had very direct video evidence of his infraction which makes the disqualification and punishment a pretty easy matter. With Sam Franklin Jr., the video is inconclusive which means we’d need to dig into the complaint in different ways. But you can rest assured, I would NEVER have issued a suspension without an investigation first. So let’s set the stage for how I would have done things. pic.twitter.com/8PJMWowADM — Kuebiko (@Kuebiko_Kami) October 22, 2026 Everything starts with the complaint. In this case it was likely something like “During the last extra point attempt, Sam Franklin spit on me.” We have a time stamp and a couple angles to work from which is where my video begins, checking the angles. They’re very much inconclusive, even with the ultra-slow motion. However, it is clear there was some fracas between the two meaning there’s definitely a chance of spitting. That means we need other evidence, and one of the most plentiful will be testimony. As you can see from the short video, it’s not remotely a “he said, he said” affair. More like a “he said, he said, he said, he said, he said, he said, he said, he said, he said…” well you get the idea. Due to Franklin engaging with Glaze you have a large group of people’s attention. The one pause shows everyone I think is reasonably looking to see what’s going on. The final pause shows how much people have gathered to see what’s going on. I would also add that people in hearing range might be useful to. This isn’t a complicated interview either. The suspension was issued on Wednesday, which meant Monday and Tuesday gave pleeeeenty of time to talk to people and look for more evidence (assuming the NFL did). Here’s an idea of the question list for something like this (remember that at this point there’s no indication of what occurred so witnesses are coming in cold): Tell me about what happened between Sam Franklin and DJ Glaze. What do you know about anything unusual going on between them? I was told something unsportsmanlike occurred between them, tell me everything about what you saw between them. Did Franklin do anything to Glaze? If so, what? Did Sam Franklin spit on DJ Glaze? Follow up questions as needed such as “How do you know that?” or “What did you see/hear?” and prompts to continue if needed such as “and then what happened?” or “and how did [person] respond?” Now comes the harder part, judging evidence for conclusions. The following is a real exercise I do with investigators to demonstrate weighing testimony and creating reports/conclusions with carying confidence levels. You obtain the following statements: Jane – “The sky is blue, the grass is green, and the flowers are red.” Suzy – “The sky is blue, the grass is green, and the flowers are purple.” Tom – “The sky is blue, the grass is orange, and the flowers are yellow.” This leads to the following conclusions: “The sky is blue” “The grass is likely green” “It cannot be determined what color the flowers are.” Now if you get the chance to go photograph the dang grass and flowers, you go do that but as we see with the video evidence in our spitting case you can’t always get that definitive view of the world and testimony and other evidence fragments are all you get. For civil matters, the word “likely” is significant as they’re generally held to a standard of “preponderance of the evidence” which is basically a fancier version of the idea of “likely.” Based on the evidence what’s the most probable thing that occurred. Not PROVEN, but probable. In the clip I have about 20 decent to great witnesses. I bet I can make a really good conclusion if I talk to everyone. In my examples above, Franklin could be found guilty with two of the three conclusions (the flowers being the “who the hell actually knows” result where the default should be innocent). I don’t have the authority to investigate fully though unless Roger Goodell reads this, likes the cut of my jib, and hires me on for a very lucrative contract that he should totally actually do. Since that hasn’t happened at the time of me writing this, I don’t actually know what everyone saw and heard so Sam Franklin’s guilt or innocence remains a question mark. That said, there is ONE more thing I would typically do before I speak to witnesses. And this thing I actually was able to do AND after I did it, I stumbled on some veeeeeery interesting facts. There’s more to the story than Franklin and his saliva There’s a really fun thing about testimonial evidence: It’s almost never perfect. One of the most toxic things in the universe in my opinion is the human inclination to automatically assume that a person giving incorrect information is lying. It’s not that people don’t lie, mind you. Generally speaking though it’s not as common as most people think and inaccuracies occur due to normal lapses in memory. I could give a dissertation on this subject, but I won’t today. Instead, here’s the short version and how it applies here. If the complaint came in as the “last” extra point of the game, you start there. That said, I wouldn’t personally immediately trust that it was the last one, especially after looking at the last one and not seeing anything definite. What if it happened on the SECOND to last extra point? Let’s face it, the circumstances between the two plays might be nearly identical. What if it was a field goal? That’s a pretty similar set of circumstances too. We don’t need to examine every play of the game. If Josh Allen is on the field, then Franklin and Glaze aren’t for instance. But Raiders kicking extra points or field goals could blur together. So I looked at those plays (Raiders extra points and field goals), starting with the last and moving backward in time based on the idea that the complainants recall of events being at the end of the game should be considered first. And you know what? I found out a lot more than I thought I would. I originally assumed all I’d do is be able to say I couldn’t confirm spitting on similar plays, and while that is accurate to what I found… Well let’s look. pic.twitter.com/QlvlXhHTMj — Kuebiko (@Kuebiko_Kami) October 22, 2026 On the kick before the one Franklin reportedly was spitting during (extra point in Q4), there’s not much to note. That’s exactly what I assumed I’d find. A handful of plays that didn’t tell me all that much. The field goal in Q3 was the same. Still, I needed to do my due diligence, right? The field…

full_text: The Buffalo Bills have won five of their first six games and sit in sole possession of first place in the AFC East. The team is firmly entrenched in the No. 2 seed in the AFC, trailing only the undefeated Kansas City Chiefs in the conference. But while the Bills are 5-1, all but one of their games has been of the one-score variety, mostly because their defense ranks towards the bottom in most of the major categories. And the defense is prone to allowing teams to hang around—the Bills are allowing 1.5 touchdowns per fourth quarter this year, the worst rate for any defense in any season going back to at least the 1977 campaign. Buffalo has needed Josh Allen and the offense to produce at a prolific rate. The offense is obliging, as the Bills lead the NFL in scoring offense (32.8 points per game) to make up for a defense that ranks 28th in points allowed and 31st in yards and first downs allowed. title: Panthers vs Buccaneers: Storylines to watch
summary: The Carolina Panthers currently lead the NFC South, and while every storyteller in the media is talking about them being kings of the division, there are still many important games to play, and this is one of them. While the Bucs have felt the bite of injuries, they are currently only two and games back […]
full_text: TAMPA, FLORIDA - JANUARY 03: Chuba Hubbard #30 of the Carolina Panthers is tackled by Lavonte David #54 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers during the third quarter during a game at Raymond James Stadium on January 03, 2026 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Mike Ehrmann/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Carolina Panthers currently lead the NFC South, and while every storyteller in the media is talking about them being kings of the division, there are still many important games to play, and this is one of them. While the Bucs have felt the bite of injuries, they are currently only two and games back from being tied for the lead in wins. All it takes is for one slate of games to go their way for them to be competing deep into the end of the season. The Panthers are playing good football, and they have to keep it going. Let’s dive right into the storylines for this week’s game. Offense: Bryce Young needs to keep up the passing party The Panthers have one of the best passing offenses from basically every yardage category. And while Chuba Hubbard has also been extremely productive leading the rushing attack all season, he’ll be facing one of the better rushing defenses in football. Per Teamrankings.com , their rushing defense ranks as 2nd in yards per rush, 3 in rushes per game, 2 in rush yards per game, and 2 in rushing TDs per game. While you might think this is a result of simply being a bad football team this year, every loss they’ve had ended up being one score games. Teams tend to run the football more when games are close, but they’ve been very productive. I would expect the Panthers to have a bit more trouble running the football this week, even if they are playing their second straight backup quarterback on the other side of the ball. Their passing defense is much more susceptible, so Bryce Young and OC Brad Idzik should resume the aggressiveness in the air, but if the rushing attack isn’t playing the complimentary football that Dave Canales always preaches about, their could be a lot more pressure for Bryce to continue this unreal campaign. Defense: Pass rush will need to get creative again Dave Canales announced this week that EDGE Jaelan Phillips is set to miss this week. That leaves an already banged up group of edge rushers down their best man. And while Phillips is obviously a big part of getting pressure on the quarterback as a rusher, he’s equally more important in collapsing the pocket and setting up other pass rushers with good matchups they can win. I’ve been very impressed with 2025 rookie Princely Umanmielen, but what made the biggest difference in this past game in Philadelphia was an extremely aggressive blitzing game plan by DC Ejiro Evero. And he’ll likely have to do that again, dialing up guys like Devin Lloyd an Bobby Okereke from the linebacking spots and sending their multi-talented group of safeties on blitzes. Bonus storyline: Get a grip on the darn penalties! The Panthers were called for a franchise record 149 yards of penalties against the Eagles, which luckily didn’t cause them to lose the game. Penalties have been a massive issue with this team all season, and they can’t get away with this and not have it come back to bite them. Whether they are playing Jalon Daniels or a beat up Baker Mayfield this week, it could and should be a very close game based on how the Bucs schedule has gone. A poorly timed penalty could very much tip the scales out of their favor in what could be an ugly contest. What are you watching for this week, Panthers fans?

title: Panthers vs Buccaneers: Matchups to watch
summary: The Carolina Panthers are coming off a comfortable win over the Philadelphia Eagles and their backup quarterback. That makes them 2-0 against backup quarterbacks so far in this young season. Up next is the Tamp Bay Buccaneers and either another backup quarterback or their starter fresh off a dislocated throwing thumb. The Bucs have had […]
full_text: CHARLOTTE, NORTH CAROLINA - DECEMBER 21: Bryce Young #9 of the Carolina Panthers looks to pass while being hit by Sirvocea Dennis #8 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in the first quarter of a game at Bank of America Stadium on December 21, 2025 in Charlotte, North Carolina. (Photo by David Jensen/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Carolina Panthers are coming off a comfortable win over the Philadelphia Eagles and their backup quarterback. That makes them 2-0 against backup quarterbacks so far in this young season. Up next is the Tamp Bay Buccaneers and either another backup quarterback or their starter fresh off a dislocated throwing thumb. The Bucs have had a season from hell so far. They carried the negative momentum they ended last season with into this season. They got a random Thursday night win over the Cowboys with Jalon Daniels leading the charge. Otherwise, it’s been bad. They’re 1-5 and desperate for a win, or really anything to go right for them. Meanwhile, the Panthers are riding high on a two game winning streak against teams that were at least supposed to be good in the Lions and Eagles. They’ll be trying to extend their division lead. Here are the key matchups that will determine if that will happen. Panthers interior offensive line vs Vita Vea Vea doesn’t have a sack yet this season, and he’s only been credited with four tackles, but that doesn’t mean he’s no longer a factor along the defensive line. He’s not quite the player he used to be, but he’s still dangerous. He’s 15th in ESPN’s pass rush win rate for defensive tackles despite being double teamed on 81% of his pass rushing snaps. Robert Hunt has struggled this year, Damien Lewis is playing through his elbow injury, and Luke Fortner is Luke Fortner. They’re going to have their hands full with Vea, and they need to keep him contained so he doesn’t kill Bryce Young. Bryce Young vs Alex Anzalone The Buccaneers gave Anzalone a decent amount of money to step in for the retired Lavonte David as both the team’s defensive leader and coverage presence in the middle of the field. He has not lived up to the second part of that. He’s currently ranked dead last by Pro Football Focus among 75 linebackers that qualify. He’s been a huge liability in coverage and seems to have lost multiple steps in his age 32 season. The Panthers have found success in the middle of the field, particularly on RPO throws to Tetairoa McMillan and Jalen Coker. Given Anzalone’s struggles this year, those short passes in the middle of the field can turn into big chunk plays if the Panthers can continue to execute them with the same success they’ve had so far this year. Bobby Okereke and Devin Lloyd vs Bucky Irving Irving has been just about the only skill position player to have any sort of success for the Bucs this season. He’s averaging 4.7 yards per carry this season and showed how explosive he could be with 165 yards against the Cowboys while looking like vintage LeSean McCoy. If he gets into space, he’s one of the more slippery backs in the league. It’ll be on the Panthers linebackers to clog up his running lanes and prevent him from breaking into space where he can slip tackles and rip off long runs. Baker Mayfield vs his thumb Todd Bowles announced that Baker Mayfield will return to practice this week with eyes on returning to game action against the Panthers this weekend. We’re right at the beginning of Mayfield’s projected recovery timeline, so making it back for this game would be very aggressive. But like I said at the top, the Bucs are desperate, and that might lead them to go back to Baker, even if it’s a risky play. If Mayfield does play, you’d have to assume there will be some degradation in how well he can grip the ball. That gives the Panthers defense some extra opportunities to hunt turnovers, whether it be airmailed passes or strip sacks.

title: Carolina Panthers 2027 NFL Draft Prospect Profile: Greg Johnson
summary: The 2027 NFL Draft feels like forever away, and we’re all caught up in the start of the NFL season. Regardless, it’s never too early to look ahead to the Draft. This weekly series will take a closer look at some of the prospects the Carolina Panthers could select in the 2027 iteration of the […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WA - SEPTEMBER 26: Greg Johnson #65 of the Minnesota Golden Gophers looks on during a game between the Minnesota Golden Gophers and Washington Huskies on September 26, 2026 at Husky Stadium in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Henry Rodenburg/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The 2027 NFL Draft feels like forever away, and we’re all caught up in the start of the NFL season. Regardless, it’s never too early to look ahead to the Draft. This weekly series will take a closer look at some of the prospects the Carolina Panthers could select in the 2027 iteration of the Draft. In this series, we’ll only be looking at prospects the Panthers could seriously consider. This week our profile will focus on Minnesota Golden Gophers interior offensive lineman Greg Johnson. Bio Johnson (6’6”, 325 lbs.) has been a jack-of-all-trades lineman for the Gophers since arriving on campus. He started at left guard as a true freshman before becoming the starting center during his sophomore campaign. He moved back to guard last season and even played some snaps at both tackle spots when needed. Johnson was slated to stick at guard this season, but injuries have forced him back to the center spot. His versatility and effectiveness across the line earned him an Honorable Mention All-Big Ten nod last year. Strengths/Weaknesses Johnson has elite size for an interior lineman. He’s tall and long, giving him a rather sizable reach advantage against most opponents. He’s an incredibly smart player, able to fill in admirably at all five positions on the offensive line and his tape inside and outside are both impressive. According to PFF, Johnson has allowed only one pressure this season in 202 opportunities, earning a quality 80.3 overall grade so far. Johnson’s durability is also a major positive as he has yet to miss any time in college due to injury. This is especially impressive given how often his cohorts on Minnesota’s line have succumb to various ailments. Johnson’s size, weight, and strength should profile much better than they do in the run game. He has a good run blocking grade from PFF this year (81.1), which shows some improvement in one of the areas of concern. Continuing to show this improvement will be a major boon to his draft stock. Another potential issue is his lack of a home on the offensive line making him a master-of-none type of player. Projection Greg Johnson is an incredibly versatile and effective lineman that every NFL team covets at least as a depth piece. His improvement in the run game has helped elevate him as high as the middle of the first round on most mock drafts, consistently being taken on day one of the Draft. He could immediately slot in anywhere on the interior and/or be a swing tackle off the bench. For a team like the Panthers, the fit makes sense. Robert Hunt could be a cap casualty, and current do-it-all lineman Brady Christensen can’t stay healthy. Unless they want more Toricelli Simpkins III tape, the Panthers might invest a high pick on someone like Johnson. Johnson could even slot in as the starting center if Sam Hecht doesn’t take firm control of the position as the season moves on. As Taylor Moton and Damien Lewis begin to age out of the league, Johnson will be hitting his prime and could take the mantle as leader of the offensive line. What do you think, Panthers fans? If Greg Johnson is available when the Panthers select in the 2027 NFL Draft, should they take him? Sound off in the comments!

title: Bears v Patriots – Bears prevail with a statement win
summary: Forty years after Super Bowl XX, the Bears and Patriots meet again under the lights at Soldier Field—this time on Thursday Night Football, with both clubs sitting at 4-2 and fighting for early-season positioning in their divisions. The night carries extra weight for Chicago: the franchise is honoring Mike Ditka, the iconic coach of that […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - OCTOBER 22: Caleb Williams #18 of the Chicago Bears throws a pass against the New England Patriots during the first quarter of the game at Soldier Field on October 22, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) | Getty Images Forty years after Super Bowl XX, the Bears and Patriots meet again under the lights at Soldier Field—this time on Thursday Night Football, with both clubs sitting at 4-2 and fighting for early-season positioning in their divisions. The night carries extra weight for Chicago: the franchise is honoring Mike Ditka, the iconic coach of that 1985 championship team, who passed away less than two weeks ago, with handout mustaches to attending fans. On the field, it’s a high-profile collision of the top two quarterbacks from the 2024 draft—Caleb Williams, the No. 1 overall pick now operating in Ben Johnson’s system after a recent return from injury, and Drake Maye, the No. 3 pick who has helped New England string together three straight wins after a shaky start. Both defenses entered the night ranked among the league’s best in scoring and against the run, setting up a physical, low-margin matchup. Instead, the first half delivered explosive plays, a critical end-zone interception, and a last-second touchdown that kept the Patriots within striking distance heading into the locker room. First Quarter: Bears Jump Ahead, 10-0 New England’s opening drive stalled when Kyler Gordon sacked Drake Maye on fourth down, giving Chicago good field position. Cairo Santos cashed in with a 43-yard field goal for a 3-0 lead. The Bears’ offense then hit a coverage breakdown. Luther Burden III took a short throw and raced 58 yards into the red zone. One play later, D’Andre Swift finished it with a 4-yard touchdown run. Santos’ extra point made it 10-0 with under two minutes left in the quarter. Gooch Observation: Chicago’s early efficiency and Burden’s explosiveness set the tone. The Patriots’ offense looked stuck, and the Bears’ run defense (and Gordon’s pressure) limited New England early. Gooch Hot take: Burden looked like the best player on the field in the opening 15 minutes. The 58-yarder wasn’t just a big play—it exposed a Patriots secondary that got caught flat-footed. Also, I hate to say it, but this defense just looks faster with TJ Edwards and some of the older defensive players on the sidelines. Second Quarter: Maye Answers, Burden Punches Back, Stevenson Crashes the Party New England finally found rhythm. A 9-play, 74-yard drive ended with Drake Maye stretching across the goal line on a 7-yard scramble. The officials initially ruled it short, but Mike Vrabel challenged and won. The score cut the lead to 10-7. Gooch Hot Take : Had it been called a TD initially, I wouldn’t really have a problem. But if the ankle is down or the ball hits bf the ball crosses – its down. You’re going to tell me that was clear and obvious? It’s just clear the NFL has utterly abandoned its preference for the call on the field. Chicago answered after a big Zavion Thomas kickoff return. The drive stalled in the red zone (penalties and an incomplete to Rome Odunze), but Santos added a field goal for 13-7. The momentum swung hard on the next possession. Maye lofted a pass into the end zone that D’Marco Jackson read perfectly and intercepted (Jackson >>>> TJ). Chicago took over and immediately scored: Williams hit Burden on a short pass, and Burden took it the rest of the way (helped by downfield blocking from Colston Loveland) for a touchdown. 20-7. It was looking like it was all coming up Bears. I had mentally already headed into halftime. Perhaps that’s what the Bears defense did – because, in an utterly inexplicable, inexcusable series of plays, the Bears allowed the Patriots to score a TD. On the final play of the half, Rhamondre Stevenson zig-zagged through the Bears’ defense for a 48-yard touchdown. The score made it 20-14 at intermission. Chicago will get the ball to start the second half. It frankly reminded me of the dark days under Eberflus when we allowed an inexplicable TD by the Arizona Cardinals at the end of a half in a game we should have won. Key moments of the First Half: Maye’s reviewed rushing TD showed his legs and New England’s willingness to fight. Jackson’s end-zone interception was the half’s biggest defensive play—it killed a potential go-ahead drive and set up Burden’s score. Stevenson’s 48-yarder at the buzzer prevented the Bears from carrying a three-score lead into the locker room. Gooch First Half Observations and hot takes: Luther Burden has been the clear standout. Between the 58-yard setup and his own touchdown, he’s already over 100 receiving yards and has completely changed the geometry of Chicago’s offense. Drake Maye is creating with his legs (rushing TD) and has been efficient overall, but the end-zone interception was a brutal mistake at a critical moment. Both defenses have largely done their jobs except on the explosive plays. The Bears’ red zone hasn’t been perfect, but they’ve converted opportunities when they appear. Stevenson’s late heroics kept this game competitive. But for that play, the Bears have completely dominated the Patriots. The Bears still control the game, but New England proved it can strike quickly, and you have to worry about a Vikings-game-like meltdown. Gooch Quip: The first half felt like two different games—Burden and the Bears building a comfortable lead, then Stevenson reminding everyone that Thursday Night Football doesn’t do quiet endings. Chicago has the lead, but the Patriots just made sure the second half won’t be a formality. A missed opportunity to be sure. Third Quarter: Immediate Answers, One-Score Game Chicago wasted no time putting the Stevenson buzzer-beater behind them. Taking the second-half kickoff, the Bears marched 72 yards in nine plays and finished with Caleb Williams’ 12-yard touchdown pass to Colston Loveland. The score pushed the lead to 27-14 and gave the home crowd early breathing room. New England responded in kind. Drake Maye found rookie tight end Eli Raridon for a 30-yard touchdown, cutting the deficit back to one score at 27-21. The Patriots overcame penalties on the drive and showed they could still move the ball through the air. Gooch Observation: Both offenses looked sharper out of the break than they had at times in the first half. Loveland’s red-zone connection gave Williams his second touchdown pass of the night, while Raridon provided Maye another reliable target. I have some questions about our defense. Gooch Hot take: The third quarter was essentially a wash—each team scored once—but Chicago’s ability to score first after receiving the kickoff kept the Patriots chasing all night. Fourth Quarter: Santos Seals It, Onside Kick Recovery Ends It The final period featured field-goal drama and a late scramble. Cairo Santos’ 53-yard attempt doinked off the upright, briefly giving New England life and field position. Later, with the game still in the balance, the Bears drove into range, but Christian Barmore sacked Williams and appeared to push them out of field-goal range. Santos answered anyway, drilling a career-long 58-yarder to make it 30-21 with just over a minute left. The Patriots managed a quick field goal to pull within 30-24, then attempted an onside kick. Rome Odunze recovered it, and Chicago ran out the clock. Key moments: Santos’ 58-yarder was the decisive blow—it came after a sack that looked like it had taken the points off the board and effectively made the game a two-score contest with little time remaining. The doinked 53-yarder earlier kept the door open longer than it should have been. Odunze’s onside-kick recovery ended any remaining suspense. GOOCH Observations and hot takes: Caleb Williams finished the night 22-of-33 for 308 yards and two touchdowns with no interceptions. He made the late throws when the Bears needed them and avoided the big mistake that haunted Maye earlier. Drake Maye was productive…
