title: Chicago Bears vs. New England Patriots – Game Picks and Predictions
summary: Hello Chicago Bears fans! It is a short week for the Beloved, as the Bears are slated to take on the New England Patriots Thursday night at Soldier Field (7:15 p.m. CT). The 4-2 Chicago Bears host the 4-2 New England Patriots on Amazon Prime Video in the first of three straight prime-time games. Chicago […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - NOVEMBER 10: D'Andre Swift #4 of the Chicago Bears carries the ball past Marco Wilson #22 of the New England Patriots during the second quarter at Soldier Field on November 10, 2024 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) | Getty Images Hello Chicago Bears fans! It is a short week for the Beloved, as the Bears are slated to take on the New England Patriots Thursday night at Soldier Field (7:15 p.m. CT). The 4-2 Chicago Bears host the 4-2 New England Patriots on Amazon Prime Video in the first of three straight prime-time games. Chicago is riding a bounce-back 31-23 road win over Atlanta, with Caleb Williams looking sharp in his return (30 of 36 for 305 yards and a touchdown). But the ground game will continue to be bereft of Kyle Monangai (out again with thumb/toe). The Bears will also be without Jack Sanborn (concussion) and will likely miss T.J. Edwards (hamstring), who is listed as doubtful. New England arrives on a three-game winning streak behind Drake Maye, but the Patriots are short-handed up front—both starting guards are out—and the Pats will be missing multiple corners, including Carlton Davis III. With two efficient quarterbacks, a banged-up New England offensive line, and both teams capable of moving the ball, the game figures to hinge on who protects the ball and who finds the end zone. If either Williams or Maye put up big yardage or turn the ball over, we could be in for some big swings. D’Andre Swift and TreVeyon Henderson will likely be the feature backs, and A.J. Brown will look to bounce back from his stone-handed performance this season. Below is our roundtable with the score predictions and the individual highlights we think will decide it under the lights. Josh : 34-31 OT for the Bears, with quarterbacks trading wow plays and the defenses doing just enough to keep scores from being ridiculous. Cairo redeems himself with a 57-yarder after the offense stalls late in overtime. Gary Baugher Jr : 27-20 Bears. At the start of the season, this was a game I had circled as a loss for us, but the Patriots OL situation and the track record for success at home tilt that for me. Caleb gets 2 touchdowns, Swift a 3rd and Cairo has a clean day. Maye gets sacked 4+ times. JB : This would be a really fun game with a full week of prep. Thursday games can be super weird and turn on things that may not be obvious until the game starts, so predicting said games can be a fool’s errand. Now that I’ve given myself an out… 44-17, Bears offense has one of those explosive games and the makeshift offensive line for the Pats gives up too many pressures, and the Bears defense takes the ball away from Maye at least twice. Bears roll. GOOCH : I’m with JB in this one. While I think Maye is a great, young quarterback, dating back to last season, when he faced significant pressure, he tended to wilt. With New England banged up as bad as it is up front, I expect Dennis Allen to scheme a number of exotic pressures that put the backup Pats in conflict and force Maye to run. I’ll predict two Maye interceptions (one by Thineman) against two touchdown passes, a Booker sack, and give me another Spidey sack to boot. I think Henderson breaks off a big one to boost the Patriots’ rushing attack, and they’re able to collectively post 150 yards on the ground. But that is countered by Swift, who notches another touchdown, and Caleb adds two more touchdowns and goes back-to-back with 300-yard passing games. Bears over the Patriots, 42-20. What is your pick and prediction for the game?

summary: The return of some key starters on both sides of the ball led to a Chicago win last week. But the way the Bears were able to mitigate the impact that some key players had also contributed to the win. Remember, in this weekly series, I’m featuring one player from the Chicago Bears opponent on […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WA - SEPTEMBER 09: Kevin Byard III #31 of the New England Patriots looks on from the sideline during the national anthem prior to an NFL football game against the Seattle Seahawks at Lumen Field on September 9, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The return of some key starters on both sides of the ball led to a Chicago win last week. But the way the Bears were able to mitigate the impact that some key players had also contributed to the win. Remember, in this weekly series, I’m featuring one player from the Chicago Bears opponent on each side of the ball who I think will be critical to their team’s success. Like seasons past, you won’t see any quarterbacks, as the nature of the position always makes them critical for a team’s success. I’ll also try and mix in a few under the radar players from time to time. For the second consecutive week, we must start with a familiar face on the defense Chicago will be playing against – this time New England. Defense: Kevin Byard, #31 – S While some younger players are stuffing the stat sheet more this season, like 2nd year player Elijah Ponder (5.5 sacks tied for 3rd league-wide) and rookie Gabe Jacas (1.5 sacks, 3.5 TFL and 1 INT,), the 11th year pro and 2025 Chicago Bear Pro-Bowler returns to Chicago for his first game against his former team and is who I will be focused on all night. Byard is just 4th on the team in tackles and has yet to cause a turnover at this point – a surprising fact considering he had 7 INTs a year ago and 36 as a pro – but make no mistake; his value is undeniable to this young Patriots squad. As team captain, Byard is the dependable vet that he has been throughout his career, and this week is no exception. Perhaps no player across the league understands this Ben Johnson offense more than the savvy vet, and I am expecting some chess matches between him and Ben Johnson tonight. Byard has already gone on record saying that he expects some trickery for the Bears offense, and how he and the talented, young Patriots defense handle those new wrinkles will be paramount on Amazon Prime in front of the whole country. Ben has tons of respect for Byard and will undoubtedly know where he is at all times tonight. If Caleb and Co. can avoid turning the ball over in a momentum-swinging play to Byard, Chicago should maintain possession and put enough points on the board to win. But if Byard can do what he did best as a Bear, Chicago could be in trouble. Offense: TreVeyon Henderson, #32 – RB After a stellar opening act and finishing 3rd in voting for Associated Press Offensive Rookie of the Year, the former Ohio State Buckeye has gotten off to a much slower start in his sophomore campaign. His success rate on both runs and catches has gone down, as has his yards per carry. Additionally, he has already matched his total fumbles from a year ago. It could be the nagging ankle injury or injuries up front to his offensive line, but either way, I remain quite high on my 2nd rated RB out of the 2025 class. Hendo is the explosive type of back who can take any run or pass to the house on any given play having had two scoring runs of 60+ yards as a rookie and taking a kickoff to the house in pre-season action as well. Though he is technically behind Rhamondre Stevenson in New England’s backfield, Hendo is the back I am more concerned about. If Devin Bush and the Bears D can contain Henderson and not allow any explosive plays to happen – Chicago should keep New England within reach on the scoreboard. But if he decides this Thursday night Primetime game is the game to break out this season, watch out. What about you? Who has you most concerned against the Patriots tonight?

title: Patriots at Bears: 3 Props to Play
summary: Last week, felt like I had a really strong grasp on how the game was going to play out, but unfortunately, it was another subpar week. We had another 1-2 week (thanks to penalties wrecking Kaliff Raymond’s day) that dropped our season record to 8-10. It’s a short week with the Chicago Bears playing tonight […]
full_text: Oct 18, 2026; Atlanta, Georgia, USA; Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams (18) throws the ball against the Atlanta Falcons during the second quarter at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Brett Davis-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Last week, felt like I had a really strong grasp on how the game was going to play out, but unfortunately, it was another subpar week. We had another 1-2 week (thanks to penalties wrecking Kaliff Raymond’s day) that dropped our season record to 8-10. It’s a short week with the Chicago Bears playing tonight at Soldier Field against the New England Patriots. This one should be interesting and a lot of fun as Drake Maye and Caleb Williams square off. Here are three props we like this week; up to you if you want to run it with me or fade me. Kyle Williams OVER 19.5 Receiving Yards -113 Sometimes you look at the opponent’s numbers and say, this one makes too much sense not to play. Kyle Williams is Drake Maye’s deep threat. His job is to stretch defenses, get behind them, and make a big play. We know speed isn’t something that the Bears handle well with the secondary, and they’ve shown that they can get beat deep. 19.5 receiving yards is basically wagering whether or not you think Williams is getting one catch. I think it makes too much sense that he snags 1 or 2 explosive plays tonight. D’Andre Swift OVER 60.5 Rushing Yards -113 It’s almost impossible to believe that Swift hasn’t surpassed this number since the Eagles game on September 28th. In the month of October, he’s totaled 58, 43, and 44 yards. With Monangai out, we know Roschon Johnson will be getting his share of carries, but I feel like Ben Johnson is going to want to establish the run and keep his defense off the field. The Patriots defense is a little stingy with the rushing yards, but I think Swift clears this number, but it may take him until the 4th quarter to do it. Caleb Williams OVER 241.5 Passing Yards -113 Right now it’s tough to hone in on the Bears receivers. If I took someone, I certainly would take Loveland because I think Ben Johnson is going to want to attack the middle of the field against NE, but with the amount of weapons they have, it’s hard to know for certain who is going to be featured in the game plan. I think we need a few more games of Caleb Williams to start looking for trends and who he targets. I think the Bears do get the passing game going, but I think Caleb will distribute it over many different receivers. The bottom line here is that the Patriots’ secondary can be beaten, and Caleb Williams in good conditions is averaging almost 290 passing yards per game.

Trey Hendrickson will be facing his former team for the first time when the Bengals play in Baltimore against the Ravens Sunday afternoon. While he’s trying to downplay the matchup against the Bengals, the reality is he can’t. “We’re a team. This isn’t an individual sport,” Hendrickson said this week. “It’s about the team and what I can bring and what they can bring, and what we can collectively do as a unit. I think that’s what makes football special, and I’m looking forward to it Sunday.” You can hear it in the tone of the Bengals’ players and head coach Zac Taylor when they’ve been asked about Trey Hendrickson. They’re ready to move on and focus on who’s on the field for them. While Hendrickson has 83 sacks in his career, now in his 10th season, he hasn’t sacked Joe Burrow. Hopefully, that doesn’t happen on Sunday. But this is a major storyline going into Sunday’s game, with Hendrickson facing the Bengals for the first time since walking in free agency in March. After all the drama between the All-Pro edge rusher and the Bengals, the Bengals want to show they were correct to move on and commit that money to different players like Boye Mafe, Dexter Lawrence, and Jonathan Allen. title: NFL teams are reportedly interested in potential Shemar Stewart trade
summary: The bye week is over, and the Cincinnati Bengals are scheduled for a trip to Baltimore where they’ll play their second AFC North game of the season. The Bengals and Ravens are both in position to push for the lead in the division in the coming weeks, and everyone in both buildings is currently focusing […]
full_text: The bye week is over, and the Cincinnati Bengals are scheduled for a trip to Baltimore where they’ll play their second AFC North game of the season. The Bengals and Ravens are both in position to push for the lead in the division in the coming weeks, and everyone in both buildings is currently focusing all their attention on how they can escape Week 7 with a win. At least everyone in Cincinnati and Baltimore. According to one report, there are some teams looking at a former first-round pick on the Bengals’ roster as a possible trade target before the November 10 deadline. “One surprise name a few teams are tracking is Cincinnati edge rusher Shemar Stewart,” ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler said on Thursday . “The 2025 first-round pick is not a factor in the team’s rotation right now. He has played 17 defensive snaps, well behind the total for the fourth defensive end, Cedric Johnson (83). And rookie second-rounder Cashius Howell has been impressive. Cincinnati typically doesn’t move its young draft picks, but it would be surprising if the Bengals haven’t received inquiries on Stewart, whose upside remains high.” Stewart suffered a hyperextended left knee at the very beginning of training camp, which forced the Bengals’ defense to move on to start the season without him. Now the Bengals are leaving the first quarter of the season behind tied for the fourth-most sacks so far this season (17). They not only signed Boye Mafe, but they completely reshaped the defensive front with the additions of Dexter Lawrence, Jonathan Allen, and Howell in the draft. They’ve accomplished this without Stewart’s help, and if a team reaches out with interest, it wouldn’t hurt to listen. Stewart was selected with the No. 17 overall pick in the 2025 draft as a developmental pass rusher, but he hasn’t been developed, and the Bengals don’t seem to be developing him. If they feel they can make a deep run in the postseason and get something for a guy who isn’t really contributing, then they could possibly have their cake and eat it too. Still, the odds of a trade actually happening are slim.

title: 3 keys to a Cincinnati Bengals victory vs. the Baltimore Ravens
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals will travel to Baltimore to face the Ravens at 1:00 pm ET this week. The Bengals are coming off a bye week, while the Ravens are coming off a close loss to the Browns in Cleveland. The Ravens are currently a half game ahead of the Bengals in the division, sitting at […]
full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals will travel to Baltimore to face the Ravens at 1:00 pm ET this week. The Bengals are coming off a bye week, while the Ravens are coming off a close loss to the Browns in Cleveland. The Ravens are currently a half game ahead of the Bengals in the division, sitting at 4-2 on the season. The Bengals are looking to drop the Ravens to 4-3 this year, while getting themselves to 4-2. Here are three keys to the Bengals winning in Baltimore for what would be their first AFC North victory of 2026. Slowing down Derrick Henry I have concerns about Justice Hill, carries to Zay Flowers on jet sweeps, and limiting either Lamar Jackson or Snoop Huntley when they break out of the pocket. The one guy that can really wear down a defense, though, is Derrick Henry. One of the best running backs of his era, Henry has 534 rushing yards already this season. He is coming off his lowest rushing total of the season, running for 58 yards against a strong Browns defense. Can the Bengals have similar success in slowing down Henry this week? To do so, they’ll have to get better at containing outside zone runs. Teams have been much more successful getting the ball to the perimeter instead of just running up the middle. Slowing down Henry will take a total team effort. The defensive line, linebackers, and secondary players will all need to bring their hard hats this week. Limiting Derrick Henry and the Ravens’ rushing attack will go a long way in pulling off the road victory. Create explosives in the passing game The Ravens are the 13th-best passing defense this season, allowing 210 passing yards per game. They are ranked 12th against the run. While they sit in the top half of the league against the pass, they haven’t faced a murderer’s row of passing attacks to start the year. The Ravens have played the Colts, Saints, Cowboys, Titans, Falcons, and Browns. The Cowboys are the only one of those teams ranked in the top 15 in passing yards per game. The Bengals have the 8th-best passing attack, averaging 260 yards per game so far this season. If I am Cincinnati, I am testing that secondary early and often on Sunday. Tee Higgins and Ja’Marr Chase are the best wide receiver tandem in the league. Dohnte Meyers has been a revelation this season and is coming off his best couple of games. Colbie Young is expected back in the mix this week after returning from injury. While it would be nice to get the running game going, you should come out looking to create explosives in the passing game to open it up. Teams always run the ball more effectively with a lead. I would come out passing to get that early lead. Take your shots down the field, and let your playmakers go make plays. Limiting Trey Hendrickson Trey Hendrickson has been the Ravens best pass rusher. Even though he has missed a couple of games with a hand injury, he is still leading the team in pressures. Hendrickson has 20 pressures in just four games played, and has added two sacks so far this season. The Bengals are very familiar with what Trey Hendrickson can do as a pass rusher. I would expect to see a tight end lined up over beside Orlando Brown Jr. quite often throughout this game. You can expect to see chips from not only those tight ends, but also extra attention from the running backs when we are throwing the football. Limiting Hendrickson’s impact as a pass rusher will let the Bengals hit those explosives in the passing game. If they do those things, they can come out of Baltimore with a big divisional win this week. What is your biggest key to a Bengals win over the Ravens this week?

title: Bengals Progress Report: Grading the Defense
summary: The first five weeks of the 2026 NFL season are in the books, and the Cincinnati Bengals are coming out of their bye week with a 3-2 record. They’re absolutely still “in it,” but they’ve been a mixed bag so far. After missing the playoffs for the third consecutive season in 2025, the Bengals completely […]
full_text: The first five weeks of the 2026 NFL season are in the books, and the Cincinnati Bengals are coming out of their bye week with a 3-2 record. They’re absolutely still “in it,” but they’ve been a mixed bag so far. After missing the playoffs for the third consecutive season in 2025, the Bengals completely rebuilt their defense. They traded the No. 10 overall pick to the New York Giants for Dexter Lawrence and signed Boye Mafe, Jonathan Allen, Bryan Cook, and Kyle Dugger in free agency. Unfortunately, after starting 2-0 and looking like everything was heading in the right direction, the Bengals spent the next two weeks repeatedly shooting themselves in the foot. Then, against the 0-4 Dolphins, they squeaked out an ugly win in which the defense surrendered 24 points to arguably the worst team in football. Before facing Cincinnati, the most points Miami had scored in a game was 13. So, yeah. Mixed bag. Here’s a progress report for the defense, starting with the… RUN DEFENSE The Bengals started the season doing an excellent job limiting explosive plays on the ground. The longest run they allowed to a running back against the Buccaneers and Texans was just 13 yards. That changed in Week 3 against the Steelers. Over the next three games, the Bengals surrendered runs of 35, 25, 39, 26 and 22 yards. Suddenly, a defense that had been effective at preventing big plays was giving them up with alarming regularity. Lawrence has been outstanding against the run. Even when he isn’t directly involved in a tackle, he’s often occupying two blockers, which should create opportunities for his teammates to make plays. Unfortunately, someone doesn’t always get the job done. Missed tackles have once again become a significant problem for Cincinnati’s defense. According to PFF, the Bengals have a tackling grade of just 50.3, the seventh-worst mark in the NFL, and have been credited with 47 missed tackles. That’s simply not good enough. With the Bengals returning from their bye week, they’ll play their second divisional game of the season, this time against Derrick Henry, Lamar Jackson, and the Baltimore Ravens. AFC North games are typically messy affairs, but Cincinnati absolutely cannot allow Henry and Jackson to get going on the ground. If they do, the Bengals risk spending much of the afternoon watching helplessly as Burrow and the offense remain stuck on the sidelines. Run-Defense Grade: 75% (C) PASS DEFENSE Pass defense really consists of two components: the ability to cover receivers and the ability to rush the passer. The Bengals have been very good at one of those things. The other? Not so much. Cincinnati’s defense has brought opposing quarterbacks down in the backfield 17 times through five games, tied for the third-most sacks in the NFL. That puts them on pace for approximately 58 sacks over a full regular season. For perspective, that’s 16 more sacks than the Bengals recorded during the 2021 regular season, when they eventually reached Super Bowl LVI. So, clearly, that part of the defense is working. Unfortunately, when the pass rush doesn’t get home, the defensive backs left on islands have struggled to keep opposing receivers from getting open. Take the Steelers game, for example. Aaron Rodgers, who is 42 years old, was somehow able to scramble around the backfield and evade pressure like he was Burrow’s age. When he extended plays, Cincinnati’s secondary struggled to maintain coverage, allowing Pittsburgh to move the ball effectively through the air. Of course, the Bengals couldn’t stop the run in that game, either, so there was plenty of blame to go around. Evaluating pass defense can be tricky because there are so many moving parts. A great pass rush can make an average secondary look outstanding, while poor coverage can make even an effective pass rush look inadequate. With that in mind, I’m breaking the pass defense into two separate grades. Pass-Rush Grade: 94% (A) Pass-Coverage Grade: 78% (C+) Overall Pass-Defense Grade: 86% (B) There’s a reasonable argument that the Bengals missed the playoffs in 2023 primarily because of Burrow’s injury. The same excuse can’t be made for 2024 or 2025. Following the 2024 season, the front office fired defensive coordinator Lou Anarumo, hoping a change in leadership would fix the defense’s problems. Unfortunately, those issues persisted in 2025 under his replacement, Al Golden. Rather than make another change, the Bengals decided to trust the process, retain Golden and give him considerably more talent to work with. So far, the results have been mixed. Of course, injuries haven’t helped matters. Bryan Cook, Jordan Battle, and Kyle Dugger have all dealt with injuries, while Jalen Davis and Ja’Sir Taylor are on injured reserve. Still, injuries or not, the defense hasn’t consistently performed at the level expected of a unit that received such a significant offseason investment. Fortunately, the Bengals got an early bye week to get healthy, evaluate what’s working, and iron out some of the issues that have plagued them through the first five games. And they’d better take advantage of it. Taylor and his entire coaching staff have a lot riding on this season. It would be difficult to imagine the Bengals allowing four of the prime years of Burrow, Ja’Marr Chase, and Tee Higgins to slip away without a single playoff appearance and still deciding Taylor is the right man for the job. The offense has the firepower to compete with anyone in the league, but that won’t matter if the defense continues to give away explosive plays and miss tackles. Taylor needs this defense to get right coming out of the bye. Otherwise, he could find himself in serious trouble when the regular season comes to an end. Overall Defensive Grade: 81% (B-) So, how would you grade the defense? Sound off in the comments section!

title: Bryan Cook is healthy and ready to go for Bengals vs. the Ravens on Sunday
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals have been missing a healthy Bryan Cook as he has been recovering from an ankle injury. full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals have been missing a healthy Bryan Cook as he has been recovering from an ankle injury. The veteran safety was in and out of the lineup in the Week 3 loss to the Steelers, then missed the following week vs. the Jaguars. The Bengals dropped both games. While he did return for the Week 5 win at Miami, he struggled to make an impact in the 31-24 victory. As the Bengals prepare for the Ravens offense, having Cook back at full strength will be a welcome sight for Bengals fans. He is also excited to get back on the field after the bye week. Cook spoke with Charlie Goldsmith of FOX 19 this week and had this to say about heading into the week: “I’m excited to really go. You don’t know how well you feel until you really push yourself. It’s like life. When you hit those extremes, you’re alive.” Cook also knows how important it will be to contain Lamar Jackson if he returns after facing him in so many important games with the Kansas City Chiefs. “You have to try to contain Lamar,” Cook said. “He’s a force to be reckoned with. He’s one of the best dual-threats if not the best dual threat of this generation. He’s very explosive. He has a tank in the backfield with 22 (Henry). You try to contain those two. They have a high-powered offense. We have to slow them down, capitalize on missed opportunities, get a turnover, and be physical. It’s the AFC North.” The defense has struggled at times this season, but getting a fully healthy Cook back will be a big win for the safeties group. It will also be a major boost to have a veteran leader on the back end of this defense, especially against an offense that can be one of the most dynamic in the league when it’s clicking. Will be fun to see Cook back on the field at full strength.

full_text: (Photo by Nick Cammett/Getty Images) | Getty Images Happy Friday, Browns fans! Today is the final day of prep for the Browns as they head to Nashville to face the Tennessee Titans. While things are going well for the first-place Browns, they can’t seem to shake the injury bug, with today’s news that linebacker Quincy Williams missed practice with a neck injury being the latest bummer. full_text: The Cleveland Browns take on the Tennessee Titans this Sunday. If the Browns were at home, they might get some more universal support. But, it’s the first time they are favored in a game this season , and many people are actually picking Cleveland to win. Here is what the national media is saying about the Week 7 game between the Browns and Titans: NFL.com (Various) Why Brooke picked the Titans: Despite the Browns possessing three more wins than Tennessee — and several of those victories were against better opponents, in my opinion — both teams rank in the bottom five in points per game with Cleveland averaging 17.7 (tied for 28th) and the latter 14 (tied for dead last). In fact, the Browns are one of just five teams in the last 20 seasons to win at least four of their first six games despite averaging fewer than 18 PPG. That’s why I can’t fully lean into Todd Monken’s group with confidence in this game. Not to mention, a baker’s dozen of Browns were on Wednesday’s injury report, including the heartbeat of the defense in LB Carson Schwesinger (ankle). I’m not overly confident about the home team, either, to be clear. But last week’s win proved to more than just the locker room that this team has what it takes to punch above its weight and win. In Jeffery Simmons and his friends on the D-line I trust against the most-sacked quarterback in the NFL. There is the question of which QB — Cleveland’s Deshaun Watson or Tennessee’s Cam Ward — will find the end zone before the fourth quarter? Heck, I’ll take a swing. Give me the second-year passer with a strong dose of rookie Carnell Tate. CBS Sports (Pete Prisco) – Browns 17, Titans 16 The Browns are 4-2 after beating Baltimore last week, while the Titans beat the Colts last week. Neither team is doing much on offense, which suggests this will be a low-scoring game. I think the Browns have a better defense, which will be the difference. They win it again on a late field goal. title: NFL trade deadline: Browns connected to a whole lot of edge defenders as targets
summary: How quickly things fly by in the NFL. The Tennessee Titans are next on the schedule, but NFL […]
full_text: How quickly things fly by in the NFL. Only a little while ago, the 2026 NFL season was kicking off, and now we are staring down a Cleveland Browns schedule that includes the NFL trade deadline and the team’s bye week before the Thanksgiving holiday. The Tennessee Titans are next on the schedule, but NFL trade deadline rumors have been swirling for awhile now, including involving the Browns potentially dealing away WR Jerry Jeudy . After his Week 6 performance, Jeudy’s time with Cleveland seems likely to last throughout at least this season. That doesn’t mean the Browns won’t be active at the deadline, and rumors will only heat up if the team continues their winning ways. The Athletic posted a list of 50 players who could be on the trade market, as well as potential suitors for their services. Jeudy was the only player on Cleveland’s current roster listed, ranked #36, but the list also had the Browns listed as a potential suitor for a ton of edge players on the list (their ranking listed before their name): #5 DE Tuli Tuipulotu, Chargers #7 DE/OLB Alex Highsmith, Steelers #12 DE Khalil Mack, Chargers #14 DE Josh Sweat, Cardinals #16 DE YaYa Diaby, Buccaneers #20 DE Will McDonald, Jets #23 DE Nolan Smith, Eagles #27 DE K’Lavon Chaisson, Commanders #46 DE Dorance Armstrong Jr., Commanders Previously, we have noted Tuipulotu, Mack, Sweat, and Armstrong as options for Cleveland GM Andrew Berry. Edge defenders are often very expensive in both trades and contracts. The younger guys on the list, like Tuipulotu and Smith, could cost the most in both compensation avenues. Sweat, signed to a long-term contract, could see his trade value drop precipitously because of the contract value. Veterans in the final year of their contract, like Mack and Armstrong, could come at a reasonable trade price, but Berry might also have interest in extending their contracts as well. For now, Cleveland is focused on Week 7 versus the Titans, but another win could stir up even more trade conversation. full_text: Mandatory Credit: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect As Eagles fans love to say, it’s “Dallas week”. The Cowboys vs Eagles matchups are some of the more anticipated matchups on the schedule every season. We already know Jalen Hurts will not be playing, but Saquon Barkley is expected to make his return. The Cowboys will also be getting some reinforcements back with Cobie Durant and DeMarvion Overshown expected to return to the starting lineup and hopefully provide a nice boost the the struggling Cowboys defense. Schottenheimer stands firm amid Cowboys’ struggles: “I know what a great coach I am” – Briana Aldridge, CBS Sports Brian Schottenheimer has done a lot of talking this season, but we have yet to see much action. If the wins don’t start coming soon, the Cowboys second-year head coach could be in trouble. “We’ve got to play better; I’ve got to coach better,” said Schottenheimer. The words might mean more in Week 7 if they didn’t seem repetitive after back-to-back losses. The honeymoon phase seems over, and Cowboys Nation’s frustration isn’t going unnoticed. “No one likes it. I block out most of it; some of it gets to me, but at the same time, I’ve got strong shoulders,” Schottenheimer said. “I know what a great coach I am, and I know what this team is capable of. That’s what I focus on.” Dallas Cowboys Injury Report For Week 7 vs Eagles: George Pickens, 10 Others Listed – Josh Sanchez, SI.com Despite remaining very healthy on the offensive side of the ball, the Cowboys defense has been very banged up to start the season. Based on the first injury report for Week 7, the Cowboys may be getting healthy at the right (most desperate) time. With practice picking up, the team has dropped its initial injury report for the week , with 11 total players getting listed. Von Miller was given a veteran rest day, while All-Pro return specialist KaVontae Turpin (ribs) and starting linebacker Dee Winters (calf) were also among those who did not participate. Star wide receiver George Pickens also popped up on the injury report, officially listed as limited with a shoulder injury. With the Cowboys’ struggling offense trying to find its groove again , the last thing they can afford is for a player of Pickens’ caliber to be sidelined, so hopefully he will be back to full participation by the end of the week. Cobie Durant aiming to do his part for Cowboys secondary, help create turnovers – Tommy Yarrish, DallasCowboys.com Cobie Durant looks to make his return in week 7. His play in the secondary has been severely missed after missing the last four games due to a hamstring injury. “A blessing for sure,” Durant said. “Injuries happen, things happen man, but you’ve just got to stack those days that you’re missing and do your part. And then be ready when your name is called when you get back out there.” Durant was officially listed as limited on the practice report Thursday, and added that detail when talking to reporters in the locker room Thursday. After years of Dak Prescott dominating against the blitz, this year has been much different. Can the Cowboys adjust their protection rules and get back on track or is the blueprint out? title: 2026 Week 7 rooting guide for Cowboys fans
summary: The mood in Cowboys Nation is pretty ugly right now. After two bad losses to the Bucs and Packers, Dallas is 2-4 and looks about as lost on both sides of the ball as they have in 20 years. As such, many are already checking out of this season and thinking about next spring. Still, […]
full_text: Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The mood in Cowboys Nation is pretty ugly right now. After two bad losses to the Bucs and Packers, Dallas is 2-4 and looks about as lost on both sides of the ball as they have in 20 years. As such, many are already checking out of this season and thinking about next spring. Still, 2026 is far from over. With 11 games to go and nobody running away with the NFC East, the Cowboys are in about as good a spot to win the division as anybody. For those who would still like to see something positive come of this season, we’ll stay focused on postseason goals until there’s just no reasonable case for it. As you well know, Dallas has a huge task this Monday night in Philadelphia. Between division standings, tiebreaker potential, avoiding a three-game losing streak, and just general morale, so much is on the line. In addition to beating the Eagles, what else could help the Cowboys from the Week 7 schedule? NFC East teams Texans d. Giants After a 0-4 start to the year, Houston has won two straight. Their last win was a solid home-field defense against the previously 4-1 Jaguars. Now they’ll host the Giants, who are coming off a loss to the Saints and, before that, a tie against Washington (that probably should’ve been a loss). Momentum favors the Texans, which is great for Dallas as they try to overtake the Giants for the NFC East lead. The Commanders are on their bye week. NFC vs. NFC Falcons d. 49ers Bucs d. Panthers Lions d. Packers San Francisco is 6-0 and probably out of the Cowboys’ reach at this point, in terms of eventual NFC playoff seeding. We will likely have games soon where we’d prefer them to get the win and help us against teams more likely to threaten us. But Atlanta doesn’t seem like one of those teams. While Tampa Bay has a head-to-head tiebreaker over Dallas, they’re going to have a tough time coming back to win the NFC South or even get into the wild card at 1-5. Carolina currently leads that division and is more likely to impact the Cowboys in January. The Packers’ tiebreaker over the Cowboys is far more concerning, especially in a wild card scenario. They’re starting to surge with three straight wins, so it’d be good to see Detroit knock them down a peg. NFC vs. AFC Patriots d. Bears Saints d. Steelers Colts d. Vikings Broncos d. Cardinals Raiders d. Rams Chiefs d. Seahawks Lots of cross-conference action this week! We generally root for AFC teams in these games, unless there’s some nuanced reason to go the other way. Most of these games follow the standard logic. If we were focusing more on the 2027 draft at this point, tonight’s game between the Patriots and Bears would go the other way. Dallas owns New England’s seventh-round pick, so their losses are our gains. But Chicago is 4-2 a very much a potential playoff threat, so the 2026 prospects outweigh that for now. On the other hand, New Orleans doesn’t look like much of a threat in the NFC. And they play the Steelers, who owe Dallas a fourth-rounder next April. Pittsburgh losses are never hard to root for, especially when they benefit us, AFC vs. AFC Nothing to see here this week. The few all-AFC games have no tangible bearing on the Cowboys. Root with your hearts.

title: Cowboys can get the victory Monday night in Philadelphia
summary: The Cowboys are 2-4 after losing to Green Bay, but Monday night gives them the perfect opportunity to change the mood. full_text: The Cowboys are 2-4 after losing to Green Bay, but Monday night gives them the perfect opportunity to change the mood. Philadelphia is also 2-4, has lost four games in a row and will be without Jalen Hurts. Hurts will miss the remainder of the season after being diagnosed with blood clots and undergoing treatment. Philadelphia will instead start Tanner McKee. McKee threw for 215 yards and one touchdown against Carolina, but Philadelphia scored only 14 points, managed 17 first downs and punted eight times with McKee having a poor 56% completion rate. Dallas now gets a backup quarterback rather than one of the league’s most dangerous dual-threat players. The Eagles are sliding down right now. They started 2-0, but are now 2-4 after four consecutive defeats, including Sunday’s 25-14 home loss to Carolina. This isn’t a Philadelphia team playing with confidence and Dallas knows it can beat this team Now put that into history and the last meeting should give the Cowboys plenty of belief. Dallas fell behind Philadelphia 21-0 last November and still came back to win 24-21. Dak Prescott threw for 354 yards and two touchdowns, while George Pickens caught nine passes for 146 yards and a touchdown. Brandon Aubrey then won it with a 42-yard field goal as time expired. Dallas has recently taken Philadelphia’s best punch and responded. The Cowboys could finally use their ground game to better effect. Carolina running back Chuba Hubbard just carried the ball 28 times for 120 yards and a touchdown against the Eagles. That should encourage Dallas to lean on Javonte Williams. Keeping the running game involved would also help Prescott after Green Bay’s pressure caused Dallas major problems. Run the football, stay away from obvious passing situations and make Philadelphia defend the entire offense. DeMarvion Overshown is expected to have a strong chance of returning after missing five games with a hamstring injury. That becomes even more important with Dee Winters expected to miss time because of an Achilles strain. Dallas could also get Cobie Durant back. Brian Schottenheimer said the cornerback is “trending to play” after missing four games with a hamstring injury. The defense desperately needs healthy bodies, and two important ones could return at exactly the right time. For the Eagles in terms of injury, Hurts isn’t Philadelphia’s only concern. Saquon Barkley missed the Carolina game, while edge rusher Nolan Smith suffered a concussion and was unable to finish it. Their status will be worth watching throughout the week. The Eagles are already struggling offensively, scoring an average of 17 points per game, that’s among the bottom of the league right now. So any further absences only make Dallas’ job easier, and things look that way as it stands.

title: Cowboys 2nd Philly visit under Schottenheimer is a sad reality check
summary: The only reason the Dallas Cowboys still have a legitimate chance at the playoffs is because the NFC East is so bad. The East is breaking records for how bad a division can be from top to bottom. Dallas’ only win against a team outside the division this year is against a Houston Texans side […]
full_text: Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images | Getty Images The only reason the Dallas Cowboys still have a legitimate chance at the playoffs is because the NFC East is so bad. The East is breaking records for how bad a division can be from top to bottom. Dallas’ only win against a team outside the division this year is against a Houston Texans side that was winless at the time, by four points. Their last win before this in the same category was last Thanksgiving, and they lost four of five to conclude that season immediately afterwards. Perhaps the good news out of all of this is the Cowboys next opponent is in the division. That opponent is the Philadelphia Eagles. Brian Schottenheimer’s head coaching debut came in the same spot the Cowboys will be on Monday night, in Philadelphia, in primetime. The Cowboys looking competitive, playing with some juice and fire, and running the ball well against the then-defending Super Bowl champs in a 24-20 loss was actually taken well and seen as a decent result. 22 games later, there is unequivocally zero margin whatsoever for a Dallas loss at Philly this time around under Schotty to be received with a single molecule of positivity. The Cowboys have already lost two straight, dropped another game this season they should have won to the Ravens, and are aiming to avoid not only a three-game losing streak for the second season in a row, but three straight primetime losses to boot. Embarrasing is a word that’s been thrown around a ton already with the second month of the season not even completed, but we might be reaching “look the word up in the dictionary and see three straight primetime losses by the Cowboys” territory. To avoid an incendiary 2-5 start, Schottenheimer will need to hand head coach Nick Sirianni his first back-to-back home losses in consecutive weeks as the Eagles head coach. Their last game was their first full game without Jalen Hurts at QB, now out for the season, a 25-14 loss to the Carolina Panthers. The Eagles would also fall to 2-5 if the Cowboys win at the Linc for the first time since 2022, the earliest in a season they’d have five losses since Sirianni’s first year of 2021. The dynamic of one of these rivals missing their starting quarterback for a head-to-head matchup is one we’ve covered a lot when checking in on the history of this series. The Cowboys slowly but surely adding the offense to their list of things that feel broken over their last two losses doesn’t help this feel like the advantage it should be, with Dak Prescott, who’s thrown the ball 96 times over these two losses, matching up with Tanner McKee. This game feels like a defining moment for both head coaches to keep their season’s ship away from the iceberg a little longer. Even with a win, there will still be loads of work to do to resemble the best the Eagles have looked under Sirianni before (perhaps an unfair expectation anyway without Hurts), or the Cowboys under Schottenheimer since the last time they played the Eagles. The Cowboys trailed the Eagles 21-0 in Week 12 from AT&T Stadium last year. Jalen Hurts had one passing touchdown and a pair of rushing touchdowns on the Eagles first three drives, which came after the Cowboys started with the ball and turned it over on downs, went three and out, then fumbled. They proceeded to throw a pick in the endzone after this, and miss a field goal following a George Pickens touchdown that made it 21-7. In the second half, the Cowboys defense amazingly forced three straight punts in the third quarter, only letting the Eagles hold the ball for a total of 5:49 across these three drives. Between the missed field goal and a three and out of their own, the Cowboys only scored once in the third quarter, but at 21-14 they got an Eagles missed field goal, fumble, and punt in the fourth quarter, got the tying touchdown with Prescott using his legs, and kicked a 42-yard field goal as time expired to come back and win 24-21. The Cowboys haven’t shown nearly the same fight in an overall sense this season, haven’t played with similar balance on offense (36 Prescott attempts to 31 rushes in that game), had success pushing the ball downfield (Prescott 9.8 YPA), or capitalized even when the defense does find a way to get off the field. Where this next opportunity to right some wrongs falls on the scale of defensive coaches the Cowboys have gone against, and mostly failed against, this season will also be super interesting. This is as much of an open notes test that Schottenheimer will have, going up against not only a familiar Vic Fangio defense, but for the first time a Fangio defense that resembles the Cowboys own defense coordinated by Fangio disciple Christian Parker. As my colleague Tom Ryle has pointed out so well, it was reps for the Cowboys offense against this type of defense all offseason that inflated the expectations for the offense and led to a poorly-placed “GOTI” nickname, but Monday night is a chance to earn at least a little respect back. They may not have to do any of these things to beat Tanner McKee, but they’d help themselves tremendously to at least leave an inkling of possibility that they can do these things in route to a Monday night win. If not, even a win stands to be forgotten about fairly quickly, much like the previously mentioned one from 2022 which was another Dak Prescott vs. Eagles backup Gardner Minshew game in a season where the Eagles went on to lose in the Super Bowl and Cowboys lost in the Divisional playoffs. The last Cowboys win at the Eagles with a bit more elevated stakes than this was likely 2018, where a Week 10 win helped turn a 3-5 Cowboys team into one that won their next four after the Philly win, finished 10-6, and again reached the Divisional round. A football Sunday without the Cowboys is probably what the collective fanbase needs right now to take a breath, but the thought of playing the next day against another inexperienced backup QB shouldn’t feel as daunting as it does.
author: Sean Martin

title: Cowboys roundtable discussion:  Dallas offense, Dak Prescott, and the Eagles game
summary: Every week, we gather to discuss the latest news about the Dallas Cowboys and seek our writer’s perspective on each headline. Welcome back to the roundtable. This week we have Jorge Guajardo, Dyllan Rivers, Tom Ryle and Sean Martin.  Whats gone wrong with the Cowboys offense these last two weeks? Mike – The biggest problem is a complete lack of creativity […]
full_text: Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images | Getty Images Every week, we gather to discuss the latest news about the Dallas Cowboys and seek our writer’s perspective on each headline. Welcome back to the roundtable. This week we have Jorge Guajardo , Dyllan Rivers , Tom Ryle and Sean Martin. Whats gone wrong with the Cowboys offense these last two weeks? Mike – The biggest problem is a complete lack of creativity and imagination from Brian Schottenheimer. Dallas has far too much offensive talent to look this predictable, yet the route concepts and combinations simply aren’t playing to the strengths of the players. CeeDee Lamb should be creating mismatches through motion and movement, while George Pickens should be attacking defenses with routes that exploit his size, speed, and ability to win one-on-one. Instead, we’re seeing static formations, predictable passing concepts, and receivers struggling to create separation because the play designs aren’t helping them. Jorge – I think what many have said thus far about identity is true. What is this team’s offensive plan/philosophy/identity? Could Schotty or Dak tell you? I don’t think so. There doesn’t seem to be a rhyme or reason for what they do; they just naturally fall behind, let Dak and Co. try to drag them back, and end up losing by a solid amount. All of that is just a sign that Schotty and, by extension, Klayton Adams, don’t have a good feel for what they have on offense. Schotty, in particular, seems so out of his element calling plays, managing the game and trying to put this offense in the best possible position to succeed. Imagine being a second-year head coach without a good feel for your offense, and you’re calling plays. That’s Schotty right now. Dyllan – This offense wants to be balanced, but they refuse to commit to it. I’m not sure of an instance where I’ve ever witnessed a team throw the ball 32 straight times in a two-possession game. If the defense is forcing you out of runs with the looks they’re presenting, maybe change the way you attack those looks. You simply cannot ask the quarterback to throw over 50 times in a game and expect to win. Stick with the run game, especially when it’s working, and you’ll find taking the load off Dak Prescott will pay dividends. Tom – I have to lean toward us being sold a real bill of goods this year. We believed the propaganda about how good this offense was and didn’t fully appreciate that they were basing that to a large degree on how they looked against their own defense while it was trying to rebuild itself under a first time coordinator. This might be as simple as they were never that good going into the season and we have suffered seeing the illusion collapse. Sean – They don’t understand that talent alone doesn’t put points on the board. Defenses should not have as many ways to put the clamps on both CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens as they do right now. Avoiding third down shouldn’t be as difficult as it is right now. Playing with more balance shouldn’t be as hard as it is right now. Not falling down on a slant route shouldn’t be hard. If these things are hard, and they just all are right now for Schotty’s offense, your team is going to have a very hard time winning games in modern pro football. Is Dak Prescott’s recent dip in form more due to the offensive line’s problems allowing pressure, or is it Brian Schottenheimer failing to make the right play calls? Mike – The offensive line isn’t helping, but Brian Schottenheimer is making a bad situation considerably worse. Dak Prescott has been under constant pressure, but that’s exactly when good coaching should make life easier for the quarterback. Instead, we’re seeing predictable play-calling and not enough quick answers against the blitz. That said, Dak isn’t blameless here and he’s been guilty of forcing throws and making poor decisions under pressure. But for me, the bigger issue starts with Schottenheimer. Jorge – It’s both the o-line struggles and Schottenheimer’s failures as a play-caller. The Cowboys got Tyler Smith back, and the offense has gotten worse, which does not bode well. On top of that, they just seem bamboozled by simple disguises and blitz coverages; they’re not making even the easy adjustment, and it’s leading to the terrible product you’re seeing on the field. This comes from not having the proper coaching to pivot easily, make adjustments and not be rattled by changes. As soon as things go off script, this offense does its best armadillo impression. Dyllan – Just can’t ask the quarterback to throw as much as they have. The offensive line will not hold up in pass protection. The quarterback will make mistakes. That is such a large volume where mistakes will be inevitable. Going back to the first question – if Dallas can become more balanced, the offense will go back to being its true self. Tom – I’m going to duck for cover after my response, because it is that we may be seeing Dak starting to decline. The other factors certainly play major parts, but there have just been too many off target throws and questionable decisions from him this year. Add in that he probably is feeling the pressure to find a way to lift the offense up, and he may well be exceeding what his body can deliver after years of injury and the constant beating that comes with quarterback territory. Sean – I’ll go with Schottenheimer’s play-calling, because asking an offensive line that features Tyler Smith, Cooper Beebe, and Tyler Booker in the middle to go backwards instead of forward in run blocking as much as they are right now is unacceptable. To make matters worse, Schotty’s explanation for why these drastic run/pass splits are happening doesn’t even hold up to logic. I know no fan wants to say or hear anything good about Terence Steele right now, but if you allow yourself to think back to when he was playing well enough to earn praise, getting out in space to run block was a big part of that evaluation. It’s a player deployment problem all across the board, you can lump the receivers and tight ends in here while we’re at it too. That’s coaching. Philadelphia will be without Jalen Hurts, leaving Tanner McKee at quarterback. Should Dallas take an aggressive defensive approach to exploit his inexperience, or is stopping Saquon Barkley and forcing McKee to win through the air the smarter route? Mike – Stop the run first and make Tanner McKee prove he can beat you. The last thing Dallas needs is another defensive disaster where an opponent controls the clock and runs the ball down their throat. If Saquon Barkley returns from injury, stopping him has to be priority number one. Without Jalen Hurts, Philadelphia loses a huge part of its rushing threat, so Christian Parker must take advantage by loading the box when necessary and forcing McKee into uncomfortable third-and-long situations. Make Philadelphia one-dimensional, then let the pass rush attack. Jorge – This defense has to force McKee to beat them. If Barkley has a Bucky Irving-type game, which is crazy to say, the Cowboys will obviously lose. If they make McKee slightly uncomfortable, they’ll be in this game. The defense has slowly improved and has life; if they keep trending up, McKee may not have enough to beat Dallas, with everything going on with the Eagles right now. Dyllan – I’d love to see Dallas attack this quarterback the way Tampa Bay and Green Bay attacked Dallas. In fact, that’s the way they should have attacked Jalon Daniels. You have to force inexperienced quarterbacks into mistakes. Be aggressive, land some hits, and don’t let McKee get comfortable. Tom – I’ll go further, and say that the chance to win this game rests primarily on the defense. The good news is that the addition of Mike Pettine seemed to have made a real difference, especially in the second half of the Packers game. If they can continue to improve, they may set the offense up with situations that are favorable enough that they can rack up some points and get the win in a…
author: Mike Poland

title: Cowboys Week 7 opponent: A look at the 2026 Philadelphia Eagles
summary: The Dallas Cowboys are heading to Philadelphia for a Monday night NFC East showdown, and both teams have plenty of questions to answer. Dallas is coming off a 23-13 loss to Green Bay that dropped them to 2-4, while the Eagles have lost four straight and are also sitting at 2-4. Philadelphia’s season has taken […]
full_text: Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys are heading to Philadelphia for a Monday night NFC East showdown, and both teams have plenty of questions to answer. Dallas is coming off a 23-13 loss to Green Bay that dropped them to 2-4, while the Eagles have lost four straight and are also sitting at 2-4. Philadelphia’s season has taken an especially dramatic turn, with quarterback Jalen Hurts sidelined for the year by blood clots and Tanner McKee stepping into the starting role. The Eagles still have recognizable talent on both sides of the ball, including running back Saquon Barkley and wide receiver DeVonta Smith. But their offense has struggled to find a rhythm, and losing Hurts only makes that challenge more complicated. Their defense has been the steadier unit, giving Philadelphia a chance to stay competitive even when the offense cannot sustain drives. For Dallas, the opportunity is obvious: take advantage of an offense in transition. The challenge is that divisional games rarely follow the script, especially when the opposing defense can make life difficult. Tanner McKee takes over as the Eagles’ quarterback The biggest story in Philadelphia is the absence of Hurts. The Eagles confirmed that he will miss the remainder of the 2026 season after further testing revealed blood clots in his lungs. The focus is rightly on his recovery, but the football implications are enormous for a team that has struggled even with its starting quarterback available. Hurts had thrown for 933 yards, eight touchdowns and three interceptions in five games before being sidelined. Replacing his production and leadership is a big ask, especially for a backup quarterback who hadn’t played a snap in the 2026 regular season before taking over against Carolina. McKee made his first start of the season in Week 6, completing 26 of 45 passes for 215 yards and one touchdown without an interception in a 25-14 loss to the Panthers. The stat line was respectable in terms of ball security, but the offense managed only 222 net yards and struggled to generate consistent momentum. McKee has shown flashes during his limited NFL opportunities, and he deserves time to settle into the role. Still, the Eagles cannot expect him to replicate everything Hurts brings to the offense. He is a different type of quarterback, and Philadelphia will likely need to simplify its approach, protect him better and create more manageable down-and-distance situations. Dallas has struggled to generate consistent pressure this season, so getting after McKee without allowing easy underneath completions should be a priority. The Cowboys cannot afford to let an offense in transition find its confidence early. Saquon Barkley and DeVonta Smith remain the key weapons Even with the quarterback change, Philadelphia has playmakers capable of causing problems. Barkley remains the centerpiece of the running game when healthy, while Smith gives McKee a reliable target who can win at multiple levels of the field. The major caveat is Barkley’s health. He missed Philadelphia’s last two games with a hamstring injury, and the Eagles have had to patch together their backfield in his absence. Through the first six weeks, Barkley had recorded 36 carries for 182 yards, averaging 5.1 yards per attempt, but he had not scored a rushing touchdown. Those numbers are limited by his missed time, and his availability for the Cowboys game will be an important storyline to watch as the week progresses. Without Barkley, Philadelphia has struggled to establish a consistent ground attack. The Eagles used Dameon Pierce and Carson Steele against Carolina after injuries depleted the depth chart, and the team finished with only 62 rushing yards. That lack of production puts even more pressure on McKee and the passing game. Smith offers a more established option in the passing game. He returned from a hamstring injury against Carolina and caught a touchdown pass from McKee. Through six games, Smith has 26 receptions for 310 yards and two touchdowns. He gives the Eagles a receiver who can separate, make contested catches and create opportunities when the offense needs a spark. Tanner McKee throws DeVonta Smith a perfect ball for the touchdown CARvsPHI on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/6xngV0MgMW — NFL (@NFL) October 18, 2026 The question is whether Philadelphia can build a functional offense around those pieces. Smith’s return is a positive, and if Barkley is available, Dallas will have to account for his ability to turn a small crease into a substantial gain. If he remains sidelined, the Cowboys should be able to focus more attention on the passing game. Philadelphia’s defense is keeping it competitive The Eagles’ defense has been the more dependable side of the team, and it could be the biggest obstacle for Dallas on Monday night. Philadelphia has not been perfect, but it has created more disruption than its offense has generated, recording eight sacks and three interceptions through six games. The defense also has young playmakers capable of changing a possession. Defensive tackle Jalen Carter and edge rusher Nolan Smith have each recorded three sacks, while cornerbacks Cooper DeJean and Quinyon Mitchell have each intercepted a pass. Linebacker Jihaad Campbell has contributed across the defense, giving Philadelphia another young player to build around. Jalen Carter has been dominant in the first half of this game. 4 tackles, 2 sacks, 2 forced fumbles @PHIvsJAX on NFL Network Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/oJIA9Heufp — NFL (@NFL) October 11, 2026 The unit’s job has become more difficult because the offense has struggled to sustain drives. Philadelphia’s defense played 79 snaps against Carolina, compared with 64 for the Eagles’ offense. That imbalance can wear down even a talented group, particularly when the offense repeatedly gives the ball back without putting points on the board. Still, the defense has done enough to keep the Eagles within reach in several games. Yet against Carolina, the Eagles allowed 25 points and struggled to stop the run, showing the defense isn’t immune to the same inconsistency affecting the rest of the roster. For Dallas, the matchup presents a familiar challenge. The Cowboys’ offense has shown it can move the ball, but the loss to Green Bay exposed problems with protection, rushing production and execution in critical moments. Philadelphia has enough talent up front and in the secondary to make those issues costly. The Cowboys need to establish the run, keep Prescott out of obvious passing situations and avoid turnovers. If the offense becomes predictable, the Eagles have the personnel to pressure Prescott and force difficult throws. Dallas cannot assume that a struggling Philadelphia team will simply roll over, especially with a defense capable of creating momentum-changing plays. A struggling offense, but no easy divisional game Philadelphia enters Week 7 on a four-game losing streak, averaging just 14.5 points per game during that stretch. The Eagles have scored 14 points against Carolina, 17 against Jacksonville, 7 against Chicago and 20 against the Rams. The results point to a broader problem, which is their offense has not been very good. Dallas has its own issues, of course. The Cowboys have lost consecutive games and are still searching for consistency on both sides of the ball. That makes Monday night an important test for a team that cannot afford to give a divisional opponent easy opportunities. The recent history between these teams reinforces how little the records matter once they meet. Philadelphia beat Dallas 24-20 in the 2025 season opener, but the Cowboys responded with a 24-21 win in Philadelphia later that year. Dallas leads the all-time series, 75-59, but recent meetings have been competitive enough that neither team can take the other lightly. If the Cowboys allow the Eagles’ defense to dictate the pace, another frustrating night could be waiting…
author: Jorge Guajardo

title: Cowboys news: DeMarvion Overshown is eager to reestablish himself
summary: Linebacker DeMarvion Overshown is set to make his return to the Dallas Cowboys on Monday, which will give a struggling defense a much-needed boost. Roster upgrades are something that the Cowboys could use, and team owner Jerry Jones is adamant about being active in that regard. Speaking of adding to the roster, Dallas has been […]
full_text: Linebacker DeMarvion Overshown is set to make his return to the Dallas Cowboys on Monday, which will give a struggling defense a much-needed boost. Roster upgrades are something that the Cowboys could use, and team owner Jerry Jones is adamant about being active in that regard. Speaking of adding to the roster, Dallas has been linked to Cardinals pass rusher Josh Sweat. Also, a sputtering Cowboys’ offense is searching for answers after consecutive bad performances. With more adversity behind him, DeMarvion Overshown ready to prove himself again – Nick Harris, Fort Worth Star-Telegram DeMarvion Overshown hasn’t played since Week 1 due to a hamstring injury. Now that he’s cleared to return against the Eagles on Monday, he’s ready to get back to making plays. What was initially thought to be a two-to-three week issue turned into five games missed for the season’s starting MIKE linebacker, but Overshown has continued to be the same person he has been during his entire tenure in Dallas: level, measured and carrying a smile on his face wherever he goes. “I’ve been taking it day-by-day, it’s really all you can do with stuff like this,” Overshown said. “I’m blessed. Of course, I want to be out there with my teammates, but then again, it’s just about being thankful about what you do have. What I do have not playing football is a loving and caring family. I do have a team that supports me and understands that I’m doing whatever I can to get back on the field.” A ‘disappointed’ Jerry Jones would like to improve Cowboys’ roster before trade deadline – Jon Machota and Mike Jones, The Athletic The Cowboys are off to a rough start in 2026. Team owner Jerry Jones is willing to make another roster move to assist in turning things around. “I don’t have a specific (trade),” he said, “but certainly I’ll be real clear, I would be active if we could get a chance to help the team this year. So, that’s important, I think.” Is there any scenario where the Cowboys would be sellers at the trade deadline? “No, no, I don’t see that,” Jones said. “But I don’t rule it out now. If somebody comes along and offers you one of those deals, like the one I made a year or so ago, then it’s just too much.” Can Cowboys’ returning defenders help ease pressure on rookies Downs, Barham – Calvin Watkins, Dallas Morning News With DeMarvion Overshown and Cobie Durant returning to the lineup, Jaishawn Barham and Caleb Downs won’t have as much on their plates in terms of responsibility. Barham was thrust into a position he might not be equipped to handle so soon. Yet, the Cowboys have confidence in his abilities to make plays. It seems Overshown will play the weakside linebacker spot upon his return. Barham and Overshown are a better combination at linebacker than Barham and Dee Winters. “I don’t know how it’s going to play out,” Overshown said. “I’m going to be out there, that’s enough for me. I feel like that’s enough to impact the game, too, just being out there whether it’s with the green dot or not, so just ready to be out there.” Download the SB Nation app today! Fewer ads Seamlessly jump between communities and conversations Faster commenting and posting experience! Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . Ryan Flournoy: Cowboys offense is having ‘the tough conversations’ – Patrik Walker, DallasCowboys.com Over the past two games, the Cowboys offense has been stuck in the mud. This has forced them to look in the mirror and get some things corrected. “We’re taking it week by week. It’s a long season. It’s only Week 6, and we’ve got [11] more games,” he said. “It’s a long season. I think we’re heading in the right direction, and correcting the things we need to correct. … It’s the attitude of wanting to get better. We know we’re better than what we’ve shown these last couple weeks. “That’s why I feel like we’re heading in the right direction. We’re having the right conversations, the tough conversations.” Cowboys trade rumor: Dallas linked to Cardinals pass rusher Josh Sweat – RJ Ochoa, Blogging The Boys Dallas needs to get a lot more pressure on the quarterback. They’ve been linked to a possible trade for pass rusher Josh Sweat per ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler. The Cowboys might have one more move in them. Perhaps that’s shortsighted, given their 2-4 record. But that might as well be 4-4 in this season’s NFC East climate, where no commodity is proven and Philly’s transitional state has cracked the door open. As one team exec pointed out to me Tuesday, Josh Sweat to Dallas makes a lot of sense. He fits Dallas’ profile, and the Cowboys need edge-rush help. Sweat’s Cardinals won S u nday , but they are not contention-adjacent just yet. Sweat has been linked to the Packers, too, but Green Bay has Micah Parsons returning eventually.

title: The Broncos offense needs more from Bo Nix
summary: Good morning, Broncos Country! Bo Nix and the Denver Broncos offense have to get better. Yet despite the offensive struggles, the Broncos are 4-2. Don’t forget the gauntlet of a schedule that Denver escaped to get to that record. That makes the first six games even more impressive for this team. Both can be true, […]
full_text: SEATTLE, CO - OCTOBER 15: Bo Nix #10 of the Denver Broncos is brought down during an NFL football game against the Seattle Seahawks at Empower Field at Mile High on October 15, 2026 in Seattle, Colorado. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images Good morning, Broncos Country! Bo Nix and the Denver Broncos offense have to get better. Yet despite the offensive struggles, the Broncos are 4-2. Don’t forget the gauntlet of a schedule that Denver escaped to get to that record. That makes the first six games even more impressive for this team. Both can be true, but it also makes you think what the Broncos are if Nix and the offense play to their potential. As head coach Sean Payton said to the media earlier this week: “I shared this with you guys, and I’ll say it again: I have to be better just relative to in the course of the game. Each game takes on a different feel or style, if you will. Collectively, I think (Nix’s) play will be a byproduct of all of us doing our jobs better.” When told what Payton said, Nix responded with this to the media: “He’s been a really good leader right now. We need that. I think it goes back to us. I have to play better. We have to play better. The offense has to play better. He’s going to take his (blame), and that’s what great leaders do. I feel like I can overcome some of the stuff that is putting us in a bad spot, and I feel like I can play better. “I’ve looked at my preparation. I’ve looked at my process, and I’ve tried to see anything that can be moved around or be changed so that I can overcome and just figure out ways to put us in a better spot. For us, if Coach is saying that, if I’m saying that, we have plenty of leadership on offense saying that, we’re going to be just fine. We’re going to be OK.” Perhaps the most telling moment of Nix’s press conference on Wednesday was his opening up about his ankle injury and overcoming the mental aspects of it, not just the physical recovery. “I’d be lying if I said no,” Nix said. “I think that’s just what happens. I think you come back, and every day is a progression. I’m not necessarily doing physical therapy treatment, but I’m out there on the practice field getting rep after rep trying to get back in super great shape so my carries can go up, so I’m ready when my number’s called and when I can run. “I’m not scared. I’m not physically worried. I just think there’s something to the sport. I think all guys, when they come back from an injury, just doing it one day at a time. I think that’s just part of the game. That’s part of the process. I had surgery probably six months ago. It takes a while for things to fully reengage. I’m confident in myself. I know I’m going to get back and be exactly what I was, if not better. My training is going like this (points upwards) , and at the end of the day, it’s all about getting better.” What gives Nix confidence that he can and will play better is that he’s done. We’ve seen Nix have success on the football field. Heck, in the game that Nix broke his ankle, he outdueled Josh Allen. Getting back to that level of play isn’t out of the question. And when it happens, the Broncos are legitimate Super Bowl contenders. “I think that’s what’s playing the biggest factor in it right now is I’ve seen what it is like to be very concise, be very crisp and to be very good on a competitive Sunday. I just am working to get back to that. At the same time, there are so many things that go into it … I know the things that I can control. I’m working to maximize those. “I just feel strong where I’m at. I’m good mentally. I had a good practice today. I feel good physically. I think it’s going to be there. It’s just in football, you have to get that one (game) that just gets you going. I think we’ve been playing some really good teams thus far and haven’t gotten that one, but we’re searching for that one game that sort of just puts us right back where we were.” Broncos links
