title: Will the Giants unmask C.J. Stroud?
summary: During the offseason, there was no lack of hate, vitriol and utter ignorance thrown at Houston Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud. After the team’s unceremonious exit from the 2025 NFL playoffs, many fans, talking heads and know-it-alls blamed Stroud for everything from losing the game against the New England Patriots to dooming the franchise for all […]
full_text: Oct 1, 2023; Houston, Texas, USA; Houston Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud (7) celebrates with wide receiver Robert Woods (2) and wide receiver Tank Dell (3) after a touchdown during the game against the Pittsburgh Steelers at NRG Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Troy Taormina-USA TODAY Sports | USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Con During the offseason, there was no lack of hate, vitriol and utter ignorance thrown at Houston Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud. After the team’s unceremonious exit from the 2025 NFL playoffs, many fans, talking heads and know-it-alls blamed Stroud for everything from losing the game against the New England Patriots to dooming the franchise for all eternity. As the old adage goes, the quarterback gets too much praise and too much shade. There’s no real point in rehashing all the data-points that Stroud was far from the only reason Houston didn’t advance to the AFC Championship last year. However, it is fun to look at his current 2026 season and say a hearty “told you so” to all the haters who said he sucks. Ha! NFL Communications OFFENSE : QB C.J. STROUD, HOUSTON TEXANS Stroud completed 24 of 34 pass attempts (70.6 percent) for 312 yards and three touchdowns for a 116.3 passer rating in Houston’s 34-31 win against Jacksonville at Wembley Stadium. He was the only quarterback with a passer rating of 115-or-higher in Week 6. Stroud is one of four quarterbacks this season with at least 300 passing yards, three touchdown passes, a completion percentage of 70-or-higher and a passer rating of 110-or-higher in a single game. This is Stroud’s fourth Offensive Player of the Week award. He becomes the third Texans player to earn the honor at least four times, joining Deshaun Watson (five-time winner) and Matt Schaub (four). Stroud joins Eddie George as the only former Ohio State players to win Offensive Player of the Week four times. QB C.J. Stroud earned his fourth career AFC Offensive Player of the Week honor after completing 24-of-34 (70.6%) passes for 312 yards and three touchdowns in a Week 6 win over the Jacksonville Jaguars. https://t.co/DidmeqWTay pic.twitter.com/mtvZCvPHzp — Houston Texans PR (@TexansPR) October 21, 2026 C.J. Stroud’s stats are definitely elite so far in 2026. Not only has Stroud overcome the naysayers, he’s won over the wider world of NFL talking heads and casual fans, forcing himself into the MVP conversation this season. Watching his highs and lows, we see: better pre-snap reads better adjustments an elevated understanding of what the defense is doing some really slick mis-direction (via pump fakes, head shakes and body aiming) improved release time. And best of all, his response to adversity has taken an upswing, possibly due to Andre Johnson’s criticism of how he handled it in the past. C.J. Stroud on his mindset after leading the Texans to a 34-31 win over Jacksonville on @nflnetwork : “I tried to choose joy. I made a mistake, but that didn’t end it for us. Our defense held them to three and they gave me the ball back.” On what was working offensively:… pic.twitter.com/iOleCdZwjt — Houston Stressans (@TexansCommenter) October 18, 2026 Heading into this weekend’s matchup with the seemingly revitalized New York Giants, history is not in Stroud’s favor. The Texans are 1-5 vs the G-Men all time, having lost the last 5 straight. However, they’ve not seen the NFC East team since November of 2022, a season we’d all love to forget. Giants QB J.J. McCarthy, drafted as the savior of the Minnesota Vikings, put on a passing clinic last weekend. If Demeco Ryans can’t get this defense to stop operating like a wet paper bag, McCarthy might have another career game this weekend. However, the current Texans offense is a far cry from the 2022 version. And Stroud will have Nico Collins, Jalin Noel, Marvin Harrison Jr., Kayshon Boutte and TANK DELL to play catch with this weekend. That’s right, after nearly 2 years, lightning bolt in cleats receiver Tank Dell returns to the field this weekend. And, as much as I’ve not been enamored with Texans offensive coordinator Nick Caley, he is growing as both a coach and a play caller. If he’s thinking what a lot of people are thinking, Dell’s first game back will see the speedster blow the top off the defense, create distractions and open up opportunities for Collins, Harrison Jr. and the rest of the receivers. The Giants have a stingier passing defense (190 yards per game) than their rushing D (135.5 ypg) so far, but they haven’t seen Stroud and his healthy receiving targets yet. And, these stats are likely due to a less than robust passing attack from Big Blue until McCarthy caught fire last week. A home game, with Stroud on a roll, a “Greatest Show on Turf – Texas Edition” passing attack and a stadium decked out in Battle Red? This has all the makings of another 300+ air yards affair for the good guys. To the opening question: Will the Giants unmask C.J. Stroud? the answer is a resounding no. Prediction: New York Giants vs Houston Texans At the end of the day, J.J. McCarthy is a long way from becoming C.J. Stroud. Unfortunately, the Texans defense has regressed to the mean, meaning McCarthy will still have plenty of big play opportunities. In the end, the wide receiving corps of Houston keeps their QB in the MVP talks. New York Giants – 31 Houston Texans – 42 CJ Stroud with a profound answer on handling the ups & downs. “My joy comes from the lord. For me it starts with gratitude, being grateful to be here. God didn’t have to choose me. I want to be a person who’s a light. I’m grateful for it all, the good and the bad.” pic.twitter.com/sz5a1tMzhi — Houston Stressans (@TexansCommenter) December 12, 2025

title: Value of Things: By the numbers
summary: “I come to praise Caesar, not to bury him.” — Marc Antony in Julius Caesar You cannot find a more embattled coach in Houston right now than Nick Caley. As in most things, much of this criticism is undeserved. That’s the general course of these things as coaching goes. You get the big bucks, but […]
full_text: “I come to praise Caesar, not to bury him.” — Marc Antony in Julius Caesar You cannot find a more embattled coach in Houston right now than Nick Caley. As in most things, much of this criticism is undeserved. That’s the general course of these things as coaching goes. You get the big bucks, but with the big bucks comes big criticism. The Houston Texans offense has looked bad at times, but all grades are overall grades and we should take a look at the Texans offense as a whole to determine whether that criticism is actually warranted or not. Points per game: 24.0 (11th) Total yards: 2130 (7th) Yards per play: 5.7 (10th) Passing Yards: 1621 (2nd) Net yards per attempt: 6.9 (7th) Rushing Yards: 509 (25th) Yards per attempt: 3.6 (28th) So, more than one thing can be true at the same time. Overall, this is a top ten offense in the NFL. They are 10th in yards per play and 11th in points per game. They are even better than that in terms of passing the football and that will end up pulling their offense up more and more as they attempt to run the ball less and less. Of course, that brings us to the bad news. This is not a good running football team. This hasn’t been a good running football team since Arian Foster roamed the plains. We can nitpick all we want, but I tend to look at things through the aggregate. When Caley was hired we wanted a few things. We wanted an offense that took care of the football and kept C.J. Stroud upright. It hasn’t always been pretty but they have limited turnovers and they seem to be doing a better job of late of keeping him upright. So, over the course of one plus season he has met the bar that he was originally brought into meet. Furthermore, he is adjusting on the fly and the team is moving the football as a result. We say all of this to say that we were not necessarily wrong about Nick Caley. The offense was bogged down initially both last season and in parts of the season this year as well. He deserves criticism for the inability of the team to run the ball effectively. However, our criticism should reflect the facts and it should evolve as he evolves. The facts on the ground say this is a top ten offense and if we are going to cut loose a guy that is leading a top ten offense then we setting an extremely high bar. Obviously, there are 11 more football games, so we at Value of Things will be monitoring the situation accordingly. Focus on Stroud When we start looking the pool Stroud is swimming in then we can get a handle on where he will likely end up contract wise. The way that this usually goes is to ask whether you would rather have a guy than the guy you have. We can do that by looking at the numbers. We will look at all of the relevant numbers to see where he ranks among quarterbacks this season. Passing Yards: 1714 (2nd) Passing Yards per game: 285.7 (4th) Net yards per attempt: 7.0 (8th) Completion percentage: 65.3 (13th) Success Rate: 48.5 (11th) Passer Rating: 100.9 (11th) One can look at a lot of different numbers, but I tend to look at a preponderance of the evidence. We can take a look at the collective numbers and make a determination, but Stroud is performing as a top ten quarterback even if it is at the bottom of the top ten. So, what do you pay a quarterback that is playing around the level of a top third overall quarterback in the league. If you are in the top third you should get paid, but you shouldn’t get paid top of the market. Of course. that is literally not the way the world works. He is getting 60+ million dollars a year at this point and he will deserve it based on the numbers.

title: Stampede Blue Reacts Survey – Week 7
summary: It’s difficult to imagine fan confidence in the Indianapolis Colts being much lower than it was following Sunday’s embarrassing 26-20 loss to the previously winless Tennessee Titans. Indianapolis entered the game as a heavy favourite, held a 13-0 halftime lead and somehow managed to collapse against a team that had averaged fewer than 12 points […]
full_text: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - OCTOBER 18: A Indianapolis Colts fan reacts after the game against the Tennessee Titans at Lucas Oil Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Andy Lyons/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s difficult to imagine fan confidence in the Indianapolis Colts being much lower than it was following Sunday’s embarrassing 26-20 loss to the previously winless Tennessee Titans. Indianapolis entered the game as a heavy favourite, held a 13-0 halftime lead and somehow managed to collapse against a team that had averaged fewer than 12 points per game entering the afternoon. The loss dropped the Colts to 2-4, with fans at Lucas Oil Stadium loudly expressing their frustration toward an organization that has seemingly been stuck in the same cycle of mediocrity for years. For many, losing to one of the NFL’s worst teams was the final straw after another disappointing start to the season. That frustration ultimately led to significant changes within the organization, as owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon announced the firing of general manager Chris Ballard less than 24 hours after the defeat. Ballard had been in charge since 2017, overseeing a franchise that reached the playoffs just twice during his tenure and had not made the postseason since 2020. While his departure does little to address the team’s immediate problems on the field, it represents a significant change in direction for an organization that had remained committed to the same leadership for nearly a decade. For fans who had been demanding accountability, the decision could provide a much-needed boost in confidence about the franchise’s long-term future. Sign up here to participate in the weekly emailed surveys: The question now is whether that renewed optimism will extend to the remainder of the 2026 season. At 2-4, the Colts have already put themselves in a difficult position, but with 11 games remaining, there is still an opportunity to turn things around and remain competitive in the AFC playoff race. Shane Steichen and his coaching staff are under considerable pressure to produce results, and a string of victories over the coming weeks could quickly change the mood surrounding the team. Whether fans view Ballard’s dismissal as the beginning of a brighter future or simply another chapter in a frustrating stretch of Colts football remains to be seen. That brings us to this week’s question: How confident are you in the direction of the Indianapolis Colts?

title: How much is Quenton Nelson worth on the trade market?
summary: This is the third and final part of a three-article series looking at the hypothetical trade value of three of the Colts’ biggest stars. This one is about Quenton Nelson. You can click here to read the previous two articles on Jonathan Taylor and DeForest Buckner. As with Taylor and Buckner, this is not an […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - SEPTEMBER 20: Quenton Nelson #56 of the Indianapolis Colts lines up before a play during an NFL football game against the Kansas City Chiefs at Arrowhead Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images This is the third and final part of a three-article series looking at the hypothetical trade value of three of the Colts’ biggest stars. This one is about Quenton Nelson. You can click here to read the previous two articles on Jonathan Taylor and DeForest Buckner . As with Taylor and Buckner, this is not an argument that Indianapolis should trade Nelson. The Colts probably should not be looking to move any of these players unless the season falls apart or another team comes calling with an offer that is too good to ignore. The point of the series is simply to determine what these players would realistically be worth if serious trade interest developed around the deadline. Of the three players, Nelson might be the most difficult to evaluate. He is 30 years old, still one of the best offensive linemen in football and has arguably the strongest individual résumé of anyone currently on the Colts roster. However, he plays a position that has historically struggled to command significant draft capital in trades, and his contract expires after this season. That combination makes determining his value a lot more complicated than simply looking at his performance. Nelson is still one of the NFL’s best guards There really is not much debate about Nelson’s ability. Since Indianapolis selected him sixth overall in 2018, he has been one of the league’s most consistent and dominant offensive linemen. Nelson has made the Pro Bowl in all eight of his completed NFL seasons, becoming just the second offensive lineman in league history to accomplish that feat. He has also earned six All-Pro selections, including three consecutive First-Team honors to begin his career. He is already building a very convincing Hall of Fame résumé, and at 30 years old, there is still plenty of reason to believe he has several productive seasons ahead of him. His recent performance only strengthens that argument. Nelson remains a dominant run blocker, capable of moving defenders off the line of scrimmage and creating running lanes that simply would not exist with an average guard. He is also a reliable pass protector and has been one of the few constants on an Indianapolis offensive line that has experienced considerable turnover around him. There is no reason to believe a team acquiring Nelson would be paying for a player whose best football is already behind him. He is still performing at an elite level, and that should make him an attractive addition for teams looking to improve their offensive line. The trade comparisons are surprisingly underwhelming This is where Nelson’s evaluation gets interesting. The best comparison is Joe Thuney, whom the Kansas City Chiefs traded to the Chicago Bears in March 2025 for a 2026 fourth-round pick. Thuney was 32 years old at the time and coming off another outstanding season. He had earned First-Team All-Pro honors, helped Kansas City reach its third consecutive Super Bowl and established himself as one of the most dependable interior offensive linemen in football. He had even demonstrated the versatility to play left tackle when the Chiefs needed him there. Despite all of that, Kansas City received just a fourth-round selection. There were reasons for the relatively modest return. Thuney was entering the final year of his contract, carried a substantial salary and the Chiefs needed financial flexibility. Chicago was also acquiring a player who would likely require another expensive contract to remain with the organization beyond 2025. The Bears eventually signed Thuney to a two-year, $35 million extension, meaning they surrendered just a fourth-round pick to acquire one of the NFL’s best guards before committing to him financially. Another comparison is Jonah Jackson, whom the Los Angeles Rams traded to Chicago for a sixth-round pick during that same offseason. Jackson was only 28 years old and had previously made the Pro Bowl, but his value had declined considerably following an injury-plagued season in Los Angeles. Nelson is obviously a much much better player than Jackson, and that sixth-round return should not be considered a particularly useful indication of his value. Thuney, on the other hand, presents a legitimate benchmark. Nelson is two years younger than Thuney was when Kansas City traded him and has an equally impressive, if not better, individual résumé. He is also still playing at an exceptionally high level, which should make him more valuable to a team considering a long-term extension. However, Thuney’s return shows just how difficult it can be to extract premium draft capital for an expensive veteran guard, regardless of how talented he is. The positional difference matters, too. Teams have historically been much more willing to surrender first- and second-round picks for offensive tackles, particularly those capable of protecting a quarterback’s blind side. Guards are certainly important, especially with the number of dominant interior defensive linemen around the league, but the trade market has rarely reflected the same level of urgency. Nelson may be one of the best players at his position, but that does not automatically make him worth a first- or second-round pick. His contract makes him a potential rental Like Buckner, Nelson is entering the final months of his current contract. He signed a four-year, $80 million extension in 2022, making him the highest-paid guard in NFL history at the time. That deal expires after the 2026 season, meaning any team acquiring him at the deadline would have contractual control for only the remainder of the year. His current cap hit is $24.2 million, although that number is somewhat misleading when discussing a potential trade. Nelson has a $16 million base salary this season, along with a $2 million roster bonus that Indianapolis has already paid. His $6.2 million prorated signing-bonus charge would also remain with the Colts, meaning an acquiring team would only be responsible for the remaining portion of his base salary. At approximately the halfway point of the season, that would amount to around $8 million, depending on the exact timing of the trade. That is a manageable number for some contenders, particularly those with sufficient cap flexibility or the ability to restructure other contracts. The bigger concern would be what happens after the season. Nelson will be 31 next year and could reasonably expect another lucrative multiyear deal. Considering the continued growth of the offensive guard market, it would not be surprising if he sought a contract worth more than $25 million annually. An acquiring team would therefore have to decide whether it wants to surrender valuable draft capital for a player it may only control for a few months, or commit significant money to a guard entering his 30s. That is a difficult combination, especially when considering the fourth-round pick Kansas City accepted for Thuney under similar contractual circumstances. How much longer can Nelson play at this level? This is where I think Nelson has a stronger argument than either Buckner or Taylor. At 30 years old, he is certainly no longer a young player, but offensive guards can remain highly productive well into their 30s. Much of the position relies on strength, technique, leverage and experience, all of which can help compensate for the gradual athletic decline that comes with age. Thuney is a good example. He was still one of the league’s best guards at 32 and earned another substantial contract from Chicago. Zack Martin also remained among the NFL’s premier interior linemen into his 30s before injuries eventually caught up with him. Nelson has the physical profile to follow a similar path. At 6-foot-5 and…

title: Jaguars bye week rooting guide: Who should Jacksonville fans cheer for in Week 7?
summary: The Jacksonville Jaguars have earned a week off, although their 34-31 loss to the Houston Texans at Wembley Stadium means they probably would have preferred to head into the bye with a little more peace of mind. At 4-2, Jacksonville remains firmly in the AFC South picture, but the Texans have just reminded everyone that […]
full_text: JACKSONVILLE, FLORIDA - DECEMBER 01: A T.V. camera as seen during the game between the Jacksonville Jaguars and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at TIAA Bank Field on December 01, 2019 in Jacksonville, Florida. (Photo by Sam Greenwood/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Jacksonville Jaguars have earned a week off, although their 34-31 loss to the Houston Texans at Wembley Stadium means they probably would have preferred to head into the bye with a little more peace of mind. At 4-2, Jacksonville remains firmly in the AFC South picture, but the Texans have just reminded everyone that this division race is unlikely to be a relaxing experience. With no Jaguars game to watch this weekend, fans can turn their attention to the rest of the NFL and hope a few results fall Jacksonville’s way. The priorities are straightforward: keep the AFC South rivals in check, avoid giving potential Wild Card competitors unnecessary help, and generally cheer for the NFC when an AFC team is on the other side of the field. Here is your Week 7 rooting guide, matchup by matchup. You’re welcome, Jaguars fans. New England Patriots at Chicago Bears (Thursday Night Football) The last time the Chicago Bears played the New England Patriots on primetime: pic.twitter.com/o2yEqqgk5B — Justin Fields Fan Club (@JustinFieldsFC) October 21, 2026 Root for: Chicago Bears The Patriots enter Week 7 at 4-2, putting them right in the mix for the AFC East title and a potential Wild Card spot. With Jacksonville holding the same record, there is little reason to help New England improve its position. The Bears are also 4-2, but an NFC victory is the preferable outcome for the Jaguars. Chicago can celebrate all it wants; Jacksonville will happily accept a Patriots loss as a small win of its own. Pittsburgh Steelers at New Orleans Saints (Paris, France) Root for: New Orleans Saints The Steelers are another 4-2 AFC team that Jacksonville could be competing against for playoff positioning later in the season. Pittsburgh has made a solid start, and the last thing the Jaguars need is for it to keep building momentum. New Orleans has had its own struggles, but this is a straightforward rooting interest: give the Saints a reason to celebrate in Paris and send the Steelers home with a loss. If the French crowd can help deliver a little chaos, all the better. San Francisco 49ers at Atlanta Falcons Root for: Atlanta Falcons This one is less about a direct Jacksonville rival and more about taking advantage of an NFC-versus-NFC matchup. San Francisco is unbeaten at 6-0 and looks like one of the NFC’s leading contenders, while Atlanta has had a more difficult start. Neither result directly changes the Jaguars’ AFC standing, so this is a chance to root for the underdog and see whether the Falcons can spoil the 49ers ‘ perfect record. Jacksonville fans can enjoy the spectacle without worrying about an AFC rival gaining ground. Cincinnati Bengals at Baltimore Ravens Ja’Marr Chase in his last 4 games vs. the Ravens: – 699 Receiving Yards (174.8 YPG) – 38 Receptions – 5 Touchdowns #Bengals #WhoDey pic.twitter.com/EdQZldzN65 — 937Bengals 🐅 (@BengalsinDa937) October 21, 2026 Root for: Cincinnati Bengals This is one of the trickier games of the weekend because both teams are AFC contenders, and somebody has to take the victory. Baltimore is 4-2, while Cincinnati is also firmly in the playoff conversation. A Bengals win would hand the Ravens a damaging loss and potentially tighten the race among the AFC’s Wild Card hopefuls. Neither team is an ideal winner from Jacksonville’s perspective, but if we have to pick one, let’s see Baltimore stumble. The Jaguars have enough to worry about in their own division without the Ravens making life more difficult elsewhere. Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Carolina Panthers Root for: Carolina Panthers This one is a little more complicated than simply backing the NFC team, because there could be a Jacksonville angle worth watching if things continue to unravel in Tampa Bay. The Buccaneers have stumbled to a 1-5 start, putting Todd Bowles under increasing pressure, and if the organization decides to make a change, it could look toward a familiar face from Liam Coen’s coaching tree. Jaguars offensive coordinator Grant Udinski has already emerged as a potential candidate for the job, and Tampa Bay could be tempted to try to poach another of Jacksonville’s rising offensive minds. A Panthers win would pile further pressure on the Buccaneers and potentially make that coaching conversation a little more interesting. Jacksonville fans should be rooting for Carolina here, because the last thing the Jaguars need is an NFC South rival getting ideas about raiding their coaching staff. New York Giants at Houston Texans Root for: New York Giants Here is one of the weekend’s biggest games for Jaguars fans, even if the matchup itself might not immediately jump off the page. Houston just beat Jacksonville at Wembley, cutting into the Jaguars’ advantage in the AFC South. The Texans are 2-4, so the Jags still currently enjoy a lead, but their head-to-head victory makes them a more dangerous opponent than their record suggests. A Giants win would stop Houston from building a winning streak and give Jacksonville a little breathing room while it rests. If the Texans could lose every remaining game without affecting Jacksonville’s own schedule, that would be lovely, too. Indianapolis Colts at Minnesota Vikings We have relieved Chris Ballard of his duties as General Manager. pic.twitter.com/BleD6bfTsG — Indianapolis Colts (@Colts) October 19, 2026 Root for: Minnesota Vikings The Colts are another AFC South rival, which makes this one simple. Indianapolis is 2-4 and has already lost ground in the division, but Jacksonville should not give it an opportunity to recover. Minnesota is unbeaten at 5-0 and has been one of the NFL’s strongest teams, so the Vikings are well positioned to take care of business at home. A Colts loss would keep them well behind the Jaguars and make the division race a little less stressful. The departure of Indy’s GM Chris Ballard this week adds a little intrigue, but is largely irrelevant to Jags fans. There is no need to overthink this one: Skol, Vikings. Miami Dolphins at New York Jets Root for: Miami Dolphins Neither AFC East team has made a convincing start, but the Jets have two wins compared with Miami’s winless record. That makes New York the more immediate concern if it can start stringing victories together. A Dolphins win would hand the Jets another loss and help prevent them from becoming a factor in the AFC Wild Card race. Yes, rooting for a winless team might feel strange, but this is a bye week rooting guide, not a popularity contest. If Miami can finally get something going, Jacksonville will gladly take the collateral benefit. Cleveland Browns at Tennessee Titans Root for: Cleveland Browns This is another non-negotiable one. Tennessee is 1-5, but the Titans are still a divisional rival, and Jacksonville needs to keep them down. Cleveland is 4-2 and could be a threat in the AFC Wild Card race, so this is not an entirely comfortable choice. However, the Browns are the better team to back here because a Titans loss is directly beneficial to Jacksonville’s chances of winning the AFC South. The Jaguars cannot afford to take divisional games for granted, even when their rivals are struggling. And let’s be honest – who doesn’t enjoy the misery emanating from Tennessee right now? full_text: (Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images) | Getty Images Each practice day this season, the Kansas City Chiefs release an official injury report ahead of the next game. In Week 7, the Chiefs play the Seattle Seahawks on “Sunday Night Football.” On Thursday, Kansas City placed left tackle Josh Simmons (Back) on the Reserve/Injured list after he didn’t practice on Wednesday. The Chiefs explained that Simmons plateaued in his rehabilitation and needed more time to return to 100%. For more information from the team’s Head Trainer Rick Burkholder, we covered his statement to local media here . Here is the Chiefs’ first official injury report of the week, courtesy of the team’s official website : Chiefs Wide receiver Rashee Rice (hamstring/knee) did not participate in practice for the second consecutive day. He tweaked his hamstring during the first quarter of the Week 4 win over the Las Vegas Raiders . He did not have the “Knee” designation on the injury report until this week. Right tackle Jaylon Moore (concussion) did not participate in practice again after entering the concussion protocol during the Week 6 win over the Los Angeles Chargers . Moore’s participation going forward is dependent on the contracted independent neurologist and completely out of the team and player’s hands. Cornerback L’Jarius Sneed (knee) was a limited participant in practice again. His time on the field is regularly managed due to a lingering knee issue. Tight end Travis Kelce (ankle) was a limited participant in practice again. Kelce briefly left in Week 6 against the Chargers and was seen multiple times having his ankle taped. Linebacker Cooper McDonald (knee) was a limited participant in practice for the second straight day. McDonald was placed on the team’s Reserve/Injured list after suffering a knee injury in Week 1. Although he has been “designated to return,” McDonald must be officially added to the active roster by Saturday in order to play against Seattle. The Chiefs seemingly opened a roster spot for McDonald by waiving linebacker Cam Jones on Tuesday. The following Chiefs players were full participants in practice: Wide receiver Cyrus Allen (knee) Safety Chamarri Conner (knee) Right guard Trey Smith (hip) Quarterback Patrick Mahomes (knee) Seahawks The team’s Senior Reporter John Boyle reported that running back Zach Charbonnet has been activated off the Physically Unable to Perform (PUP) list after full participation in Wednesday’s practice. Charbonnet has not played since the Seahawks’ Divisional Round win over the San Francisco 49ers last season. The backfield partner of Kenneth Walker in 2025 racked up 874 yards and 12 touchdowns last season. Veteran defensive end Demarcus Lawrence (non-injury related – rest) was a limited participant in practice on Thursday after sitting out on Wednesday. Starting outside linebacker Uchenne Nwosu (hip) popped up on Thursday’s injury report as a limited participant after not appearing on the list on Wednesday. Linebacker Connor O’Toole (hamstring), linebacker Chazz Surratt (calf) and linebacker Drake Thomas (ankle) did not participate in Wednesday’s ot Thursday’s practice. Former Missouri quarterback, the backup to Sam Darnold, Drew Lock (right elbow) was a limited participant in practice on both days this week. Wide receiver Rasheed Shaheed (hip), linebacker Tyrice Knight, and guards Anthony Bradford (knee) and Beau Stephens (knee) were full participants in Thursday’s practice after limited action on Wednesday. Check back in on Friday afternoon for the final injury report.

title: Steve Spagnuolo endorses Chris Roland-Wallace after ejection in Week 6
summary: On the first play of the fourth quarter in the Kansas City Chiefs’ Week 6 win over the Los Angeles Chargers, officials called offsetting unnecessary-roughness penalties. Chargers offensive lineman Alex Harkey shoved Chiefs safety Christian Roland-Wallace well after the play, and the young defender responded with a quick left-hand jab at Harkey. As often happens […]
full_text: (Photo by David Eulitt/Getty Images) | Getty Images On the first play of the fourth quarter in the Kansas City Chiefs ’ Week 6 win over the Los Angeles Chargers , officials called offsetting unnecessary-roughness penalties. Chargers offensive lineman Alex Harkey shoved Chiefs safety Christian Roland-Wallace well after the play, and the young defender responded with a quick left-hand jab at Harkey. As often happens in these situations, the agitator gets the best of the agitated. The penalties offset, but Roland-Wallace was disqualified from his best game of the season. In 20 defensive snaps, he had four tackles (three solo), including one for loss. The moment was disappointing to see from an ascending player in Kansas City’s secondary; Week 6 marked his first start of the season. To Roland-Wallace’s credit, he is making a concerted effort to put the play behind him and move forward. Defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo shared his response to the ejection during his press conference on Thursday. “I didn’t get a chance to actually see him right after that, but true to his character, first thing Monday morning, he’s apologizing for it,” Spagnuolo told reporters. If there was worry that the play would put Roland-Wallace in the doghouse, Spags made it clear that the third-year member of the secondary has built up a strong enough reputation to put it behind them. “That’s not him,” Spags said. “I just think the emotion got the best of him, and I don’t think you’ll ever see him get in that situation again. That’s just how I feel about Chris; he’s solid as a rock.” It’s a positive note on an important role player in the Chiefs’ Dime formations (6 defensive backs). Roland-Wallace has often manned the slot opposite cornerback L’Jarius Sneed when the defense spreads out against pass-minded offenses and has allowed only 28 receiving yards on five catches, according to Pro Football Focus . Against the Chargers, he allowed just three yards on three receptions. He has also generated quarterback pressure three times over five blitzes. As the season wears on, Roland-Wallace’s role could grow within the scheme, and a bad moment in Week 6 doesn’t sound like it will stop that momentum.

title: Josh Simmons to IR, ‘needs more time to return to full function’
summary: After the Kansas City Chiefs’ Wednesday injury report revealed that left tackle Josh Simmons did not practice with both a “back” and “personal” designation, the ears of Chiefs Kingdom perked up. On Thursday, the team had Vice President of Sports Medicine and Performance Rick Burkholder go to the podium to explain the setback for Simmons, […]
full_text: (Photo by Scott Winters/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images After the Kansas City Chiefs ’ Wednesday injury report revealed that left tackle Josh Simmons did not practice with both a “back” and “personal” designation, the ears of Chiefs Kingdom perked up. On Thursday, the team had Vice President of Sports Medicine and Performance Rick Burkholder go to the podium to explain the setback for Simmons, who practiced in a limited capacity last week. Burkholder revealed that Simmons would be placed on the Reserve/Injured list because his rehabilitation has “plateaued.” He will miss at least the next four weeks of games and practices, and if he is reactivated after that point, he would have up to 21 days to practice before returning to play. We have placed T Josh Simmons on Reserve/Injured. — Kansas City Chiefs (@Chiefs) October 22, 2026 The team announced Simmons was put on IR roughly an hour after Burkholder’s press conference. Here is the entire timeline Burkholder provided on Simmons’ back injury, starting during training camp in St. Joseph, Missouri. “On August 17th, Josh came to me with calf discomfort, feeling that he couldn’t post on a single leg in training camp practices,” Burkholder told local media. “This was the same leg that he had knee surgery on in 2024. He was evaluated by our physicians who, thankfully, suspected a low-back injury instead of a lower-leg or knee ailment.” In 2024, playing for Ohio State, Simmons tore his patellar tendon, which ended his season. “We obtained an MRI in St. Joe that confirmed that he had a bulging, herniated disc in his lumbar spine,” Burkholder clarified. “That disc problem was higher up than what we normally see in our offensive linemen, which complicated the case.” “We recommended a second opinion, as we always do with all of our injured guys, and through his agent and Josh, they selected a spine specialist in California that we have used previously, and that is really well-known in the NFL. He went there and was evaluated, and the recommendation was to do rehabilitation — not surgery — with the intent that we would do an MRI in the future to see what the disc looked like.” “Josh continued to progress, and the repeat MRI a few weeks later showed that the disc had improved, so no surgery was recommended and rehab would continue.” With no surgery necessary, head coach Andy Reid said Simmons had a “ramp-up” period starting with the limited practices last week. That process has now come to a halt. “Josh worked his tail off; he worked diligently with my staff every day and has improved to the point where he returned to practice in a limited capacity last week. However, we feel that he has plateaued in the rehab process as he’s trying to get to the final steps of recovery with return to competition, and he’s just not there yet.” Burkholder emphasized that final statement: “He’s just not there yet.” Simmons’ job on the field is to wrestle the world’s top athletes weighing over 250 pounds up to 80 times a game. His back is not ready to do that this week, and it won’t be ready for the next few weeks either. “After discussion with Josh yesterday, we gave him some time to talk with his family and representatives to investigate next steps as he goes through this process, and that’s why he was listed as both personal and with the back injury… he took the day off to get with his people.” “It was decided and agreed upon by everybody — his people, his agent, him, myself, Andy, and Veach — that he should be placed on IR to give him more time to return to full function. He’ll continue with the rehab process with the goal of returning to play at the high level that he achieved in the past.” Here are Rick Burkholder's full comments on #Chiefs LT Josh Simmons: pic.twitter.com/jpIcod2zWb — Marleah Campbell (@MarleahKCTV5) October 22, 2026 The earliest Simmons could return is the Week 11 home game against the Arizona Cardinals . “I give a lot of credit to Josh, my docs, my physicians and my staff,” Burkholder said. “I just give them a ton of credit for navigating through this injury to the point where surgery is not recommended, and that he just needs more time to return to full function.”

title: The Chiefs are one of the best tackling teams in the NFL
summary: Through five games, the Kansas City Chiefs’ defense has been unquestionably sound. The unit ranks in the top 10 in points allowed, yards allowed, third-down conversion rate and red-zone conversion rate. It isn’t flashy at times, but the statistics back up the bend-don’t-break ability of defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo’s unit. When it comes to tackling, […]
full_text: (Photo by David Eulitt/Getty Images) | Getty Images Through five games, the Kansas City Chiefs ’ defense has been unquestionably sound. The unit ranks in the top 10 in points allowed, yards allowed, third-down conversion rate and red-zone conversion rate. It isn’t flashy at times, but the statistics back up the bend-don’t-break ability of defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo’s unit. When it comes to tackling, the numbers and the eye test match up: the Chiefs are one of the league’s best tackling teams. According to Pro Football Focus , the Chiefs have the NFL’s lowest missed-tackle rate. Pro Football Reference has the Chiefs c redited with 20 missed tackles this year , the fourth-fewest in the league. According to Sumer Sports , the Chiefs had the league’s lowest missed-tackle rate through four weeks (7.4%) ; the league average was 11.9% at the time of the post. When you look at the individuals that make up Kansas City’s defense, most of its back-end players have a missed-tackle rate in the single digits ( PFF ): Linebacker Nick Bolton (7.4%) Linebacker Drue Tranquill (2.7%) Cornerback L’Jarius Sneed (6.5%) Cornerback Mansoor Delane (8.7%) Safety Jaden Hicks (6.9%) Cornerback Nohl Williams (15%) Safety Alohi Gilman (5.6%) Slot defender Christian Roland-Wallace (No missed tackles) Cornerback Kristian Fulton (No missed tackles) Safety Chamarri Conner (No missed tackles) Chiefs' CB room should be nicknamed The Pound Dogs only pic.twitter.com/RYOkUQ2jb7 — Ron Kopp Jr (@RonOnChiefs) October 20, 2026 In the Week 6 win over the Los Angeles Chargers , the defensive backfield’s tackling was especially on display. Roland-Wallace has stood out in this respect, although he was ejected in this game for throwing a punch. The rookie, Mansoor Delane, has arguably been the most impactful tackler in the back end despite missing time. He has eight Stops this year, tackles that constitute a failure for the offense, and only Sneed has more from the Chiefs’ secondary. The cornerback room’s highest missed-tackle rate comes from Nohl Williams, who has clearly shown the physicality and aggression needed to defend runs and quick passes to his side. If there’s one thing Spags’ unit can hang their hat on right now, it’s tackling. It’s a big reason why the unit has allowed the fifth-fewest runs of 10 or more yards this year (11), according to NFL Next Gen Stats . As the pass rush gains momentum and the team sharpens its slot-receiver coverage, Chiefs Kingdom should be able to trust that its defenders bring ball carriers to the ground as often as any team in the league.

title: Patrick Mahomes praises rookie  Cyrus Allen’s contested catches
summary: Amid injuries at wide receiver, the Kansas City Chiefs asked unproven players to step up in the Week 6 win over the Los Angeles Chargers. Rookie Cyrus Allen was one of them, catching two passes for 27 yards in a season-high five-snap appearance. On both catches, Allen was met with contact soon after, but the […]
full_text: (Photo by Jamie Squire/Getty Images) | Getty Images Amid injuries at wide receiver, the Kansas City Chiefs asked unproven players to step up in the Week 6 win over the Los Angeles Chargers . Rookie Cyrus Allen was one of them, catching two passes for 27 yards in a season-high five-snap appearance. On both catches, Allen was met with contact soon after, but the receiver, listed at 5 feet 11 inches and 180 pounds, impressed his quarterback by playing through it. When asked about Allen at the podium on Wednesday, Patrick Mahomes pointed to Allen’s ability at the catch point. “I thought he did a great job of making contested catches,” Mahomes reflected. “Obviously, the one-on-one man coverage on third down didn’t get the first down,” Mahomes said. “But got himself open and almost got it.” Allen was barely forced out of bounds, nearly tiptoeing his way past the chains. “And then the one down the middle was a big time catch in between a lot of traffic.“ “So that’s stuff we saw from him in training camp,” Mahomes continued. “I think now that he’s getting more and more comfortable within the offense, we’ll continue to give him more and more of a role within the offense.” Mahomes threw a third pass Allen’s way against the Chargers, and it helped move the chains. On second-and-6, a downfield, back-shoulder fade attempt to the rookie drew a defensive pass interference flag. Allen appears to have the route-running chops to win quickly out of the slot, but as Mahomes said, the throws into tight windows are what got Chiefs Kingdom excited in training camp. He has company in the young receiving corps, whether it’s second-year wideout Jalen Royals or practice-squad elevation candidate Andrew Armstrong, but Allen can build on the flashes we saw against the Chargers and earn more throws his way moving forward. “He’s got a lot of talent, and he plays fast, and he plays hard,” Mahomes said. “Now it’s about just continuing to give him confidence to go out there and make plays happen. And so, I’m sure that we’ll continue to get him more and more involved as the year goes on.”

title: Los Angeles Chargers news: Omarion Hampton still ranked highly among 2nd-year backs
summary: It’s been a rough season thus far for Omarion Hampton. He was supposed to be one of the best young backs in the league. NFL insider Jordan Schultz at one point made a bold prediction that Hampton would lead the NFL in scrimmage yards while finishing with 12+ touchdowns. He’s currently barely on pace for […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - OCTOBER 18: Linebacker Nick Bolton #32 of the Kansas City Chiefs tackles running back Omarion Hampton #8 of the Los Angeles Chargers in the second quarter at Arrowhead Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by David Eulitt/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s been a rough season thus far for Omarion Hampton. He was supposed to be one of the best young backs in the league. NFL insider Jordan Schultz at one point made a bold prediction that Hampton would lead the NFL in scrimmage yards while finishing with 12+ touchdowns. He’s currently barely on pace for that amount of touchdowns and you can’t lead the league in yards from scrimmage if you are barely on the field. That’s what it’s been like for the 23-year old who came into the league with the expectation that he’d be a lead guy for a team. Hard to imagine he’s in any kind of good spirits since the two lost fumbles in the first two weeks of this season. But despite that, outside of the team, there are believers. Take Bleacher Report’s Gary Davenport who just recently re-ranked the second-year backs in the league. Hampton came in third, behind only Ashton Jeanty and TreyVeon Henderson. “ Omarion Hampton has had little opportunity to establish a rhythm. ” “ When the 23-year-old was drafted 22nd overall last year, it was with the expectation that he would be the Chargers’ lead back from the jump. He was widely considered a first-round talent after a wildly productive two-season stretch at North Carolina. ” “ An ankle injury sidelined Hampton for almost half his rookie season, but he was effective when available. He averaged 4.4 yards per carry, scored five touchdowns and contributed just under 82 total yards per game. Then 2026 rolled around, and the wheels came off. ” “The winless Chargers are a mess, and Mike McDaniel’s decision to use a three-back committee has done little to help Hampton find his groove. Hampton has exceeded 15 carries just once this season, while his yards-per-carry average has dropped by nearly a full yard. ” “ The talent is there, but the situation is a nightmare. ” Do you think Davenport is correct to still hold Hampton in such high regard? Should he be lower based on his current situation? Let us know below! And now for today’s links. title: Puka Nacua injured in Rams’ Thursday practice
summary: Los Angeles Rams star Puka Nacua left Thursday’s practice with a calf injury and will be listed as limited on the injury report. The Rams are already dealing with the loss of Davante Adams for 6-10 weeks, and now Nacua is in danger of missing Sunday’s game against the Las Vegas Raiders. Are the L.A. […]
full_text: Los Angeles Rams star Puka Nacua left Thursday’s practice with a calf injury and will be listed as limited on the injury report. The Rams are already dealing with the loss of Davante Adams for 6-10 weeks, and now Nacua is in danger of missing Sunday’s game against the Las Vegas Raiders. Are the L.A. Rams having the worst injury week in franchise history? Rams WR Puka Nacua left practice early today due to a calf injury. pic.twitter.com/YDtwN3XyCx — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) October 22, 2026 The Rams placed Kobie Turner on injury reserve this week, as well as Poona Ford. They did not active Myles Garrett from IR and there is no imminent return expected for Terrance Ferguson. L.A. also placed kicker Blake Grupe on IR with a torn ACL. Trent McDuffie was held out of the last game and his status for Week 7 is also uncertain. Nate Landman is on the injury report too . This is just a historically bad week with the addition of Nacua to the injury report, and he already sat out weeks two and three. For Nacua, the 2026 season also represents a turning point in his life financially. The Rams have not extended him despite being a superstar and a 2027 free agent, likely partially related to his injury history, as well as his off-field exploits. Now Nacua is on a 2-4 team that is falling well short of expectations and putting players on IR left and right, it’s hard to not think of this as a repeat of 2022. That’s when the Rams started off the season so bad that by the end of the year it felt like everyone was on IR, including Matthew Stafford, Cooper Kupp, and Aaron Donald. If Nacua misses this game, Stafford’s top-two targets would be anyone’s guess.

title: Rams could help resurrect this receiver’s career with trade
summary: The Los Angeles Rams could have another wide receiver trade target in their sights in Jerry Jeudy of the Cleveland Browns. Now in his seventh year in the NFL, Jeudy is still just 27, and despite not quite living up to being a top-15 draft pick, he’s still been a productive player throughout his career. […]
full_text: The Los Angeles Rams could have another wide receiver trade target in their sights in Jerry Jeudy of the Cleveland Browns. Now in his seventh year in the NFL, Jeudy is still just 27, and despite not quite living up to being a top-15 draft pick, he’s still been a productive player throughout his career. He could immediately replace a large portion of Davante Adams’s snaps now that the latter is out for 6-10 weeks , which would help buoy the Rams’ struggling offense at least a bit. Trade deadline receiver targets The Athletic first tied Jeudy to Los Angeles on Thursday in their 50-player NFL trade deadline big board. Regarding Jeudy, The Athletic’s Daniel Popper wrote: The Todd Monken-led Browns are rolling, sitting atop the AFC North at 4-2. Jeudy has become more of a role player with the emergence of rookies Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion. Still, he is making an impact in Cleveland. He caught a 33-yard pass on the Browns’ winning field goal drive in the fourth quarter against the Ravens, hauling in an in-breaker before finding open grass down the left sideline. The likelihood of a Jeudy trade seems low. Winning teams tend to hang onto good players. But the diminished role might leave the door slightly ajar. 2026 Trade Deadline Big Board From dream swings to more realistic options, I ranked 50 players who could be available on the trade market. Projected cap hits, best fits, analysis and more: https://t.co/sZ0Rm9q4D9 — Daniel Popper (@danielrpopper) October 22, 2026 For what it’s worth, Popper listed the Rams as a best fit for Jeudy alongside the San Francisco 49ers, Pittsburgh Steelers and Kansas City Chiefs, all of whom also have obvious deficiencies at wide receiver. Jeudy wouldn’t be as exciting of a trade target as Brian Thomas Jr. of the Jacksonville Jaguars, whose name came up earlier this week . And, admittedly, there are a few different concerns at play. He’s been criticized for drop issues in the past, and as Popper pointed out, he’s not exactly a featured piece in Cleveland anymore due to their rookies’ emergence. Plus, his contract situation isn’t especially favorable, though smart teams like Los Angeles can mess around with those details to make it work. It’s also worth noting the same issue with a potential Thomas trade, that good teams don’t typically like to trade useful players. Debate all you want about how “good” the Browns actually are, but they’re leading their division through six weeks. That’s an enviable position to be in. #Browns WR Jerry Jeudy asked if he's heard the trade buzz: "I mean you see it around, but you don't do (anything) about it. You see it, but you can't do (anything) about it. You just keep continuing to do what you do everyday.' On if he's had talks with Andrew Berry: "I'm going… pic.twitter.com/l0Pu9EpVMr — 92.3 The Fan (@923TheFan) October 21, 2026 Jerry Jeudy’s potential impact But if you’re trying to make a run to a Super Bowl, or at least back to relevancy (in terms of the standings, not brand recognition), you have to take chances. It’s not as if Jeudy is a bad player, just not a true superstar. He would immediately add more juice to a wide receiver room that currently looks alarming. The Rams don’t need to make a move just for the sake of making a move, but at positions of need they also can’t afford to be too choosy. One, the season is already a third over and they have plenty of ground to make up. Secondly, it’s simply not easy to find franchise-shifting players at the trade deadline. It’s not a perfect fit, but Jerry Jeudy is at least a functional player with a skill set that should mesh well with Matthew Stafford’s traditional desire to push the ball down the field. In a best-case scenario, he could even help reinvigorate that part of the offense. One way or another, the Rams have to be willing to gamble on an imperfect player if they want to shore up their receiver corps midway through the season.
author: Brendan Dzwierzynski

title: Rams have signed 9 different kickers since Greg Zuerlein left
summary: The Los Angeles Rams parted ways with kicker Greg Zuerlein in 2020 to get younger, and perhaps a little cheaper at the position, as the veteran was coming off of his worst season with the team. Little did Sean McVay realize that six years later, the Rams would be trying out 42-year-old Matt Prater (that’s […]
full_text: The Los Angeles Rams parted ways with kicker Greg Zuerlein in 2020 to get younger, and perhaps a little cheaper at the position, as the veteran was coming off of his worst season with the team. Little did Sean McVay realize that six years later, the Rams would be trying out 42-year-old Matt Prater (that’s four years older than Zuerlein is today, by the way) and cycling through multiple kickers midseason for the fourth time since Zuerlein’s departure. The Rams can afford a minimum of $20 million for a reunion with Aaron Donald after two years away from football, but their frugality on special teams over a fraction of that money bites them every season. The recently-signed Brandon McManus is L.A.’s 10th different kicker since 2019, including Zuerlein. If you include Ethan Evans, who kicked an extra point on Sunday, that’s another. This chart shows which teams have signed the most kickers since 2019, with the Rams’ soon going up from 9 to 10 when McManus takes the field against the Las Vegas Raiders: Only the Jets, Titans, and Commanders have had more. But the season isn’t over yet … Greg Zuerlein left When the Rams parted with Zuerlein in 2020, he was coming off of a season in which he went 5-of-11 between 40-49 yards, which is really bad. The team let him move on and he signed with the Cowboys to reunite with fired special teams coordinator John Fassel. It’s not as though Zuerlein is specifically a big loss. He spent two years with the Cowboys, then 2.5 years with the Jets, and he hasn’t kicked since 2024. But the Rams replaced Zuerlein by holding a three-way competition between seventh-rounder Sam Sloman, Austin MacGinnis, and Lirim Hajrullahu . There’s a reason that none of these names are notable unless you’re someone who likes obscure Rams trivia. It’s because L.A. didn’t seek a good kicker. They sought out a cheap kicker. Sloman won the job. He lasted seven games. The Rams signed Kai Forbath. He suffered an ankle injury after two games. The Rams signed Matt Gay and that was a lucky find in the middle of the season. But McVay lamented their decision process at the time , just months after he endorsed Sloman: “Sometimes you don’t realize how good you have it until you don’t anymore, and I think that’s the honest answer,” McVay said about Zuerlein being gone. “I think it’s been a struggle. It’s been something that I know we’re working on and guys are certainly trying to get it figured out.” Matt Gay era The Rams first signed Gay to a two-year deal that kept him through 2021, then RFA tender that helped them retain his rights for cheap in 2022. The key word being “cheap”. Gay made over 92% of his field goal attempts with the Rams and made the Pro Bowl in 2021. Making the Pro Bowl was his first mistake. Gay signed a four-year, $22 million contract with the Colts in 2023, way out of L.A.’s price range. After all, they need that money for guys like Tutu Atwell and Allen Robinson! 59-yard field goal ‼️ A new career long for Matt Gay! LVvsLAC on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/oynUzQH41x — NFL (@NFL) September 20, 2026 Gay had a few struggles with the Colts and there after, but he’ll be on the field against the Rams as a member of the Raiders this weekend. He’s 32 years old and he’s 14-of-15 on field goal attempts in 2026. He hasn’t missed an extra point. 2023-Present Needing more volatility and uncertainty at the position, the Rams held a competition between Tanner Brown and Christopher Dunn in 2023. Neither of them were good enough to make the roster . Instead, L.A. signed Brett Maher at the last minute, a former Cowboys kicker with a strong leg and inconsistent accuracy. Maher was released on October 24 after a bad game against the Steelers. Did the Rams turn to one of their camp kickers? No. Like in 2020, they actually didn’t like the kickers who they tested all offseason. Instead they brought in Lucas Havrisik, who had been released by the Browns. Maher hasn’t kicked since 2023. Havrisik had a brief audition with the Packers in 2025. In 2024, the Rams drafted Joshua Karty in the sixth round. He was released in the middle of 2025 and hasn’t kicked for any team since then. The Rams replaced him with Harrison Mevis. He only lasted 14 games. He probably won’t kick for anybody again. There are only two themes at play here: The Rams don’t want a kicker who is established because that would make him “expensive” The Rams’ former kickers don’t pop up somewhere else and become good The only exception is Gay, but he was already good. That’s why the Rams didn’t keep him. He was a good free agent. Blake Grupe didn’t even last 5 minutes as a Rams kicker. Now the team turns to McManus, and he could soon be replaced by Prater. Hell, at this rate. Should we be surprised if the Rams kicker next season is … Greg Zuerlein?

title: Another Rams starter lands on injury report
summary: Linebacker Nate Landman could miss Week 7 after he entered the concussion protocol on Wednesday. The Los Angeles Rams have already lost several key starters this week, including Davante Adams and Kobie Turner, but now their top linebacker could be held out against the Las Vegas Raiders. What the Rams need is to be healthy, […]
full_text: Linebacker Nate Landman could miss Week 7 after he entered the concussion protocol on Wednesday. The Los Angeles Rams have already lost several key starters this week, including Davante Adams and Kobie Turner, but now their top linebacker could be held out against the Las Vegas Raiders. What the Rams need is to be healthy, and that’s not happening. Will L.A. get healthy? Will Myles Garrett play again this season? Things aren’t looking good. You know what would make things look better? If the Rams could find way to win on Sunday, but that looks less likely each day this week as the injuries continue to pile up. The team can say they aren’t giving up, but at a certain point this season will be lost, unless they can turn it around. The way the Rams turn this all around is with a win. Now, they may have to find a way to win without Landman. Rams LB Nate Landman in concussion protocol (ramswire) “Only missing one play, Landman recorded 71 snaps on Sunday during the team’s loss to the Arizona Cardinals , picking up 10 total tackles. Since joining the Rams last season, he has not missed a game for the franchise. This season, he has 51 total tackles (27 solo), six stuffs, and two forced fumbles. If he is unable to play, Omar Speights should be the player to step up in his role, while Shaun Dolac and Grant Stuard will serve as backups. Considering the team’s heavy use of their nickel and dime defense, Landman’s potential absence could lead to problems on the interior as they’re set to face the tight end duo of Brock Bowers and Michael Mayer this week when they play the Las Vegas Raiders .“ Rams Get Ominous Injury Timeline Update on Myles Garrett (sports.yahoo) “Rams head coach Sean McVay announced in Week 6 that Garrett would not return to action. McVay did the same ahead of Week 7. Unfortunately, it appears Rams fans could hear that familiar refrain for several more weeks. This comes as at least a mild surprise after previous reports suggested it was possible that Garrett could return in Week 7. Garrett also received a possible six-to-eight-week timeline, which would put his return at Weeks 8 through 10.“ Rams waiting to schedule Adams’ (hammy) surgery (nbcsports) “Surgeries are sometimes delayed to help reduce swelling. Occasionally, new information is gathered during this time and/or during the surgery. Adams is currently expected to be sidelined for 6-10 weeks. Perhaps the wide return-to-play timeline is due to the fact that the surgeon has not yet fully assessed the injury. We tentatively expect the team to share an updated recovery timeline once Adams undergoes the procedure on his ruptured hamstring tendon. Stay tuned.” Rams have no consolation prize waiting in 2027 draft (no matter how the season ends) (ramblinfan) “Los Angeles made 14 draft selections in 2023 . Shockingly, nine of those players are still with the team, and many are vital starters. That’s how the Rams were able to rebound so quickly. Rather than cling to veterans, they shed highly compensated stars, gathered as many draft picks as possible, and completely overhauled the roster. What felt like insanity at the time proved to be inspired wisdom. On a roster filled with holes, rookies easily earned starting roles. The team benefited from developing plug-and-play dynamos who have become the roster’s core. The gamble paid off with a jackpot. With a first-round draft pick, the Rams had to begin the rebuild in Round 2. They made the practical decision to commit their first three selections to addressing the line of scrimmage on both sides of the ball.“ Rams face another looming threat as Puka Nacua’s NFL review drags on (nypost) “Wide receiver Puka Nacua and left tackle Alaric Jackson remain under league review for off-field incidents, NFL spokesman Brian McCarthy told The California Post on Wednesday. There is no timeline for a decision in either matter. That leaves the Rams trying to rescue their season while waiting to learn whether their path will become even more difficult. The hope had been to build enough of a cushion in the standings to absorb potential suspensions. Instead, the Rams have left themselves little margin for error, and an injury to wide receiver Davante Adams has further complicated their situation.“ CELEBRITY PHOTOS: Blue Man Group, Travis Bennett, Jordan McCullough & more celebrities in attendance at SoFi Stadium for the Rams’ Week 6 matchup vs. the Cardinals (therams) “The stars were out at SoFi Stadium on Sunday! Swipe through photos of Blue Man Group, Travis Bennett, Jordan McCullough & more celebs in attendance as the Los Angeles Rams took on the Arizona Cardinals in Week 6.” Matthew Stafford and Puka Nacua discuss Rams’ loss to Cardinals in postgame press conference (nfl.com) “Los Angeles Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford and wide receiver Puka Nacua discuss the Rams’ loss to the Arizona Cardinals in the postgame press conference” Rams drop in Week 7 power rankings (therams) “Here is the power ranking roundup heading into Week 7. USA Today : 13 As they enter a new Bill Parcells reality − “You are what your record says you are” − the Rams (2-4) have also added injuries to Sunday’s (latest) insult. Moving forward, they won’t have WR Davante Adams (hamstring) or DL Kobie Turner for at least the next month. NT Poona Ford is out for the year. And the kicker? Sean McVay needs another one of those, too.“ The Rams and Chargers are both a mess, and it’s only getting worse (sports.yahoo) “The preseason hype surrounding football in Los Angeles was real. The Rams made bold, splashy moves to tweak an already stellar team and presumably turn them into a monster. The Chargers retooled their coaching staff, adding vaunted offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel in a move assumed would finally get the hapless franchise over the hump and into contention. Fast-forward six weeks and both organizations are a dumpster fire. The Rams (2-4) have drastically underperformed their potential, losing to the Cardinals over the weekend and finding themselves at the bottom of the NFC West with no clear way to catch up. The Chargers (0-6) are even worse, boasting one of the worst offenses in the NFL, hurtling towards a No. 1 overall pick, with a coaching staff that seems incapable of turning the ship around. The idea of an all-Los Angeles, Chargers vs. Rams Super Bowl at SoFi Stadium didn’t feel like it was outside the realm of possibility at one point. Now the notion of putting these teams together on football’s brightest stage is a hilarious joke. Neither team is likely to make the playoffs at all, and everything that could go wrong, has.“ Comment of the day: “We’re going with a guy who used to be good but hasn’t been recently. Sounds like a good plan. I am losing my trust in this organizations ability to make good decisions. I am very interested to see what happens against the Raiders. If we split with the Sea Hawks, lose to the Niners and Chiefs, and win every other remaining game, we would be 10-7 which may not be good enough with tie breakers. That’s our margin for error to be a wild card. It is possible but highly unlikely considering the way we are playing. It’s very possible for us to win the next 4 and then things get much more difficult. However, this week is probably the toughest of the next 4. It will be interesting to see what we’re made of. After losing to the Cardinals, it’s tough to feel like we’ve just been unlucky since it wasn’t a fluke and they flat out played us. It was really a must win and we didn’t show up. Hopefully we’ll get it together this week.“ -JWgorams Feed post of the day:

title: Klint Kubiak knows his Raiders must course correct in the red zone
summary: Klint Kubiak is clearly a big baller, shot caller, of a play caller. That was the reputation the 39-year-old built as an offensive coordinator and a big reason why the Las Vegas Raiders were deliberate and patient in hiring the hot shot as the new head coach this offseason. And through six games in the […]
full_text: (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images Klint Kubiak is clearly a big baller, shot caller, of a play caller. That was the reputation the 39-year-old built as an offensive coordinator and a big reason why the Las Vegas Raiders were deliberate and patient in hiring the hot shot as the new head coach this offseason. And through six games in the 2026 campaign with the rookie lead man helming the Silver & Black, Kubiak has nearly doubled the offensive output with this rendition of the Raiders compared to six games in 2025. With 162 total points and averaging 27 points per game, Kubiak’s offense is the sixth-ranked scoring group amongst the 32 NFL teams and is a torrential downpour compared to the output Las Vegas had last season with an anemic 86 total points and an average of 14.3 points per contest. The Silver & Black’s high mark at 3-3 overall was in a 35-27 victory at the New Orleans Saints with the low point in a 45-17 defeat at the New England Patriots, in terms of point production. In comparison, the Raiders were 2-4 last season with twin 24 outputs in Week 3 and 4 (both losses) as high points and a meager six points the low point in Week 5. Hence Kubiak’s rightful disappointment after losses this season. He’s taking ownership of the shortfalls in both post game press conferences and media sessions throughout the week as his team lost three-straight games. Particularly on offense as he makes the obvious crystal clear: Kubiak the one with the play sheet and the one delivering calls to trusty veteran quarterback Kirk Cousins. “Yeah, that’s the expectation. We have really talented players and that was the expectation to bounce back,” Kubiak said after the 33-30 loss to the Buffalo Bills this past Sunday. “That’s the type of football that we need to play, but we got to do it for four quarters. We’ve got to get the ball in the red zone. We’re 2-for-5 in the red zone, and that’s unacceptable. And that starts with me.” Kirk Cousins ➡️ Tre Tucker for the TD! BUFvsLV on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/Gl1Uln47Gx — NFL (@NFL) October 18, 2026 Ah, red zone. It’s an unquestioned area of opportunity for a bright mind like Kubiak. The skinny: Out of 23 visits to area between the opponent’s 20-yard line and goal line, the Raiders offense totals 12 red zone touchdowns. That’s 11 trips without an end zone visits giving Kubiak an overall 52.2 red zone percentage — which ranks 21st. Now imagine how much more potent Las Vegas offense would be if even one of those 11 trips was a touchdown instead? Perhaps the tale of the Week 6 loss would be different if Kubiak’s offense found the end zone just one more time instead of going 2-for-5? (For reference: The unbeaten San Francisco 49ers own the best red zone percentage at 85 percent (17 touchdowns on 20 visits), with the 2-4 Saints second at 84.2 percent (16 touchdowns on 19 visits). The bottom dwellers are the 2-4 New York Jets (dead last at 37.5 percent six touchdowns on 16 attempts) and the 4-2 Cleveland Browns (46.2 percent, six touchdowns on 13 attempts.) Kubiak expanded on the myriad of issues that continue to haunt his Raiders — particular in the loss to the Billls — in the money zone this past Monday. “Yes, well, key fourth and one, we have a penalty. We lost. We dropped the ball in the red zone in two-minute, right before half, had an opportunity to go score before half. Didn’t get it done. Penalties, lack of execution. It’s not one thing,” Kubiak explained. “But I think mainly when you want to be a good red zone team, you got to run the ball well in the red zone. We didn’t do that.” The lack of coaching and player execution is hurting Las Vegas when it’s within striking distance of the end zone and Cousins echoed Kubiak’s statements. “You had the first and goal from the two that we were unable to go forward, and then we had the incompletion. I’ll go back and watch the tape, but I felt like whether it’s staying with Brock (Bowers) there, even though he was doubled and had tough leverage, you stay with him, or you put a better ball on Cody (White),” Cousins said immediately after the loss to Buffalo. “Those are the things we’ll be talking about tomorrow, and then honestly the other several possessions run together right now. But anytime you leave points on the board in the red zone, it’s hard.” "I like the Raiders and I think Klint Kubiak is a very good football coach.. I think they have the start of something special in Las Vegas" ~ @JJWatt #PMSLive pic.twitter.com/foJf4PAFMH — Pat McAfee (@PatMcAfeeShow) October 21, 2026 Kubiak isn’t alone in the red zone plight. His chosen defensive coordinator, fellow rookie Rob Leonard, is also wallowing in impotence in the same area — and then some. In total, opponents visited the Raiders red zone 23 times so far and on 17 of those occasions got into the end zone. That 73.9 conversion rate gives Leonard’s group the 26th ranking in that regard. And this past Sunday, the Bills finished 3-for-5 in the money zone. (For reference: The 1-4-1 Washington Commanders allow a league-high 81.8 conversion rate in the red zone (18 touchdowns on 22 attempts) with the 3-2 Detroit Lions right behind at 81 percent (17 TDs on 21 visits). The stingiest teams are the 5-0 Minnesota Vikings (25 percent, just three touchdowns on 12 visits) and the 5-0 Kansas City Chiefs (33.3 percent, four touchdowns on 12 attempts).) Overall, Leonard’s defense allowed 162 total points in six games (27 points per game average) giving Las Vegas the 26th-ranked group in points allowed. In comparison, the 2025 Raiders defense allowed 149 total points (24.8 points per game average) through a similar point in time last year — hence the “and them some” portion above. This 2026 Raiders team is scoring and giving up more points than the previous year’s squad. “We got to the quarterback twice, got two sacks. You know, number 17 (Josh Allen) is one of the best in the free world at extending plays,” Kubiak said of the defense’s performance against Buffalo last Sunday. “I think he only had five yards rushing, but he definitely made plays with his legs moving and throwing off schedule. But overall, if you’re going to win the game, it’s about limiting points, and we have to limit points in the red zone.” One of the red zone conversions the Bills had in Week 6 included a dazzling and disconcerting (depending on if you root for Buffalo or Las Vegas) play where quarterback Josh Allen was able to evade defenders and flip the ball to wide open wide receiver Keon Coleman to lift Buffalo’s lead to 23-13 in the third quarter: JOSH ALLEN DOING JOSH ALLEN THINGS!!!! 📺: CBS pic.twitter.com/F0GGilwmd6 — Buffalo Bills (@BuffaloBills) October 18, 2026 Talk as they might, the time for action from Kubiak, Leonard, and the rest of the Raiders coaching staff and players was a while ago. But there’s plenty of opportunities in the remaining 11 games of the 2026 slate for the team to course correct. On offense, Las Vegas needs to resuscitate a flat-lined ground game — especially within striking distance of the end zone. A sharper quarterback-pass catcher timing would also do wonders as windows shrink massively in the area inside the 20-yard line. All of which can help the Raiders finish drives with six points instead of three points off the foot of accurate veteran kicker Matt Gay (who is 3-for-3 from 20 to 29 yards out and 4-for-4 30 to 49 yards out). Defensively, becoming more physical and dominant inside the 20 is a must-do. Also coverage in the red zone as miscommunication and blown assignments have left pass catchers and ball carriers open to punch it in. Defensive linemen and edge rushers alike need to anchor and pressure while linebackers and defensive backs flow and close passing windows more rapidly than what’s been seen. Acknowledging the red zone issue is a sound first step. Executing the improvement plan is another. But Kubiak and Co. have no other choice but to execute.
author: Ray Aspuria

title: Mike Washington Jr. misses Las Vegas Raiders’ Thursday practice ahead of Week 7 Los Angeles Rams’ matchup
summary: Las Vegas Raiders running back Mike Washington Jr. was absent during the media viewing portion of Thursday’s practice ahead of the Week 7 matchup against the Los Angeles Rams, according to The Athletic’s Sam Warren. Washington was listed as a limited participant with foot and back injuries during Wednesday’s session, but was listed as a […]
full_text: (Photo by Morgan Simmons/Getty Images) | Getty Images Las Vegas Raiders running back Mike Washington Jr. was absent during the media viewing portion of Thursday’s practice ahead of the Week 7 matchup against the Los Angeles Rams , according to The Athletic’s Sam Warren . Mike Washington Jr. is not here with the Raiders RB group to start practice. He was limited yesterday with foot and back injuries. pic.twitter.com/O2e9yBP08p — Sam Warren (@samwarren83) October 22, 2026 Washington was listed as a limited participant with foot and back injuries during Wednesday’s session, but was listed as a non-participant on Thursday’s injury report. So, it appears he suffered a setback. The fourth-round pick has been the second back behind Ashton Jeanty through the first six games this season but had 10 touches for 50 yards from scrimmage last week against the Buffalo Bills, including nine rushes for 43 yards . His role is expected to increase as the Silver and Black figure out their rushing woes, ranking 30th in the NFL for total rushing yards and 31st in yards per attempt this fall. Obviously, that requires Washington to be healthy, though. Meanwhile, Jeanty, who has also battled injuries this year, hasn’t been listed on the injury report this week and appears to be a full go. So, if Washington isn’t available, the offense will still have its lead back, barring a significant change in the coming days. In other injury news, defensive tackle Tonka Hemingway was spotted wearing a red, non-contact jersey on Thursday, per Warren . Hemingway suffered a concussion against the New England Patriots two weeks ago and missed last Sunday’s game against the Buffalo Bills. Wearing the red jersey suggests he’s limited in practice and one step closer to clearing the NFL’s concussion protocol. Warren also posted a video of tight end Brock Bowers warming up before Thursday’s practice. Bowers was limited Wednesday with hamstring and calf injuries, which is different from the knee injury that caused him to miss Weeks 1 and 2. That being said, he’s been limited on Wednesdays every week since returning to action. Tonka Hemingway (concussion) returns to Raiders practice today in a red non-contact jersey. pic.twitter.com/SVvGhDPgsv — Sam Warren (@samwarren83) October 22, 2026 The Raiders released the official injury report, in which Bowers (hamstring/calf), defensive tackle Foley Fatukasi (shoulder) and offensive tackle Kolton Miller (shoulder) were upgraded from limited to full participants during the team’s second practice of the week.
