title: Las Vegas Raiders need Eric Stokes’ best performance vs. Puka Nacua in Week 7 key matchups against Los Angeles Rams
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders and Los Angeles Rams entered the 2026 NFL season with very different expectations but find themselves entering the Week 7 contest in very similar situations. To a certain degree, this feels like a swing game for both clubs as the 3-3 Raiders and 2-4 Rams are clinging to playoff hopes as […]
full_text: (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders and Los Angeles Rams entered the 2026 NFL season with very different expectations but find themselves entering the Week 7 contest in very similar situations. To a certain degree, this feels like a swing game for both clubs as the 3-3 Raiders and 2-4 Rams are clinging to playoff hopes as we approach the halfway point of the campaign. That adds importance to the key matchups below. Stokes vs. Nacua Even when Davante Adams was available, the Rams’ passing offense primarily ran through Puka Nacua. Despite missing two games, Nacua leads the team in targets (52) and receptions (37) while ranking second behind Adams in yards (417) and touchdowns (one), per Pro Football Focus . Now that Adams is on injured reserve , Nacua’s workload should increase even more. While the fourth-year pro doesn’t have blazing speed, he’s a very good route runner and one of the most efficient wideouts in the league. According to PFF , he ranks fifth at the position with 2.78 yards per route run so far this season, which would be just the third-highest YPRR he’s had during his four regular seasons. Also, that’s almost a full yard lower than Nacua’s 2025 figure ( 3.71 ). In other words, the BYU product is a tough cover that commands attention from the opposing defense’s top cornerback. That’s where Eric Stokes steps in for Las Vegas. After having a breakout performance last year, Stokes had a slow start this fall. He was targeted 24 times and allowed 15 receptions (62.5 completion percentage) for 209 yards and a pair of touchdowns in Weeks 1-5, per PFF , after yielding just a 56.0 completion percentage, 261 yards and one score over 16 games in 2025. However, the six-year veteran is coming off his best outing of the current campaign, surrendering just two catches on four targets for 29 yards to post a season-high 71.3 coverage grade against the Buffalo Bills’ high-powered offense. Diving even deeper, one catch and 23 of those yards came on a screen to running back James Cook, meaning Stokes only gave up one grab and six yards to the Bills’ receivers . So, there is a question of which version of the defense’s top corner the Raiders are going to get on Sunday. The lockdown perimeter defender from a year ago and last week, or the corner who seemed to struggle fitting into new defensive coordinator Rob Leonard’s system? Obviously, the Silver and Black hope it’s the former. Granted, Nacua lines up all over the Rams’ offense with 109 snaps as a right outside receiver, 66 snaps on the left and 56 in the slot, per PFF , while Stokes is almost exclusively left outside corner ( 343 snaps out of 387 total, 88.6%). However, given that the Raiders are currently playing musical chairs at the other cornerback spot and the Rams don’t have many other notable receivers with Adams out, it’d make sense for Leonard to tweak his approach and have his top corner shadow Sean McVay’s top receiver on Sunday. Bowers vs. McDuffie It’s no secret that Klint Kubiak’s offense runs through “tight end” Brock Bowers. Like Nacua, Bowers missed two games and still leads his team in targets ( 40 ), receptions (28, tied with Michael Mayer) and receiving yards (382). He’s also tied with wide receivers Tre Tucker and Cody White for the team lead in receiving touchdowns with three. An “offensive weapon” is a more accurate description for the 2024 first-round pick since he’s only spent 15.8 percent of his pass snaps as an in-line tight end this season, according to PFF . As a result, opponents typically treat him like a ‘WR1’ by putting their top coverage defender on him. The Denver Broncos figured that out a few years ago with cornerback Patrick Surtain II, and several teams have followed suit, including the Bills last week. Buffalo did a decent job of keeping Bowers bottled up by matching him up against cornerback Christian Benford, resulting in just two catches for 23 yards on five targets . But when other defenders were covering Kubiak’s “football robot from heaven” a week ago, he hauled in two of three targets for 47 yards. So, expect the Rams to follow suit and go with a best-on-best matchup in the secondary. While the “Super Team” Los Angeles assembled this offseason hasn’t panned out so far, cornerback Trent McDuffie — who was acquired via a trade with the Kansas City Chiefs — isn’t part of the problem. The two-time All-Pro has been targeted 18 times but has yielded just five completions for a 27.8 completion percentage that ranks first among corners with at least 52 coverage snaps, according to PFF . That’s due in part to recording five forced incompletions at the third-highest rate (28 percent) for the position, resulting in the second-best coverage snaps per reception allowed (31.8) and second-highest coverage grade (88.7). Despite being division foes in 2024 and 2025, these two have only faced each other twice, with both matchups coming in Bowers’ rookie season since he was injured for both bouts against the Chiefs last year. The good news for the Raiders is that he had two catches for 48 yards on two targets against McDuffie that year, per PFF . So, the defensive back has been waiting about two years to get some payback. That being said, McDuffie missed last week’s game with a groin injury and sat out of Wednesday’s practice. So, there’s a chance McDuffie doesn’t play on Sunday. Dean vs. Rams’ RBs Circling back to Los Angeles’ offense, McVay will likely lean more heavily on the rushing attack without Adams, especially since he has a strong running back duo. Kyren Williams is still the Rams’ lead back with 80 carries for 393 yards and four touchdowns on the season. Additionally, he’s been one of the most efficient backs in the league, ranking tied for eighth (minimum 27 carries) with 4.9 ypc and 10th in EPA per rush (0.03), according to Sumer Sports . Meanwhile, Blake Corum has about half as many rushes (47) but has been just as efficient with 223 yards, 4.7 ypc (tied for 12th) and 0.07 EPA per attempt (fourth). In other words, L.A. has a potent rushing attack no matter who is in the backfield. That raises the importance of Nakobe Dean’s role on Las Vegas’ defense this week. Among linebackers with at least 44 snaps against the run, Dean ranks 23rd with a 70.3 PFF run defense grade this season. That’s due in part to ranking tied for 14th with 12 ‘ defensive stops ’ in that phase of the game. Additionally, the free agent addition is tied for the league lead in forced fumbles with three through six weeks. Corum hasn’t had much of a fumbling issue in the NFL, with just one (Week 2 of 2026) in his three-year career. However, Williams has coughed up the rock 11 times during the regular season in his five-year career, and had another fumble in the postseason a couple of years ago. To the latter’s credit, he’s only had one this fall (also in Week 2), but Dean will certainly be looking to test Williams’ ball security. In the passing game, Corum has never been much of a threat in the past. But he does have nine catches for 91 yards in 2026, and both of those figures are already career highs. That being said, Williams is still the bigger threat out of the backfield. He’s logged 141 career catches for 962 yards and nine receiving touchdowns , and ranks first (30), fourth (217) and tied for seventh (one) for those metrics among running backs this season. That’s where the Rams could have an advantage since Dean has had trouble covering running backs, drawing seven targets and allowing seven catches for 67 yards to the position this year, per PFF . That being said, he is an effective blitzer with six pressures on 19 pass rushes in 2026. Meanwhile, Williams has yielded five pressures on 54 opportunities — something Leonard might game plan for — but Corum has yielded just one on 21 opportunities. Long story short, we’re in for a good running back(s) versus linebacker matchup on Sunday in several phases of the game.

title: Michael Mayer is living up to his new contract
summary: Las Vegas Raiders tight end Michael Mayer has had his ups and downs during his career. He started out as the franchise’s future tight end. That changed when the Raiders drafted Brock Bowers in 2024 and demoted him to a backup role. He struggled with personal issues and injuries over the next two seasons. Despite […]
full_text: (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images Las Vegas Raiders tight end Michael Mayer has had his ups and downs during his career. He started out as the franchise’s future tight end. That changed when the Raiders drafted Brock Bowers in 2024 and demoted him to a backup role. He struggled with personal issues and injuries over the next two seasons. Despite these events, the Raiders’ front office gave him a new deal. The deal shocked many in the NFL landscape, with an APY of $15 million over the next three years. People questioned why the team would give so much money to a backup tight end. After the first six games, the way the Raiders deploy their offense with Bowers and Mayer has it making complete sense. Mayer is the inline tight end for most snaps, and the team uses 12 personnel on most downs. Mayer has started the season with 266 receiving yards with 28 receptions and a touchdown. He is on pace for 753 yards, which is a high total for tight ends in the NFL. Against the Buffalo Bills, he had a career-high 95 yards on seven receptions, giving Kirk Cousins another option as the Bills tried to take away Bowers. It wasn’t just checkdowns, either; he made big plays downfield. On Sunday, he showed he could be a serious threat in the offense with a 28-yard seam-route catch. Michael Mayer would be a TE1 on a lot of teams. Adjust his route slightly to find the hole in the zone and Cousins hits him for a big gain. pic.twitter.com/Nc6XXNGnu4 — Marcus Johnson (@TheMarcJohnNFL) October 19, 2026 Mayer is happy with his role and is proving he is worth every penny. The Raiders have two tight ends who will be the catalyst for how Kubiak wants to execute his passing game.

title: Raiders continue to manage Maxx Crosby snap counts
summary: In Week 1, the Las Vegas Raiders revealed their new plan to manage Maxx Crosby’s play time. It has, for the most part, continued through the first six weeks of the season appears to be the way the team will manage their 29-year-old star pass-rusher moving forward. In Week 1, against the Miami Dolphins, Crosby […]
full_text: (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images In Week 1, the Las Vegas Raiders revealed their new plan to manage Maxx Crosby’s play time. It has, for the most part, continued through the first six weeks of the season appears to be the way the team will manage their 29-year-old star pass-rusher moving forward. In Week 1, against the Miami Dolphins, Crosby played 82.1 percent of the season. He has since played between 80 percent and 91.7 percent of the defensive snaps. His per game average is 86 percent of the snaps. He played 89 percent in Week 6, his second highest total. So, Crosby is still, of course, playing the vast majority of the snaps, but it is noticably less than in the past. In the previous two seasons, Crosby played 100 percent of the snaps in 17 of the 27 games he played. He played 100 percent of the snaps in 10 of 17 games in 2023. But playing every snap of most games took its toll. Crosby missed the first seven games of his career in past two seasons and had off-season surgeries. Of course, a failed physical nixed his trade to the Baltimore Ravens in March. So, the Raiders became dedicated to giving Crosby some more in-game rest starting in 2026 and they appear to be sticking with that plan. Raider Nation, take the conversation everywhere! title: Brock Bowers barely leaves field
summary: Here is a look at how the Las Vegas Raiders’ 2024 draft class fared in a 33-30 home loss to the Buffalo Bills on Sunday and what to look for Sunday at home against the Los Angeles Rams: Brock Bowers: The first-round pick played 65 of 66 offensive snaps against Buffalo. It was his second […]
full_text: (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images Here is a look at how the Las Vegas Raiders’ 2024 draft class fared in a 33-30 home loss to the Buffalo Bills on Sunday and what to look for Sunday at home against the Los Angeles Rams: Brock Bowers: The first-round pick played 65 of 66 offensive snaps against Buffalo. It was his second highest snap percentage of his career. He wasn’t targeted until there were less than five minutes remaining in the third quarter. Still, he ended up being targeted nine times. He had four catches for 70 yards, both season lows. The Bills covered him primarily with a cornerback. We will see if that happens again Sunday against the Rams. Whatever happens, the Raiders need to get him the ball earlier. Jackson Powers-Johnson: The second-round pick returned was benched in favor of 2025 third-round pick Caleb Rogers. Powers-Johnson did playa few plays on special teams. He and Rogers are competing in practice this week. D.J. Glaze: The third-round pick started at right tackle as usual. Tommy Eichenberg: The fifth-round pick from Ohio State played 6 defensive snaps, his second fewest of the season. He did play 26 snaps on special teams. Dylan Laube: The sixth-round pick played five offensive snaps a week after he played a season-high 23. He had one carry for no yards against the Bills. Coach Klint Kubiak said this week Laube will be needed on offense as the Raiders try to get the ground game going. He had 54 yards on two kick returns.

title: Miami Dolphins news: Speeding up team development, injury updates, Jets game prep
summary: The Miami Dolphins are the youngest team in the NFL this season, kick-starting their franchise rebuild with an influx of rookies and second-year players. The team hopes to move from a consistently mediocre franchise that fights just to make a cameo in the playoffs to one that consistently battles for deep postseason runs. While the […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - SEPTEMBER 13: Caleb Douglas #7 of the Miami Dolphins gets set during the second quarter of an NFL football game against the Las Vegas Raiders at Allegiant Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins are the youngest team in the NFL this season, kick-starting their franchise rebuild with an influx of rookies and second-year players. The team hopes to move from a consistently mediocre franchise that fights just to make a cameo in the playoffs to one that consistently battles for deep postseason runs. While the goal is lofty, the Dolphins have had to tear down their roster for 2026, taking a massive immediate salary cap hit to get the future cap under control. Development is the Dolphins’ name for the game, as they hope their young roster can learn and grow quickly. South Florida Sun Sentinel columnist Chris Perkins took a look at how Miami is hoping to speed along that learning curve with a weekly addition to the practice schedule: Every Thursday, after the Miami Dolphins conclude their regular practice, many of the second- and third-team players gather for a brief 7-on-7 session. It sounds minimal, but coaches and players say the extra work is helpful because it better acquaints backups on Miami’s offense and defense, offers more hands-on coaching, and familiarizes them with playing alongside the starters… “It’s been really important to me,” said [head coach Jeff] Hafley, who detests 7-on-7 sessions during training camp. “I think regardless of where you’re at, I think we’re still in a developmental league.” The 7 on 7s are only seven or eight plays, but the repetitions and additional coaching add up over the course of a season for Dolphins backup players, most of whom spend midweek practices playing on the scout team. And here’s the big thing: in the 7-on-7 sessions, backups run the Dolphins offense and defense, they’d run if they’re suddenly inserted into a game. When they play on the scout team during midweek practices, they run the opponent’s offense and defense. Note: only starters on IR are listed. Player Name* = Starter. Injury designation definitions: Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and played on game day. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being ‘uncertain’ of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and played on game day. Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day and league rules prohibit them from playing. Notes on Injured Players For the Vikings, full roster participation apart from those on injured reserve. Unlikely to be any injury designations. title: Costly Drake Maye mistake looms large in Patriots’ loss to Bears
summary: Standing at the postgame podium, Drake Maye shook his head and looked down at ground. He let out an audible sigh of frustration. The Patriots quarterback was replaying his second-quarter interception that helped swing Thursday night’s loss to the Chicago Bears. “Huge point in the game. Gosh,” Maye said after the game. “Those plays can […]
full_text: Standing at the postgame podium, Drake Maye shook his head and looked down at ground. He let out an audible sigh of frustration. The Patriots quarterback was replaying his second-quarter interception that helped swing Thursday night’s loss to the Chicago Bears . “Huge point in the game. Gosh,” Maye said after the game. “Those plays can swing the game, can impact the game, and that was definitely one of them right there. I wish I definitely had that one back.” After a slow offensive start Thursday night while dealing with Chicago’s pressure packages, New England’s offense found its footing with a pair of strong drives to open the second quarter. Maye finished the first with a rushing touchdown, then led the Patriots back into the red zone with a chance to take the lead. Instead, his pass up the seam to rookie tight end Eli Raridon sailed short and was intercepted. “We hit the same thing, the same exact play later in the game,” Maye said, recalling his 30-yard touchdown pass to Raridon in third quarter quarter. “I like my chances in there. It’s frustrating … I let my team down.” The interception cost the Patriots a chance to add seven points, a missed opportunity that loomed large in their 30-24 to the Bears. Trailing 27-21 in the fourth quarter, New England had two possessions to take the lead but managed just one first down between them. The Bears then drained more than 11 minutes of clock across their following two possessions. Those missed opportunities weighed on Maye as much as the interception. “That’s probably what I’ll be thinking about most over the weekend, having two chances with the ball down 27-21,” Maye said. “We got a good chance to go score and trust our defense … We just fell short tonight.” Despite the costly turnover, Maye kept New England within striking distance against Caleb Williams and Chicago’s high-powered offense. With little help from the running game, he completed a season-high 77.4% of his passes and was nearly perfect against pressure, completing 11 of 12 attempts for 151 yards and a touchdown. “He gave us a chance. He competed,” head coach Mike Vrabel said. “I know he’d like to have that one back. He’ll learn from it like he always does. I’m glad he’s ours.”
author: Brian Hines

title: 10 things we learned from Patriots vs. Bears
summary: The New England Patriots lost a wacky Thursday night game to the Bears in Chicago. As injured as they were, and as bad as they played at times, especially defensively, they still had a real chance to win the game in the fourth quarter. It was a frustrating way to end the game. Without further ado, let’s […]
full_text: The New England Patriots lost a wacky Thursday night game to the Bears in Chicago. As injured as they were, and as bad as they played at times, especially defensively, they still had a real chance to win the game in the fourth quarter. It was a frustrating way to end the game. Without further ado, let’s get into our lessons learned for the Patriots’ 30-24 loss . Typical Thursday night shenanigans Every Thursday Night Football game is filled with bizarre plays, partially because the teams are playing on such a short week. This game was no different. The Patriots gave up a touchdown on 3rd-and-17 at the end of the first half, only to be outdone by the Bears giving up a 48-yard touchdown to the Patriots with three seconds left on a check-down. This happens every week, but the NFL doesn’t care about doing anything about it. I wish the Patriots had looked better and not made as many mistakes, but it seems par for the course on a Thursday night. Injuries may have caught up with the Patriots The Patriots have more injuries right now than they had all of last year, and those depth concerns reared their head on Thursday night. They have good players, but simply didn’t have enough of them available to make life difficult for a talented Bears team. There are no excuses to be made here either, because the Patriots had opportunities to win regardless of the circumstances. Still, it seems that part of the reason they came up short was because of the lack of depth that they were dealing with. Tough night for a pair of starters I might be the world’s biggest Marcus Jones fan, but he had a bad night on Thursday, and Christian Elliss was equally as bad. The amount of missed tackles by Jones was alarming, and he wasn’t particularly good in coverage either. Meanwhile, Elliss missed quite a few tackles too, and gave up a huge play to Luther Burden because of a blown assignment. Elliss finished as the leading tackler for the Patriots, and Jones racked up nine tackles of his own, but the tape tells a different story. Both players have made huge contributions for the Patriots, and are important players for the defense. A better game from one or both of them, and the outcome might have been different. Gabe Jacas continues to play well The Patriots defense struggled, but Gabe Jacas made his presence felt again. He also should have had a sack; they gave it to teammate Leonard Taylor, but it was Jacas who made the play. He was pretty solid against the run as well. Jacas has become one of the Patriots’ most consistent edge defenders, and is already a better run defender than Elijah Ponder, who had a tough night on Thursday. It wasn’t perfect, but the second-sound rookie continues growing into one heck of a player. Drake Maye has a great night, with one costly exception Drake Maye played a good game on Thursday. He did a fantastic. job of taking what the defense gave him, he was great maneuvering in the pocket, and also was the Patriots’ leading rusher for the game. His one big mistake, however, cost them dearly. His end zone interception in the second quarter gave the Bears the ball back when the Patriots had a chance to take the lead. Chicago would end up scoring on the subsequent drive, and although Maye and company managed to match that score on their following possession, the Maye pick would be the last time they got into the red zone all night. Those are opportunities that you can’t afford to lose out on. The hard part is that Maye was far and away the best player on the field for the Patriots on Thursday, but that turnover changed the complexion of the game. Despite an entire half of football being left to be played, it had a large impact on the game’s final outcome; a touchdown here, and the game probably looks a lot different down the stretch. Through seven games, the Patriots have yet to play a turnover-free game on offense and have not once won the turnover battle. A.J. Brown is a non-factor again Maye Brown isn’t back at a 100% yet, or he’s still rusty from the time missed, but he was a non-factor again on Thursday. He did catch three passes for 48 yards, but when he had chances to make big plays, he was unable to finish them. With Romeo Doubs and Mack Hollins on injured reserve, the Patriots need more of him. I will say that I’m already having some really mixed feelings about sending that first-round pick to the Eagles to get him, especially with no protections tied to it as well. Maybe Brown can prove me wrong the rest of this year and next year, but it certainly hasn’t looked good so far. Eli Raridon is a stud The Patriots may have found a gem in the third round of the draft this year. Eli Raridon looks like the real deal, and had another solid game for the Patriots on Thursday. He’s not the best run blocker, but he can do it. Where he really shines, however, is in the passing game. We saw him on some crossing routes, and on a few seam passes as well. One of those went for a touchdown, and the other would have, if Drake Maye put the ball on him instead of on the defender. Hunter Henry is still as reliable as ever, but now Raridon brings some real juice to the tight end room that the Patriots haven’t had in quite a while. If he continues to improve, he’s going to be a true impact player for them. TreVeyon Henderson can’t read a hole to save his life TreVeyon Henderson looked like he was going to be a stud last year. This year, not so much. He has struggled with his vision since entering the league as a second-round draft pick, but he had a bunch of big plays that offset things last year. He hasn’t had those plays so far, with one exception (Week 2), and what this has done is make people acutely aware of his struggles trying to run between the tackles. There was a play early on in the game when a back with vision might have picked up 30 yards, but Henderson only picked up 5. Mike Vrabel did express confidence in him after the game, but don’t be surprised if the Patriots continue keeping Corey Kiner involved as well. Personally, I would like to see the Patriots get Henderson the ball in space and see if he can do anything with that. Running up the middle, frankly, has been a disaster this season. Caleb Williams is really good Caleb Williams was fantastic on Thursday night. The Bears quarterback was in command the whole game, and seemed to have the answers to what the Patriots were throwing at him, for the most part. His third-down throw to Rome Odunze where he shook off Christian Elliss at the goal line was great, and his arm strength is close to breathtaking. His ability to play within himself and not make stupid decisions when throwing is what impressed me the most on Thursday, though. If he can stay healthy, he and Maye are going to be two of the best quarterbacks in the league for many years to come. The ironic part is that if Cairo Santos misses the game-icing 58-yard field goal, we might be talking about how both Maye and Williams made costly mistakes, and that giving up a 10-yard sack to almost get knocked out of field goal range ultimately cost the Bears the game. However, Santos hit that field goal, and the sack — plus Ben Johnson’s decision to try a career-long kick with his team up by less than a touchdown — will be nothing more than a footnote. Mini bye before trip to Miami The Patriots have 10 days off until their next game, which will come against one of the worst teams in the NFL, the Miami Dolphins. The game is in Miami, which makes it a little more complicated, since the Patriots typically struggle down there. They are still going to need to take care of business in the division, especially against the bad teams, if they want to have any chance of catching the Bills for the AFC East title. This also could be a good time to start exploring some trade options. Colts guard Quenton Nelson is a name that makes a ton of sense, but there are others out there that could help the Patriots as well. With the extended time off, now might be the time to jump at…
author: Pat Lane

title: 6 winners and losers from Patriots loss to the Bears
summary: The New England Patriots lost their Thursday night primetime game to the Chicago Bears with a final score of 30-24. They have now dropped to 4-3 on the season, and currently out of the playoff picture in the AFC. Here is who caught our eye for better or worse upon live-viewing the Week 7 contest. […]
full_text: The New England Patriots lost their Thursday night primetime game to the Chicago Bears with a final score of 30-24 . They have now dropped to 4-3 on the season, and currently out of the playoff picture in the AFC. Here is who caught our eye for better or worse upon live-viewing the Week 7 contest. Winners QB Drake Maye: The Patriots quarterback lamented postgame about his second quarter interception that proved costly, but Maye was a key reason New England stayed competitive Thursday night. He completed a season-high 77.4% of his passes and again eclipsed the 300-yard mark while being nearly perfect against pressure completing 11 of 12 attempts for 151 yards and a touchdown. His +0.34 EPA/play (84th percentile) was identical to Caleb Williams. Maye was also the team’s leading rusher Thursday night as he also added a third touchdown with his legs and made several plays out of structure. TE Hunter Henry: The veteran tight end continued to be a steady source of offense for the Patriots, leading the team with seven receptions and targets. Henry took his seven receptions for 71 yards as he was a reliable outlet for Maye over the middle of the field and against pressure. Losers Tackling: The Patriots defense was credited with missing 16 (!) tackles Thursday night in Chicago. That was their most in a game since last year’s Super Bowl (18). The usual steady Marcus Jones led the way with five, including a whiff on Colston Loveland’s third quarter touchdown. In total, the Bears totaled 163 yards after the catch and 96 rushing yards after contact. “The tackling wasn’t good enough, not against this team. We knew coming in, certainly against this team,” Mike Vrabel said. LBs Robert Spillane and LB Christian Elliss: Caleb Williams found great success over the middle of the field Thursday night as the Patriots struggled in zone coverage. As a whole, Williams went 14-of-18 for 208 yards and a touchdown against zone. The big plays started in the first quarter with a 58-yard completion to Luther Burden as Christian Elliss and Charles Woods both ended up in the flat busting the coverage. Spillane and Elliss were both credited for missing three combined tackles and allowing four receptions, while Elliss was also had a prime opportunity to sack Williams on a late 3rd-and-11, but saw the quarterback evade him and fire a laser to Rome Odunze to move the chains. WR A.J. Brown: It was another quiet day for the Patriots’ top receiver, who finished with just three catches for 48 yards on six targets. Brown had another go-ball opportunity he could not finish as Maye dropped a dime in the bucket. The defender forced Brown to play through contact, but it’s a play you’d like to see the three-time Pro Bowler make. Brown will get some extra time off now after returning from the high ankle sprain, where the Patriots will then need a bigger impact from their No. 1 wide receiver. Honorable mentions A pregame key here: stay out of third-and-pass situations. The Patriots found themselves in too many of those spots in the first quarter which allowed Dennis Allen’s blitz package to create havoc. As Maye noted postgame, they dealt with those better with the Patriots finding more early-down success as the game went on. The Patriots run game was largely non-existent. Removing Maye, the Patriots finished with 13 carries for 44 yards and a 20% success rate (6th percentile). Despite those struggles, Rhamondre Stevenson had the best run of the night (13-yard wham) and made an impact elsewhere. He finished with five receptions for 93 yards and a wild end-of-half touchdown, while also doing his usual work as a pass protector. Eli Raridon joined Henry with productive game, finishing with three receptions for 56 yards and a touchdown. A better ball from Maye on the interception in Raridon’s direction could have also resulted in another touchdown. As for the offensive line, the makeshift group largely protected well 1-on-1 but dealt with penalties. The Will Campbell false start still was questionable from this point of view. Besides a poor roughing the passer penalty, Gabe Jacas was a bully along the defensive line. He finished with a team-high five pressures and allowed teammates to clean up two sacks. On the other end, Elijah Ponder finished with four pressures but found himself out of position on multiple big plays against. Mitch Wishnowsky continues to punt well while Andy Borregales made all of his kicks. New England did allow a 47-yard kick return.
author: Brian Hines

title: Patriots try unconventional late-game tactic in loss to Bears
summary: Trailing six points to the Chicago Bears in the late fourth quarter, the New England Patriots needed two things: a stop and time. When the former was unlikely to happen, though, they prioritized the latter. That is what happened when defensive tackle Cory Durden jumped offsides on a 3rd-and-1 coming out of the two-minute warning. […]
full_text: Trailing six points to the Chicago Bears in the late fourth quarter, the New England Patriots needed two things: a stop and time. When the former was unlikely to happen, though, they prioritized the latter. That is what happened when defensive tackle Cory Durden jumped offsides on a 3rd-and-1 coming out of the two-minute warning. Durden did not do so by accident or overeagerness to make a play; he encroached because he was told to do so by his head coach. “We told Cory to jump off sides and third-and-six inches or whatever it was,” Mike Vrabel said during his postgame presser after his team’s 30-24 defeat . “We felt like that was going to be the best way to get them stopped. That’s on me.” Up 27-21, the Bears took possession with 6:22 left in the game. The Patriots did have a chance to get a quick stop, but quarterback Caleb Williams connected with wide receiver Rome Odunze for a 21-yard gain on 3rd-and-9 to keep the drive going. Five plays later, on 3rd-and-1, New England already saw the writing on the wall and opted for the unconventional tactic. Durden was instructed to jump offsides, allow a conversation, and save some time and preserve all three timeouts. The plan came close to working, too, when Christian Barmore sacked Williams to set up a 58-yard field goal try. However, Bears kicker Cairo Santos, who had missed a 53-yard attempt earlier in the game, was perfect this time around to effectively ice the game with 1:34 remaining on the clock. “Our guys executed and then Cairo made a huge kick,” said Vrabel about a player he coached back in Tennessee in 2019. “I didn’t want him to make it tonight, but a former guy that we coached. Caleb’s going to make some plays. I don’t know how you get out-executed when a guy makes a 58-yard field goal. We executed well at times and didn’t get the drive stopped enough.”
author: Bernd Buchmasser

title: Instant analysis from Patriots’ loss to Bears
summary: A week that began at Gillette Stadium soon ended at Soldier Field. And in defeat. The New England Patriots fell to the Chicago Bears by a score of 30-24 on Thursday night, snapping a three-game winning streak. Here’s a glance back on the 8:15 p.m. ET kickoff as head coach Mike Vrabel’s side returns home […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - OCTOBER 22: Rhamondre Stevenson #38 of the New England Patriots runs the ball during the second quarter of a game against the Chicago Bears at Soldier Field on October 22, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images) | Getty Images A week that began at Gillette Stadium soon ended at Soldier Field. And in defeat. The New England Patriots fell to the Chicago Bears by a score of 30-24 on Thursday night, snapping a three-game winning streak. Here’s a glance back on the 8:15 p.m. ET kickoff as head coach Mike Vrabel’s side returns home for the mini bye with a 4-3 record. Midway Maye delivers three touchdowns, one pick The month of October had brought AFC Offensive Player of the Week honors along with 10 passing touchdowns, one rushing touchdown and one interception. The trend didn’t end in the Midwest. Drake Maye completed 24-of-31 passes for 321 yards with two touchdowns and one interception through the air against the Bears. By ground, the Patriots quarterback added 26 rushing yards and a third touchdown. Taking the field in “11” personnel, the opening drive included one first down before ending in an aggressive fourth-and-5 takedown. New England’s next pair of drives brought three-and-outs with the help of simulated pressure as well as run-run-pass sequences from offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels. But the sticks would be moved on a 15-yarder to rookie tight end Eli Raridon and a 16-yarder to veteran tight end Hunter Henry as the first quarter reached the second quarter. That grew into nine-play, 74-yard drive to get the visitors across the plane on an extension from the QB for a TD. The underneath had its openings as Maye was intercepted in the end zone by linebacker D’Marco Jackson on an underthrow intended for his third-round target from Notre Dame. Even so, a catch-and-run touchdown out of the backfield soon got things to halftime from midfield. By intermission, with the score reading 20-14, Maye stood 12-of-15 for 169 yards with two touchdowns, the lone turnover and a 108.1 passer rating. That deficit had swelled by the time the ball was back in his hands. The 24-year-old captain and his supporting cast proceeded to respond from a false start with a 30-yard scoring strike down the seam to Raridon to cap off a nine-play push. A familiar throw with a different result. Back-to-back punts got the fourth quarter underway for the Patriots, however, and it’d be a 30-21 gap by the time Maye was back on the field with no timeouts remaining. New England finished 2-of-7 on third down, 0-of-1 on fourth down and 1-of-2 in the red zone. The tandem at tight end finished with 10 receptions for 127 yards and a touchdown. Down No. 87, wide receivers net 87 yards Just as New England’s No. 1 wide receiver returned last weekend at Gillette Stadium, Romeo Doubs headed the other direction and joined eldest statesman Mack Hollins on injured reserve after sustaining a shoulder injury on a 42-yard touchdown. That left the depth chart with an active four that would combine for 87 receiving yards. A.J. Brown led the shorthanded position. In his second game back from a high ankle sprain, the June trade acquisition caught three of the six passes sent his way for 48 yards. The drops did not make the trip to Soldier Field. But his first reception, which provided 18 yards and reason for a timeout, did not arrive until the closing seconds before halftime. DeMario Douglas and Kyle Williams joined the three-time Pro Bowler, three-time All-Pro and Super Bowl LIX champion in the starting lineup. Efton Chism III filed on. Two guards missing from New England’s starting five The starting left guard and the starting right guard from four days prior weren’t on hand. Alijah Vera-Tucker and Ben Brown had been ruled out due to a hamstring injury and a knee injury , respectively. The former has since landed on injured reserve. But a duct-taped offensive line that finished without allowing a sack or a penalty against the New York Jets let pressure in at Soldier Field. It’d be Will Campbell at left tackle next to August trade acquisition Walter Rouse. It’d be Jared Wilson at center. And it’d be October signing Matt Pryor next to questionable captain Morgan Moses at right tackle. Blitzing cornerback Kyler Gordon got the first sack in the first quarter. A sack split between defensive tackle Grady Jarrett and safety Dillon Thieneman surfaced in the fourth quarter. There were two false starts and two holding penalties charged to the combination along the way. Stevenson hears no bell despite Patriots’ backfield combining for 44 rushing yards Rhamondre Stevenson lowered the boom in pass protection. The Patriots starting running back did so while logging 22 rushing yards to go with a career-high 93 receiving yards on 11 touches. A grab-and-go, 48-yard touchdown through a sea of Bears was in the cards as time expired in the first half. But New England’s quarterback led the team on the ground by game’s end. A three-headed committee had emerged during last Sunday’s clock-killing win in Foxborough. Corey Kiner’s trust in the closing minutes continued early on Thursday. The trade pickup from the league’s 53-man roster deadline totaled 13 rushing yards across four handoffs while serving as the primary kickoff returner. And then there was TreVeyon Henderson, whose recent high ankle sprain ultimately did not keep him away from a practice or a game. The No. 38 overall pick in the 2025 draft class was still kept to 23 scrimmage yards on a handful of chances. Williams finds room to outlast Patriots’ secondary Nearly two years had passed since the Bears last hosted the Patriots. The records at the time were 4-5 and 3-7. The head coaches were Matt Eberflus and Jerod Mayo. Much has changed since that November 2024 meeting. A former Heisman Trophy winner provided a reminder. Caleb Williams went 22-of-33 passing for 308 yards on Thursday night. The Bears quarterback did so while delivering two touchdowns and no interceptions. He added 18 rushing yards. Chicago’s opening series brought a 26-yard connection on the initial snap and ended in a 43-yard field goal. The next possession brought a three-and-out checkdown for no gain versus zone coverage. The third possession, though, brought a wide-open over route that suddenly netted 58 yards more. From the goal line to the end zone, the Bears gained a 10-point cushion late in the first quarter. After the Patriots got on the board, a nine-play trek to a 13-7 lead ensued. And after a sudden change kept things that way, it was back to Luther Burden III once again for a 24-yard TD on third-and-17. The sophomore wide receiver found himself with 130 yards at the half, while the past No. 1 overall pick out of Oklahoma and USC stood 9-of-16 for 167 yards with one touchdown and a 113.3 passer rating. New England started in the nickel secondary. All-Pro Christian Gonzalez was joined at cornerback by Charles Woods, who was called for holding on third-and-4, as well as sacking captain Marcus Jones. The defensive backfield was missing Carlton Davis III for a third consecutive game because of a neck injury. Yet it had an ex-Bear who led the NFL in interceptions in 2025, as Kevin Byard III and Craig Woodson occupied the safety spots. Coming out of halftime, Chicago traveled 72 yards in nine plays en route to tight end Colston Loveland reeling in a 12-yard touchdown for a 13-point advantage. But a three-and-out followed as it became a one-score game. In the final frame, Williams slipped out of a blitz and kept downfield eyes on third-and-11 with the uprights at his back. A fourth-and-2 conversion and a missed field goal off the right upright from 53 yards away were the result. Time soon became a factor regardless. And with 4:59 and then 3:32 left on the game clock, physical wideout Rome Odunze kept things rolling with a pair of 21-yard pickups in a span of three snaps. Three sacks notched, one Swift score allowed The Patriots’ defense hit…

title: 5 moments that defined the Patriots’ loss to the Bears
summary: The New England Patriots’ win streak came to an end on Thursday night versus the Chicago Bears. In what was a competitive game for the most part, the team of head coach Mike Vrabel suffered a 30-24 defeat. Here is a Patriots-centric view at some of those key moments from the Week 7 contest. Moment […]
full_text: The New England Patriots’ win streak came to an end on Thursday night versus the Chicago Bears. In what was a competitive game for the most part, the team of head coach Mike Vrabel suffered a 30-24 defeat . Here is a Patriots-centric view at some of those key moments from the Week 7 contest. Moment No. 1: Game of inches The Patriots offense had its fair share of issues to start the game, but it finally showed some life early second quarter. Driving all the way up to the Bears 7-yard line, quarterback Drake Maye finished the series off himself: Drake Maye reaches for the score 🙌 📺 Prime Video pic.twitter.com/GvRdrWHNp5 — New England Patriots (@Patriots) October 23, 2026 Maye’s ninth career rushing touchdown gave the Patriots some much-needed offensive momentum, but it only counted because Mike Vrabel had the challenge flag ready. The third-year QB was initially ruled down short of the goal line, but Vrabel — likely at the behest of his right-hand man, John “Stretch” Streicher — successfully. disputed the spot. Moment No. 2: Bad memories With the offense starting to show signs of life, the Patriots were in a position to take the lead late in the second quarter. But while they did return to the Chicago red zone, a promising drive ended in disappointment. @DMarcojackson20 picks it off in the end zone 🙌 📺: Prime Video pic.twitter.com/q7i8VOFjbf — Chicago Bears (@ChicagoBears) October 23, 2026 Instead of the Patriots coming away with points, Drake Maye threw an interception reminiscent of his early-season work: he failed to see the defender underneath and did not put enough air on the ball for an easy interception in the end zone. In what ended as a one-score game, it was a crucial play — one made even worse by Chicago scoring a touchdown on the ensuing possession. Moment No. 3: Madness The Bears left only nine seconds on the clock for the Patriots to end the first half, but that’s all they needed. Scoring their longest end-of-half touchdown in 16 years, they cut into what was a 13-point deficit at that point. RHAMONDRE STEVENSON‼️ 📺 Prime Video pic.twitter.com/heXDiTFnzW — New England Patriots (@Patriots) October 23, 2026 The drive started with A.J. Brown’s first catch of the day, before Rhamondre Stevenson took a short pass 48 yards into the end zone. Despite Chicago defending the long play, the veteran running back had to evade just one tackle attempt — a testament to his vision and his teammates’ blocking downfield. Moment No. 4: Penalty woes The Patriots and Bears were both flagged quite often on Thursday, getting penalized a combined 19 times. Every penalty is a potentially costly play, but the biggest “what could have been” flag came on the first play of the fourth quarter. Down 27-21 and with the ball at their 48-yard line, the Patriots were prepared to go for it on 4th-and-2. A conversion was not a guarantee — they had missed one attempt earlier in the game — but momentum seemingly was on New England’s side after scoring touchdowns on back-to-back possessions before that moment. Alas, Matt Pryor jumping offsides forced Mike Vrabel to reconsider and opt for a punt instead. Moment No. 5: Opportunity missed Trailing by six points with 5 minutes left on the clock, the Patriots defense found itself in what should be a favorable position: in a 3rd-and-9 at the Bears 10-yard line. A stop, and Drake Maye and company would get the ball in possibly good field position with plenty of time left on the clock. However, that stop never happened. @RomeOdunze SNAGGED that 📺: Prime Video pic.twitter.com/pxd9LY1sgp — Chicago Bears (@ChicagoBears) October 23, 2026 Caleb Williams and Rome Odunze showed why they are one of the top young quarterback-receiver tandems in the league, by hooking up for 21 yards despite Marcus Jones being all over the pass catcher. Still, Odunze hang on and the conversion gave Chicago’s offense some breathing room. It eventually went on to three more minutes off the clock before kicking what was effectively a game-icing field goal.

title: Patriots playoff picture after losing to the Bears in Week 7
summary: The New England Patriots came up short on Thursday Night Football, losing 30-24 to the Chicago Bears. Besides putting an end to the team’s three-game winning streak, the defeat also impacts its standing in the AFC playoff picture. With the majority of Week 7 games left to be played, the Patriots now find themselves out […]
full_text: The New England Patriots came up short on Thursday Night Football, losing 30-24 to the Chicago Bears . Besides putting an end to the team’s three-game winning streak, the defeat also impacts its standing in the AFC playoff picture. With the majority of Week 7 games left to be played, the Patriots now find themselves out of the postseason slots. AFC East standings Buffalo Bills (5-1) New England Patriots (4-2) New York Jets (2-4) Miami Dolphins (0-5) The Patriots remain in second place in their division even after losing to the Bears, and would have stayed put regardless of what the weekend slate would have brought. The Bills, after all, are on a bye, meaning New England would not have overtaken them even in case of a win. That said, what was a one-game deficit entering Thursday is now a 1.5-game gap that needs to be overcome. AFC playoff standings Kansas City Chiefs (5-0) Buffalo Bills (5-1) Jacksonville Jaguars (4-2) Cleveland Browns (4-2) Denver Broncos (4-2) Pittsburgh Steelers (4-2) Baltimore Ravens (4-2) On the bubble: 8. Cincinnati Bengals (3-2) , 9. New England Patriots (4-3) , 10. Las Vegas Raiders (3-3), 11. New York Jets (2-4), 12. Indianapolis Colts (2-4), 13. Houston Texans (2-4 ), 14. Tennessee Titans (1-5) Not yet eliminated, but let’s be real here: 15. Miami Dolphins (0-5), 16. Los Angeles Chargers (0-6) As mentioned earlier, the Patriots are currently out of the playoff picture. In fact, they made a sizable drop from the fifth to the ninth position in the standings. They will overtake at least one other team again, however, given that the Ravens and Bengals are going against each other on Sunday. To reenter the playoff spots before the end of Week 7, however, New England will need other games to go in its favor as well.

title: Patriots vs. Bears final score, highlights, game recap for NFL Week 7
summary: Even though they entered Thursday night facing personnel questions at multiple positions, the New England Patriots had their chances to compete for a victory against the Chicago Bears. At the end of the day, however, they simply made too many mistakes to hang with one of the better teams in the NFC. Whether it was […]
full_text: Even though they entered Thursday night facing personnel questions at multiple positions, the New England Patriots had their chances to compete for a victory against the Chicago Bears. At the end of the day, however, they simply made too many mistakes to hang with one of the better teams in the NFC. Whether it was a costly red zone interception, multiple missed tackles, coverage breakdowns on defense and special teams, or untimely penalties, the Patriots did not play as clean a game as they needed to. The end result was a 30-24 defeat. The team of head coach Mike Vrabel therefore heads into its mini-bye with a 4-3 record. Final score: Patriots 24 : 30 Bears Thursday, Oct. 22, 8:15 p.m. ET | Soldier Field (Chicago, IL) | Broadcast information | Game day roster | Inactives | Weather forecast First quarter The Patriots started the game on offense, and with an incompletion that sailed high over wide receiver A.J. Brown’s head. Drake Maye found more success targeting his running backs, hitting Rhamondre Stevenson for a gain of 19 yards and later finding TreVeyon Henderson on back-to-back plays. However, a Stevenson run on 3rd-and-6 didn’t get the proper yards and New England turned the ball over on downs after a sack on the subsequent 4th-and-5. The Bears offense started its Thursday night in good field position, and with a chunk play to Luther Burden for 26 yards against Marcus Jones. However, an inaccurate pass on a subsequent 3rd-and-7 ended the drive and set up a 43-yard field goal for the game’s first points. | Patriots 0 : 3 Bears The Patriots offense went nowhere on its second possession. After two short runs to start the series, quick pressure off another Bears blitz look forced a throw off the mark and Mitch Wishnowsky punt. Patriots fans, join the game-day huddle! Follow every snap and discuss every decision with fellow fans on the SB Nation app. Connect through our live game chat Browse with fewer ads Seamlessly move between communities Enjoy faster commenting and posting Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . Chicago’s offense did not fare much better, answering with a three-and-out-of its own. Two short runs set up a 3rd-and-6. A short Caleb Williams pass to D’Andrew Swift gained no yards thanks to Charles Woods and Christian Elliss quickly bringing down the ball carrier. Drake Maye and company, meanwhile, went three-and-out in a similar fashion on their next series: a short Corey Kiner run was followed by two negative plays, including DeMario Douglas losing a yard on 3rd-and-8. After neither offense managed to do much on the last few drives, the Bears not only gained a first down again but then beat the Patriots defense on a 58-yard catch-and-run to Luther Burden against a coverage bust involving Christian Elliss and Charles Woods. The play set the home team up with a 1st-and-goal at the 4-yard line, and it took D’Andre Swift just one play to find the end zone for the first touchdown of the night. | Patriots 0 : 10 Bears Deciding to focus more on the passing game to start the next drive, the Patriots finally picked up a first down again when Drake Maye connected with Eli Raridon for again of 15 to close out Quarter 1. Second quarter New England kept moving the chains to open the second period, driving into Bears territory for the first time all game. A 16-yard pass to Hunter Henry and a 13-yard run by Rhamondre Stevenson then set up a goal-to-go situation, with Drake Maye capping the series on a touchdown scramble from 7 yards out. Maye initially was ruled down short of the goal line, but Mike Vrabel successfully challenged the spot and was rewarded with seven points. | Patriots 7 : 10 Bears Drake Maye reaches for the score 🙌 📺 Prime Video pic.twitter.com/GvRdrWHNp5 — New England Patriots (@Patriots) October 23, 2026 Momentum quickly shifted back Chicago’s way after Drake Maye’s touchdown. The team started its next series with a 47-yard kickoff return, and thanks to a tagged-on penalty found itself on the New England side of the field right away. The Patriots did get a chance to stop the Bears on 4th-and-inches shortly thereafter, but D’Andre Swift moved the chains. However, back-to-back penalties against the Bears — including one negating a 2-yard Joe Thuney run — ended the series with a field goal. | Patriots 7 : 13 Bears New England started its next drive with a 16-yard pass to Efton Chism, and a couple of good Corey Kiner runs plus an Eli Raridon catch and Drake Maye scramble later found itself in the red zone. However, the opportunity went to waste when Maye was intercepted on an attempted end zone pass for Raridon. The Patriots kept hurting themselves on the next drive. A Charles Woods hold negated a third down stop, while Gabe Jacas was flagged for roughing the passer to help the Bears get into field goal range again. New England did find itself in a favorable position on a 3rd-and-17 after a Marcus Jones sack, but Luther Burden again managed to make a big play when he took a short pass 24 yards into the end zone for a touchdown. | Patriots 7 : 20 Bears The Patriots had only nine seconds on the clock, and they made them count. First, Drake Maye hit A.J. Brown for 18 yards, before finding Rhamondre Stevenson with three seconds left.The veteran running back took a short pass 48 yards into the end zone as time ran out on the second quarter. | Patriots 14 : 20 Bears RHAMONDRE STEVENSON‼️ 📺 Prime Video pic.twitter.com/heXDiTFnzW — New England Patriots (@Patriots) October 23, 2026 Third quarter Starting the second half on defense, the Patriots were in a position for a quick three-and-out but surrendered a conversion to a scrambling Caleb Williams. A pair of short passes to D’Andre Swift allowed the Bears to set up shop in New England territory again, and not just that: they capped their nine-play, 72-yard drive with Colston Loveland breaking a tackle on a 12-yard touchdown. | Patriots 14 : 27 Bears The Patriots could have answered with a big play right on the next drive, but a deep pass intended for A.J. Brown was broken up at the catch point. The pair did connect later on the series to pick up 16 yards. That play plus a pair of completions to Hunter Henry allowed New England to return into field goal range. The team’s ambition went beyond three points, though, and it capped the drive accordingly when Drake Maye hit Eli Raridon for a 30-yard touchdown. | Patriots 21 : 27 Bears Drake Maye DIME to Eli Raridon 🪙 📺 Prime Video pic.twitter.com/ajUvbcD8Oo — New England Patriots (@Patriots) October 23, 2026 After taking some hits the last few drives, the Patriots delivered a big three-and-out following their touchdown to Eli Raridon. A short pass followed by two incompletions — prompted by the defensive front generating some pressure — allowed the ball to return to New England via punt. That punt was fielded by Marcus Jones at the 7-yard line and returned 19 yards to improve what would have been some bad starting field position. The Patriots managed to get the ball out even further but right before the end of the quarter found themselves 2 yards short after a Drake Maye third-down scramble near midfield. Fourth quarter The Patriots started the fourth quarter intending to go for it on 4th-and-2, but a false start penalty against Matt Pryor cost them 5 yards and brought out the punt team. The Bears’ subsequent drive looked similar to the Patriots’ last one, with the team driving the ball well early but eventually stalling near midfield to set up a 4th-and-2. Unlike New England, Chicago did go for it and moved the chains. However, the series still ended with no points when a Cairo Santos field goal attempt from 53 yards out hit the right upright. Starting in good field position and with a chance to drive for their first lead of the day, the Patriots offense went three-and-out. An incomplete pass followed by a 9-yard sack put the unit in an unfavorable 3rd-and-long position, and a pass to Rhamondre Stevenson did not gain enough yards to…

title: Patriots vs. Bears game day roster for Thursday Night Football
summary: The hits just keep coming for the New England Patriots offensive line. The veteran hurt his knee on Sunday against the […]
full_text: The hits just keep coming for the New England Patriots offensive line. After the unit already lost right guard Mike Onwenu and his replacement, Greg Van Roten, to respective ankle and thigh injuries earlier in the season, it is now also without third-string option Ben Brown. The veteran hurt his knee on Sunday against the New York Jets and was subsequently unable to practice during a short week leading up to Thursday’s game in Chicago. With Brown out , in-season pickup and nominal fourth-stringer Matt Pryor is now the starter at right guard. At left guard, the team will start a third-stringer, who also joined the club fairly recently, Walter Rouse. Rouse will take the field to replace Alijah Vera-Tucker, who is now on injured reserve after hurting his hamstring versus the Jets. With the usual backup at that spot, Brown, out as well, it is the late-August trade pickup’s turn. The starter level is obviously in the spotlight against the Bears, but so are the backups. With Morgan Moses active despite nursing a foot issue, Caleb Lomu projects as a super backup who might play tackle or guard if needed. Rookie Dametrious Crownover is active for only the second time since the season opener to provide tackle depth, with practice squad elevatee Xavier Newman-Johnson an extra interior option. The Patriots’ full game day roster looks as follows. title: Patriots inactives for NFL Week 7 vs. Bears
summary: Just 30 minutes before announcing their game-day inactives for their Thursday night game in Chicago, the New England Patriots made an update to their injury report. Cornerback Christian Gonzalez was now questionable with an illness. However, the Pro Bowler has ultimately been cleared for the game and is not listed among the six inactives. Whether […]
full_text: Just 30 minutes before announcing their game-day inactives for their Thursday night game in Chicago, the New England Patriots made an update to their injury report. Cornerback Christian Gonzalez was now questionable with an illness. However, the Pro Bowler has ultimately been cleared for the game and is not listed among the six inactives. Whether or not he will play his usual high number of snaps remains to be seen, but he did go through pre-game warmups without any noticeable limitations. As for the players who are out for Week 7, they look as follows: Patriots inactives QB3 Behren Morton OL Ben Brown DT Joshua Farmer CB Carlton Davis III CB Karon Prunty CB Channing Canada The Patriots originally ruled out five players on their final injury report on Wednesday . Besides right guard Ben Brown (knee) and cornerbacks Carlton Davis (neck), Karon Prunty (hamstring) and Channing Canada (hamstring), the team also placed left Alijah Vera-Tucker (hamstring) in that particular group. However, he has since moved to another: those on injured reserve, where he was placed on Thursday. This meant the Patriots had to deactivate two extra players on top of the four remaining inactives. They did so through a pair of healthy scratches: quarterback Behren Morton and defensive tackle Joshua Farmer. The former is the emergency option at his position, the latter missed two days of practice this week for personal reasons. Bears inactives QB3 Case Keenum RB Kyle Monangai OL Jordan McFadden DT Jayden Loving LB T.J. Edwards LB Jack Sanborn CB Nick McCloud Like the Patriots, the Bears are missing some important players either on a reserve list or because they have been made inactive for Thursday’s game. The latter group includes No. 2 running back Kyle Monangai (thumb, toe) and a pair of linebackers in T.J. Edwards (hamstring) and Jack Sanborn (concussion) — the former a starter on defense, the latter a core special teamer. Kickoff between the Patriots and Bears at Chicago’s Soldier Field is scheduled for 1 p.m. ET .

title: NFL Picks Week 7: Laissez Les Bon Temp Rouler
summary: The New Orleans Saints make their way to Paris to face the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 7 as part of the NFL’s International Game series, the first ever in France. The Saints enter this pivotal game coming off an uneven win over the Giants, while the Steelers enter this showdown fresh off an overtime win in […]
full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - NOVEMBER 13: Chris Olave #12 of the New Orleans Saints attempts to catch the ball while being guarded by Arthur Maulet #35 of the Pittsburgh Steelers during the first half of the game at Acrisure Stadium on November 13, 2022 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Justin K. Aller/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New Orleans Saints make their way to Paris to face the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 7 as part of the NFL’s International Game series, the first ever in France. The Saints enter this pivotal game coming off an uneven win over the Giants, while the Steelers enter this showdown fresh off an overtime win in Tampa. The second and third quarters last week showed the Saints looking their very best this season, while the fourth quarter almost saw the Saints squander it all away. It was thankfully more good than bad in the end, but the Saints need to be good for four quarters this Sunday in France. The famously known Louisiana French phrase: “ Laissez les bon temp rouler ” means “ Let the good times roll ”, but good times have not rolled in New Orleans this season, and honesty haven’t for quite some time now. It has gotten to the point that team owner Gayle Benson has publicly stated dissatisfaction with the coaching staff and front office recently. If Mrs. Benson and the Saints aren’t rolling in good times following a statement win in Paris on Sunday, it may be heads that roll on Airline Drive on Monday. Now let’s take a look at this and all of the matchups in Week 7. Last week, I went 8-6 I told you so : Broncos over Seahawks! What do I know : Ravens over Browns? *** WEEK 7 Thursday, October 22nd – Thursday Night Football Patriots(4-2) at Be ars (4-2) This should be an offensive showdown between Drake Maye and Caleb Williams but this one will surprisingly turn out to be a defensive affair in the Windy City. New England wins 24-17. Pick: Patriots *** Sunday, October 25th – Very Early Game Steelers(4-2) at* Saints(2-4) – Stade de France – Paris, France The New Orleans Saints being the ambassador team to be the first to take the NFL to France is as much of a no-brainer decision as you can get. The city, founded by France, named after the Duke of Orléans, is famous for its French Quarter and French influences that permeates every part of its being. As obvious as the choice was, it was apparently a choice that Gayle Benson had to work extremely hard to secure, and she absolutely wants to leave Paris with a great showing from her team, highlighted by a win. A win for a city and franchise that has seen few of them in big moments in recent years. The Steelers themselves may not represent a monumental win, but what the game represents is even more important than the opponent being faced. The Saints and Steelers are almost mirror-image middle of the road NFL offenses this season. Both are average at passing and below average at rushing. Neither have inspired confidence for their fanbases, but the differences between the teams become clear when you look at their defenses, and it is there where this game will ultimately be won. Pittsburgh’s top-ten passing defense will make the difference in this close contest as the game tightens up in the fourth quarter. Thankfully, the Saints won’t embarrass their fans or their owner in a big game this time, but they simply won’t have enough to pull out this win in a big spot. Do they want to win? Certainly. Are all parts of this team motivated to win this game? Absolutely. Unfortunately, want and motivation aren’t enough to win football games, no matter how badly that win is needed. We’ll soon see if close is enough for Mrs. Benson. Pittsburgh wins 27-23. Pick: Steelers *** Sunday, October 25th- Early Games 49ers(6-0) at Falcons(2-4) Atlanta’s winless streak at home continues here against the NFC’s top team. San Francisco wins 26-12. Pick: 49ers *** Bengals(3-2) at Ravens(4-2) This AFC North showdown will come down to a game-winning field goal in the closing moments for Cincy. Cincinnati wins 20-17. Pick: Bengals *** Buccaneers(1-5) at Panthers(3-2) Another week without Baker Mayfield, another loss for Tampa, as Carolina widens their lead in the division. Carolina wins 21-14. Pick: Panthers *** Giants(3-2-1) at Texans(2-4) After losing their first four games, Houston will win three-straight with a home win over JJ McCarthy and the Giants. Houston wins 24-21. Pick: Texans *** Colts(2-4) at Vikings(5-0) The front office shake-up in Indy won’t provide any help yet this week at undefeated Minnesota, as the Vikings stay on a roll. Minnesota wins 30-24. Pick: Vikings *** Dolphins(0-5) at Jets(2-4) The Jets get their first layup win since Week 1, in the form of the Dolphins. New York wins 31-16. Pick: Jets *** Browns(4-2) at Titans(1-5) Fresh off a huge win over the Ravens last week, Cleveland gets an easy win over the Titans. Cleveland wins 28-17. Pick: Browns *** Sunday, October 25th – Late Games Broncos(4-2) at Cardinals(2-4) Arizona is fresh off a massive win over the Rams, and could catch Denver overlooking them as well, as the Broncos are eyeing their showdown against Kansas City next week, but they won’t. Sean Payton will have his team well prepared for a definitive win in Arizona. Denver wins 30-14. Pick: Broncos *** Packers(4-2) at Lions(3-2) Since their low-point home loss to Atlanta, Green Bay has been on a roll, and that roll continues in Detroit against their NFC North rivals. Green Bay wins 30-20. Pick: Packers *** Rams(2-4) at Raiders(3-3) Sean McVay and Klint Kubiak could have an offensive show on their hands in Sin City, but it will be the defenses that control this game, as the Rams defense finds a way to hold off Vegas in the end. Los Angeles wins 19-14. Pick: Rams *** Sunday Night Football Chiefs(5-0) at Seahawks(3-3) – Game of the Week Seattle has been struggling as of late, losing their last two games. To be fair, those losses came to two of the NFL’s best teams this season, but it doesn’t get any easier, as now they face arguably the NFL’s best team this season. Kansas City has impressed, looking again like the team that has dominated the AFC for almost a decade now, but the reigning Super Bowl Champions will fight them all the way through in this showdown. Ultimately, Patrick Mahomes finds a way to seal the win in the end. Kansas City wins 28-24. Pick: Chiefs *** Monday, October 26th – Monday Night Football Doubleheader Cowboys(2-4) at Eagles(2-4) Tanner McKee has been thrust in the spotlight, on Monday Night Football no less, but despite a solid effort, his Eagles will lose at home to their bitter NFC East rivals. Dallas wins 21-20. Pick: Cowboys *** That’s how I see Week 7 shaping up. Leave us your picks, comments, and insight below!

full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - OCTOBER 18: Chase Young #99 of the New Orleans Saints celebrates a play against the New York Giants during their game at MetLife Stadium on October 18, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Al Bello/Getty Images) | Getty Images Finally, another win for the New Orleans Saints, and that should improve the rankings after a tough couple of games. NFL.com – 20 (+7) “If you’re in the market for the wackiest game of the week, it took place at MetLife Stadium. New Orleans faced a 10-0 deficit just before halftime, then rattled off five straight scoring drives — and that was before an outrageous fourth quarter that saw the Saints possess the ball seven times, scoring once to ultimately hold on for a 34-27 win over the Giants. Chaos aside, the Saints’ defense finally found a competitive streak and capitalized on opportunities, giving Tyler Shough and Co. enough chances to climb back into the game and build a healthy lead. The finish left plenty to clean up, but that’s better than a fifth loss.” Fox Sports – 24 (+3) “ Kellen Moore held off what might have been his own Waterloo when his Saints held on by their fingernails to beat the Giants on Sunday. Before that, they had lost three straight, and that seemed to have Saints owner Gayle Benson fuming. Now they’ll all head to Paris for a game against the Steelers, feeling at least a little better about things. A win there would give them a nice boost heading into their bye week. But the way their defense nearly threw away the game against the Giants, I wouldn’t count on that.“ Bleacher Report – 24 (+1) “The New Orleans Saints came close to putting together a statement game, but the New York Giants turned it into a fourth-quarter nail-biter. The win shouldn’t shield head coach Kellen Moore from criticism. His team still needs to put together complete performances. Tyler Shough didn’t take any sacks against the Giants, which is ideal for a quarterback playing with two broken bones in his non-throwing hand (h/t ESPN’s Adam Schefter ). New Orleans can gain some momentum with a win over the Pittsburgh Steelers in Paris. If the Saints pull that off, Moore would quiet his critics for now. — Moton ” CBS Sports – 26 (=) “With the heat from the owner, they won a tough road game against the Giants. But they sure did make it interesting.” Sports Illustrated – 25 (=) “Kellen Moore pulling his starters (because of Paris, which is a fine reason in retrospect) and nearly giving up a 24-point comeback to J.J. McCarthy was very nearly the move that would have defined Moore’s coaching tenure in New Orleans.”

title: Our Offense vs. Their Defense: Pittsburgh Steelers
summary: Bonjour, Who Dat Nation! The Saints have traveled across the world and will find their offense going up against one of the best defenses in the league. The Steelers’ defense is a top-10 unit overall, and the matchup advantages they have could allow them to exploit the biggest issue with the Saints’ offense. The Steelers’ […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - OCTOBER 18: Tyler Shough #6 of the New Orleans Saints scrambles with the ball under pressure from Charlie Jones #89 of the New York Giants during the second quarter at MetLife Stadium on October 18, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Al Bello/Getty Images) | Getty Images Bonjour, Who Dat Nation! The Saints have traveled across the world and will find their offense going up against one of the best defenses in the league. The Steelers’ defense is a top-10 unit overall, and the matchup advantages they have could allow them to exploit the biggest issue with the Saints’ offense. The Steelers’ defense is led by a legend in the making, T.J. Watt. So far this season, Watt has 4.5 sacks, 6 tackles for loss, and 15 total tackles. He also has a forced fumble and an interception, which he returned for a touchdown. The Steelers’ defensive unit as a whole has 16 sacks on the season, which ranks in the top 10 in the league. They are also in the top 10 in turnover differential at +3 on the season. The Steelers’ defense is what is carrying the team. So far, no opponent has been able to score more than 27 points against them. They feature elite players at every level, including Watt and Alex Highsmith as pass rushers, along with Jalen Ramsey, who can play all over the secondary. This is not a matchup that will be easy for the Saints. If anything, the Steelers may very well be able to exploit the Saints’ biggest weakness, which is the offensive line. The Saints average 224 passing yards per game, while the Steelers allow only 204 passing yards per game. The Steelers average about 2.7 sacks per game, while the Saints are allowing 2.17. Having Asim Richards on the offensive line against T.J. Watt and Alex Highsmith is something Kellen Moore will have to prepare for. The Steelers’ rushing defense does present an opportunity for the Saints to have some success, as Pittsburgh is allowing 103.2 rushing yards per game. Unfortunately, the Saints are averaging only 97.3 rushing yards per game. The Saints were able to establish a running game last week against the Giants and will have to do so again in Paris. If they are unable to establish the run, it will put them in obvious third-and-long situations. If the Saints are going to win this game, they will have to make sure to utilize motion to identify coverages, establish the running game early, and keep the offense on schedule. Third-and-long situations are a recipe for disaster against a pass rush this dangerous, especially with an offensive line that has obvious protection issues. There is some excitement building around the possibility that Jordyn Tyson could make his season debut this week since he traveled with the team. If he is able to play in this game, it would be a big addition, giving the Saints another weapon in the passing game. Tyson is also a very willing blocker at the receiver position and could help improve the running game a little bit as well, especially if the Saints are able to get their running backs to the edge. This will be a big test for the Saints’ offense and coaching staff. Hopefully, they are fully prepared and up for the task. How do you think the Saints’ offense matches up against the Steelers’ defense? Share your thoughts in the comments.

summary: Last week, the New Orleans Saints’ draft position didn’t change after losing to the Vikings, but a win over the Giants had a major impact. Entering Week 7, the Saints are now projected to select pick 12 overall in the 2027 NFL Draft. Georgia LB Chris Cole Last year’s NFL Draft had an incredible linebacker […]
full_text: ATHENS, GA - OCTOBER 17: Georgia linebacker Chris Cole (9) reacts during the college football game between the Auburn Tigers and the Georgia Bulldogs on October 17th, 2026, at Sanford Stadium in Athens, GA. (Photo by Rich von Biberstein/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Last week, the New Orleans Saints’ draft position didn’t change after losing to the Vikings, but a win over the Giants had a major impact. Entering Week 7, the Saints are now projected to select pick 12 overall in the 2027 NFL Draft. Georgia LB Chris Cole Last year’s NFL Draft had an incredible linebacker duo out of Ohio State, and so far this season, Sonny Styles has been an incredible addition to the Washington Commanders, and the same is true for Arvell Reese with the New York Giants. Linebacker has become even more important in today’s NFL World, and after Demario Davis left in free agency and Kaden Elliss went down with injury, it’s clear the Saints need upgrades. Pete Werner hasn’t been bad, and Danny Stutsman is still developing, but adding a long-term, high-potential, talented LB to this group could improve everything. Out of Georgia, Chris Cole is having a season of his own. At 6-foot-3, Cole is incredibly fast, a hard hitter, a consistent tackler, can rush the QB at OLB, is good in pass coverage, and will not stop moving. He’s one of those players that you say throughout the game, “oh, there he is again”. Clemson CB Ashton Hampton Sticking with defense, cornerback is still one of the Saints’ biggest needs. The Saints may have benched Kool-Aid McKinstry, but they say he had a migraine early in the game, which is why Martin Emerson Jr. was playing. It’s a bit of a confusing situation, but no matter what, the Saints need a new CB1. To find that cheap, selecting one in the first round is the way to do it, and Ashton Hampton could be that player. For Clemson this season, Hampton has been lockdown. He is leading the nation in pass deflections and shut down one of the most talented WRs in college football, Malachi Toney. He, of course, has some things to work on, but with his length, Hampton is a lockdown corner that the Saints should consider adding to their defense.
