summary: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are the stories you need to know as the Giants get set to travel to Houston to face the Texans this Sunday. Why the Giants felt compelled to turn to J.J. McCarthy now | The Athletic It was immediately evident that the coaching staff viewed McCarthy’s legs as […]
full_text: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are the stories you need to know as the Giants get set to travel to Houston to face the Texans this Sunday. Why the Giants felt compelled to turn to J.J. McCarthy now | The Athletic It was immediately evident that the coaching staff viewed McCarthy’s legs as an asset. Even as he was cramming to learn the playbook, the coaches installed quarterback-run packages for McCarthy. McCarthy’s scrambles will be a bonus. The true value of having him under center is that he will allow the Giants to reincorporate the quarterback-run elements that were a pillar of their offensive identity with Dart. Even though McCarthy isn’t as effective as Dart as a rusher, defenses will at least need to respect the quarterback as a running threat again. That should open lanes on zone reads, which are desperately needed as the offensive line and running backs have struggled. #BaldyBreakdown on McCarthy’s top attribute . @Giants @jjmccarthyy18 the very best thing he does is he throws a great deep ball..It was on display last week..Yes, he does have other areas that has to improve but if you are a Giants fan this is one area i would look for v @texans and beyond #BaldysBreakdowns pic.twitter.com/HC5Ni7iPZd — Brian Baldinger (@BaldyNFL) October 22, 2026 How the Giants offense changes with J.J. McCarthy at quarterback | The Record In a quest to rediscover his game with the Giants, J.J. McCarthy has also found his voice. Offensive coordinator Matt Nagy spearheaded the challenge of creating a player-driven offense centered around the diversified skill set of Jaxson Dart, and what the Giants developed in terms of identity and influence lasted one game and seven snaps. John Harbaugh has no time for second-guessing in pursuit of his singular Giants goal | New York Post No big announcement. No detailed explanation of why, why now and what it all means. The Giants reported to work Wednesday, the game plan was put out there and that was when the players learned what the two quarterbacks involved were told a day earlier: It is J.J. McCarthy in, Jameis Winston out. Giants Mailbag: How long is J.J. McCarthy’s leash? | SNY.tv What would the Giants have to see from McCarthy to give him a legit shot to compete for the starting QB job in 2027? This is among my favorite topics because of how heated people get over the hypothetical world where Dart loses his job. He is the starting quarterback for New York. The Giants plan for him to be their starting quarterback the next decade-plus. They love the player. They love the person more. Top to bottom they believe in him. Dart is a major reason Harbaugh took this job. McCarthy would need to go on a truly remarkable run over these next 12 weeks/11 games to shake that up. Play like a top-10 quarterback in the NFL during that stretch. Lead the Giants to double-digit victories. Secure the NFC East. Then, in my opinion, get the Giants to (at least) the NFC Championship, or at the minimum, not be the reason they lose in the divisional round. I understand how much fans believe in and love Dart, but if McCarthy can do all that, you’re probably willing to move forward with what’s working, no? Nabers scouting report on McCarthy "Very good arm talent, throws a great ball…that's what we're going to rally around" Malik Nabers on J.J. McCarthy: pic.twitter.com/YOMwjULsl2 — SNY Giants (@SNYGiants) October 22, 2026 2026 NFL offensive line rankings | PFF 17. New York Giants (no change). The Giants went into last week without right tackle Jermaine Eluemunor, and then sat left tackle Andrew Thomas for the final 25 snaps of the loss to the New Orleans Saints after being checked for a concussion. Rookie right guard Francis Mauigoa was the only player to secure a PFF pass-blocking grade below 65.0, coming in at 33.0. Further, the Giants struggled to get much room in the run game, with their running backs rushing for just 34 yards on 14 carries. Re-Ranking Ashton Jeanty, 2nd-Year NFL RBs After Week 6 | Bleacher Report 8. Cam Skattebo, New York Giants. Not that long ago, Cam Skattebo would have ranked far higher on this list. After showing some flashes as a rookie, the 2025 fourth-rounder entered Year 2 as the lead back for a young and exciting Giants offense.Many expected a breakout 2026 season from Skattebo, but his ball-security struggles have complicated that outlook. Ball security hasn’t been his only concern; his rushing efficiency has also declined. In five starts as a rookie, he had two games with at least 100 total yards, scored five touchdowns and averaged 4.1 yards per carry. In six games this year, Skattebo has one 100-yard performance and one touchdown while averaging just 3.6 yards per carry. Ball security has also been a concern, and he received no touches in Week 6. Proposing NFL trade deadline offers | ESPN.com Giants get: DT Dalvin Tomlinson, 2028 seventh-round pick Chargers get: 2028 sixth-round pick. Another veteran reserve for the Chargers who could be on the move between now and the deadline, Tomlinson would be coming full circle after starting his career in New York. The well-traveled defensive tackle isn’t the interior disrupter we saw earlier in his career, but Tomlinson is also only two years removed from an 18-knockdown season with the Browns in 2024. He’s a pending free agent with Los Angeles and due $2.1 million over the rest of 2026. The Giants started the season thin on the interior after trading away Dexter Lawrence II and losing Roy Robertson-Harris to a torn Achilles. New York has gotten by through adding veterans such as Shelby Harris and DJ Reader, and Tomlinson would be another defensive tackle in that vein. The only Giants DT with a sack this season is CJ Okoye, so even a modest contribution from Tomlinson while playing about 35-40% of the defensive snaps would go a long way. NFL Trade Deadline: The Top Trade Candidate On All 32 Teams | FOX Sports Trade Candidate: Edge Kayvon Thibodeaux. It would be hard to do if the Giants stay in contention because of the season-ending injury to Brian Burns, but Thibodeaux is still their most valuable trade chip — a young pass rusher with an expiring contract. He hasn’t been the same since he had 11.5 sacks in 2023, and hasn’t had any in the last 11 games. He’s been mostly a non-factor on the Giants’ defense this season. Surely someone who needs pass-rushing help sees his talent and believes they can untap whatever is left of his potential. From Big Blue View Does J.J. title: Fantasy Football 2026: Week 7 preview – Start/sit and more
summary: Welcome to Week 7! Week 6 was lowest scoring week of the season so far. Across the land, fantasy players kept refreshing their devices all day Sunday, to no avail. No player hit 30 fantasy points in Half PPR for the first time since Week 6 of the 2024 season (excluding Week 18). Only four […]
full_text: Ken Walker - revenge game? | Getty Images Welcome to Week 7! Week 6 was lowest scoring week of the season so far. Across the land, fantasy players kept refreshing their devices all day Sunday, to no avail. No player hit 30 fantasy points in Half PPR for the first time since Week 6 of the 2024 season (excluding Week 18). Only four players topped 25 points. I guess this is what we should expect when the Lions and Bengals are on a Bye. Unusually low fantasy scoring wasn’t the only anomaly in Week 6. The Colts outgained the previously winless Titans by 213 yards and lost. The Ravens held the Browns to three points through 50 minutes and lost. The Rams kept the Cardinals out of the end zone and lost. The Saints scored 34 straight points, pulled some of their starters, and were in real danger of losing. But wait, there’s more! The four NFC East teams went winless for the second straight week – something that has never happened, for any division, since the AFL-NFL merger (there are intra-division games almost every week, so that’s not quite as crazy as it sounds). And more craziness — Myles Garrett left the Browns for the Rams this past offseason – the NFL’s premiere pass rusher would finally get to play on a Super Bowl contender! Well, guess what? The 4-2 Browns are in first place, while the 2-4 Rams are in last. Will normal scoring return in Week 7? Fantasy managers certainly hope so. Stats of the Week : Every team in the AFC North and NFC North is over .500. 2. K enneth Walker III has 665 rushing yards in his first five games with Kansas City – that’s the most for any player in his first five games on a team in NFL history. 3. Patrick Mahomes got his 100 th win in his 131 st start, tying Tom Brady for the fastest to 100 QB wins in NFL history. 4. The Cardinals have more wins at SoFi Stadium this season (2) than the Rams and Chargers combined. 5. The 2-4 Rams have outgained their opponents by 644 yards this season, the widest margin in the NFL. 6. Since Aaron Glenn became Head Coach of the Jets at the start of the 2025 season, his team has been outscored 97-6 in the final two minutes of the first half. 7. You can’t make it up: The Chargers are 0-6 to start a season for the first time since 2000. 37 year-old Jim Harbaugh started the first five games at QB for the Chargers in 2000. And with that…let’s get to week 7. Note: The PIT@NO game is in Paris – reveillez-vous, and set those lineups early! Bye Weeks: BUF, JAC, LAC, WAS Week 7 Rides, Fades and Sleepers For those who are familiar with this column, you know the drill. For everyone else: The Rides, Fades, and Sleepers is an analysis of players that I think are primed for an especially strong or poor performance, often as compared to consensus expectations. This isn’t a straight-up Start/Sit exercise. As a general rule, start your studs. I’ll rarely list the most obvious names at a position as “Rides” because those players are almost always expected to have strong performances. You don’t need me or anyone else telling you to start Jaxon Smith-Njigba . While this analysis is intended for season-long play, it works for DFS formats too. Half PPR scoring and Expert Consensus Rankings (ECR) are used for the column. Each week, I’m picking a Ride, Fade, and Sleeper of the Week. The rules: The Ride of the Week can’t be a truly elite option, the Fade can’t be someone who nobody is starting anyway, and the Sleeper must be an actual sleeper, from down in the rankings. Last week, my Rides, Fades, and Sleepers did well, with more hits than misses. You can check my work here. *** Ride of the Week: Tucker Kraft (@DET). Kraft only has one TD on the season and is averaging just 7.3 fantasy points per game (FPPG), so you might be surprised to see this choice. He did see eight targets last week, and that’s encouraging. Green Bay’s offense is mainly flowing through Matthew Golden and Christian Watson, but there’s room for Kraft. I think he’ll show up this week against the Lions, in what should be a high-scoring divisional tilt. Detroit has yielded nine TDs to opposing tight ends in just five games, and the most FPPG to the position. They’ve also allowed the most catches and yards to TEs even though most teams have played six games to their five. The return of safety Brian Branch should help, but the Lions’ defense hasn’t stopped anyone. Don’t overthink it – Jordan Love is dealing, the offense should be more efficient with Josh Jacobs returning, and the Packers’ passing game is in a smash spot this week. Play them all. Fade of the Week: Patrick Mahomes (@SEA). The Chiefs are undefeated, but Mahomes hasn’t exactly been lighting it up for fantasy, and I doubt that changes in the Ken Walker revenge game. Mahomes hasn’t topped 17 fantasy points in any of his last three games after a fast start, and the injuries to his receivers haven’t helped. The Seahawks need this game badly and their defense is allowing the fewest passing yards and third fewest FPPG to opposing QBs. I hate betting against Mahomes, and with the Byes and injuries you might not have a better option, but temper expectations on the road against Mike McDonald’s defense. Sleeper of the Week: Kyler Murray (vs. IND). Murray is ranked just outside the Top-12 QBs this week and with several prominent QBs out and a favorable home matchup on tap, I think that’s too low. Murray has been disappointing but he’s coming off his best effort of the season (18 fantasy points) and importantly, for the first time this year he looked comfortable taking off from the pocket. That translated to 10 carries for 51 yards against the Saints. It might not be the Kyler of old, but for those who were all over Kyler as a sleeper in the preseason (I was not in that crowd), it’s a good sign. The Vikings are rolling and the Colts (who fired GM Chris Ballard earlier this week) are reeling. Murray is rested off the Bye and should have plenty of success against a subpar defense that likely will be without top corner Sauce Gardner. He’s a QB1 for me this week. Quarterback: Elite options this week – Brock Purdy and Drake Maye ; the analysis starts below them. Rides: Jordan Love (@DET) and Jared Goff (vs. GB). Play what you can in this big divisional game, which has the highest Vegas total of the week (53.5). Both QBs come in hot, and because the Lions can’t stop anyone, they’re playing shootout after shootout. Goff is the QB3 on the season, while Love clocks in at QB10. Love has accounted for two TDs in every start so far this season and but for some horrible drops from his receivers he could’ve had four or five this past Sunday night against Dallas. I could bore you with more stats but just trust me on this. Both QBs are Top-5 plays this week. Others ranked in the Top-15 this week who I think will outperform their ranking: Joe Burrow (@BAL, based in large part on history as the last six meetings between these two teams have averaged almost 54 points), the red-hot C.J. Stroud (vs. NYG) and the orange-hot Aaron Rodgers (@NO, who allow almost 30 points per game). Sleepers: Geno Smith (vs. MIA) has a good matchup this week (seventh most FPPG allowed to opposing QBs) and he’s been slowly getting some of his weapons back, including Omar Cooper, Jr. with a big contribution last week. He’s a pretty safe floor play if you need him. If you need a second QB in a Superflex, or a streamer for someone who is hurt or on a Bye, there are some OK options, including Tanner McKee (vs DAL; I’m not much of a believer but guys, it’s Dallas) , and Michael Penix, Jr. (vs. SF). Fades: I just can’t do it, Bo Nix (@ARI). It’s a great matchup (fourth most FPPG allowed to opposing QBs), but he’s been SO BAD. When a QB throws for less than 125 yards in back-to-back starts, he’s a very tough click. He’s also not running (less than ten fantasy points, total, from rushing through six games), and that’s been a big component of his fantasy value in the past. It’s tough to sit Tyler Shough (v. PIT) after he finished as the QB2 last…

title: Former NY Giant joins the Philadelphia Eagles
summary: The Philadelphia Eagles have signed former New York Giants offensive lineman Evan Neal to their practice squad. Neal had recently been released from the Las Vegas Raiders practice squad, where he landed after being released in the Giants’ final cutdowns following the 2026 training camp. Neal, the 7th overall pick in the 2022 NFL Draft, […]
full_text: ﻿Former New York Giants offensive lineman Evan Neal | Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles have signed former New York Giants offensive lineman Evan Neal to their practice squad. Neal had recently been released from the Las Vegas Raiders practice squad, where he landed after being released in the Giants’ final cutdowns following the 2026 training camp. Neal, the 7th overall pick in the 2022 NFL Draft, has been the biggest draft bust in recent memory for the Giants. He hasn’t played a regular season snap for the Giants since the 2024 season, when he filled in for Jermaine Eluemunor at right tackle. Eluemunor had originally been slated to play guard that year, but moved out to right tackle when Neal suffered an injury in camp. The Giants then converted Neal to guard in 2025, which was where he played in the 2026 off-season as well, but he never found his way to the field on game day. The Eagles’ decision to sign Neal comes as their offensive line is reshuffled by the retirement of RT Lane Johnson and the trade of OC Cam Jurgens. Philadelphia always seemed like a likely landing spot for Neal after he was released by the Giants. The Eagles have long prized size and power in their offensive linemen, both of which Neal has in spades. It remains to be seen if he’ll get the chance to compete for a starting job — or even be active on game days — as he attempts to salvage a once-promising career.

full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. — The New York Giants top three offensive tackles returned to the practice field on Thursday, one day after all were held out of practice due to injuries. Left tackle Andrew Thomas (groin), right tackle Jermaine Eluemunor (calf), and swing tackle Marcus Mbow were all practicing in some fashion on Thursday. Defensively, the news was not as good. Starting inside linebacker Tremaine Edmunds (shoulder) and starting cornerback Greg Newsome II (concussion) did not practice for a second straight day. Tight end Chris Manhertz (calf) also missed practice. Safety Jevon Holland, who is in the concussion protocol, was a limited practice participant. Cornerback Paulson Adebo, who was designated to return from IR this week, was another limited participant. Defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson said this about Adebo: “He’s healthy right now. We’ll see how it all plays out. I just love having the young man back out there, man,” Wilson said. “His energy, his personality, back asking questions. We’ll see how all that shakes out in terms of who plays or not, but he’s been a very good player in the National Football League, and if he gets his opportunity to play, we expect him to play well.” Punter Jordan Stout remained on the injury report for a second straight day, but special teams coordinator said “I don’t have any concerns” about Stout. title: NY Giants DC Dennard Wilson won’t tolerate ‘traitors to the defense’
summary: The New York Giants surrendered 34 straight points to the New Orleans Saints last Sunday. Defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson was critical on Thursday of the effort of players he felt did not hustle to the ball, calling it “unacceptable” and calling them “traitors to the defense.” “A few plays got out, especially in the pass […]
full_text: Alvin Kamra of the Saints en route to a 31-yard touchdown reception vs. the Giants on Sunday. | Getty Images The New York Giants surrendered 34 straight points to the New Orleans Saints last Sunday. Defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson was critical on Thursday of the effort of players he felt did not hustle to the ball, calling it “unacceptable” and calling them “traitors to the defense.” “A few plays got out, especially in the pass game, because of missed tackles. Then last week, we’re not happy, and I wasn’t happy with our effort running to the ball,” Wilson said. “We put some stuff on tape that was not characteristic of a New York Giant defense, and it’s unacceptable, and it will be changed. “I look at guys that don’t run [to] the ball, and I call them traitors because they’re traitors to the defense. At the end of the day, when you have a traitor to the defense, you either have to make adjustments to get them off the field, you have to get somebody else on the field, or they have to correct their behaviors. Last week was one of those things where we did not, on every play, run to the ball, and it was unacceptable.” Wilson did not specify the play or plays he was referring to. He was adamant, though, that he won’t tolerate it. “The guys know it, and this week when you see them out there, they will be flying around 100 miles per hour with a hair on fire,” Wilson said. “It’s 11-1 when you play defense. It’s 11 guys humming to the ball, and when you don’t do that, you don’t erase plays. We had a few plays that got out on us. “Everybody’s hunting. It’s probably not a touchdown. You get them down on the ground. It’s not an explosive play. You eliminate explosive plays with energy and effort. That’s how you eliminate it.” This might be the play that annoyed Wilson the most: Had to be uncomfortable re-watching the Kamara touchdown in the film room… pic.twitter.com/FORqfv4rMa — Dan Duggan (@DDuggan21) October 22, 2026 Nickel cornerback Dru Phillips on Thursday took accountability for his part in the play. He said it was “embarrassing” to be called out in front of his teammates. “You have 10 other guys depending on you as well. You can’t expect just one guy to make a tackle,” Phillips said. “These guys are depending on you, and when you’re just not giving that hustle that you should be you feel like I let this person down, or I let everybody down. “There’s no excuse for it. I’ve gotta hustle.” The Giants were one of the worst tackling teams in the NFL in Week 6. Missed Tackles in Week 6 Data: @pfref pic.twitter.com/GGPjUBLUuK — SFdata9ers🏈📊 (@sfdata9ers) October 22, 2026 “Last week was one of our worst tackling games for whatever reason,” Wilson said. Wilson said he has no issue calling out players “We confront everything,” Wilson said. “If you’re not doing something to help the team and you’re hurting the team, if your effort is bad, if you have a lack of toughness, it gets pointed out, and it gets pointed out in front of everybody. Not only in a defensive meeting, it gets pointed out in the full team meeting. “When you have behaviors that’s unacceptable, we’re not going to accept it. If you don’t change the behaviors, we have to change the players.”

title: NFL predictions, Week 7: Not much faith in Giants to upset Texans
summary: How does the Big Blue View staff see Sunday’s New York Giants vs. Houston Texans game? See our picks for that game and the rest of the NFL Week 7 slate below. Chris Pflum Bottom line up front: I don’t expect the Giants to win this game. I won’t go so far as to say […]
full_text: How does the Big Blue View staff see Sunday’s New York Giants vs. Houston Texans game? See our picks for that game and the rest of the NFL Week 7 slate below. Chris Pflum Bottom line up front: I don’t expect the Giants to win this game. I won’t go so far as to say that they can’t win the game, but things are stacking up against them. The Giants are, frankly, beat up. left tackle Andrew Thomas is dealing with his groin injury, right tackle Jermaine Eluemunor has his calf injury, and offensive tackle Marcus Mbow suffered a knee injury at the end of the Saints game. Cornerback Greg Newsome II, safety Jevon Holland, and cornerback Colton Hood are in the concussion protocol, and tight end Theo Johnson is still dealing with a neck injury. On the flip side, DeMeco Ryans has retaken control of the Texans’ defense, while C.J. Stroud has been playing some of the best football of his career. And though the Texans’ run game has been bad, Stroud is getting weapons in WRs Marvin Harrison Jr. and Tank Dell, while the Giants are scraping the bottom of the depth chart in their secondary. Starting J.J. McCarthy could provide a spark to the Giants’ offense and allow them to play the style of football for which they were built. But I just don’t know if that would be enough in the face of the Giants’ injuries. A win going into the BYE week would be an amazing boost and allow the Giants to keep pace in the division. And the upset could absolutely happen — football has been weird this year and we’ve seen some absolutely wild outcomes. But I’m afraid this could be an ugly one for New York. Pick: Texans Tony Del Genio I’ve thought since before the season started that this was one of the most likely games for the Giants to lose. The Texans’ poor start made me start to reconsider. Their defense, one of the best in the NFL last year, has had a slow start. Cornerbacks Derek Stingley Jr. and Kamari Lassiter have not played up to their previous standards, so there is an opportunity for the Giants to stay in the game and pull off an upset if they can get their passing game to click. The Texans have given up more than 30 points three times. Last week Trevor Lawrence shredded them for 306 yards and 4 TDs. Alas, the strength of the Texans’ D is their pass rush off the edge, with the NFL’s best pass rusher, Will Anderson Jr., and Danielle Hunter (14 sacks and 60 pressures between them) leading the way. The Giants sadly have Andrew Thomas and Jermaine Eluemunor both dealing with injuries. If both cannot play or play at less than 100%, it may be a long afternoon for J.J. McCarthy in his first Giants start. Despite my misgivings about John Harbaugh making him the starter in this game rather than after the break, McCarthy does give them the best chance to mitigate the Texans’ pass rush. The Texans’ run defense is not formidable, but to say the least the Giants’ run blocking is not either, regardless of who the lead running back du jour is on Sunday. When Houston is on offense, C.J. Stroud got off to a bad start this season but has played much better for the past month. The Giants’ defensive back room is decimated by injury, with Greg Newsome, Jevon Holland, and Colton Hood all dealing with concussions, although Paulson Adebo is expected to be back this week. Who is going to cover Nico Collins, one of the NFL’s best big receivers, is anyone’s guess. Jaylin Noel and Xavier Hutchinson are no slouches, either, and the Giants will see Marvin Harrison Jr. for the second time after he caught his only TD of the season again them in the Arizona game. Pick : Texans David Hartman The Giants head to Houston this Sunday after a disappointing home loss to the Saints. J.J. McCarthy came out of the bullpen in the second half of that contest and the Big Blue news of the week is that McCarthy will start this game. The timing is slightly surprising given that New York has its Bye next week, but here we are, with a former Top-10 pick getting a shot at reviving his career after he failed in Minnesota. Can J.J. lead his team to victory, and keep the G-Men in first place in the division? This writer is very skeptical, although to be fair the Giants will remain in first place through Week 7 regardless of the outcome of this game. Weird, right? The plight of the once-mighty NFC East is a story for another day. Houston has some of the best defensive personnel in the NFL, led by edge Will Anderson, Jr. and corner Derek Stingley, Jr. In last year’s AFC playoffs, C.J. Stroud was a turnover machine and an absolute mess, but Demeco Ryans’s defense was suffocating and almost carried the Texans to the AFC Championship game. This season has been an inexplicable reverse, with Stroud playing out of his mind and the defense giving up a ton of yards and points, especially through the air. The Texans started 0-4 but have won their last two, including a huge win in London last week over the first place Jaguars. Don’t expect a letdown, as they’re still reeling from their horrible start, and need this game badly. McCarthy’s play last week was encouraging, but it was in mop-up duty against a bad defense that pulled some of its starters. This is a real test, and it’s hard to ignore the 2025 tape of J.J. He was that bad (hence, his fifth round price tag when New York traded for him). His mobility is a plus, and Malik Nabers and Isaiah Likely have been uncoverable recently. Still, I don’t see McCarthy avoiding mistakes and playing well for 60 minutes, or the Giants pulling off the upset. Houston is a very good team, despite its losing record. Pick: Texans Valentine’s View Whether I picked them to win or not, with the exception of the Week 2 game against the Los Angeles Rams, I have felt that the Giants have had a good opportunity to win each game thus far this season. I can’t say I feel good about their chances. I am not sure why the point spread has ballooned from 7.5 points to start the week to 10.5 as of Thursday, but I know I don’t have confidence in the Giants’ ability to upset the Texans. The Giants squandered real opportunities to win games the last two weeks, coming away with a tie and a loss in games they easily could have won. That stretch may haunt them. What I fear most, honestly, is the Texans’ defense. Houston has been middling on defense so far, but allowed the second-fewest points in the NFL last season. There is a breakout game coming. With the Giants switching quarterbacks, struggling to run the ball, and entering the game with their top three offensive tackles at less than 100%, I think that might be this week. I don’t want it to be, but I think J.J. McCarthy’s debut as the starting quarterback might turn ugly. Pick: Texans

title: Does J.J. McCarthy give the Giants worse odds against the Texans?
summary: We already knew that the New York Giants were going to be underdogs going into their Week 7 match against the Houston Texans. The line has moved significantly by Thursday, dropping the Giants to 10.5-point underdogs against the Texans, per Fanduel. The Texans have consistently been viewed as being better than their record despite their […]
full_text: ﻿New York Giants quarterback J.J. McCarthy runs with the ball against the New Orleans Saints. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co We already knew that the New York Giants were going to be underdogs going into their Week 7 match against the Houston Texans. The line has moved significantly by Thursday, dropping the Giants to 10.5-point underdogs against the Texans, per Fanduel . The Texans have consistently been viewed as being better than their record despite their 0-4 start to the season. The Giants, meanwhile, have been viewed with skepticism despite their 3-1 start. So it was expected that the Giants would be underdogs when this week’s opening odds came out. The Giants’ odds have been dropping all week, and they were 9.5-point underdogs by Wednesday. It’s notable that the Giants’ odds got longer the day after they made a quarterback change, dropping a full point despite J.J. McCarthy coming off a game in which he threw for nearly 250 yards and a touchdown in less than a quarter. The change in the odds is likely due to a combination of factors. The Texans are getting explosive playmaker Tank Dell back from an injury that cost him the 2025 season, while the Giants could be without multiple starters in their secondary. The Giants are also dealing with injuries along their offensive line while still searching for an answer for how to run the ball. That said, the change does seem to reflect the fact that there just isn’t much confidence in J.J. McCarthy. He’s an undeniable draft bust for the Vikings and he’ll be going against a defense that was the class of the NFL the last time DeMeco Ryans was running it. Whatever the reason, or reasons, the Giants are facing long odds on what could be a very consequential game before their bye week. A win going into their bye (with the Eagles and Commanders looming after the BYE) would mean that the team will maintain their 1.5-game advantage in the division and have a better-than-even chance of making the playoffs. However, a loss will shrink that lead down to just half a game and make it significantly less likely that they make the playoffs. The Giants could certainly use the upset win, but that seems to be increasingly less likely.

title: Giants-Texans ‘5 questions’: What should we make of Houston’s 2-4 start?
summary: The New York Giants are facing the Houston Texans on Sunday, the first time since 2022 the teams have met. Giants fans have seen quarterback C.J. Stroud and the Texans on TV, but there is a lot about Sunday’s opponent we don’t know. We try to fill in the gaps with our ‘5 questions’ segment. […]
full_text: C.J. Stroud | Getty Images The New York Giants are facing the Houston Texans on Sunday, the first time since 2022 the teams have met. Giants fans have seen quarterback C.J. Stroud and the Texans on TV, but there is a lot about Sunday’s opponent we don’t know. We try to fill in the gaps with our ‘5 questions’ segment. Scott Barzilla of SB Nation’s Battle Red Blog fills us in. Ed: How are Texans fans feeling about the team right now? An 0-4 start wasn’t expected, but Houston has won two in a row. Is there a belief that they are back on track? Scott: This team has done this before in two out of the last three seasons, so I guess it isn’t completely unexpected and there is some level of faith that they can get back into the hunt. Personally, I am of the belief that you will eventually dig yourself a hole you cannot get out of, but maybe that will happen some other season. I think the key is the schedule that seems to be getting easier on the Texans in the middle. If they can get back to 6-4 then they can get to that magical ten win plateau and sneak into the playoffs. I feel like there are some systemic issues that cause these slow starts, but some of that is theory and not necessarily hard data. It seems to take this team longer to figure out what works and what doesn’t. A part of that is an effort to be a hard nosed running team when that has never been their identity. It seems every year we come back to the same place where we finally give up on that notion and go back to being a more open offense. Of course, that is just a theory. Ed: Even with two wins in a row, the Houston defense has not resembled the dominant group of last season. What has gone wrong? Is there a breakout defensive performance coming? Scott: DeMeco Ryans took back play calling duties two weeks ago. We had one really good week and then the last game. He blamed the conditions of the field and I’m sure Giants fans know all about field conditions. My personal view is that you cannot do anything in the league very long before teams begin to figure it out and make adjustments. The Ryans defense had been brilliant in San Francisco before coming to Houston, so he had a really strong five-year run. I just think opposing offensive coordinators have figured out ways to beat it. It is time for Ryans to counter with some new wrinkles. I think he is more than capable of it and will eventually get there, but he has a stubborn streak and needs to overcome the pride of thinking these guys are good enough to do whatever they want. Superior schemes win in the league and his scheme is no longer superior. Ed: If you could take one player off the Giants’ roster and put him in Houston’s lineup, who would it be? Why? Scott: Ooh, that’s a great question. I would be very tempted to take Arvell Reese right now and plug him in at linebacker. The Texans defense has been getting eaten up in the middle of their defense and a part of that is that they employ linebackers that are very stout against the run, but get eaten up in coverage. It would be really tempting to add Malik Nabers because he might be the best overall football player on the field on Sunday, but the Texans have a strong receiving core and they need some serious help on the defensive end. I would look at Skattebo as well, but he has had some fumbling issues that worry me. However, I love his running style and it is something the Texans really don’t have. Ed: What has been the biggest difference in C.J. Stroud this season? He is playing much better. Scott: I think the key with Stroud has always been what you ask him to do. There is a PepBoys commercial from the 1990s where two mechanics are trying to fit in a battery that obviously doesn’t fit. They flash back to them as kids trying to hit a square peg into a round hole. That is what the Texans offense has felt like for much of the last two seasons. They try to be a running team and that doesn’t work. They want Stroud to be a ball control quarterback that manages the game. That probably isn’t him either. The last few weeks they have abandoned that and opened the offense up. Stroud works better when things are spread out and he is working in tempo. He is not as athletic as other quarterbacks, but he is athletic enough. He doesn’t have as strong an arm as others, but he is extremely accurate when he has time to throw. So, I’d say the biggest improvement is simply recognizing what he does well and accentuating that. It seems so simple, but so few coordinators actually do that well. Ed: The Giants are a clear underdog in this one. If they are going to have a chance to pull off the upset, what should their game plan look like? Scott: As I sit here, the line has gotten to 10 points, which seems insane to me. The Texans shouldn’t be double-digit favorites in any game until they can prove they deserve it. I see them as the favorite, but not overwhelmingly so. I think the Giants offense can definitely exploit the middle of the field with ease. Even though Derek Stingley and Kamari Lassiter have the pedigree of Pro Bowl corners, they haven’t played like that this season. CeeDee Lamb torched them for 17 catches and other number one wide receivers/tight ends have torched them. So, Malik Nabors could go off on Sunday. McCarthy will have to get the ball out quick because that pass rush is coming, but if he can make quick decisions with the football then the Giants have a chance. As for the other side of the ball, that vaunted pass rush from the Giants does concern me. If they can effectively make the Texans one-dimensional then they have a definite chance on Sunday.
author: Ed Valentine

title: NY Giants QB Jameis Winston on benching: ‘My week has been the same’
summary: New York Giants quarterback Jameis Winston is heading back to the sidelines after it was announced that J.J. McCarthy would start the team’s Week 7 matchup against the Houston Texans. Winston isn’t changing his routine much even after the announcement. “My week has been the same. You move forward by continuing to focus on what […]
full_text: Jameis Winston | Getty Images New York Giants quarterback Jameis Winston is heading back to the sidelines after it was announced that J.J. McCarthy would start the team’s Week 7 matchup against the Houston Texans. Winston isn’t changing his routine much even after the announcement. “My week has been the same. You move forward by continuing to focus on what you love, and that’s my desire is being the starting quarterback for the New York Football Giants. And that’s also pointing to those around me and impacting them the best way that I can. Because like I always say, what I want for myself, I want for everyone. So, when I say that, I mean it. So, I go out there and apply it,” Winston said. Winston knows that his number can be called at any moment, just like it was in Week 2 against the Los Angeles Rams. He’s preparing for that opportunity while simultaneously supporting McCarthy in his stint as the team starter. “By being my very best,” Winston said in how he is supporting McCarthy. “That’s how you support a young man, by coming to work, being the same person every single day, by showing respect and gratitude for the opportunity that he’s presented with and the opportunity that I had and understanding that gratitude is the key to abundance in all of this. So, when you come to work and you approach it from a grateful mindset, it kind of leads out to the entire building and nothing really changed but the role itself.” Winston has been through the ups and downs of being a quarterback in the NFL. He’s been on the mountaintop as the No. 1 overall pick in the 2015 draft, and he’s also experienced plenty of lows. Winston is still why he is viewed as a valuable piece of the puzzle for the Giants. His ability to accept decisions like this is part of the reason why. “Just focusing on one day at a time is the biggest thing. I’m extremely grateful that I still get to do what I love, and that’s play football at a high level for the New York Football Giants. And being able to accept roles and understand what is your significant role, how can I be the best at my role with this team, is one of the things that you have to adjust to in this league,” Winston said. Big Blue View community, what do you make of Winston’s comments in regards to his benching? Let us know in the comments section below.

Breaking down this dysfunctional division | The Athletic Will the team you cover be a buyer before the deadline? Should they be? Carroll: The ultimate question this time of year, and the division-leading Giants will have a nicely timed bye week to evaluate their future. If they remain atop the NFC East, there’s a strong argument to be made to add pieces and try to take advantage of a weak division. But will that really be useful in a season they’re operating with backup quarterbacks? The Giants only own six picks in the upcoming draft, so trading away draft assets, particularly premium picks, for short-term gains might be shortsighted. And while John Harbaugh has been aggressive in trying to plug the holes on this team, he values draft capital. There’s no doubt the Giants could use help along the defensive line and at running back — especially after they just released Najee Harris — but a blockbuster move still feels like it’d be a surprise. That said, it’s been a season full of those, so perhaps we’re in for a few more. QB1 for Week 7 against the Houston Texans QB1 pic.twitter.com/4TDjeyUnkU — SNY Giants (@SNYGiants) October 21, 2026 CB Paulson Adebo designated for return; OL Josh Sills signed to active roster | Giants.com Cornerback Paulson Adebo has been designated for return from injured reserve and practiced Wednesday in a limited capacity. Adebo was placed on injured reserve with a knee issue on Sept. 18 in the wake of the season-opening win against the Cowboys. Once a player is designated for return, the team has 21 days to add him to the active roster or place him on season-ending injured reserve. Adebo’s return comes after Greg Newsome II suffered a concussion last week against the Saints. Newsome had been the only member of the secondary other than safety Jevón Holland to start all six games. New York Giants DTs detail motion, fits behind run defense issues | USAToday.com Harris described how motion changes the defensive picture before the snap. “Pre-snap motion, really what it does, it can exchange gaps,” Harris told reporters on Tuesday. “It can make it where linebackers have to move, DBs have to have communication, and that’s really the main thing that it does, is it forces communication between defense and it kind of shifts responsibilities.” “I think sometimes just a little bit of the fits on just some of the stuff, cleaning up that type of thing,” Reader said. “We’ve let some quarterback runs kind of beat us in some places. And that’s always a little bit difficult, especially last week. In a rain game, it was a little bit hard but this week, let a couple quarterback runs beat us.” NFL insider on the arm talent of J.J. McCarthy THIS is the throw that made J.J. McCarthy QB1 for the Giants… Back-shoulder corner routes are nearly impossible to execute. But it’s the anticipation and TRUST to let it rip to Isaiah Likely that separates him. https://t.co/fTBIvH1VcN pic.twitter.com/06qLkBw5Qe — Chase Daniel (@ChaseDaniel) October 21, 2026 10 fairytale trades ahead of the 2026 NFL trade deadline | PFF RB Jonathan Taylor to the New York Giants. Of all the lucrative chips in Indianapolis, none would surpass Taylor. It is worth mentioning that Taylor has been less dynamic in 2026, with his 67.3 rushing grade sitting 16th out of 27 qualified backs and averaging just 2.79 yards after contact per attempt. John Harbaugh’s offense has not found sustainable production on the ground through six games. Indeed, the Giants are 25th in rushing EPA per play, and their running backs rank 30th in PFF rushing grade. The team’s backfield committee has not only not worked, but also remains volatile given the release of Najee Harris and effective benching of second-year rusher Cameron Skattebo. Still just 27 and under contract through 2028, the Colts probably won’t be inclined to trade Taylor. Then again, for a franchise operating without a 2027 first-round pick, moving Taylor could be worth it to recoup necessary capital for a rebuild. Whether or not the Giants would buy this deadline given their quarterback situation is another complicating factor, but a player of Taylor’s ilk may give them an advantage in a lowly but tight NFC East. title: Scouting Jets edge defender Quinton Bell
summary: The Jets recently signed journeyman edge defender Quinton Bell to their practice squad. Today, we break him down in detail. The 30-year old Bell is listed at 6’4” and 253 pounds and was a seventh round pick out of Prairie View A&M in 2019. He has played in 33 regular season games in his career, […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CA - AUGUST 20: Quinton Bell #58 and Jaden Dugger #53 of the San Francisco 49ers tackle Amar Johnson #35 of the Los Angeles Chargers during the game at SoFi Stadium on August 20, 2026 in Inglewood, California. The 49ers defeated the Chargers 41-17. (Photo by Michael Zagaris/San Francisco 49ers/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Jets recently signed journeyman edge defender Quinton Bell to their practice squad. Today, we break him down in detail. The 30-year old Bell is listed at 6’4” and 253 pounds and was a seventh round pick out of Prairie View A&M in 2019. He has played in 33 regular season games in his career, starting three, with 38 tackles and one sack recorded. Background Bell was an unranked prospect as a high school recruit, following a career where he played wide receiver and outside linebacker, while also being on the basketball team and running track. He headed to Prairie View A&M as a wide receiver in 2015. In three seasons, he played in 25 games and caught 19 passes for 169 yards, including a 47-yard touchdown. Ahead of his senior year, the coaching staff suggested that Bell should move to defensive end and he embraced the move as he earned second team all-SWAC honors. In 10 games, he made nine starts and ended up with 46 tackles, 10 tackles for loss and 7.5 sacks with five of those sacks coming in the last four games. After a terrific pro day workout, Bell started to receive some draft buzz and was eventually selected in the seventh round by the Raiders. He failed to make the roster as a rookie, although he was initially signed to the practice squad. However, he ended up on Tampa Bay’s practice squad by the end of the year and then signed a futures deal with them. In 2020, Bell made the Bucs roster and made the first five appearances of his career, although he didn’t register any stats and ended up back on their practice squad. Having re-signed for the Bucs in 2021, he failed to make their roster and ended up on the Falcons’ practice squad, then signed a futures deal with them at the end of the season. In 2022, Bell made the Falcons’ roster and played in four games with them, recording three tackles, including a tackle for loss. Again, he ended up on the practice squad and signed a futures deal for 2023. He didn’t play in 2023 as he spent time with the Falcons, Eagles and Dolphins, eventually signing another futures deal, this time with Miami. 2024 was Bell’s best season as he made the Dolphins roster and played in every game. He made three starts and had 27 tackles and three tackles for loss with the first sack, forced fumble and pass breakup of his career. Last season saw him back with Miami again, although he was on and off the practice squad all year. He ended up making seven appearances off the bench with eight tackles, a quarterback hit and a fumble recovery. Bell signed for the 49ers ahead of training camp but was released in final cuts and without a team until the Jets worked him out and signed him to the practice squad earlier this month. Let’s move onto some more in-depth analysis of what Bell brings to the table, based on in-depth research and film study. Measurables/Athleticism Bell has decent size and good length. His athletic numbers at his pro day were outstanding as he ran a 4.53 in the 40-yard dash with a 41-inch vertical and 136-inch broad jump. He also posted a 7.25 in the three cone drill. He managed 23 bench press reps at his pro day and looks to have improved his play strength at the NFL level. Usage Since converting from wide receiver, Bell has played purely on the edge, with any reps in the slot, off the line or on the interior being rare. He has experience of standing up or having his hands in the dirt. Motor Bell is a player who battles and works hard in the trenches and shows hustle in pursuit. It’s fair to question whether he’s equipped to handle a starter’s workload because he’s never played more than 32 defensive snaps in an NFL game. He did once play 47 in a preseason game but that was when he was a rookie. Pass rush Bell’s strong finish to his college career helped him get drafted based on projection but he’s never really been able to prove he can be productive at the NFL level as a pass rusher. His pressure rates have been low at the NFL level, although he did have one sack. In preseason action, he’s played a lot but again had a low pressure rate with no sacks. Nevertheless, Bell has an impressive get-off and the burst to chase down quarterbacks in pursuit. His only sack at the NFL level was an impressive rep against a long-time starter in Alaric Jackson. Run defense Bell’s run defense grades have typically been about average on analysis sites such as Pro Football Focus, and are no better in preseason where he’s seen more work. However, he has made some good plays at or behind the line when he’s had opportunities, impressing specifically with his ability to pursue from the backside. The book on Bell when he entered the league was that he would need to improve his play strength to set the edge but it’s become a major strength of his, and was arguably his main role with Miami. Technique Bell didn’t come into the league with an arsenal of pass rush moves, or any kind of ability to transition smoothly into a counter, but on his lone NFL sack he came off the edge well and ripped through for the strip sack. He just hasn’t done this enough. On this play, the linebacker got credit for the sack, but Bell still beat his man impressively with a hesitation and an effective rip move. His hand placement and technique was also extremely raw when he first entered the league but he’s shown an improvement in how he takes on blocks and has shown he can shed them at times. Special teams Bell wasn’t used much on special teams in college but has plenty of experience within that role at the NFL level, having played on all units apart from the placekicking unit. He has had six special teams tackles with one penalty (for defensive holding on a punt) in regular season action and another five with one more penalty in preseason action. In one preseason game, he set up a touchdown with this blocked punt. Tackling Bell’s tackle efficiency numbers have typically been good, as he seems to wrap up consistently with a good closing burst where necessary. However, he failed to complete the sack on this play, leading to a first down scramble. He only has one forced fumble in his entire career, including college and preseason games. Coverage Bell’s experience as a receiver could give him an edge in coverage situations if he needs to make a play on the ball but it’s been rare for him to drop into coverage too often at the NFL level and when he does it will usually be into zone coverage. Still, he has shown some flashes of ability in making tackles on short passes and with this pass breakup on Brock Bowers. Instincts/Intelligence Being relatively new to the position, Bell may have taken some time to learn all the nuances of an NFL scheme but his film doesn’t show any glaring issues with missed assignments, even if he is reacting more than anticipating. As a pass rusher, his approach has always been pretty raw and mechanical and he hasn’t developed into a player who can set up and execute a counter. Attitude/Demeanor Bell’s uncle played for three years in the NFL, so he has a good idea of what it takes and has impressed with his hard work and dedication in terms of not only making it into the league, but also still being here now that he’s in his thirties. He has a team-first mindset, earning plaudits for his work on the scout team in Maxx Crosby’s role a few years back while the Dolphins were preparing to face the Raiders. His on-field discipline has been solid with just two defensive penalties at the NFL level. He jumped offside once and was flagged for a face mask penalty. Injuries Bell doesn’t have any significant documented injuries during his professional or college career. Scheme Fit Bell would be a solid fit for the Jets’…

title: Eagles Injury Report: Saquon Barkley limited while other key offensive starters miss practice
summary: The Philadelphia Eagles issued their first injury report of the week on Thursday in advance of their Week 7 Monday Night Football game against the Dallas Cowboys. The Eagles listed six players under DID NOT PARTICIPATE: DeVonta Smith, Dontayvion Wicks, Dallas Goedert, Nolan Smith, Willie Lampkin, and Michael Carter II. DeVonta also missed the first […]
full_text: Oct 26, 2025; Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, USA; Philadelphia Eagles tight end Dallas Goedert (88) celebrates scoring a touchdown with running back Saquon Barkley (26) in the second quarter against the New York Giants at Lincoln Financial Field. Mandatory Credit: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Philadelphia Eagles issued their first injury report of the week on Thursday in advance of their Week 7 Monday Night Football game against the Dallas Cowboys. The Eagles listed six players under DID NOT PARTICIPATE: DeVonta Smith, Dontayvion Wicks, Dallas Goedert, Nolan Smith, Willie Lampkin, and Michael Carter II. DeVonta also missed the first practice of last week before being progressively being ramped up over the next two days. We’ll see if him and/or Wicks follow that pattern this week. If not, the Eagles will sure be short-handed at receiver. DeVonta is still listed with a hamstring injury while Wicks is newly listed with an ankle injury after previously missing practice time due to a hamstring injury of his own. Goedert missed practice due to a knee injury. Unclear if it’s the same one that previously caused him to miss time. One would assume so. With the Eagles waiving E.J. Jenkins, Johnny Mundt is currently the only healthy tight end on the active roster. But the Eagles could look to sign Zach Ertz from the practice squad … and/or activate fan favorite Grant Calcaterra and/or rookie Eli Stowers from injured reserve. Smith missed practice due to the concussion he suffered in Week 6. He’s in danger of missing at least one game. Lampkin missed practice due to illness. Assuming it’s not something serious, he should be available to dress for the game this week. MC2 was seen doing some rehab work on a side field, which seems like an upgrade from last week. But he’s still not practicing. Maybe next week is in play for him. The Eagles listed eight players under LIMITED PARTICIPATION: Saquon Barkley, Landon Dickerson, Jalyx Hunt, Jonathan Greenard, Drew Kendall, Tyler Steen, Moro Ojomo, and A.J. Epenesa. Barkley is reportedly “in line” to play for the first time since suffering a hamstring injury in Week 4. But how he progresses over the next two days will be key. Guessing he’ll at least try to suit up but we’ll have to see if he can manage to hold up over the course of the game. Dickerson has only been limited in practice since the Eagles opened his 21-day practice window to return from injured reserve. Seems unlikely to me that he plays until he fully participates in a practice first. Also, he’s now being listed with both “knee/pectoral” injuries after previously only being listed with the knee last week. Hunt returning to practice this soon after watching him go down with a scary injury in Week 5 is encouraging. Hunt wouldn’t tell reporters if he’s going to play on Monday but it seems like there’s a chance. If not then, perhaps Week 8. Greenard was on a pitch count in Week 7 as he plays through a nagging ankle injury. Guessing he’ll try to suit up again but he’s hardly 100%. Kendall might be able to return to the starting lineup this week; the Eagles kept him active as an emergency backup option in Week 6. But he’ll probably need to get at least one full practice in before playing center. Steen suffered a shoulder injury in Week 5. The Eagles seem to be managing their starting right guard to help get him to Monday. Ojomo got banged up in Week 6. Guessing he’ll play but he might see a smaller workload than usual. Epenesa missed Week 6 due to a back injury. We’ll see if he’s able to play on Monday. With the edge rusher rotation banged up, they could use him out there. The Eagles listed 10 players under FULL PARTICIPATION: Zack Baun, Jalen Carter, Jordan Davis, Arnold Ebiketie, Jihaad Campbell, Britain Covey, Grant Calcaterra, Eli Stowers, Jakorian Bennett, and Hollywood Brown. Notable from this section: Davis was full go after having to be helped off the field on Sunday. Great to see he’ll be able to play on Monday. Campbell had “knee” removed from his injury description. Now just “wrist.” Covey is a new addition to the report with a shoulder injury. Calcaterra was limited in the first two practices last week before going full on Friday. He was full again today, which could point to the Eagles activating him from injured reserve for Monday’s game. Feel the excitement! Epenesa (back) EDGE Jonathan Greenard (ankle) EDGE Jalyx Hunt (knee) OL Drew Kendall (knee) DT Moro Ojomo (abdomen) OG Tyler Steen (shoulder) FULL PARTICIPATION CB Jakorian Bennett (knee) WR Hollywood Brown (ankle) TE Grant Calcaterra (back) LB Jihaad Campbell (wrist) DT Jalen Carter (wrist) WR Britain Covey (shoulder) DT Jordan Davis (shin/thumb) EDGE Arnold Ebiketie (shoulder) TE Eli Stowers (hamstring) DALLAS COWBOYS INJURY REPORT ( THUR SDAY) The Cowboys listed four players under DID NOT PARTICIPATE: starting off-ball linebacker Dee Winters, All-Pro returner KaVontae Turpin, veteran edge rusher Von Miller, and depth tackle Drew Shelton. Winters got banged up in Week 6. The Cowboys’ defense already isn’t very good, so, it doesn’t seem great for them that they could be missing a player who’s actually been good for them this season. Then again, it looks like they’re getting DeMarvion Overshown back this week. Turpin, one of the better returners in the NFL, is also in danger of missing this week’s game. Miller was resting and the rookie Shelton doesn’t play much anyway. The Cowboys listed four players under LIMITED PARTICIPATION: starting wide receiver George Pickens, starting cornerback Cobie Durant, starting left tackle Tyler Guyton, and edge rusher Marist Liufau. Pickes is a new addition to the report after apparently getting banged up in Week 6. Durant could potentially return to the starting lineup for the first time since getting hurt in Week 2. Guyton was listed on the Cowboys’ report as a full participant with a back injury last week. Apparently he injured his calf in Week 6. Liufau is participating in practice while in his 21-day window to return from injured reserve. The team also announced re-signing RB Jaydon Blue and LB Anfernee Orji to the practice squad, and made the E.J. Jenkins waiving […]
full_text: Photo by Kathryn Riley/Getty Images | Getty Images A day after bringing in former first-round draft pick Evan Neal for a tryout, the Eagles are signing the former New York Giants offensive lineman to the practice squad, according to multiple reports. The team also announced re-signing RB Jaydon Blue and LB Anfernee Orji to the practice squad, and made the E.J. Jenkins waiving official . We have signed RB Jaydon Blue, G Evan Neal, and LB Anfernee Orji to the practice squad. We have also waived TE E.J. Jenkins. pic.twitter.com/8ngJbpakmw — Philadelphia Eagles (@Eagles) October 22, 2026 As Brandon Lee Gowton wrote on Wednesday about adding Neal to the roster : “It doesn’t hurt for the Eagles to take a flyer on Neal, who turned 26 in September. Maybe there’s some untapped potential here for this coaching staff to maximize (you might feel better about that much if Jeff Stoutland was still around). More likely, he’s just not going to pan out in the NFL. But, hey, you never know.“ At this point the Eagles need depth up front and if there’s a shred of potential with Neal, it’s worth a shot to sign him. His versatility at multiple spots along the line is also a plus, since there’s still no continuity in Philly and players are still settling into new roles. The team still has several roster spots they can fill on the 53-man roster, and could sign some guys off the practice squad. Bottom line, with the growing list of injuries, this isn’t the last round of roster moves for the Eagles.

title: NFL Power Rankings: Week 7 Edition
summary: Now that Week 6 of the 2026 NFL season is in the books, it’s time for an incredibly meaningful and serious exercise: NFL Power Rankings! What differentiates these rankings from all others is that they’re THE only truly accurate ones in the entire universe. Hard to believe, I know. But it’s true. Let’s take a […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PA - OCTOBER 18: Eagles fans react during the game between the Carolina Panthers and Philadelphia Eagles on October 18, 2026 at Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia, PA. (Photo by Kyle Ross/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Now that Week 6 of the 2026 NFL season is in the books, it’s time for an incredibly meaningful and serious exercise: NFL Power Rankings ! What differentiates these rankings from all others is that they’re THE only truly accurate ones in the entire universe. Hard to believe, I know. But it’s true. Let’s take a look at how all 32 teams stack up. BLG’S WEEK 7 NFL POWER RANKINGS 1 – Kansas City Chiefs (Last Week: 1) – Kenneth Walker is the Chiefs’ 2024 Saquon Barkley. 2 – San Francisco 49ers (LW: 2) – Despite not being the only undefeated team in the NFC, they’re clearly in a tier of their own. Maybe this is finally the year for Kyle Shanahan. 3 – Buffalo Bills (LW: 5) – Josh Allen is driving an offense averaging a league-high 33.3 offensive points per game. They’ve needed that production because their defense is allowing the fifth-most offensive points per game. 4 – Minnesota Vikings (LW: 6) – The Vikings return from their bye to host the Colts. 6-0 is within reach … but it does feel like their lackluster offense will catch up to them sooner than later. 5 – Chicago Bears (LW: 7) – With Caleb Williams back, the Bears are heating up in an ultra competitive NFC North. 6 – Seattle Seahawks (LW: 3) – Drew Lock was looking better than Sam Darnold is right now. When will Seattle have the guts to make the switch? 7 – Baltimore Ravens (LW: 4) – A loss to the Browns hurts but Lamar Jackson’s return positions this team well moving forward. 8 – Detroit Lions (LW: 10) – The Lions return from their bye week to host the resurgent Packers. Time for Detroit to show us how seriously (or not) they should be taken. 9 – Jacksonville Jaguars (LW: 9) – Travis Hunter’s historic performance was ruined by a close loss in London. The Jags will be OK but a win over Houston would’ve really given them a chokehold on the AFC South. Missed opportunity. 10 – Cincinnati Bengals (LW: 11) – The Bengals return from their bye week to play in Baltimore. Measuring stick game for Joe Burrow’s side. 11 – New England Patriots (LW: 12) – A.J. Brown mightily struggled in his first game back from injury. Probably gotta get your laughs in now before he rebounds. 12 – Los Angeles Rams (LW: 8) – Maybe the Rams aren’t going to be okay. I still think they will be. But they’re decreasing their margin for error in a tough division. And the panic seems to be there with some calls for Matthew Stafford to be benched. 13 – Las Vegas Raiders (LW: 13) – Three straight losses for the Raiders, although two only came by three points each. They’re a good but not great team, which is a massive upgrade on what they’ve been for a long time prior to this season. 14 – Carolina Panthers (LW: 16) – Bryce Young continues to ball and Chuba Hubbard continues to run over those in his path. 15 – Denver Broncos (LW: 15) – The Broncos have a Bo Nix problem. They’re capable of winning in spite of him … but that can only last for so long. 16 – Green Bay Packers (LW: 18) – Whereas it once looked like the Packers were cooked due to their offensive line issues, they’ve since turned it around. 17 – Dallas Cowboys (LW: 14) – The Cowboys are the favorites to win the NFC East at this point in time … but they’re allowing all their division rivals to hang around. Unserious behavior. 18 – Cleveland Browns (LW: 27) – The 4-2 Browns (-16) only have a slightly better point differential than the 1-5 Bucs (-19). Weird to think of Cleveland being a “lucky” team but their record is painting them to be better than they actually are. Still, they’re not a total joke, which is what almost everyone expected them to be. 19 – New Orleans Saints (LW: 21) – It felt like the Saints were due for a big performance after ownership publicly put pressure on the coaches and players to turn things around. We’ll see if they can actually keep it up. 20 – New York Giants (LW: 17) – The G-Men are making the right move by benching Jameis Winston in favor of J.J. McCarthy. The latter showed some promise (albeit in garbage time during a loss) last weekend. He offers more upside than Winston does. 21 – Pittsburgh Steelers (LW: 22) – The Stillers need OT to beat the Bucs but, hey, they’re 4-2. If the season ended today, which it doesn’t, they’d be the No. 7 seed in the AFC. 22 – Houston Texans (LW: 24) – Make that two straight wins for the Texans after an 0-4 start. With entering this week as 10.5-point home favorites against the Giants before playing the Bolts in Week 9, they could soon be back to .500. 23 – Atlanta Falcons (LW: 20) – The Falcons signed Andy Dalton, so, I’d say that’ll fix their problems. 24 – Philadelphia Eagles (LW: 19) – The 2026 season has been very tumultuous for the Eagles … both on and off the field. Their offense is terrible and their defense is underperforming relative to high expectations. With Jalen Hurts out for the season, it’s not easy to see things getting better for this group. It’s not like you can count on the coaching staff to maximize the talent they’re working with. #Eagles are still the only team in the NFL to have zero successful under center play action plays when blitzed. They have an 0/18 (0%) success rate & are losing an average of almost a full expected point when they run UC PA and get blitzed. pic.twitter.com/T1WpcmlUUK — Deniz Selman (@denizselman33) October 21, 2026 25 – Indianapolis Colts (LW: 23) – Chris Ballard was fired … five years after trading what turned out to be a first-round pick for Carson Wentz, who was coming off the worst season of his career. Better later than never, I suppose. 26 – Tampa Bay Buccaneers (LW: 25) – Baker Mayfield is back. We’ll see if that actually makes a positive difference for the Bucs, who have two big NFC South games coming up. 27 – New York Jets (LW: 26) – The Jets aren’t doing anything to be taken seriously. 28 – Arizona Cardinals (LW: 29) – With wins over the Rams and Chargers, the Cardinals apparently own Los Angeles. Only two wins away from hitting the over on their 2026 projected win total! 29 – Washington Commanders (LW: 28) – Dan Quinn is very much on the hot seat but the Commanders don’t appear to be making a coaching change during their bye. 30 – Tennessee Titans (LW: 31) – Robert Saleh is on the board with his first win as the Titans’ head coach. Can’t imagine many more are to follow. 31 – Los Angeles Chargers (LW: 30) – Bleak. 32 – Miami Dolphins (LW: 32) – The Dolphins return from their bye to play the Jets in North Jersey. Seems like a winnable game?

title: Eagles reportedly waive E.J. Jenkins
summary: The Philadelphia Eagles are waiving tight end E.J. Jenkins, according to a report from NFL insider Mike Garafolo. Jenkins was a surprise inclusion on the Eagles’ roster back in late August when the team went from the offseason limit of 90 players down to the regular season limit of 53. To this point, Jenkins had […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - AUGUST 22: E.J. Jenkins #84 of the Philadelphia Eagles looks on against the New England Patriots following an NFL preseason football game at Gillette Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles are waiving tight end E.J. Jenkins, according to a report from NFL insider Mike Garafolo . Jenkins was a surprise inclusion on the Eagles’ roster back in late August when the team went from the offseason limit of 90 players down to the regular season limit of 53. To this point, Jenkins had served as a third or fourth tight end on game days. With zero targets in 67 offensive snaps played over six games, Jenkins contributed as a blocker in addition to helping out on special teams. Jenkins’ dismissal could be related to the Eagles running out of practice squad elevations for franchise legend Zach Ertz. Perhaps the team is planning to sign Ertz to the roster while bringing back Jenkins on the practice squad, assuming he clears waivers. The Eagles could then use Jenkins’ three temporary elevations to still get him involved in game action for a few weeks. We’ll see what corresponding roster move(s) follow this report. For now, the Eagles only have Dallas Goedert and Johnny Mundt at tight end on the 53-man roster.

title: Eagles host two former high draft picks on tryouts
summary: The Philadelphia Eagles hosted two recognizable free agents at the Jefferson Health Training Complex on a tryout basis on Wednesday, according to an official NFL personnel notice: Let’s sort through this news on a player-by-player basis. EVAN NEAL Eagles fans will recognize Neal from his time with the New York Giants, which didn’t go very […]
full_text: TOKYO, JAPAN - 2021/03/03: Decorative Bowser sticker on a glass wall inside Nintendo Tokyo store in Shibuya. (Photo by Stanislav Kogiku/SOPA Images/LightRocket via Getty Images) The Philadelphia Eagles hosted two recognizable free agents at the Jefferson Health Training Complex on a tryout basis on Wednesday, according to an official NFL personnel notice: OT Evan Neal EDGE Tyus Bowser Let’s sort through this news on a player-by-player basis. EVAN NEAL Eagles fans will recognize Neal from his time with the New York Giants, which didn’t go very well for either side after he was selected with the No. 7 overall pick in the 2022 NFL Draft. Between injuries and struggling whenever he was healthy, Neal made 27 starts in 29 games played for the G-Men from 2022 through 2024. There was a last-ditch effort to transition him from tackle to guard in 2025 but he ended up being a healthy scratch for most of the 2025 season. The Giants finally cut Neal prior to the start of the 2026 regular season. The Alabama alumnus then spent a little over a month on the Las Vegas Raiders’ practice squad before they released him last week. It doesn’t hurt for the Eagles to take a flyer on Neal, who turned 26 in September. Maybe there’s some untapped potential here for this coaching staff to maximize (you might feel better about that much if Jeff Stoutland was still around). More likely, he’s just not going to pan out in the NFL. But, hey, you never know. TYUS BOWSER Bowser, 31, was originally selected by the Baltimore Ravens with a second-round pick (No. 47 overall) in the 2017 NFL Draft. Making 28 starts over 98 career games played, he’s logged 19.5 sacks, 22 tackles for loss, and 48 quarterback hits. Bowser played for the Ravens from 2017-2023 before stints with the Seattle Seahawks and Miami Dolphins in 2024. He did not play in the 2025 season. The Eagles are currently thin at edge rusher. Jalyx Hunt missed Week 6 due to knee/ankle injuries and it’s unclear if he’ll play in Week 7. Jonathan Greenard looks to be less than 100% while dealing with an ankle injury. Nolan Smith suffered a concussion during the Eagles’ last game. A.J. Epenesa did not play against the Carolina Panthers after being ruled doubtful with a back injury. And so the Eagles were down to just Arnold Ebiketie and seventh-round rookie Keyshawn James-Newby as their top (and only) two edge rushers last weekend. Signing Bowser would give the Eagles a veteran option to help fill some snaps in their edge rusher rotation.

Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … Sources: Nick Sirianni, Mike Vrabel among coaches fined for conduct toward refs – ESPN The NFL fined Philadelphia Eagles coach Nick Sirianni $250,000 for conduct toward game officials, a source confirmed to ESPN on Wednesday night. New England Patriots coach Mike Vrabel was fined the same amount for similar conduct, a league source confirmed to ESPN’s Mike Reiss. New York Jets coach Aaron Glenn also was fined $250,000, according to Sports Illustrated, which first reported the fines. The fines are temporarily on hold and can be repealed with good behavior, the source confirmed to ESPN, as the league tries to make a point to all coaches about their treatment of officials. It wasn’t immediately known when the fines were handed down or from what specific incidents they stemmed. Eagles Film Analysis: Can empty formations help solve the offense’s pressure problems? – BGN Empty won’t magically fix the Eagles’ protection, but the numbers give them an obvious place to start. Spread things out, build in clear answers, and give McKee and the rest of the offense a chance to find some rhythm. The stats do not lie. The frustrating part is how straightforward this is to identify through basic self-scouting. Mina Kimes On Jalen Hurts Saga, Whether Eagles Can Compete With Tanner McKee At QB – PHLY Eagles Podcast ESPN’s Mina Kimes joins the PHLY Eagles podcast with Bo Wulf and Brandon Lee Gowton to discuss the latest developments as Jalen Hurts sits on injured reserve with his future in the balance thanks to blood clots in his lungs. While we wish for the best for Hurts, the Eagles hand the ball to Tanner McKee, hoping to turn around what has been the worst offense in football this season. Does Sean Mannion have what it takes to design a new offense on the fly? Sean Mannion remains Eagles’ play-caller. Can his offense work with Tanner McKee? – The Athletic Eagles coach Nick Sirianni said “everything is on the table” to fix the offense. That will not include a change at play-caller — Sirianni said Mannion will remain in that role — nor changes to the coaching staff. It remains to be seen what will be different. Mannion made it sound as if the approach is no different than any other week, and that the search for answers isn’t any more pronounced on a four-game losing streak. “I think you look at a lot of the things that we need to improve, and I think they’re totally fixable,” Mannion said. “It’s a double-edged sword, right? You look at that, and you can get frustrated by it. You can also look at that and put a silver lining on it and say, ‘Man, if we just handle our simple stuff, we’re going to yield a better result.’” If it happens, it must happen with McKee. But it won’t be without Hurts’ presence. Mannion said Hurts has “been around.” He expects Hurts to be a resource for McKee this season. “He’s got a ton of starts in this league, especially going against a slate of division opponents coming up,” Mannion said of Hurts. “He’s played against these guys a bunch. I know Tanner’s been around for that, too, but I think the insight that you have from being on the field is so valuable. … It’s just the game experience and the insight of playing specifically these upcoming opponents. I think Jalen will be able to give Tanner some great help there.” Senator Lisa Blunt Rochester seeks answers from Roger Goodell regarding the Jalen Hurts situation – PFT Someone also should ask whether the league will implement a protocol for blood clots and other potentially serious health conditions, similar to the procedures utilized for diagnosing concussions and clearing players to return to play. The league has used an unaffiliated neurotrauma consultant in such situations for 17 years, in order to counter the inherent biases of doctors hired by the various teams. The NFL Players Association has requested a full investigation. Under the Collective Bargaining Agreement, it has the absolute right to initiate one. Congress, through its oversight powers as to an industry that enjoys a federal broadcast antitrust exemption, also has the ability to investigate. Given the league’s effort to sweep this one under the rug and move on, anyone with the power to force the NFL to answer for the Hurts situation absolutely should. Philly fans are expressing love for Jalen Hurts through various get-well cards: ‘Everybody has Jalen’s back and supports him’ – Inquirer “Next day, got the text, ‘Jalen’s got the card and he’s very thankful,’” Petrilli said. “That’s what we do at Club Hurts. We bring people together, and we have QB1’s back.’ The card was delivered to Hurts before fans knew the extent of his injury. Now, with the quarterback likely missing the rest of the season after blood clots were found in his lungs, Petrilli hopes to continue to support the Super Bowl LIX MVP from the sideline. “We should be counting out blessings a little bit that we’ve had a guy like this in our lives for the last five, six years,” Petrilli said. “He’s been consistently winning football games for us, let alone just being the great person that he is in the community here. “Hopefully, he doesn’t really let this rub him the wrong way with the franchise, and he can keep being a part of the community here because he’s done so many great things. We want to keep helping those things that Jalen’s been pushing with his own charity aspects and just keep bringing the positivity that Jalen does in this city.” What’s going on with Cooper DeJean’s tackling issues? – NBCSP Throughout the first two seasons of his NFL career, Eagles defensive back Cooper DeJean was such a sure tackler. That hasn’t been the case this year. So what gives? “I don’t know,” DeJean said after the loss to the Panthers on Sunday afternoon. “I just have to find ways to get guys down. Part of it is different angles and where I’m hitting the guys. But I have no doubt that I’m going to continue to work on that and fix that. I’ve continued to work on it the last couple of weeks especially and will continue to, to be better in that area.” Missed tackles aren’t an official stat and they’re subjective. So there’s no official tally of how many missed tackles DeJean has this season. But by all accounts, he’s among the league leaders. According to ProFootballFocus, DeJean leads the NFL with 12 missed tackles this season. And among 82 defensive backs with at least 300 snaps, he’s at the very top of the list. His missed tackle rate of 24.5% is the third-worst among that group behind just Tre’Von Moehrig (30.8%) and C.J. Gardner-Johnson (25.7%). 2026 NFL offensive line rankings: Lions retain top spot, Browns ascend – PFF 18) PHILADELPHIA EAGLES. Making matters worse, Eagles backup running backs Tank Bigsby and Will Shipley have ended up on injured reserve.
