The Eagles’ running game has really struggled without Barkley; they’ve logged just 57 rushing yards in their last two games combined. For context, Barkley is averaging 45.5 yards per game this season. Barkley’s return alone does not fix one of the NFL’s worst offenses. Especially against a Dallas defense that’s tied for allowing the seventh-most yards per carry this season.

title: Are the young Steelers living up to their new money?
summary: With the win last Sunday against the Buccaneers, the Steelers wrapped up the first third of the NFL season 4-2. While there is still plenty of game action left in the season, it does feel like a checkpoint where we can do our first check-in on one of the biggest storylines of the Steelers’ 2026 […]
full_text: (Photo by Justin K. Aller/Getty Images) | Getty Images With the win last Sunday against the Buccaneers, the Steelers wrapped up the first third of the NFL season 4-2. While there is still plenty of game action left in the season, it does feel like a checkpoint where we can do our first check-in on one of the biggest storylines of the Steelers’ 2026 offseason: which young members of the 2023 draft class the organization would commit to long-term. The 2023 draft class was the first group selected by the tandem of general manager Omar Khan and assistant general manager Andy Weidl. While both were in place for the 2022 season, the Steelers made the unusual move of having retiring general manager Kevin Colbert stick it out through the draft process before hanging it up. That meant this offseason was the new duo’s first time attempting to decide which of their personally selected homegrown talents would remain in their plans, and which would not. They ultimately decided that three players — outside linebacker Nick Herbig (four years, $100 million), defensive tackle Keeanu Benton (four years, $72 million), and tight end Darnell Washington (four years, $42 million) — were worthy and willing enough to accept an extension. Meanwhile, two others — cornerback Joey Porter Jr. and tackle Broderick Jones — were not able to do the same. We don’t need to relitigate why Porter Jr. and Jones are no longer Steelers. Jones will go down as a misstep from Khan and Weidl’s first draft. How the Porter Jr. decision will be remembered is slightly more complicated. The way we’ll talk about his departure in the coming years will depend partially on how Porter performs post-Pittsburgh. It’s also hard to make any definitive claims about how this decision will affect the franchise in the long term until we see how Pittsburgh addresses the cornerback position this spring, as well as how they spend the second-round pick from his trade package when they finally get to use it in 2028. Regardless, it’s a disappointing outcome for two players who once held so much promise for the team. In deciding to pay Herbig, Benton, and Washington, but not Porter, the Steelers have once again affirmed that they value building in the trenches. For two straight years, they have dispensed with players who play more in the boundaries of the field — last year it was wide receiver George Pickens — and looked to retool those positions in the draft and free agency. Certainly, there were indeed other factors at play in the decision to let both of those players go, but it is revealing about the team’s priorities, nonetheless. This week, we’ll be looking at the players from the 2023 class the organization did commit to. While none of them have started to receive that new money on the books just yet, we’ll try to determine if they’re still trending in the right direction in terms of development. We’ll be taking their entire seasons thus far into account, but will be looking closely at the most recent game against Tampa Bay with this week’s film study. Let’s dive in. Nick Herbig New deal total: 4 years, $100 million (10th among edge rushers) AAV: $25 million (11th) Guaranteed money at signing : $21 million (29th) RB : After failing to record a sack in the first five games of 2026, Herbig logged two against Tampa Bay last week – in arguably the toughest assignment of his season thus far with most of his snaps coming against All-Pro tackle Tristain Wirfs. While I certainly wasn’t shocked to see Herbig get the big contract he did this offseason, it felt like one that was paying for future usage more than past output. But don’t get me wrong: Herbig has been ridiculously efficient during his past seasons as a Steeler, logging a 7.5 sack season in 2025, good for second-best on the team. The impressive part was that Herbig put up those numbers playing just 59.6% of the Steelers’ defensive snaps in 2025 – a number that was only as high as it was due to both TJ Watt and Alex Highsmith missing some games. While Herbig was undoubtedly worth $25 million per year as a pass rusher, could the Steelers justify paying him that with both Watt and Highsmith still under contract, and with Herbig still losing snaps to both? Of course, that’s not an entirely fair way to frame things: As Ryan mentioned in the intro, Herbig’s new-contract cap hit won’t kick in until 2027 (it jumps from $5.4 million to $25.2 million), meaning that the Steelers won’t really have a dilemma about paying too many good edge rushers until next year. But at the same time, the Steelers made a big commitment to Herbig, and in 2026 he’s played just 54.3% of the team’s defensive snaps (and still 37% of the team’s special teams snaps) and saw his efficiency numbers drop with a 10.2% pressure rate through six games – on pace for the worst of his career by over four percentage points. While only pass rush snaps count towards pressure rate, it is fair to point out that Herbig has had far more varied usage in Patrick Graham’s defense, with 63 of his 138 snaps so far this season coming at positions other than edge — something he’s admitted has been a challenge . Herbig has been playing off-ball linebacker more and rushing everywhere from over guards to being lined up in the slot. And in a new defense with a higher emphasis on simulated pressures and stunts, not every snap is designed for Herbig to get home to the quarterback, either. According to NFL Pro, Herbig is only averaging 14.7 pass rush snaps per game, down from 21.9 last year. Still, Pittsburgh paid Herbig as a pass rusher, and the team’s usage of him – and his production – hasn’t entirely reflected that yet. But against Tampa Bay on Sunday, Herbig showed any doubters that the speed rusher Steelers fans fell in love with is still absolutely there. His burst and bend remain unbelievable. Always fun to watch Nick Herbig zooming around pic.twitter.com/sQIEishp6T — Ryland Bickley (@_Ryland_B) October 22, 2026 That said, Herbig still has room to grow when it comes to finishing plays, especially if the team continues to experiment with him as an off-ball linebacker. Causing chaos alone can make a good front seven player, but making more of those tackles can take Herbig’s game to the next level. It could've been an even bigger game if he had finished a few more plays (not saying it would've been easy — I definitely think he got dragged down on that last one) pic.twitter.com/fdOmYfjDFB — Ryland Bickley (@_Ryland_B) October 22, 2026 The big question of this article has been if these contracts are aging well through six weeks. With Herbig, I’d say “yes” with some caveats. His current AAV currently ranks between Nik Bonitto ($26.5 million) and the Jonathan Greenards, Andrew Van Ginkels, George Karlaftises of the league ($24.5 to $23 million) – right in the sweet spot between the “star” and “very good player” tiers of the position. And of course, that ranking will only move more in the Steelers’ favor as the market inflates in the years Herbig is under contract. It’s also worth noting his guarantees are far from crippling. Herbig fits in that area of the market well right now, and his “it” factor as a pass rusher gives him the potential to move closer into star territory. Of course, the Steelers will have to give him more opportunities to get there first. Final verdict : Living up to the new money, but still some questions about role on team. title: Seahawks defense ailing ahead of matchup against Chiefs
summary: The 2026 season has not started the way the Seattle Seahawks and their fans had hoped, with the offense struggling with turnovers on the heels of a 2025 season that saw the team lift the Lombardi Trophy after defeating the New England Patriots 29-13 in Super Bowl LX. Consecutive losses to the division rival San […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - OCTOBER 20: Uchenna Nwosu #7 and DeMarcus Lawrence #0 of the Seattle Seahawks celebrate during the NFL 2025 game against the Houston Texans at Lumen Field on October 20, 2025 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Jane Gershovich/Getty Images) | Getty Images The 2026 season has not started the way the Seattle Seahawks and their fans had hoped, with the offense struggling with turnovers on the heels of a 2025 season that saw the team lift the Lombardi Trophy after defeating the New England Patriots 29-13 in Super Bowl LX. Consecutive losses to the division rival San Francisco 49ers and the once division rival Denver Broncos have Seattle at 3-3, the eighth best record in the NFC. Of course, with only the top seven teams making the postseason, that would leave the Seahawks on the outside looking in as they gear up for a key matchup against the Kansas City Chiefs. At 5-0 the Chiefs are one of just three undefeated teams in the NFL, as their offense is rejuvenated thanks to a return to health for Patrick Mahomes and the little-discussed addition of Kenneth Walker as a free agent in the offseason. Walker leads the NFL in rushing yards through the first six weeks of 2026, even though Kansas City has already has its bye week, meaning they have only played five games. Averaging 133 rushing yards per game, Walker is set to face a defense that has not allowed a one hundred yard rusher since October 27, 2024. However, while Walker will get to face a Seattle run defense that has played at an elite level so far in 2026, it’s a group that is far from healthy, particularly the front seven. A few changes to Seahawks injury report today from Wednesday, including two new injuries to veteran defensive linemen: pic.twitter.com/3bDeEP69mk — Bob Condotta (@bcondotta) October 22, 2026 Starting linebacker Drake Thomas missed the Week 6 game against the Broncos and did not participate in practice Thursday, while Demarcus Lawrence and Uchenna Nwosu were both limited on Thursday. Lawrence sat out of practice Wednesday as a veteran rest day, but had a knee injury notated on the injury report for Thursday, while Nwosu is now dealing with a hip issue according to the report. The depth at linebacker could be tested, as backups Tyrice Knight, Chazz Surratt and Connor O’Toole are also all listed on the report. Those three have not contributed quite as much on defense so far this year, but they have been mainstays on the special teams units, which will be something to keep in mind if the game stays close and comes down to special teams. On the good news front, Zach Charbonnet, Anthony Bradford and Rashid Shaheed were all full participants for the offense, which could help a struggling Sam Darnold against a Kansas City defense that is second in the NFL in points allowed thanks to a stout run defense, the ability to hit the quarterback and force turnovers. And now it’s on to the Friday injury report.

title: Seahawks TE Elijah Arroyo to undergo season-ending shoulder surgery
summary: The Seahawks announced a couple of roster transactions ahead of their Week 7 matchup against the Kansas City Chiefs. The happy and expected news was Zach Charbonnet being activated from the PUP list. The bad news is Elijah Arroyo has been placed on injured reserve. ESPN’s Adam Schefter reported on Thursday that Arroyo will have […]
full_text: The Seahawks announced a couple of roster transactions ahead of their Week 7 matchup against the Kansas City Chiefs. The happy and expected news was Zach Charbonnet being activated from the PUP list . The bad news is Elijah Arroyo has been placed on injured reserve. ESPN’s Adam Schefter reported on Thursday that Arroyo will have to undergo shoulder surgery and will miss the rest of the 2026 NFL season . Arroyo injured his shoulder last week against the Denver Broncos while attempting to recover Rashid Shaheed’s fumble . Coming out of the Broncos game, it did not sound positive. In fact, an injured reserve stint was expected for Arroyo . That his season is already over is surely a big blow for the second-year tight end out of Miami. Arroyo had an electric 2026 training camp , which brought a lot of optimism that Arroyo could have a big sophomore jump this season. Unfortunately this strong training camp did not continue into the regular season. Arroyo has seldom seen any targets this season and will finish his 2026 season with only one catch for 17 yards and 0 touchdowns. Entering the draft, Arroyo was heralded for his pass catching ability. However, with questions around his blocking ability and injury history (including an ACL tear), Arroyo managed to slip to Seattle at 50th overall. Unfortunately, the injury concerns have continued for Arroyo into the NFL. Arroyo missed the back-end of the 2025 regular season after injuring his knee in Week 14. As for the Seahawks, their tight end room is left with AJ Barner, Eric Saubert, and Nick Kallerup on the 53-man roster, with Josiah Deguara recently joining the practice squad . Saubert and Kallerup are known for their blocking rather than receiving abilities. Because of this, Seattle could potentially add a bigger pass catcher to the active roster.

title: Seahawks activate running back Zach Charbonnet off PUP list
summary: The Seattle Seahawks’ season-long battle of attrition in the backfield will get a reinforcement. Just under the wire of the three-week practice window to be activated, the Seahawks did just that with running back Zach Charbonnet, adding him back to the 53-man roster, the team announced on Thursday. In an expected corresponding move, second-year tight […]
full_text: The Seattle Seahawks’ season-long battle of attrition in the backfield will get a reinforcement. Just under the wire of the three-week practice window to be activated, the Seahawks did just that with running back Zach Charbonnet, adding him back to the 53-man roster, the team announced on Thursday . In an expected corresponding move, second-year tight end Elijah Arroyo was placed on injured reserve after hurting his shoulder last week against the Denver Broncos. The fourth-year tailback has been out since January, when he tore his ACL in Seattle’s Divisional Round win over the San Francisco 49ers and missed the rest of the team’s march to Super Bowl glory. After Kenneth Walker’s departure to Kansas City in free agency, it left the Seahawks with a thin backfield — one that got even thinner after rookie first-round pick Jadarian Price went on injured reserve himself in early October . The banged-up nature of Seattle’s backfield in 2026 has seen it become a group effort. Veteran Emanuel Wilson has led the way with 303 yards on 87 carries, while Price rushed for 119 on 28 carries before going down injured. Third-year pro George Holani, in his biggest opportunity to date, has added 97 yards on 31 touches. All three running backs have lost at least one fumble, whereas Charbonnet has never fumbled in his NFL career. Prior to Charbonnet’s season-ending injury, the 25-year-old was fresh off a career-best season in which he ran for 730 yards and a team-high 12 touchdowns. With Price sidelined for at least this week before he’s eligible to return in Week 8 versus the Chicago Bears, the former UCLA Bruin should immediately step into a major role for the Seahawks’ running game. As a full participant in Wednesday’s practice, it seems more likely than not that Charbonnet will make his 2026 debut this Sunday, with his former backfield mate on the opposite sideline.

title: 12 trade deadline targets who could help the Seahawks make a run
summary: The Seattle Seahawks don’t need to make a trade just because the deadline is approaching. But after a 3-3 start, an offense that has struggled to find consistency, and two difficult games against the Kansas City Chiefs and Chicago Bears ahead, John Schneider has plenty of reasons to explore the market. The NFL trade deadline […]
full_text: The Seattle Seahawks don’t need to make a trade just because the deadline is approaching. But after a 3-3 start, an offense that has struggled to find consistency, and two difficult games against the Kansas City Chiefs and Chicago Bears ahead, John Schneider has plenty of reasons to explore the market. The NFL trade deadline is November 10. By then, Seattle should have a much clearer idea of what this team can realistically accomplish. If the Seahawks lose both upcoming games and fall to 3-5, the front office will have to confront an uncomfortable question: is this roster one or two additions away from getting back on track, or are the problems too widespread for a deadline deal to fix? The timing of the Indianapolis Colts’ decision to fire general manager Chris Ballard makes that question even more interesting. Ed Dodds, a former Seahawks executive who worked under Schneider, is now overseeing Indianapolis’ personnel department on an interim basis. That doesn’t guarantee a trade between the two teams, but it creates an opportunity worth examining. Running back: Should Seattle spend big on a star? The Seahawks’ ground game has been a major concern. Kenneth Walker III departed in free agency, first-round rookie Jadarian Price has been dealing with an injury, and Zach Charbonnet has also been unavailable. Seattle has struggled to replace Walker’s production, leaving the offense without the balance it needs. Jonathan Taylor is an obvious name to consider. He remains one of the league’s most productive backs, with 1,585 rushing yards and 18 touchdowns in 2025. Through six games in 2026, he has 492 rushing yards and seven touchdowns. Taylor’s combination of acceleration, vision, contact balance and finishing ability would give Seattle a runner capable of creating yards even when the blocking isn’t perfect. He could transform the backfield and take some pressure off the passing game. There is also a historical connection. Taylor was a popular potential target for Seattle in the 2020 draft, and footage of him expressing interest in the Seahawks has resurfaced amid the trade speculation. However, Taylor is not an expiring-contract player. He is under contract through 2028, with $16 million owed in 2027. A deal would likely cost at least a second-rounder plus additional compensation. Seattle would be making a substantial financial and draft investment in a position with a short career window. That is where the argument against a Taylor trade becomes important. The Seahawks already used a first-round pick on Price, and both Price and Charbonnet are expected to return. They also have future extensions to consider, including defensive tackle Byron Murphy II. Saquon Barkley offers a comparable high-end alternative. His 2024 season was extraordinary, with 2,005 rushing yards in the regular season and a Super Bowl championship with Philadelphia. His production fell to 1,140 rushing yards in 2025, and he has been limited to four games in 2026 by a hamstring injury. Barkley is a versatile runner and receiver who could give Seattle another explosive weapon. But the injury situation, contract and acquisition price would all need to be evaluated carefully. The Eagles would also have to be willing to move a player who remains a major part of their offense. Tony Pollard is a more economical possibility. He has surpassed 1,000 rushing yards in four seasons and could offer a dependable veteran presence. He wouldn’t solve the offense’s structural problems, but he could strengthen the rotation and reduce the pressure on inexperienced or returning players. Omarion Hampton is a different kind of gamble. The Chargers selected him in the first round in 2025, and he has shown potential despite a modest statistical start to his NFL career. A change of scenery could help, but Los Angeles invested too much in him to move on without a meaningful offer. Edge rusher: Khalil Mack could make the defense even better The Seahawks’ defense has generally been more reliable than the offense, but the edge rush has not produced consistently enough. Mike Macdonald’s scheme can generate pressure from the interior, yet Seattle still needs players who can win from the outside. Dante Fowler was a reasonable low-cost gamble, but his impact has been limited. If the Seahawks want to improve their ability to pressure quarterbacks in critical situations, Khalil Mack is an obvious target. Mack has three sacks and five tackles for loss through six games in 2026. The veteran is playing on a one-year, $18 million contract with the Chargers, who have struggled badly enough to invite questions about whether they might consider moving veterans. Mack would bring proven pass-rush ability, strength against the run and experience in high-leverage situations. He could also help Seattle manage the workload and maintain a higher level of pressure throughout the game. The cost would matter. Other contenders would likely be interested in a player with Mack’s résumé. Still, if Los Angeles makes him available, this is the kind of short-term acquisition that could improve Seattle without requiring a long-term commitment. YaYa Diaby is another possibility. He recorded nine sacks and 62 pressures in 2025, but has started slowly in 2026, with no sacks and seven pressures. Diaby is younger than Mack and offers more long-term upside, particularly because his contract is expiring. He also has the athleticism and run-defense ability to fit Macdonald’s scheme. The uncertainty is whether Tampa Bay would actually sell, and whether Seattle would be willing to pay enough to beat competing offers. Carl Granderson could provide another option. He recorded six sacks in 2025 and has 2.5 through four games this season. His size and ability to defend the run make him an interesting fit, although his contract runs through 2027, so he would not be a rental. New Orleans also has its own division race to consider. Will McDonald IV would offer explosive speed, but the New York Jets exercised his fifth-year option, making him a more complicated and potentially expensive target. Cornerback: The value of insurance Brandon Stephens is worth monitoring if the Jets become sellers. He spent four seasons in Baltimore, including the period when Macdonald was part of the Ravens’ coaching staff. That familiarity could ease his transition, although it would not automatically make him a perfect fit. Cam Hart of the Chargers is a more developmental option. His size and physical profile are intriguing, but Seattle would need to determine whether he is ready to contribute consistently. Kelee Ringo of the Eagles is the speculative alternative. He entered the league with considerable potential after playing at Georgia, but has yet to become a consistent contributor. A change of scenery could help, particularly if the acquisition cost is low. Quenton Nelson: The opportunity Seattle shouldn’t ignore If the Seahawks are serious about improving the offense, Quenton Nelson may be the most compelling target available. Nelson is 30 years old, a six-time first-team All-Pro and an eight-time Pro Bowler. He is in the final year of his current contract, making him a different proposition from Taylor. Nelson has a elite zone-blocking performance and the possibility of acquiring him for a second-round pick, similar to what Seattle paid for Leonard Williams in 2023. Maybe Anthony Bradford could be included in a package, giving Indianapolis a younger guard to evaluate while Seattle opens a spot for Nelson. Nelson would also force a decision about Grey Zabel. Both players are left guards, so Seattle would need to consider moving Zabel to right guard or exploring another reshuffle. The important point is that the adjustment is manageable. Seattle should not reject the opportunity to acquire an elite guard simply because it would require changes elsewhere on the line. The comparison with Leonard Williams is especially strong. How Raheem Morris has made 49ers’ defense a force despite injuries, reliance on rookies (paywall) “ The 49ers still play a high rate of cover 3, but Morris has added funky disguises, so they are getting to their coverages in unorthodox ways. He’s also increased their use of cover 6 (cover 4 and cover 2 combo) up to 17.4 percent. The 49ers used cover 6 on only 7.1 percent of snaps from 2022 to 2025, signaling a move away from the Legion of Boom-influenced system Shanahan has favored throughout his 49ers tenure. Morris has put his stamp on a 49ers defensive scheme and matches some of Shanahan’s offensive creativity. If the rookies keep improving as the season progresses and Bosa looks like himself, this 49ers unit can have an exceptional pass defense.” 49ers DE Romello Height, with a club, new helmet and new cleats, is finding his groove (paywall) “After playing throughout the preseason and in Week 1 with a Guardian Cap, he decided it was too heavy and was slowing him down. Juszczyk said he was drawn to the helmet because of its weight and safety rating. “It’s a little bigger,” he said. “It has a little astronaut look to it. But your neck is so much less sore.” Mostly, Height has had to adjust to playing with the bulky club he’s been wearing on his right hand since breaking it in the Week 2 win over the Miami Dolphins. He said the cast has compromised his power rush and that he’s had to compensate with a better get-off, sharper inside moves and more research on his adversary’s tendencies. “Basically, I had to change up my game plan,” he said. The Bears have faced the 10th-most difficult schedule, while the Patriots sit 28th. The Bears took the league by storm after they scored 59 points on the road to begin the season. They lost their quarterback and the game the next week against the Vikings. Since then, their other slip-up was with a backup quarterback. In his first game in nearly a month, Caleb Williams threw for over 300 yards and a touchdown against the Atlanta Falcons last week, doing it exclusively from the pocket. The Patriots are down multiple cornerbacks, and All-Pro corner Christian Gonzalez has an illness. It could be a long night for New England’s secondary, and a big night for Luther Burden and Colston Loveland. It took a bit for him to warm up and be aggressive, but Michael Penix ended up throwing for three touchdowns and 225 yards against the Bears in Week 6. Jordan Love threw for 367 yards against Chicago the week before. You can throw it on the Bears. Drake Maye has been on a three-week heater, throwing 10 touchdowns to one interception in the past three games. The Patriots have scored at least 26 points in each game. However, the Patriots are down multiple starting offensive linemen on this side of the ball. That could slow them down, or at least lead to more mistakes that put them behind the chains. Whenever it’s an AFC versus NFC matchup, I’ll side with the latter. It’s the stronger conference from top to bottom. With Williams, Chicago looks closer to a top-5 team. Their floor is one of the highest in the league. Maye might come back down to earth without a healthy offensive line, while the Pats’ could be leakier than usual in the secondary without Carlton Davis. Bears 31, Patriots 20.

title: ESPN proposes a 49ers-Colts trade
summary: The San Francisco 49ers are undefeated and sit atop the NFC. In an interview last week, general manager John Lynch joked about how the team was connected to every player on the trade market. The 49ers could stand to add depth at defensive tackle. You can never have enough pass rushers, so any defensive lineman […]
full_text: (Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers are undefeated and sit atop the NFC. In an interview last week, general manager John Lynch joked about how the team was connected to every player on the trade market. The 49ers could stand to add depth at defensive tackle. You can never have enough pass rushers, so any defensive lineman would be a welcome addition. Here’s ESPN’s Bill Barnwell’s excerpt from one of his trade proposals in today’s article: San Francisco fans are understandably dreaming about a reunion with DeForest Buckner , who was once dealt in the opposite direction between these two teams for a first-round pick, but I’m not sure that’s as great of a fit as it might seem. The 49ers already have Osa Odighizuwa playing in that penetrating defensive tackle role, and rookie Gracen Halton has flashed alongside him, with sacks in each of the past two games. Buckner is still a great player, and I wouldn’t fault the 49ers for just lining up as many superstars up front as possible and daring opposing offensive lines to simply figure it out, but this team really needs more help at nose tackle. San Francisco is 27th in success rate against the run so far this season. A year ago, it was 31st. The 49ers have been able to insulate themselves against run game issues by playing from ahead for most of the season, but they’ll need to be better against the run by the postseason. Adding Stewart to the defensive line rotation would go a long way in helping San Francisco plug up those run game woes. The 33-year-old is a useful player and in the final year of his deal, but his contract is also expensive; he’s owed $8.2 million in cash over the remainder of the season. The 49ers don’t have cap concerns after restructuring some of their more significant deals, but that’s a big cash outlay. They could encourage the Colts to absorb more of the money by offering a better draft pick, but with the 49ers still undefeated and fielding one of the oldest cores in football, I’d push ownership to spend now to try to build a team that can win a title. Stewart isn’t the most exciting addition, but he’s the sort of player the Niners need. Sidebar: Right underneath it, Barnwell has the Rams trading for…a kicker. For what it’s worth, Sumer Sports has the 49ers 16th in rushing success rate. RBSDM has them 14th. If you filter it down to success rate against running backs, you still get 16th. So the defense is league average no matter how you split it. That doesn’t change the point of adding a nose tackle. I’d still push back, though. Raheem Morris is thriving with athletes up front. They are winning with quickness and are always on the move. The 5-down fronts help, too. For a seventh-rounder, sure. But, in my opinion, not having “space eaters” who aren’t agile, like Alfred Collins and CJ West, has quietly benefited the defensive line. They are covering more ground and causing more chaos. With a body type like Stewart, you’re unlikely to yield similar results.
author: Kyle Posey

title: 3 things to watch for in 49ers-Falcons: Battle of two top-7 run defenses
summary: The San Francisco 49ers are 6-0, looking to go into their bye week undefeated, but the Atlanta Falcons stand in their way. Historically, the 49ers have struggled in Atlanta. You will have to go back to 2013 to find the last win for the 49ers in Atlanta. In fact, the 49ers have won just once […]
full_text: Photo by Lachlan Cunningham/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers are 6-0, looking to go into their bye week undefeated, but the Atlanta Falcons stand in their way. Historically, the 49ers have struggled in Atlanta. You will have to go back to 2013 to find the last win for the 49ers in Atlanta. In fact, the 49ers have won just once in the last five meetings in Atlanta. Teams and coaches change, but the 49ers are looking to snap the streak on Sunday. Health, particularly at wide receiver, will be a huge part of any preview. While we still have no official word on Mike Evans’ status for Sunday, I wouldn’t count on him being active with the bye week coming up. Christian Kirk is trending toward his first action, but what will his snap share be, and how effective can he be after such a long stretch of inactivity? Still, the hope is that Kyle Shanahan can devise a game plan to counteract the potential losses at receiver and put his team in a position to put points on the board. Here are three things to watch for on Sunday: Atlanta’s run defense vs. San Francisco’s run defense With Bijan Robinson, Atlanta is dangerous running the football. The dynamic weapon is incredibly hard to contain. Even the addition of former 49er Brian Robinson makes Atlanta’s rushing attack as potent as any in the NFL. The 49ers’ run defense ranks sixth in the NFL, behind Seattle, with an EPA/rush allowed of -0.16. The addition of Nick Bosa, potentially, and Dre Greenlaw, fresh off suspension, only boosts the entire defense. Now, conventional wisdom would say that since the 49ers are down weapons on the outside, they should lean on the run game. That is a wise assumption, but Atlanta leads the NFL in EPA/rush allowed at -0.20. Atlanta’s defense has an EPA of zero on passes. So can the 49ers afford to try and test the passing defense without reliable route runners and separators? The chess match will be between Shanahan and Jeff Ulbrich on Sunday. Limiting Atlanta’s explosive plays through the air The 49ers defense has done well limiting explosive plays through the air and on the ground in 2026. Sunday proves to be an interesting challenge for the defense. Michael Penix’s return has given the Falcons offense life. In fact, the Falcons are fourth in the NFL with an explosive play rate of 7.2%. Now, credit has to be given to Robinson on the ground for contributing to this number. The marquee name is Drake London, and with good reason, but it’s journeyman Jahan Dotson who has come on as of late. The receiver has a modest seven receptions over his last three games, but looking at the nature of the catches tells a different story. Dotson has averaged 27.0 yards per catch twice and, last week, averaged 29 yards per catch with two touchdowns. Dotson running routes from the slot can be an issue, as Upton Stout is dealing with an injury and Washington picked on him in coverage. Capitalizing in the red zone The 49ers have been incredibly efficient in the red zone. Yes, Evans has a great deal to do with that, but George Kittle and Christian McCaffrey do as well. The 49ers will have to capitalize on any and every red zone opportunity with touchdowns on Sunday. Atlanta’s red zone defense ranks 26th in the NFL with a success rate allowed of 49.38%. While Atlanta’s run defense has been stingy overall, in the red zone their EPA number plummets to 0.15/rush. The EPA/pass number is at zero, but the 49ers will have to bully their way into the end zone in the red area. Expect a heavy dose of McCaffrey in this game through the air and on the ground, but these opportunities need to be punctuated on the ground.
author: Jason Aponte

title: Fact or fiction: The 49ers need to trade for a wide receiver ahead of the deadline
summary: After their Week 2 win over the Detroit Lions in 2018, San Francisco 49ers cornerback Richard Sherman told the media, “A win is a win, but it feels like a loss.” That’s how fans are reacting to the 49ers’ Week 6 win over the one-win Commanders. The 20-3 halftime lead became a distant memory as […]
full_text: (Photo by Stephen Lam/San Francisco Chronicle via Getty Images) After their Week 2 win over the Detroit Lions in 2018, San Francisco 49ers cornerback Richard Sherman told the media, “A win is a win, but it feels like a loss.” That’s how fans are reacting to the 49ers’ Week 6 win over the one-win Commanders. The 20-3 halftime lead became a distant memory as Washington crossed midfield with under a minute left and a chance to win. That’s led to overreactions, from trades that’ll upgrade the team to doubts about the defense. Today, we’ll play a fact-or-fiction game with one hypothetical question on each side of the ball. Fact or fiction: The 49ers need to trade for a wide receiver ahead of the trade deadline The most popular thing being talked about surrounding the 49ers is the one I vehemently disagree with. The Niners’ offense didn’t stall in the second half because they were without Mike Evans. They had an 11-play drive that chewed up over six minutes on the clock on their first drive of the second half. But Brock Purdy’s third-and-three pass was tipped, and the offense settled for a field goal. The throw was intended for Brandin Cooks in the end zone and would’ve likely resulted in a touchdown. On the same play, Kyle Juszczyk and Christian McCaffrey were open to the left at the top of the screen. Here is the screenshot from when Purdy released the ball: The idea that the Niners couldn’t create separation without Evans is off base. Three targets were open on this play. On their next drive, Cooks’ timing was off on a deep crossing route. He ran into George Kittle, resulting in a sack and eventually a punt. Had those two not collided, Cooks would’ve been wide open for an explosive play. The second-to-last drive stalled on another sack. This time, there was a free rusher, but Purdy didn’t find his outlet receiver out of the backfield. Instead, he attempted to scramble at the last minute. I’m more inclined to believe the Kyle Shanahan-led offense, with a week of practice to prepare without Mike Evans, will be well-equipped to score. I’d also argue the pass-catching corps heading into Week 7 without Evans is still better than what the offense trotted out on a weekly basis in 2025—not to mention the improved offensive line and quarterback. The panic centers around Evans and his potential absence. It comes off as a prisoner-of-the-moment move, wanting to trade for a wideout. The team could essentially give Evans close to three weeks off so he can recover ahead of Week 9 against the Raiders. The thought of adding to a strength makes sense on the surface. It’s part of the reason the Niners should be open to adding to the defensive line. However, the players being floated around don’t move the needle enough to warrant moving draft picks. They would if the 49ers were going to miss the wideouts currently injured for the rest of the season, but that’s not the case. Christian Kirk practiced in full on Wednesday. He appears set to make his debut. Let’s use Colts receiver Josh Downs as an example, a player we highlighted as a trade target earlier this month . Downs runs 70% of his routes from the slot. That’s where Kirk figures to line up. Just last week against the Titans, Downs caught a few underneath throws, couldn’t hold onto a contested catch against Isaiah Oliver- yes, that Isaiah Oliver- and also dropped a wide-open pass. He caught a 23-yarder that was a deep pass over the middle. But nothing about his game suggests Kirk or any of the other wideouts couldn’t do the same with the same opportunity. Downs currently has a 20.6% target share. He wouldn’t sniff that number on a team that throws the ball to Evans 23.5% of the time, George Kittle 21.7% of the time, and Christian McCaffrey 21.1% of the time. Downs, or any wideout under consideration, isn’t on the same level as those three. Between Kirk, Demarcus Robinson, and Deebo Samuel—not to mention De’Zhaun Stribling—the 49ers already have a bit of a logjam in their receiver room. But it is the Niners, and the primary concern, per every year ever, is health. Shanahan can weather the storm without a week of Evans. After all, no offense has generated a higher EPA per pass or success rate through the air than San Francisco. The receiver room should be as close to healthy coming out of the bye week, making the need for a receiver moot with Robinson and Samuel back. Where would the targets go to Downs, or Brian Thomas, or pick your receiver? A rental, like Downs, makes less sense. If the 49ers are going to swing, it should look more like Bryce Eldridge than a guy who blends in with the rest of the Triple-A lineup — looking at you, Shay Whitcomb. Like Eldridge, that player needs to be a legitimate impact player. If you’re looking for a playmaker, call the Saints to see if Chris Olave is for sale. Check with the Jets to see if Garrett Wilson is available. Those are game-changers who complement Evans and will be around beyond this season. Even then, you’re stunting Stribling’s growth and basically pulling the plug on Ricky Pearsall. From a team-building perspective, the 49ers have everything they need at receiver in-house. The reason the Niners will win the Super Bowl is already on the roster. We’ve been watching him for six weeks. It’s the receiver who has the highest EPA per target in the league. They already went out and got Brock a WR1. Now, it’s about keeping him healthy and ensuring he’s available late in the season. Fact or fiction: Fiction, easily. If the 49ers are calling the Colts, Downs should be third on the list. DeForest Buckner is No. 1, with Quenton Nelson 1b. You know how to improve your offense? Go out and get the left guard with the fifth-most impact blocks of any player this year who hasn’t allowed a sack and has the same pressure percentage as Trent Williams. Now that’s a rental that makes sense. Downs or a 6-time All-Pro who makes your run game better, gives your quarterback more time to throw, and allows your wideouts more time to get open? Tough choice. Buckner doesn’t need any explanation. But if the Niners make a trade, it should build on their strength. This season, that’s in the trenches on both sides of the ball.

title: NFL Week 7 Super Bowl odds: Are the 49ers distancing themselves from the field?
summary: Heading into the season, the San Francisco 49ers were seen as the clear No. 3 team in the NFC West across all sportsbooks, with many having the Los Angeles Rams as the Super Bowl favorites and the Seattle Seahawks as true contenders as well. Fast-forward six weeks, and the 49ers are 6-0, while the reeling […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 19: Christian McCaffrey #23 of the San Francisco 49ers runs with the ball in the second quarter during the game against the Washington Commanders at Levi's Stadium on October 19, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images Heading into the season, the San Francisco 49ers were seen as the clear No. 3 team in the NFC West across all sportsbooks, with many having the Los Angeles Rams as the Super Bowl favorites and the Seattle Seahawks as true contenders as well. Fast-forward six weeks, and the 49ers are 6-0, while the reeling Rams lost to the Arizona Cardinals this weekend to fall to 2-4. The Seattle Seahawks, on the other hand, have lost two straight and now sit at 3-3 with problems to address on offense. Still, for weeks, the oddsmakers had the Rams as a top-two team to win the Super Bowl, even with their poor early results. We’re finally starting to see things really shift, especially when looking at the NFC picture. For the second straight week, the 49ers are the clear favorites to win the Super Bowl. On DraftKings, they have +540 odds to win, with the Buffalo Bills at +750 odds in second place. On FanDuel, they’re +600 to win the Super Bowl, while the Bills are +700. Things change, though, when you look at the NFC pennant. The 49ers are clear favorites to make it to the Super Bowl out of the NFC at +240 odds. The Seattle Seahawks and Los Angeles Rams come in next at +670 and +700, respectively, followed by the Minnesota Vikings (+700) and Chicago Bears (+790). The Niners are -650 favorites to win their division, easily the best mark of any division favorite. On the NFC side, the 49ers seem like the clear favorites right now. They’re the only 6-0 team, with the other undefeated NFC team, the Minnesota Vikings, still looking shaky on the offensive end. The two top contenders from the conference, the Rams and Seahawks, both look like they’ve got a number of problems to work out. The NFC North has four contenders that could all be a tough matchup, leaving for a crowded division picture. Meanwhile, the NFC South and NFC East haven’t been very inspiring so far. The Rams have fallen all the way to +1200 odds, while the Seahawks are now at +1350 odds to win the Super Bowl. Interestingly, both teams are still favored to make the playoffs on FanDuel, but public opinion has soured on them from their preseason position. The AFC side is where the top competition for a Super Bowl currently lies. On DraftKings and FanDuel, the three teams with the best Super Bowl odds after the 49ers are the Buffalo Bills, Kansas City Chiefs, and Baltimore Ravens. But through seven weeks, we’re starting to see the 49ers distance themselves from the field, at least in the NFC, more, even with their injury situation.
author: Rohan Chakravarthi

title: Kyle Shanahan’s former star WR believes he’ll never win a Super Bowl
summary: The San Francisco 49ers are at the top of the NFL right now, sitting at 6-0 after their 23-17 win over the Washington Commanders. After starting the year with the third-best odds in their own division, the 49ers are the clear frontrunners to win the NFC and currently stand as the favorites to win the […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WA - OCTOBER 11: Head Coach Kyle Shanahan of the San Francisco 49ers awards a game ball to Mike Evans #5 in the locker room after the game against the Seattle Seahawks at Lumen Field on October 11, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. The 49ers defeated the Seahawks 32-29. (Photo by Michael Zagaris/San Francisco 49ers/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers are at the top of the NFL right now, sitting at 6-0 after their 23-17 win over the Washington Commanders. After starting the year with the third-best odds in their own division, the 49ers are the clear frontrunners to win the NFC and currently stand as the favorites to win the Super Bowl at +600, according to FanDuel. San Francisco has been clicking everywhere this season, despite their bevy of injuries. Behind MVP-level play from Brock Purdy and an elite No. 1 receiver in Mike Evans, the 49ers offense has been quite efficient throughout the year. The defense, on the other hand, has overcome the loss of Nick Bosa over the last few weeks to be a strong finishing team with a ton of growing young talent under Raheem Morris. Even with the injuries, it feels like this could be the year for the 49ers, and they’ll get a chance to get a lot of players healthy following their bye in Week 8. Ultimately, it will come down to the playoffs, where the 49ers have had their moments over the last seven years, but have come up short in their pursuit of the Super Bowl. They made it there in 2019, lost in the NFC Championship Game in 2021 and 2022, made it there again in 2023, and then lost in the divisional round last year. Will Kyle Shanahan finally get his Super Bowl here in 2026? One of his former star receivers, Roddy White, doesn’t believe so, and also doesn’t ever see him winning a ring for a few reasons. “No,” White said when asked about Shanahan winning a ring during his career on The Up And Adams Show. “They start like this every year. That team starts very fast every year. The only time they haven’t started fast is when they had everybody hurt. And this year they’re still managing to get people hurt, but they’re off to a good start. I think, me personally, that he’s a great offensive mind, right? “But in tough situations, in pressure situations, the over-aggressive play calls always get him in trouble. And I think that’s just his mentality. He doesn’t play situational football well. That’s the only thing that I think that’s really like a knock on his game. And the thing that he does, he doesn’t play like situational football well. And that gets his team in trouble when you play against great quarterbacks. And when you make it to a Super Bowl, you’re gonna be playing against a great quarterback.” The four-time Pro Bowl receiver for the Atlanta Falcons believes Shanahan has yet to learn game management and handling those situations in playoff games. “Your ability to understand the flow of the game and the things like that is going to help you win those games,” White continued. “And I think especially if you have to play Patrick Mahomes in the Super Bowl. That guy has learned from Tom Brady, just playing him each and every year, playing him in Super Bowls. He knows what it takes. He can read what’s going on. He knows how to handle those situations, and he always comes out as a winner because he doesn’t give himself an opportunity to lose the game. And I think that Kyle always thinks about I have to win the game. I have to win the game instead of putting his players in the best position to win the game. “He’s a great play caller, like great play caller. The play call sheet is deep. I will say that. But he seems to have a guy that can handle it. Being a part of that and just doing everything when Matt [Ryan] was there and going through everything. I mean, man, we’ll be on the sideline, and he’ll see something, boom, boom, boom. He’d be like, hey, man, I know we didn’t work this in practice, but it’s gonna work. Hey, this is what I want you to do. Boom, go out there, extra eye, execute the play, works. Boom, explosive play. So he’s very, very smart. I just think the aggressive play calling when not needed in pressure situations always gets the best of him.” Shanahan’s game management, especially in go-for situations, had been one of the more scrutinized parts of him as a head coach earlier in his career. He had generally been too conservative in those situations and often went against analytics with his decisions. That has changed over the past few years, but White believes he’s gotten too aggressive as a play-caller. So far this season, he’s been having a great year after arguably the best coaching season of his career in 2025 with a battered 49ers team. We’ll see if that can translate to postseason success, but the 49ers are putting themselves in a great spot to be successful in January with their start to the season.
author: Rohan Chakravarthi

title: 49ers News: We’re on to Atlanta
summary: My bad on missing yesterday’s nuggets. Even Christian McCaffrey fumbles sometimes.  Atlanta is always a tough out, no matter how bad they are. They can just bizarrely win against the 49ers for whatever reason. Their defense is looking good. I read an interesting article on the Athletic about it… their d-line coach, this guy named […]
full_text: SAN FRANCISCO, CA - DECEMBER 23: Inside linebacker NaVorro Bowman #53 of the San Francisco 49ers returns an interception for a touchdown in the fourth quarter against the Atlanta Falcons during a game at Candlestick Park on December 23, 2013 in San Francisco, California. (Photo by Stephen Dunn/Getty Images) | Getty Images My bad on missing yesterday’s nuggets. Even Christian McCaffrey fumbles sometimes. Atlanta is always a tough out, no matter how bad they are. They can just bizarrely win against the 49ers for whatever reason. Their defense is looking good. I read an interesting article on the Athletic about it… their d-line coach, this guy named Nate Ollie, does a Kris Kocurek / peak Saleh days impersonation with his “attack-style defense”. He tells his players that if “they think, they stink”, so the defensive linemen have to do nothing but go after the ball. It’s lead to their interior defenders leading the league, with Brandon Dorlus tied for #1 most QB pressures from an interior d-lineman. Their back seven is asked to do more, and while Divine Deablo is one of the better linebackers (and best names) in the league, there’ll often be space to be found if the 49ers linemen get to the second level effectively enough. It’ll be fascinating to see how Kyle Shanahan attacks that without anybody at wide receiver. The end of last game has my antennas up a little bit, but I’m still confident in my preseason prediction. No Nick Bosa for the 49ers; Kyle Shanahan is hopeful he returns on Thursday “Since the 49ers played on Monday, Shanahan said Wednesday’s practice will be a walkthrough. Linebacker Dre Greenlaw returns to practice. As for wide receiver Christian Kirk, Shanahan said, “He had a good week of practice last week. He’ll be out there again today. Hopefully, he feels good at the end of the week.” Kyle Shanahan shares updates ahead of 49ers-Falcons game “It’s actually not call the play faster. It’s, ‘I need it again.’ It gets cut off at 15, so sometimes no one can hear and a lot of the quarterbacks do it because I always call a play and then I just walk and think. I don’t always watch the huddle and a lot of times [QB] Mac [Jones] or someone, because they’ll be like, ‘Hey, we didn’t get it. It was choppy.’ Or someone will yell, ‘Brock’s yelling at you,’ which I can’t always hear. I did hear him a couple of times in this game, so I look up and then I try to do it again as long as it’s not past 15 seconds. Sometimes he’ll do it and I don’t get a heads up to like 16 and I start to do it again and he hears half the play call because it shuts off at 15…..I don’t remember what the play was. Probably happened five times in the game, so that’s something that happens a lot. Headsets do that.” Nick Bosa misses practice Wednesday, but 49ers hope he will return this week “(He) can’t go today but hoping he’ll be out there tomorrow,” Shanahan said of Bosa. 49ers minutia minute: Rookies Romello Height, Jaden Dugger shined on defense (paywall) “ In the run-up to the game, Halton talked about “building a cage” against the elusive Daniels, who ran for 103 yards and two touchdowns a week earlier, then followed through by snagging Daniels for a sack as he tried to escape in the second quarter. Fred Warner was blitzing on the play, and Daniels would have had room to roam had Halton not taken him down. The 49ers hit Daniels a season-high 10 times. To put that in perspective, they sacked Sam Darnold five times last week but finished with eight quarterback hits. Raheem Morris is back in Atlanta — and he’s bringing his surging 49ers defense “Morris is also utilizing more “match” coverage, which asks defenders to start in traditional zone drops, keep their eyes on the quarterback and read routes to tighten up throwing lanes. If a pass catcher crosses into their path, the defender picks up that player, often only turning him loose for checkdowns and short gains. The approach has not only served to limit big plays, but it has also allowed the secondary to be more active. That was evident in Green’s two-interception game in Seattle and Mustapha’s jarring hits to help seal Monday night’s win over Washington. “Those guys aren’t counting on linebackers, so they have to be more aggressive in coverage,” Shanahan said. “Those guys are playing concepts to stop plays without any help and that’s been their edge. I think it’s made them better. It’s given them more confidence in practice, and I think that’s what we’re all seeing in games.” How long might 49ers’ Mike Evans be sidelined? Surgeon provides perspective on Achilles tendinitis (paywall) “Achilles tendinitis is an overuse injury, an inflammation of the tendon, that causes pain and tightness. Serious cases can involve microscopic degeneration, small tears in the fibers in the middle of the tendon, that can increase the odds of a rupture. Given Evans’ age, and history with Achilles tendinitis, Jung said Evans is likely dealing with “wear and tear,” minor tissue degeneration that might have progressed to the point where he has had a flare-up severe enough to sideline him. Evans did not miss a game due to an Achilles issue in his first 12 seasons. Achilles tendinitis is often treated with rest, icing and supportive footwear. Many cases can resolve within a few weeks. Assuming Evans didn’t seriously exacerbate his condition by playing Monday, it’s conceivable he could miss just one game….“If it’s just some (Achilles) wear and tear, then you’re probably in a situation where you’re managing it,” Jung said. “You try to get it to a point where it settles down, it doesn’t flare up and you just kind of keep managing it.”

title: How to win, how to lose: Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Carolina Panthers week 7 game preview
summary: After week five’s phenomenal upset of the Dallas Cowboys in primetime, week six featured a nice fall back down to earth for Todd Bowles, the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, and their fans. The Buccaneers, despite leading for the entirety of the game, managed to be outscored 16-3 in the fourth quarter and then 7-0 in overtime, […]
full_text: Dec 1, 2024; Charlotte, North Carolina, USA; Tampa Bay Buccaneers running back Bucky Irving (7) outruns Carolina Panthers linebacker Trevin Wallace (56) during the second quarter at Bank of America Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jim Dedmon-Imagn Images | USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Con After week five’s phenomenal upset of the Dallas Cowboys in primetime, week six featured a nice fall back down to earth for Todd Bowles, the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, and their fans. The Buccaneers, despite leading for the entirety of the game, managed to be outscored 16-3 in the fourth quarter and then 7-0 in overtime, pulling a loss from the jaws of victory. This week, Tampa Bay travels north for a divisional matchup against the 3-2 first place Carolina Panthers. Sunday’s week seven battle between the Panthers and the Bucs is a tougher one than most feel out because their is a momentous what if on Tampa’s side of the equation. — What if Sunday is Baker Mayfield’s first game back? — If this Sunday features Baker Mayfield under center for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers as opposed to Jalon Daniels, everything shifts for Tampa. Mayfield versus Daniels wouldn’t spell a clear victory for the Buccaneers or be a definitive reason they should be favored, but it would represent a significant alteration in the way the Buccaneers’ offense can approach the game. Baker Mayfield was reported to have been throwing this week (with a glove on) so for the first time in nearly a month, Mayfield suiting up feels like a possibility. That being said, for the context of this article, we will be operating as if it is going to Jalon Daniels and not Baker Mayfield throwing passes for the Bucs on Sunday. “Even when I don’t see, I still believe.” Jeremy Camp How can the Buccaneers win? Great question. The 2026 season is six weeks in and the reality is the Tampa Bay Buccaneers are a bad football team. They are not well coached, they come into games with poor strategy and gameplans, they lack the ability as players to overcome those shortcomings, and as a result they’ve lost five of six to start. Not only is the record bad, but they don’t even do very many things particularly well. They have an inconsistence rushing attack (albeit good at times), pass protection has been largely optional, when there is time to throw accuracy isn’t a given, but even when there are well placed accurate passes drops are running a muck. The team’s defense has been solid, but also not so solid depending on the day, time of day, and time of the game as it pertains to that time of day, as evident by their highly inconsistent stats— Ranking top five in both rush yards allowed and total yards allowed, but bottom-half of the league in points allowed. Special teams has the crown of boasting the team’s best individual player— Chase McLaughlin. There is no better Tampa Bay Buccaneer at this point in time than McLaughlin, however, on the other side of things they have a highly inconsistent, unreliable, well-paid punter. With an underratedly-formidable opponent on the schedule this week, the Buccaneers don’t have a significantly clear path to victory. Tampa is the underdog, should be the underdog, and will need to play above their skis just to hang around and maybe pull out a close victory. The issue, even in that game theory, is the Buccaneers have been absolutely horrendous in close games. Every week the Buccaneers seem to find themselves in one-score games and they manifest ways to lose them. Tampa has been 1-5 in one-score games this season— That’s bad, but it gets worse. The Buccaneers have been 3-9 in their last 12 one-score games. Worse still, the team’s record in games that have been decided by one score, under Todd Bowles is an appalling 19-24. So it would seem their best path to victory would be blowing out the Carolina Panthers, and somehow that seems even more unlikely. Can the Buccaneers win? Yes, any team can have their day on any given Sunday (or Thursday ), but the scenario is not one that lends itself towards that conclusion. Sometimes there is not much more than hope. “Sacking a quarterback is just like you devastate a city or you cream a multitude of people. I mean it’s just like you put all the offensive players in one bag and I just take a baseball bat and beat on the bag.” Deacon Jones How can the Buccaneers lose? Fail to slow down Bryce Young. Simply put, Bryce Young has been sensational this season. In 2026, national media will treat the Carolina Panthers and the entire NFC South like speed limit signs on the I-95. While being ignored, Young has produced. The Panthers are only 3-2 (not great, but by the standards of the NFC South— Superb), however, Young has been lights out. Carolina’s former number one overall pick, turned bust, has now transformed himself into a very good player. In five games, Young’s thrown 11 touchdowns to go along with only two interceptions. Those are numbers that weren’t even in the range of reachable for Young based on his performance over the last few seasons, but we are here not there. Carolina’s offense has totaled 25+ points in all but one game this season, they average the fourth most points per game in the league. The Buccaneers’ defense has been fluky in 2026. The group has been really reliable and able to stall offenses of both high and low caliber, until the team really needs them to. At that point, they tend to fold. Statistically, the matchup should be a good one. The Buccaneers have the defense to combat Carolina’s attack and favor may even be on the Bucs’ side as Bryce Young has been pretty consistently sacked this season— 12 times in just five games which plays right into what has been a weakness for Todd Bowles’ defense for nearly a half-decade now. Sunday would be an excellent opportunity for guys like Yaya Diaby and Calijah Kancey to start their seasons and also for Rueben Bain Jr. and David Walker to continue to build on their momentum from a week ago— three sacks between the two of them. In 2026, Young and the Panthers are an opponent that needs to be respected. They are in first place and will be motivated to stay there. For the better part of the 2020’s, the NFC South has been victim of tiebreakers— Divisional games matter and there is a zero percent the Panthers will be overlooking the Buccaneers on Sunday.
author: Will Walsh

summary: The Tennessee Titans released veteran defensive tackle Jordan Elliott earlier this week. The complete details are now available. A to Z Sports and Easton Freeze reported Elliott allegedly threatened a teammate (reportedly JC Latham) with gun violence, even showing intent before the situation was calmed. Unacceptable stuff. Naturally, the Titans released Elliott even though head […]
full_text: NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - AUGUST 29: Solomon Thomas #90 of the Tennessee Titans looks on during the second half of the Week 3 preseason game against the Chicago Bears at Nissan Stadium on August 29, 2026 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Johnnie Izquierdo/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Tennessee Titans released veteran defensive tackle Jordan Elliott earlier this week . The complete details are now available. A to Z Sports and Easton Freeze reported Elliott allegedly threatened a teammate ( reportedly JC Latham ) with gun violence, even showing intent before the situation was calmed. Unacceptable stuff. Naturally, the Titans released Elliott even though head coach Robert Saleh vouched for him to receive a future opportunity elsewhere during Wednesday’s presser. Elliott was playing quality football as a rotational defensive lineman after signing a two-year contract with the team in free agency. Saleh, Aaron Whitecotton, and Mike Borgonzi must deal with the fallout. We’ve identified three Titans players who could help the defensive line replace Elliott. Nazir Stackhouse Nose tackle Nazir Stackhouse helped replace Elliott in Sunday’s Week 6 win over the Colts. He served as the primary interior run stopper behind Jeffery Simmons and John Franklin-Myers. Remember, that is essentially the role Elliott was playing. The Titans claimed Stackhouse off waivers from the Green Bay Packers after final cuts. He played well as a big-bodied space eater. Solomon Thomas The Titans brought Elliott to Tennessee as a free agent this past offseason partially because he played for Coach Saleh before. Understanding his system is vital to the success of the scheme. Well, following Elliott’s departure, the only Titans interior defender on the roster who has played for Saleh before is veteran DT Solomon Thomas. Timmy Horne When the Titans ruled out Elliott for Sunday’s game versus the Colts, they made Timmy Horne a gameday call-up. The four-year pro ended up playing a sizable 25 snaps. Horne is listed as being 312 pounds via the team’s official website; he’s a more traditional nose tackle who can play a similar role to Elliott. With the Titans having an open spot on the 53-man roster following Elliott’s release, promoting Horne from the practice squad would make sense.
